The main question.Was it worth it? A thousand times yes. I'll gladly visit s&w even if it isn't restaurant week. The food, service, attention to detail was all impeccable. 10/10 or 5/5 (on Yelp)

Title: A Trendy Twist on Chinese Cuisine

I recently dined at a restaurant that struck an impressive balance between traditional Chinese aesthetics and modern vibes. The ambiance was incredible—authentically Chinese with a trendy edge that made for a fantastic dining atmosphere.

The food did not disappoint. The pork feet were a standout, an incredible dish that paid homage to authentic flavors. While the Peking duck was delicious, I did miss the traditional thin flour shells, as they were substituted with buns—a minor detail that could be improved upon for authenticity's sake.

What truly surprised me was the extensive non-alcoholic drink menu. The milk tea I opted for was delightful, adding to the already enjoyable meal.

Service was top-notch with waiters who were as friendly as they were attentive. Overall, my experience was stellar, and I'm certain I'll be returning. With such high standards, it's only a matter of time before this place becomes the talk of the town. Highly recommended for those seeking an authentic yet contemporary Chinese dining experience.
Was starving at 12:30am and couldn't find any quality eats.  Decided to come here on a whim and I regret not coming here sooner. Food was fresh and fast and service was good.

Title: Good Taste Comes with a High Price at Local Korean Spot

I recently stopped by a Korean restaurant near my office for lunch, intrigued by the menu. The meal for two included three dishes, totaling $88 without any beverages, which felt steep for a midday meal. While the flavors were generally pleasing, the fired chicken disappointed - its sizable appearance was deceptive, with a thick batter overshadowing the scant meat. The large hotpot, though flavorful, seemed rather simple for its nearly $40 price tag. Despite these setbacks, the overall taste earns my approval.

Service, however, was a mixed bag. Initially, the staff appeared overly eager to take our order, making frequent interruptions. Yet, when we were finally prepared to order, it became a challenge to attract their attention. All things considered, for those willing to spend a bit more, the restaurant does offer decent Korean cuisine – just don't expect a consistent service experience.

I've had the pleasure of dining at Jeepney on multiple occasions and it has consistently been a delightful experience. As a fan of Filipino cuisine, I consider it to be one of my go-to comfort foods, and Jeepney never disappoints. Their ability to accommodate a large group of twelve for brunch was impressive; the staff was attentive and ensured our mimosas never ran dry, contributing to a festive atmosphere. While the pancakes were satisfying, I'm eager to explore other brunch options on my next visit. Above all, the lumpia stands out as my personal favorite, a must-try for anyone visiting Jeepney. Highly recommended for both their food and service.

This is a Hong Kong style cafe serving comfort food such as instant noodles, baked spaghetti and appetizers like curried fish balls, etc.   Iced lemon tea is my go-to drink, I usually request it with less ice and less sweet.  Occasionally, I would order their noodle soup with the thick vermicelli noodles.  Try their baked dishes and appetizers if you have never been exposed to food from a Hong Kong teahouse. Do not come here to expect Tsui Wah (a famous Cha Chaan Tang chain in Hong Kong) style dishes or anything special, but this place would definitely do it if you miss food or drinks from a Hong Kong style cafe.

Title: A Delightful Foray into Georgian Cuisine

As a Georgian cuisine novice, I ventured to a well-situated eatery, easily accessible by various trains and a mere stroll away. The space, a lengthy gallery of tables culminating in an enchanting back area with an almost al fresco ambiance, seemed perfect for a romantic outing.

In the company of friends, we embarked on a culinary sharing spree. The salads were the first to impress, with a beet creation that converted even my beet-averse palate. A succulent medley of chicken, lamb, and fish followed, alongside a cheese platter and a remarkable cheese boat. The standout was the garlic chicken, which offered comfort in every bite.

Swift and synchronized service ensured a steady flow of dishes, keeping our table continuously graced with a variety of Georgian flavors. This well-orchestrated dining experience has left me eager for a return visit.

Amazing value for the price of the premiere omakase! The two appetizers were interesting I really liked to tofu skin under the maine uni but the nigiri is the star of the show for sure. The three types of toro were so fun to try back to back. The toppings and sauces chef used were interesting and flavorful without overpowering the fish. I really liked the use of shaved egg yolk. There is also a good selection of sake and wine but I love the two japanese beers by kagu both the white and the rouge are excellent companions to sushi. By far the most unique thing we had as part of the omakase was ikura that was still connected and could be sliced like a steak. I've never had it with the fish eggs still attached and served like nigiri instead of as a gunkan. Truly different than any other sushi in the city!! I loved it.

During our visit to NYC, my boyfriend and I enjoyed a delightful brunch at this gem of a restaurant. The venue was quiet, allowing for immediate seating. I opted for the eggs Benedict and was thoroughly impressed by the flawlessly poached egg, which oozed its golden yolk over fresh spinach and a tender brioche bun. The accompanying side salad was a refreshing complement. Service was top-notch, marked by our friendly and attentive waitress. We left satisfied and would undoubtedly return on our next trip to the area.

DELICIOUS Spicy Noodle. I wanted Drunken Noodles, so this is what I ordered and it was great. I had chosen shrimp as my protein, and they were very nice size and very nice amount.   The amount of food was a nice amount.  I ordered thru the "Ritual" app, which I've just been using for about a week or so, and I go in to pick up my order. It's been really quick.  I will update when I enjoy a meal inside the restaurant .  I can say the service, and staff were very nice when I went in to pick up. The restaurant is small and the dish I had tonight , SPICY NOODLES", was excellent.  I will definitely be enjoying more food from Pa Pa Thai Cuisine.  See my photos. UPDATE:  Finally had time to enjoy a Lunch Special inside the restaurant.  Food is still DELICIOUS AND VERY NICE SERVICE.  See more of my LUnch Menu photos.I enjoyed my Pad Thai w/Chicken.  I asked for more of the special sauce and that made it just the way I like it, flavorful in a lightly sweet way.  The salad that comes with the Lunch Special was very good, also with a lightly sweet dressing.  You have a CHOICE of salad, soup, fried tofu or spring roll with lunch special.Since I had also wanted to try the Spring Rolls, I paid for an additional, regular size appetizer of Spring Rolls. See photos. Regular appetizer portion has 6 Spring rolls. Delicious !The food and service here are VERY GOOD.  This is my favorite neighborhood Thai Restaurant .  I also loved the Spicy Noodles from my previous food orders.  I will certainly continue to enjoy the food here, and I will try hard to try many other dishes from the menu. It's a bit of a challenge only because the Spicy Noodles were SO DARN DELICIOUS THAT I COULD ORDER THEM EVERY TIME!!!  And be VERY, VERY HAPPY.  Note: Restaurant closes for an hour around 3pm or so, so that the staff can enjoy their own lunch.  Very nice and civilized.  I like that!  Note:  It says Pa Pa Thai in the window.  There is no sign above the storefront.  So look for PA PA THAI on the West side of FIRST AVE, between East 58th and East 59th Streets. ON FIRST AVENUE.  Enjoy!!

We indulged in an array of dishes at this restaurant, from scallion pancake to chili shrimp, bao buns, and churros. Each plate was a delightful mix of flavor and texture, served piping hot. The buns, churros, and shrimp stood out as favorites. While the service was satisfactory on the whole, there was a brief period where we seemed to be overlooked. Despite this minor hiccup, our visit was a thoroughly enjoyable experience.

Overall: good tasting authentic szhechuan Chinese foodFoodSteamed pork chili dumplings, pork was tasty, the skin was cooked to perfection. the chili oil had just enough heat and sweet flavordan dan mien noodles: noodles were a little over cooked and too soft, but the sauce was bursting with flavor. just a little less time in the boiling water and it would have been perfectmamo tofu: tofu was silky texture and sauce was good. I asked for mild heat and it was still spicy, but yummysautéed spinach garlic...good nothing special

Wow my new favorite taco place! We stumbled upon this place because our original plan to go to Chelsea market failed. It was apparently closed for a private event. I quickly found this nearby using yelp and we headed over. This reminds me of Oscar's in San Diego. It is a causal place focused on Mexican seafood. Food is authentic and flavorful. I love spicy food, a little too much, and this place had so many hot sauces and dishes to please me! Service was friendly too. It was a bit crowded. More like a grab and go type of place but there are a few tables that you can easily sit down at. The scallops were so spicy and flavorful! Absolutely mouthwatering. I also had the spicy shrimp taco which was delicious and the sea bass ceviche. I would go here over and over again. Too bad I live in Boston and not New York though! I hope this place opens up in Boston someday! Me and my friends really enjoyed it.

Limani brings the fresh breeze of the Aegean Sea right to the heart of Time Square. We came here for a restaurant week adventure. First impression is how beautifully decorated the interior is. Fishes and arts on the wall, live lemon trees behind every several seats, and a mysterious blue water fountain situated in the centre of the restaurant.For restaurant week, there are four appetizers and four main courses to choose from. My curious self went with the Mediterranean meze, which turned out to be a six block sample plate of various hummus and small treats, and then the tuna burger with zucchini fries, which was a very meaty burger and fun tasty fries. My dinning companions got fried calamari or fresh scallops for appetizers, but all went for the Fish of the Day as entree. They all  loooooved the Fish of the Day. Services were quick and attentive. Loved the atmosphere. Would definitely come back!

Absolutely worth the hype! These tacos are the epitome of deliciousness, capturing the authentic essence of Mexico City street food right here at home. Despite a lengthy queue that tests your patience, the service operates efficiently—minimizing wait time once your order's placed. The standout dishes during my visit were the carne asada quesadilla and the pork taco. The carne asada is grilled to perfection, with flavors so reminiscent of traditional Mexican cuisine that you'll be transported with each bite. Highly recommended for a genuine taco experience!

Great place for brunch! Delicious drinks and food! Wait staff was amazing! They were kind, professional and attentive. We had a great meal and a good time! If you are in the area this a great place for a bite!

First off, the food here was 5 stars, hands down.  One of the best Chicken BLT's I've had.  Reasonably priced for the area at $13.  Comes with fries or a salad.  I opted for the salad and it was equally excellent.Bartender dude Zach was a cool and personable young man.  He handled the lunch crowd with prompt professionalism.   Overall, the setup at the bar is a little tight with servers moving through the space and the bathrooms are in the building next door, so a star off for those small points.  However, if you want a truly quality meal at reasonable prices for a high priced area, this a good spot.One more side note...I don't drink trendy liquor, but it looks like they have a nice selection.  Brooklyn Gin?  Who knew?

On a recent Saturday visit for a 2pm lunch at this eatery, the absence of a line was a pleasant start, and the prompt service further impressed. I opted for the black bean burger which was sandwiched between delicious multigrain bread—a highlight. However, the patty itself didn't quite hit the mark, tending towards the dry side. The price point was reasonable, which softened the blow of the less-than-stellar main. Fries were standard fare, nothing noteworthy, but the overall cleanliness of the establishment and the cordial nature of the staff added to the experience. It's worth noting that my review covers the vegetarian option; their beef burgers might very well be a different story. While I wouldn't make a special trip, this spot could be a decent choice if you find yourself nearby with a craving for a quick bite.

What a find near Rockefeller Center! I've never tried dry pot and malatang before, and I'm so glad I had the opportunity before heading into the Nintendo store.So first thing's first. I agree with other Yelpers that walking into the restaurant could be confusing for the first time. So step one, decide what you want. Their American-style Chinese food (the classics like Sweet & Sour Chicken and General Tso's) is the section closest to the door and is quick-serve.Walk further back into the restaurant if you want to dine-in for their specialties (of course you can take it to go), which are the dry hot pot and the malatang dishes. For the dry pot, you get to pick your proteins and veggies, then they'll cook it for you in the kitchen. I'm happy to say that my beef and chicken dry pot was flavorful and just the right amount of spicy that I was craving for the day. I usually like things super spicy, but it was lunch for me and I went with their medium level. I had it with a side of egg drop corn soup, which was well-seasoned without being too salty and had the right level of thickness. We also had the scallion pancakes, which were delicious! They do have sauces by the counter, including soy sauce and sriracha, and they came out nice and hot. The egg on one side of the pancakes was a surprisingly nice touch. I do think it could've benefited from a little more scallions, just a bit more, but we ate it up all the same. It's worth getting with your entrée!Wow, but I really think their malatang is the star here. The broth is so great for the winter cold, let me tell you, and the portion size is great! The bowl is deep and food just kept coming out.We got the beef version, but I would probably get the fish, seafood, or chicken next time. I'm a bit picky about my thinly sliced beef, and theirs were slightly on the fatty side for me, but that's just a matter of preferences since I like things lean. But seriously, the depth and flavor was real! I would actually come here for take out as well, because the fast-food style Chinese food looks to be of good quality. Like I've seen a lot of places in the city that serve super bready fried chicken with a spoonful of bright orange glop, but I'll say their sweet and sour chicken was nothing like that. It looks delicious! Staff were friendly, food came out fairly quick and hot, and the portion to price ratio is solid. Two thumbs up!

Title: Refreshing Take on Ramen: A Promising Newcomer

Just visited this new spot that's bringing a fast-casual twist to the typical ramen experience, reminiscent of popular chains like Dos Toros, Cava, and Chipotle, but with an innovative dry ramen concept.

On my initial visit, I sampled their ramen chili tantan topped with beef, a perfectly pink soft-boiled egg, and bamboo shoots. Despite not being traditional soupy ramen, the flavors were on point, and the dish maintained its texture superbly—even after a short travel time.

The restaurant itself boasts a spotless environment, clearly benefiting from its recent opening. The staff exudes enthusiasm and is eager to guide customers through the straightforward menu.

Though it's early days to award it a full 5-star rating, the first impression is certainly promising. For those seeking a change of pace from the usual lunch options like Pret, this establishment is a breath of fresh air in the neighborhood. Definitely give it a try!

Just like most restaurants anywhere, the food cannot stay consistently good. Last time I had Taco Inn, the food was disgusting... I mean DISGUSTING! I ordered a carnitas quesadilla; the meat was nothing but fat pieces. I was spitting out every bite into a napkin since I could not even chew on the "meat."I also ordered breaded chicken cutlets. The chicken was black and freezing; it smelled horrible. How do you serve freezing cold chicken cutlets on top of hot microwaved bland rice. You could just tell it was old chicken grabbed out of a refrigerator and thrown into my order. I called immediately to complain, and spoke to Anna. She said she would refund me or send me another replacement order. I did not take the offer, and just threw out all the food.Maybe they had an off day, but I am not eating here again to find out if they have anymore.** Due to Guillermo's comment:: The pictures that I have are from other/past visits; you can see how old they are. I was a returning customer. I have been to the actual restaurant and ordered multiple times. Should I have taken pictures of the food in the garbage? As I stated before your employee ANNA offered me a refund or the order to be sent out again... It was so NASTY that I said NO THANK YOU! -- Learn from Yelp reviews, instead of being so defensive.

HOOOOO boy. This place was BIG hyped and lived up to it (and then some). First of all, the decor and ambiance are exactly what I think of when I think of "New York neighborhood pizza". I assumed we had no shot at 8pm on a Friday -- and it WAS packed --  but we rolled up to the bar and enjoyed our meal there. And what. A. Meal. Pepperoni pizza, meatball parm pizza and the titular artichoke pie. All 10s. Special in their owns ways -- truly can't pick a favorite. Bartender was fast and friendly. Slice service in the back is a brilliant idea. So full, so happy.

Opened yesterday! I've been waiting ages for a pho shop to open in the UWS, hah so I'm very pleased by this new addition. I got the shaken beef lunch special (figure I'll be back many times for pho and will update after I do). There's probably space for about 50-60 customers, with about 16 tables. Nice space with bar like seating in the back. My shaken beef was a little heavy on the sauce, so I'm not sure that I would get it again, but I've ordered from the UES location before so I have faith in the rest of their menu. Most tables were full even at 2:30pm on a Tuesday!

Shout out to the bartender! I honestly didn't even ask for his name but he was a dope individual. Stopped by at lunch hour, the spot was empty but that's good on my end, service was quick. The music was flowing at 2pm with a lot of Spanish. I came for tacos, something light but filling. I had tried the sweet plantains, pork, & chicken tacos.. let's be real whoever thought about sweet plantain tacos must of been high off something cuz that's something you usually don't see! But they were good, it's also paired with peppers and chipotle sauce. The pork taco was delicious, pineapples, onions, and perfect tender pork! This one was my favorite one. The chicken taco was okay. I opted out for one of the drinks on menu, the Frosé, It was good, refreshing but I felt like it was just missing the kick in it. Otherwise service & food was great.

Title: A Brunch Delight at Pig And Khao

Pig And Khao emerges as a true winner in the culinary scene. Don't let its unassuming size or simplicity fool you – this gem proves that ambiance doesn't need to be ritzy to be just right. It's clear from the bustling crowd that the locals adore it, and its reputation is well-deserved.

On a recent visit for their bottomless brunch, which truly lives up to the "bottomless" promise, the food was the star rather than the usual mimosa fare. The ramen dishes were standout choices: I relished the spicy ground pork with crispy anchovies, while my friend enjoyed a savory curry ramen with chicken. We indulged in a sumptuous coconut French toast to cap off the meal, which was nothing short of heavenly.

Pig And Khao caters to a variety of palates, making it a brunch haven for enthusiasts. I wholeheartedly recommend this spot for anyone looking to treat themselves to an exceptional meal. Pig And Khao is not just a meal, it's a brunch experience that shouldn't be missed.

**Mealpal Review**Ordered this via my MealPal subscription rather than a regular take out order. Upon first sight I thought I was going to be disappointed as all I saw was all lettuce but once I mixed in the sauce and started eating I was pretty happy. Hidden underneath the lettuce was a gem made out of grilled chicken and vermicelli. I would definitely order this again as it was had enough salad to make it feel healthy and enough salad and noodles to fill me up. Dish came with nuts FYI for those who have nut lerg

Title: Mixed Feelings on a Beloved Spot's Delivery

As a long-time fan of Uncle Boons and its culinary ventures, it saddens me to pen a review that's less than glowing. My latest experience involved a home delivery ordered through Caviar, which was punctual and well-packaged, but the fare from the Uncle Boons Sister delivered a mixed bag of results.

My boyfriend and I shared a meal that included a papaya salad, Khao soy with chicken, and pad Thai with prawns, setting us back about $70 with tax and tip. While the pad Thai was a hit with its robust flavor and sizable portion, the prawns suffered from being overcooked to the point of chewiness. The Khao soy presented a heavy coconut profile that strayed from the memorable version served at Uncle Boons, albeit the chicken was perfectly tender with generous serving. The papaya salad, on the other hand, was a disappointment with its lack of dressing and odd crunch.

In summary, the dishes were satisfactory but failed to dazzle, especially considering the price point which wasn't substantially lower than dining in at Uncle Boons. Although I didn't expect an exact replica of Uncle Boons' delights, I believed the Sister could better echo the beloved recipes. Thai food enthusiasts might find better value and authenticity elsewhere.

I came here with a friend on a weeknight. We ordered gold and silver mantou, fried pork buns, shrimp summer roll, chongqing spicy popcorn chicken, fried pork and chive dumplings, and braised beef noodle soup.The popcorn chicken and braised beef noodles were the highlights of the meal! Definitely order the popcorn chicken if you like spicy food. It was crispy and fried to perfection. The meat is nice and juicy. The braised beef noodles came with a rich broth that washes over you like a warm blanket. The pork belly in the fried pork buns is tender and melt in your mouth. It provides a nice contrast to the crunch in the bun. The fried mantou was delicious as always! The summer rolls are only okay. I would probably skip this next time I come back. Drop by here for some Chinese comfort food!

Title: Happy Hour Haven with a Side of Patience

Upon heeding the chorus of reviews forewarning of wait times, my dining companion and I braved the Friday evening rush to arrive at 7 pm, managing to secure a spot half an hour later—a small price to pay for the forthcoming delights.

The staff greeted us with amiable smiles, setting the stage for an evening of indulgent libations. The lychee martinis stood out, both potent and palatable, and at a mere $4-$5 per spirited concoction, they were a steal. The strawberry daiquiris were no less impressive in their strength, making the establishment an ideal locale for a frugal pregame session.

Our taste buds embarked on a culinary tour starting with the highly commendable pork dumplings, followed by the regrettable Korean chicken sliders which, despite their disappointingly dry and underwhelming presence, were somewhat redeemed by a delectable sauce that we liberally applied to every morsel within reach. The calamari's delicate and crispy batter did little to mask its lack of freshness, an unfortunate blemish on the otherwise flavorful selection.

The cheese fries, laden with seasoning and a welcome addition to our table, could have benefited from a crisper finish to reach their full potential. 

In sum, the evening’s array of appetizers coupled with the spirited drinks amounted to a modest $60—a testament to the value proposition offered by this bustling spot. For those undeterred by a brief interlude before dining, the rewards, particularly in liquid form, are ample.

(3.5 stars) Il Buco is a good Italian restaurant, maybe even very good, but for New York City, it wasn't one that I would run back to. I left with more things that I was disappointed with than I was content with. The restaurant I will say though is absolutely beautiful, definitely makes you feel as though you've been transported to a rustic kitchen in Tuscany. The menu is actually fairly small and boasts only a few pasta dishes. I went with the lasagnette, which had solid al dente pasta and nicely tender lamb, both of which were very pleasant individually. But there wasn't really a bridge between them in the dish, so having the two combined didn't really add much to the bite. Nevertheless still a dish you won't be disappointed with. As for what I wasn't crazy about, the prices of the appetizers are just way too high, nearly as much some of the main dishes. They charge for bread and olive oil--which some places do--but the olive oil wasn't very memorable (was better with some black pepper added in), and yes it was good but not like, this is awesome and here's a few pages about our olive oil in the menu. Plus it was served with sea salt on the side, which made it unclear how to actually consume the salt with the oil since dipping the bread directly in makes a single bite unbearable. If it's meant to be sprinkled in to the oil, than they should really do it for you or guide you through it. Also, most but not all of the pastas are made in-house, which I wouldn't expect to be the case for a top Italian restaurant.

Love this place so much. The food gets an  A+. Some of the best noodles I've ever had. I usually get the Spicy Cumin Lamb stir fry with ribbon noodles. I love the texture of the Ribbon Noodles and the size. The cumin lamb is very flavorful and not too spicy. I also love the Cumin Lamb Soup and the cumin beef soup. Besides noodles, this place makes some good dumplings. Be sure to try the Pork and Chive Dumplings. They are very good. This place is small so I usually get my food to go--very limited seating inside. I think that they are reasonably priced and that you get a good amount oF food for your buck. Sometimes I'm able to save half of my food for the next day. I also like that they accept online orders and they aRe on Ubereats.

Title: A Lackluster Culinary Experience at a "Fine Dining" Establishment

Nestled in a prime location with prices suggesting an upscale experience, the restaurant only manages to achieve a middling 2.5-star rating in my book. Service left much to be desired, with the staff's clatter during plate exchanges disturbing the ambiance of what is advertised as a fine dining experience. 

The sommelier was the sole beacon of professionalism, standing out from the otherwise unremarkable service. Unfortunately, the food itself proved forgettable as soon as we stepped out the door. The chilled Maine lobster was the highlight among the appetizers, offering a burst of freshness and perfectly poached finesse. However, the East and West Coast oysters and roasted Maine scallops were just passable, lacking the wow factor one would expect for the price.

The Santa Barbara uni and marinated mackerel were disappointing, failing to justify their cost. Moving onto the entrees, the Day Boat cod was well received with its pleasing flavors, and the Long Island duck breast was competently prepared. Nevertheless, the 40 Day Dry Aged Prime Côte de Boeuf, though acceptable, left us questioning the authenticity of its size. The roasted loin of lamb was a letdown, imparting an intense gamey taste that was off-putting even to lamb enthusiasts. 

In conclusion, the dining experience was uninspiring, with high points few and far between. The culinary execution and service did not match the expectations set by the prices and "fine dining" premise.

Finally found a dine-in sashimi counter that was worth the $30 price tag.  Portions are big.  If you have been to Japan and are missing good chirashi bowls, Kaguro has what you need.The bowl I ordered came with 1/2 a pound of uni, both a good and bad thing.  Uni is best enjoyed in small doses.  I was sadly unable to finish the last few bites.The maguro and hamachi that accompanied the uni were also delicious.  As expected at the price point we paid.Comparatively, we have gone to lesser sashimi spots in Midtown that present themselves as quality restaurants but give much less by way of their sashimi dishes.  Either in quality or in volume.And as a side note, if for some reason you like your sashimi with mayonnaise they also prepare more Americanized versions of their sashimi bowls for those that crave spicy ahi and California style sushi.  But as a personal recommendation, do yourself a favor and ditch the sauce.  You don't want to mask the taste of these premium cuts of sashimi.Each order comes with a side miso soup.  Enjoy it best while it is piping hot.  My only criticism would be of the rice.  A bit too sour.

Title: Quick Bite at Midtown's Pizza Gem

Stopped by a popular pizza joint known for its artichoke slice. Standing tables encourage a quick dining experience, though the space doesn't feel crowded. The artichoke slice is a local favorite, but I found it a bit rich for my taste. However, the round pepperoni slice was a hit—massive in size with a perfectly thin and audibly crunchy crust. The cheese was a bit scarce, but the sauce won me over, striking a good balance without the typical tomato overload. Speedy service and high-quality toppings make this place a solid choice for a rapid and tasty pizza fix.

Great spot for tasty NY Neopolitan-style pizza.Shared 3 large pies between 7 people and had a couple of slices left over. Started with a Tie-Dye and a Supreme, then half-half Fresca and Funghi. If I had to choose one, I'd pick the supreme, but all of their "presets" sound, look, and are good. Tie-Dye was also good for those of us who were indecisive about sauce. Can't choose one? Why not have them all? Superthin crust, but still with enough structural integrity and chew so it's not just a cracker.Showed up at 11:30 ish on a Sunday and waited about 15-20 minutes to be seated. I'd imagine it'd be even faster if we were a smaller group.Also a minor note, friends who had been before said when they split a pie it was simply 50% of each pie then added together, but this time our waiter informed us they just charge the price of the more expensive of the two? It wasn't much of a difference, but a little confusing.It definitely holds its own against all the other classic pizza institutions in NY.

Tucked away in the heart of the city lies a charming little Turkish gem, featuring a warm, inviting atmosphere complete with an array of captivating paintings adorning the walls and quaint outdoor seating available. Each table is graced with a delicate oil lamp, adding to the cozy ambience.

The menu, although on the pricier side, surprises with an eclectic mix beyond the traditional kebabs, including pasta and a variety of customary Turkish delights. The fluffy, complimentary bread served as a perfect preamble to the main course. 

I savored the hunkar begendi, a succulent lamb dish bathed in tomato sauce, nestled atop a bed of creamy, pureed eggplant that bore a striking resemblance to hummus both in appearance and texture, veering away from the expected eggplant flavor. The lamb melted effortlessly in my mouth. In contrast, my friend's chicken sauté in tomato sauce was deemed rather ordinary.

While the pricing may give a moment's pause, the inventive menu and the exceptional takes on Turkish classics like the hunkar begendi make this cozy spot worth a visit.

My office is right around the corner so I've come here for lunch a couple of times. It's cozy and friendly and the staff is attentive. They make their own sausage and it's really delicious. Desserts here are fantastic. I highly recommend the creme brûlée. The mini cannoli are popular with my coworkwThe entrees are a bit pricey, but I found my fettuccine flavorful. My friend got one of the daily specials and he didn't think it was seasoned enough, but I tasted a bite of his and thought it was fine. As he kept eating, he changed his mind and said it was okay. The grilled octopus was flavorful and pretty, but chewy. In my experience, the uglier the octopus, the more tender (I guess from beating it into tasty submission?)

Title: A Delightful Culinary Experience Marred by an Unpleasant Odor

I recently ventured to the new Wolfgang Steakhouse in Midtown, nestled comfortably between Herald Square and Times Square. The highlight of our meal was, without question, the Porterhouse for Three, served a perfect medium rare alongside classic accompaniments of creamed spinach and sautéed mushrooms. The chef's prowess was undeniably impressive; the steak was sublime.

Our visit was elevated to exceptional thanks to the attentive staff. With the restaurant quiet in the mid-afternoon, we benefited from what felt like VIP treatment. Harris, our server, was the embodiment of friendliness and efficiency, leading a team that provided superb service. Even the manager took a hands-on approach, ensuring our experience was without fault.

The establishment itself boasts a pristine interior that contributes to an inviting atmosphere. Unfortunately, despite the excellent service and delectable fare, there was an off-putting aspect of our visit. En route to the restroom, we were greeted by a pungent smell reminiscent of a subway station's less favorable scents. Although the bathroom was clean, the unpleasant odor from the hallway lingered.

For the aforementioned reason, I am compelled to give this Wolfgang Steakhouse location a 4-star rating. While the culinary and service experience was near flawless, the aromatic nuisance was a detractor. Nevertheless, the quality of dining and service leads me to recommend this location with the caveat of the hallway's unfortunate fragrance.

Love this place that just opened up for a quick, affordable lunch to go! Come well before noon if you don't want to wait in line. Service is quick and the food is really good. Another great thing is the sandwich containers and bags are all plastic free!

Hidden in plain sight among the hustle and bustle of Chinatown on the Bowery is this seafood heaven.  I have shellfood allergies but my tablemate looovvveeesss seafood so I dared to step into the seafood world for a meal for her birthday.We had the $99 Combo which offers various selections for appetizers and main course.When I tell you... my personal experienceChicken wings were superb -perfect crunch-Cajun fries freshly done and crispPopcorn chicken had a nice spicy kick (not overly spicy)I dipped everything in their sauce which was effectively a spicy duck sauce that made everything come even more alive.My friend's experience... all she could say was "mmm, outstanding, mmm, mmm, outstanding". And that was the extent of our conversation while she enjoyed the snow crab legs seafood boil which also came with crawfish, jumbo shrimp, potatoes, corn and sausage.  In all the years I have known her, I have never seen her chow down like this. Seafood heaven for seafood lovers indeed!Importantly, for value seekers - $99 is a steal dinner for 2 with great options of snow crab legs, canada lobster or Dungeness crab boils. Although I did not (could not) taste it, the visual was amazing. You could SEE the seasonings galore and for the first time ever I wished I could taste it.A special shoutout to our server, Mike, who made sure he advised the kitchen of my allergies, and he checked in on us regularly, smiling all the while, to make sure we had all we needed. After we left I wished I got an order of wings to go. But have no fear, I have already calendared my next visit with my mom who is also a seafood fanatic.Well done Sup Crab!!

This place has the best rice noodle rolls ever. They are not chintzy with the fillings and the rolls are big. But there's a steep price to pay for them. $2.50 each. But they are really good. Tons of shrimp, scallions, sesame seeds, etc. it's filling. I highly recommend this place to those who have a fondness for these rolls. This place apparently has only been open a few months. Their rolls apparently sell out by 4 so don't wait too late in the day to get them.

Navigating my experience at this peculiar bar/restaurant is like trying to describe a dream that oscillates between fun and bewildering. The establishment's theme throws you into a bizarre mixture of slapstick horror reminiscent of the mid-60's, replete with spooky animatronics and actors engaging in smoke-enshrouded performances that manage to be both loud and captivating.

Amongst the oddities, a T-Rex skull looms on the wall, contrasted by an incongruous, cheerful photo booth nestled below – a physical manifestation of the venue’s thematic disorientation. Nonetheless, this eccentric backdrop seems to add to the place's unique charm.

The bar's offerings include an array of themed drinks that impress, such as the potent 'Lucid Dream,' a commendable absinthe-based concoction. The option to purchase a keepsake souvenir cup adds a touch of memorabilia to the experience, albeit at a price point that might raise an eyebrow.

In summary, this establishment is an entertaining enigma that serves up both confusion and delight in equal measure, with a price tag that is, perhaps, the only clear-cut aspect of the visit.

Very pricey, food is a hit or miss depending on what you get. Fast causal. Came here for lunch one day and got a few items to share. Got the shellfish platter which included several types of oysters both from east coast and west coast and a few mussels. The oysters were all very good, but the mussels were stale and not fresh at all. The fish sandwich was ok but the bun was really dry and the patty had no flavor at all. It's fast causal so you sit at the counter and order your food. Very fast service but more cafeteria style with no ambience. Overall pricey and I would only just get oysters and skip all the other food items.

Title: A Late-Night Savior with Satisfying Slices

After a buzzing event at Madison Square Garden, my ravenous state led me to a pizza haven just a stone's throw away, ready to serve the post-event crowd even at 1:30 a.m. Despite the line snaking out the door, a mere 10-minute wait seemed a small price to pay for the promise of cheesy comfort.

My order: a square of pepperoni Sicilian, a slice bustling with peppers and onions, and a classic cheese - all swiftly reheated to hit that late-night spot. To wash it down, a simple water bottle did the trick.

While it may not top my pizza charts, the quick service and satisfying slices made this spot a go-to for the nocturnal nosh. Perfect for quelling midnight cravings, it's the kind of place that's less about culinary fireworks and more about reliably good, comforting bites when you need them most.

This place is close to where I live and I like going there for a quick delicious meal. They have a great dessert selection as well and the prices are great. You never have to wait for a table which is great and it's the perfect place do get some work done as well.

Title: A Delightful Experience at Hexagon

I recently attended a friend's book event at Hexagon and was immediately captivated by the breathtaking mural adorning the wall as I entered. Despite it being a Saturday, I was pleasantly surprised to find a happy hour special in full swing.

The rosé sangria was a highlight, providing a delightful buzz after just two servings. The shrimp dumplings were incredibly flavorful, but the standout dish for me was the tangy gold wings—an absolute must-try.

The atmosphere at Hexagon was exceptionally relaxed, complemented by a team of courteous and attentive staff members. Based on this enjoyable experience, I'm already looking forward to my next visit to Hexagon.

Title: Hit-or-Miss Rice Cakes at an Affordable Spot

I recently visited a restaurant renowned for its spicy rice cakes and kimbap. The flavor profile was delightful; however, the rice cakes' texture was inconsistent. A fresh batch offered the perfect chewy bite, but at times I found them overcooked and too soft. Complementing the rice cakes, the spicy tuna kimbap was tasty, though it tended to disintegrate upon dipping into the sauce. The assorted fried combo with dumplings and seaweed-wrapped glass noodles was a crunchy delight. For a budget-friendly meal, the set menus are your best bet, providing a substantial duo for around $10. Despite minor hiccups, the experience promises a fast and flavorsome meal that won't break the bank.

After shopping for a while, we decided to try out the popular dim-sum place on Mott Street called Royal Seafood but the wait was too much and a large party was going to be there at 2pm. My mom and cousin have eaten at this place before and we decided to try it on Pell Street called Delight 28. It's not a fancy place but at least wasn't crowded. We got a shared table with 2 other patrons. The staff were still going around with the dim-sum carts. My mom picked out a plate of shumai (steamed pork & mushroom  dumplings ), hargow (shrimp Cantonese dumplings) and chicken feet. Since my  partner doesn't eat seafood or pork, he ordered the beef chow fun with bean sprouts surrounded by Chinese broccoli. It was delicious and not to greasy. These just hit the spot before we continued shopping. If need be that the dim-sum places are full again, we'll come back here.

Title: Cozy Spot with Generous Combos, Service Could Improve

Visited this bustling eatery on a Thursday evening and found a compact yet inviting space. Despite the crowd, our party of four was seated promptly. However, the service left something to be desired, as we often had to seek out a waitress for assistance.

I opted for the hot soba soup to combat the chill outside. While comforting, I'd recommend the cold soba for its superior texture. Surprisingly, they offer a choice between a 100g and 300g serving of soba with no price difference; the larger portion is a no-brainer.

The standout was the $25 combo. It's an absolute steal, featuring 6 slices of fresh sashimi, flavorful tuna tartare, crispy fried shrimp and vegetables, and a sweet mochi dessert. It’s a hearty offering that could easily satisfy two diners.

In conclusion, while I was let down by the service, the quality and quantity of the food were commendable. This fact alone earns the restaurant a solid rating, minus one star for the service hiccups.

My boyfriend and I came for dinner and we loved it!!! I got the unagi don (eel rice bowl, the one without onions) and the scallop appetizer and both were great. The unagi don was so tasty, tender, and flavorful and such a good value. A similar sized and similar quality one in Tokyo would be easily over $40 and it's under $30 here. My boyfriend got the karaage (fried chicken) and a curry rice bowl and enjoyed both of them a lot as well, although I tried the chicken and thought it could have been more crispy.While waiting for our table we sat at the bar and the bartender was very nice and helpful with recommend sakes, and my boyfriend had trouble picking one because all the ones he tasted were so good! I had a yuzu hojicha iced tea which was also great.

Title: A Pasta Lover's Haven with Customizable Delights

If you're a pasta aficionado, this place is a must-visit! The ability to mix and match your pasta and sauce is a game-changer, offering a tailored dining experience that caters to individual tastes. The pesto cream sauce, in particular, is a standout and comes highly recommended.

The wait times here are generally reasonable, which is always appreciated. In the summer months, the outdoor seating is a pleasant touch, allowing diners to enjoy their meal in the fresh air – just be mindful of choosing a spot away from the walls to avoid any uninvited gastropod guests.

Overall, this restaurant is a hidden gem that promises an exceptional pasta dish that's worth every penny. Don't miss out on this culinary treat!

Title: A Journey of Taste with Highs and Lows at Pricey Eatery

My experience at this restaurant was a rollercoaster of flavors and emotions. Although the prices were steep, the culinary delights mostly justified the cost. The evening began on a disappointing note with a glass of red vermouth diluted with soda, not to my preference. My anticipation for the Razor Clam dish was promptly dashed upon learning it was out of season.

However, the small dishes redeemed the initial letdowns. The Bluefish Tuna was an unexpected treat – fresh, simple, and irresistible, making it hard to stop at just one piece. The Baby squid stuffed with sobrasada and potatoes were tasty but disappointingly sparing with the filling for the $32 price tag. In stark contrast, the Shrimp elBulli, a nod to the famed 1996 elBulli creation, was a fascinating and delicious gem well worth trying.

The service, unfortunately, lagged behind the food quality, with a seemingly inexperienced waiter who needed frequent prompting to attend to our table. Despite these service hiccups, the unforgettable flavors have me eager to return for the Fideuà and Paella.

This was our first trip to NYC and our first experience with real New York pizza. I've heard about how incredible it is, but when we had these huge slices in front of us and tasted the exquisite blend of crust, sauce, cheese and toppings, I can't imagine being satisfied with any other pizza. I had the Hawaiian pizza and hubby had a meat lovers blend. I couldn't finish one slice and took home. It was delicious the next day. We brought for our daughter and she's ready for a trip there, just for the pizza. Thank you for such a great culinary experience. We'll make sure to stop next time we're in the City.

This review is for the bar only. Looked like a cozy place to catch up with friends so we stopped for a drink. The bartender looked absolutely puzzled when we said we didn't need a table, so maybe the drinks aren't their focus. The cocktail list sounds lovely on paper, but we found them less than impressive to taste. The tree tap old-fashion barely had any recognizable flavor and the reverse monarch was oddly confusing in what it was supposed to taste like. Not to mention the service was incredibly slow for a quiet late afternoon. Willing to come back to try the food, but likely not to add on a drink.

We happened to pass by this restaurant and decided to try it. It was Sunday night. This restaurant was nicely decorated. Hubby and I thought why not trying another schezuan restaurant other than the one we liked in Vegas. They have quite the same menu but what a big difference when it comes to the taste and flavor. To me, this was an average schezuan food, didn't quite hit the note. We had the Chengdu wonton, shrimp with vegetable and beef with broccoli. Of all the three I liked Chengdu wonton appetizer better than the two entrees. The beef broccoli was too sweet. The shrimp dish didn't have enough flavor. We don't mind trying a second time if we're in the area. The service was ok, wasn't special but wasn't bad.

Spot Dessert Bar offers a whimsical array of sweet treats, featuring inventive presentations that are sure to catch your eye. On my journey through their menu, I sampled fan-favorites priced at $11.95 each, a result of their recent price adjustments.

The Harvest, a delightful creation with a charming aesthetic, invites diners to pour earl gray milk tea over an "edible dirt" of Oreo crumbs and cheesecake. However, the taste, particularly the overly sour raspberry sorbet, fell short of the visual promise. The Matcha Lava was decent but didn't leave a lasting impression.

On the brighter side, the Golden Toast and Coffee Mountain shined through. Both offered satisfying flavors and textures that redeemed my dessert experience at Spot. The ice creams and milk teas rounded out the experience with a comforting touch of familiarity, though nothing to write home about.

Patrons should note that the St. Mark's location, equipped with a bathroom, might require a wait due to its popularity. Luckily, their secondary location, just down the block, often provides a quicker alternative. Whether for the Instagram-worthy aesthetics or the hits among the misses, Spot Dessert Bar has grown on me, much like it has with my friends who introduced me to this sweet enclave.

This review is mostly for the bar, which happens to stay quite lively even on a Sunday evening. It can get pretty crowded which means you might end up standing, but we eventually found a place to sit and enjoy our drinks.The cocktails are nicely made and the ambiance of the place is quite nice, giving a nice warm throwback to the bars of the olden days.I particularly enjoyed the Monkey Business, it was a  nicely made cocktail with rather unique flavors and taste.The Almost There on the other hand was a little boring and tasted kind of watered down in the midst of all that ice they put in it.

Tucked away in Soho lies a charming pasta haven that feels like a slice of Italy. With its extensive menu of homemade pasta dishes priced between $15-$20, this cozy spot offers a delightful bang for your buck. Standout choices are the Taglierini Sorrento and Black Taglierini—each dish bursts with authentic flavor that's simply irresistible. Seafood enthusiasts will be glad to hear high praise for the seafood pasta options.

Alongside the scrumptious food, the wine list is thoughtfully curated, offering bottles from $25-$30. Our selection, a crisp $28 Riesling, proved to be the perfect accomplice to our pasta feast.

While the space is on the smaller side and can feel quite bustling, this only adds to the authentic, intimate dining experience. It's a gem worth discovering for anyone craving a taste of home-style Italian in Soho without breaking the bank.

I felt like I stepped into a little stall in Tokyo! It's so cute inside. You know you're in the right place when 80% of the people are Japanese. We had the griled steak appetizer and it was AMAZING! My ramen was on point and I was very much satisfied with my meal. I know for sure if I stay in that area of town again I will be going back to try something else on the menu. It closes really late and we got there at about midnight. It was pretty packed but we found a small table for 2 near the back. They don't let you tip which is something I found interesting. Either way makes you want to get more food!=)

I never really understood pizza until moving to New York. It MUST be something in the water. While looking for something to eat before going to the movies, I wanted a quick snacc. Essex market closes around 9 and most shops in the market line were closing. I decided to take my changes at slice joint.I thought I knew my favorite square slice in NY, but boy was I wrong. The square slices here looked bomb. The cashier mentioned that their meatball pizza was coming out fresh from the oven, so I tried that too. I'm not usually a crust person, but the crust here was extra crispy and light. The dough was also very light and airy while holding the toppings. The pepperoni slice was pretty darn good and the pepperonis were PS pizza like. My favorite slice was the meatball pizza. It was fresh out the oven and piping hot. So bomb!I'll def be back to slice joint and I'm so happy it's just a few blocks away from my apt.

Title: A Gastronomic Treasure Well Worth the Splurge

My latest culinary adventure led me to indulge in a truly delectable dining experience. The highlight, without a doubt, was the 'treasure box meat'—an absolute favorite of mine now, thanks to its sumptuous flavors that tantalized my taste buds. The presentation of each dish was impeccable, adding to the allure of the meal.

Though the prices are steep, it's clear you're paying for top-notch quality. The fries sprinkled with truffle salt were an unexpectedly delightful treat, enhancing the humble potato to gourmet levels. Opting for the $85 per person set was a decision well made, as it afforded a variety of cuts and starters, each more delicious than the last. The cold noodles, in particular, provided a refreshing interlude between the richer dishes.

The famed Hamideru cut lived up to its reputation, albeit a tad fattier than expected. Yet, the flavor was exceptional—just remember to reserve it a day ahead to avoid disappointment. A special shoutout must go to the uni, caviar, and wagyu sushi pieces, as well as the foie gras and wagyu combination—each one a culinary masterpiece.

My verdict? This restaurant is a must-visit for those who appreciate fine food and are willing to pay for quality. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

I recently dined at a local gem that truly captivated my taste buds with its Som Tam Platter - a delightful combination of fried pork, grilled chicken, and sticky rice that brought back a wave of nostalgia; it was reminiscent of the heartwarming meals my mother used to prepare. The restaurant's ambience was inviting and soothing, providing a perfect backdrop for a culinary trip down memory lane. The service was impeccable, with attentive staff ensuring a pleasant dining experience. I would highly recommend this establishment to anyone in search of delicious food in a comfortable setting.

When I came to LoLo's I wanted the Lime Boneless Chicken Breast but they sold out.  The look of Chicken A La Brasa didn't apeal to me at all.  so instead of getting a main meal I went for the sides.  I settled on the Mac & Queso, Sweet Plantains, and the empanada of the day which was chicken.  The Mac & Queso was good, plus I like it when it is a bit of a crusty top. The Plantain where OK.  The empanada was the best their is a real good sauce mixed with the chunky shredded pieces of chicken and it was made it real tasty and I should have gotten two instead of one. I also got 3 sauces all spicy with the Pineapple Chutney the sweetest and mildest of the bunch and the Peppa the hottest.The staff was helpful and friendly so that pushed the stars I gave to 4.

Title: A Zesty New Player in the East Village Bar Scene

I recently had the opportunity to visit a new bar in the bustling heart of the East Village. Thanks to its prime location nestled among popular restaurants, this sleek watering hole is conveniently positioned for both pre-dinner aperitifs and post-meal nightcaps.

My companion and I indulged in the bar's signature concoction, 'The Ginger Man,' which certainly lived up to its name with a piquant punch and an intensified zest courtesy of an actual ginger candy garnish. The cocktail menu also teased with intriguing options like 'greentea' and 'rollercoaster' shooters – mysterious offerings that beckon a return visit for the adventurous drinker.

Admittedly, we found the ambiance quieter than expected, with the evening rain perhaps dampening the usual foot traffic. However, this lull could make for a more personalized outing on what I anticipate would be a busier, sunnier day.

A slight chill from the bartenders did contrast with the warm libations, yet I'm optimistic that sunnier skies might bring out warmer service. Its spacious setting promises a good fit for group gatherings or intimate dates.

In summary, this fresh East Village addition has potential, especially for those who favor a strong ginger kick and a calm spot to enjoy it.

Cheap, fast, and tasty.Your typical roast duck and pig deli. We got the large trio box with chicken, duck and char siu over rice with veggies. The rice was pretty bad tbh, it was kind of on the mushy side, but if you eat it with the sauce and meats it's fine. All the meats were tender and flavorful, even the chicken, which in the past I've found to be more on the dry side.They also have the option to just buy the meats by themselves. Would go back and would recommend if you want something cheap, fast, and good.

Tucked away on a quiet street in the Financial District, finding this gem required a bit of effort. The front of the restaurant featured an elaborate pasta-making setup that seemed excessive at first glance. However, the lasagna takeaway dispelled any doubts. Encased in a rich, hearty sauce, the pasta—fresh or not—was delectable and generously portioned. The eco-friendly plant-based packaging was a thoughtful touch. Definitely worth a return visit.

I recently visited Cantina Rooftop for the first time and had a fantastic experience. The service was excellent, with staff being attentive and quick to respond. For my meal, I opted for the grilled chicken nachos with jalapeños, which were both tasty and delicious. The guacamole stood out due to its freshness and creamy, buttery texture - a real classic. While the views were unfortunately obstructed by renovations at the neighboring building, this did not detract from the overall great experience. I would definitely recommend a visit to Cantina Rooftop and look forward to returning.

I'm not really a fan of vegan restaurants, but I knew I could trust J-G. I was very excited to try his new restaurant, and sure enough, we were thrilled. J-G's abcV embraces the ingredients rather than trying to transform them into something they are not (i.e. a veggie burger). Every dish was phenomenal, tasted fresh, and felt healthy to eat.The decor and atmosphere of abcV are also wonderfully sophisticated, yet simple and classy. The cocktails were also excellent.Highly recommended for trying "vegan" food. Definitely make a reservation!

Title: Quick, Flavorful Lunch at Taim

I stopped by Taim for a swift lunch fix and was immediately taken by their falafel pita. The falafel itself was a highlight - crunchy on the outside and perfectly cooked. Topped with a zesty green sauce, the pita was a flavorful treat. Service was efficient enough, though there was a noticeable wait for others. The tight seating might be a drawback for some, but as a solo diner, I found it manageable and was back on the street within 20 minutes. While the food hits the mark, be wary of potential delays at Taim, especially if your schedule is tight.

Let me start by saying that the ramen was very good and the decor was very nice. I really liked the flavor in the meat and bamboo of my spicy miso ramen. The corn in it was fresh and the noodles were cooked well. I would've left a 4 star review (I can't justify giving a 5 star review to a place that's cash only, sorry...it's 2019, get with it) but midway through my meal I saw the waitress run out the door, demanding that the customer leave a higher tip. While I generally tip 20% and understand the etiquette of tipping, I also know that it is NOT mandatory. That left a very bitter taste in my mouth for the rest of the meal. We left a 20% tip and didn't get asked to leave more so I'm not sure what the other people left but from what I overheard, they did tip. Just a warning to all.

We had a private party here in their downstairs area, and I can't say enough about how easy it was to coordinate or how professional the staff was.  We were looking for a place to host a birthday party and learned that this space has a downstairs area that they offer for such occasions.  They state that the maximum capacity is around 60 people and they require a minimum spend to reserve the space (but they don't charge for the actual space rental).  The private space is downstairs, away from the huge crowd upstairs, and it has a fairly sized bar area in the front with a half dozen tables/benches in the back.  They decor is rustic, similar to the upstairs area, with raw wood and overhead stringed bulb lighting.We had ordered balloons to be delivered from Balloon Saloon.  When we arrived about 30 minutes before our designated start time, balloons were in the middle of the room waiting to be setup, and we were greeted by the friendliest and most helpful staff.  They served us drinks throughout the night and updated us on the bar tab periodically.  They also let us know the amount we were projected to reach based on the pace of the night in case we needed to close down earlier or encourage people to have a few more drinks.  They had a great selection of cocktails and beers on tap, and their kitchen offered a range of small platters--think mac and cheese bites, bruschetta, etc.Everything from the drinks to the staff and the space was perfect for our party!  The one critique that I'll make is that leading up to our party we emailed a few different times without response and needed to ask multiple times for a response from the staff responsible for their correspondence.  Despite that, I'd easily recommend this place for anyone hosting a small party in the area.

Used the Pulsd coupon. We were seated immediately with our reservation. Our server was wonderful as we took a few minutes to digest the menu. Her service was impeccable and she was extremely professional. The food came out piping hot and it tasted like grandma was in the back cooking the yummy dishes. Not too spicy, not too salty. Basically perfect. Only negative: the cocktails weren't that good. Overly sweet and didn't taste fresh. Overall: would still go back, but I'd order wine or beer next time instead of a cocktail

I regret to say that my experience at this bao eatery was far from pleasant. The word "icky" springs to mind. Initially greeted by a cramped, dimly-lit space blaring loud music, any semblance of a welcoming atmosphere was lost. It's not suited for large groups, given the scarcity of tables.

Cleanliness clearly wasn't a priority; sticky surfaces and littered floors contributed to an unappetizing environment. The bao, though central to their offerings, was unremarkable and overpriced, failing to live up to the buzz. The unkempt setting only detracted from the culinary experience, rendering the food less enjoyable.

In conclusion, between the subpar ambiance, unexceptional food, and overall lack of dedication to a clean dining experience, I find no reason to return or recommend this establishment.

Title: A Delicious Find - Oath Pizza

On my recent quest for exceptional pizza, Yelp led me to the doorstep of Oath Pizza. The online acclaim and appetizing photos had raised my expectations, which, I'm delighted to say, were met and surpassed.

As I stepped inside, I was welcomed by the clean surroundings and a warm, inviting decor that immediately put me at ease. The staff was notably friendly, especially when I mentioned it was my first visit; they enthusiastically explained the concept of customizable pizzas with unlimited toppings—a dream for any pizza lover.

Deciding to gauge their standard flavors, I chose a classic pepperoni pizza. The short seven-minute wait was a small investment for the reward that followed. Served piping hot, each bite delivered a burst of rich, well-balanced flavors, a testament to the fresh, high-quality ingredients.

Oath Pizza didn't just satisfy my craving—it set a new benchmark for it. I wholeheartedly recommend this gem to all and eagerly anticipate my next visit.

Title: Happy Hour Haven with Tasty Treats

I recently visited a fantastic spot for happy hour that I can't recommend enough. Not only do the drinks and food specials run until 8pm, despite the menu listing them until 7pm, but the atmosphere is perfect for unwinding after a long day. The waiters truly elevate the experience; their helpfulness is noteworthy, ensuring you're well taken care of.

The kimchi fried rice was an absolute hit, delivering the satisfaction needed when hunger strikes. As for the fried wings, we opted for them dry, and they were wonderfully crispy—a delightful crunch with every bite.

A bonus perk for patrons: keep your receipt! It grants you 10% off at their sister karaoke and billiards establishments. This place is not just a restaurant but a gateway to a full evening of entertainment.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Local Soul Food Spot

My recent visit to this soul food restaurant was a rollercoaster, with highs overshadowed by significant lows. The chicken and waffles dish was a delight, especially the succulent dark meat, though the waffles themselves could have done with a touch more seasoning to elevate the flavor. The shrimp and grits, meanwhile, were tasteful, but the portion of shrimp felt a little stingy with just six pieces.

Where the experience truly faltered was in the service department. A 55-minute wait for our food was excessive, and the staff's reassurances did little to alleviate our frustration, especially when we noticed later arrivals receiving their meals ahead of us. Our concerns were met with dismissive responses, which only added insult to injury.

While the food had its merits, the poor service left a sour taste. This area is rich with exemplary soul food options that come with the added benefit of efficient and courteous service. I'd recommend exploring those before opting for a potentially aggravating experience here.

Ordered delivery from this restaurant twice now and was underwhelmed both times. Unfortunately, the second and last time, my red curry arrived warmed up and infinitely oily. To add insult to injury, there just wasn't much curry soup in the bowl. See pictures attached. I called the restaurant to explain what I received and they were immediately dismissive. Their response was that no one else had complained the entire day so therefore it was me. Next to pho and soul food, Thai red or Panang curry is my go to. Living in Hell's Kitchen left me no option other than to become a Thai food aficionado. This was unacceptable and I will not be ordering from here again. With the portions here, you would run out of curry before you ran out of rice and where does that happen?....Nowhere.

Title: A Warm Celebration at Cask Bar & Kitchen

After the joyous birth of my sister's first grandchild at NYU Hospital, my family and friends found solace in the cozy embrace of Cask Bar & Kitchen. Our party of five, including two sisters and friends of the new mom, was greeted by the comforting atmosphere and the prompt, attentive service upon our 8 pm arrival.

The Cask Bar & Kitchen, with its inviting brick and wood decor, set the stage for our celebration. I indulged in a perfectly crafted Makers Manhattan – twice, in fact – and a special 9 oz Cask pale ale, which pleasantly surprised my usual non-pale ale palate.

Our shared starters, a mushroom flatbread and fries, were both delectable and set the tone for the meal. My main, a generous roast squash, goat cheese, and arugula salad with a maple sherry vinaigrette, was fresh and flavorful. The rest of the party was equally impressed with their dishes, ensuring a satisfied table.

The evening ended on a sweet note with a shared jelly donut dessert that left us all savoring the flavors. Cask Bar & Kitchen proved to be an exceptional venue for our familial celebration. It gets an enthusiastic thumbs-up from me!

Title: A Nugget Above the Rest!

I recently visited a restaurant that truly knows their nuggets - and these are the best I've had, bar none. The restaurant serves both fried and grilled versions, each cooked to perfection with a succulence that speaks to the high quality of the chicken used.

The accompanying BBQ sauce was a delightful surprise, skewing sweet and pairing beautifully with the nuggets. But what set the experience apart was the inclusion of fries seasoned with Old Bay - a genius touch that elevated the meal.

Service was as wonderful as the food, with attentive and friendly staff. While the seating area is a bit limited, it's a small compromise for such delectable fare. Overall, my lunch experience was thoroughly enjoyable and I left extremely satisfied. Highly recommend for any nugget aficionado!

I came here after being recommending by a friend and visiting the other location near 50th st. I specifically came for the shin tantan-men since 1. I love super spicy foods and 2. ground pork in ramen is my favorite!  I came with my boyfriend around 4pm on a Saturday and we were seated instantly.  It's a cute vibe with a mostly communal table feel.  We were seated at a communal table and quickly ordered our ramen and pork bun appetizers.  The hostess/wait staff service was so-so, not really too friendly.  Our food came out fairly quickly with the pork buns coming out first.  At $10 for 2 they were pretty good and consistent with most others that I've tried.  Next came the ramen.  Mine was extra spicy and came with cilantro and a lime to squeeze on top in addition to the spicy broth and ground pork. It was definitely 10/10 spicy which is usually what I am aiming for when ordering something spicy.  The overall flavor was just okay though and not my favorite (CC: Ivan Ramen Spicy Red Chili Ramen!!) The broth really stuck to the noodles as any good ramen should.  Overall pretty good food but after trying 2 locations, there's nothing about this place that I have experienced so far that would make me a repeat customer.

I recently visited a ramen restaurant that delivered a solid dining experience. The cuisine was traditional, with each element of the ramen bowl tasting fresh and well-prepared, though nothing particularly stood out as exceptional or unique. The service was commendable, with attentive staff and quick service. However, the price point was slightly steep at $17 before tax and tip, which is likely attributed to its Chelsea location. Nonetheless, despite the cost, it's a reliable spot for a tasty bowl of ramen without any significant drawbacks.

Title: Rolling in Flavor – A Pizzeria Review

If you're on the hunt for pizza with a twist, look no further. This pizzeria's claim to fame is a crust so delicately thin, you can roll it up like a culinary scroll! The novelty doesn't wear off – the pizza is exceptional.

Admittedly, if the pizza cools down, it tends to soften. But fear not, a quick stint in a toaster oven revives its crisp glory. As someone who often orders delivery to the office, I can attest that the pies arrive still tantalizingly warm.

My go-to choices? The Margherita pizza – a simple yet flavorful blend of fresh tomatoes, basil, and mozzarella. And for something a little more decadent, the Mushroom Truffle Madness is a must-try, with its rich mushroom and truffle oil topping, balanced perfectly by the stretchy mozzarella.

A delightful touch is the side of arugula and alfalfa sprouts they include, adding a fresh, peppery contrast to the savory slices. It's innovations like these that keep me coming back.

For anyone seeking a new pizza experience, I highly recommend giving this place a try. It’s become a regular fixture for my pizza cravings.

Loved the fresh pasta here! Space however is a little bit tight. It would be nice if you had a large group, and then able to have the whole table to yourselves (which is essentially  the whole restaurant). Portions are on the small side though, especially the gnocchi. For an appetizer,  I recommend the burrata toast.

Bohemian Restaurant... you're so, so good. We initially ordered a ton of food, but didn't realize it until we were 2 plates in. Would have liked it if our waitress offered suggestions to let us know this. All in all, we ordered WAY too much food. We shared 5 dishes... two/three would have been perfect.Get* Fondu - AMAZING... must get!* Wagu beef tartar - AMAZING... must get!Don't Get* Uni Croquets (I'm in the minority here, but, we weren't impressed initially. Once we saw the price tag of $18 per croquet, we were 100% unimpressed. Pro's* Awesome & very cozy space - makes you feel like you're in someone's living room. * Great bartender that gets his groove on when he's making your cocktail. And they're delicious. * The food is really super tasty & quite creative* Vibe is chill * Not only are you dining in style, but you're dining in a part of history... BASQUIAT HISTORY. Just Google it. Con's* I can understand a mark-up at a restaurant, but $15 for a bottle of Badoit sparkling water? That's kind of highway robbery.* Reservations system is bonkers

First off, for the quality of the food, too expensive. You order from the iPads at the table, everything down to gratuity is paid for before you actually get any of the food or service. I ordered a cheese omelette that comes with "breakfast potatoes" which seem to be a frozen blend of home fries and bell peppers. The omelette was so fluffed up it made it seem like there was barely any cheese in it. Very bland, more on the flavorless side. The food takes a while to get to the table also.

During my recent visit to Tasty Hand Pulled Noodles, I was pleasantly surprised by their incredible shrimp and vegetable pan-fried dumplings—easily on par with the best I've tasted. The namesake hand-pulled noodles, which can be enjoyed in soup or pan-fried, are the highlight of this establishment. Opting for the latter, the pan-frying technique accentuates the noodles' texture, offering an opportunity for them to shine. However, I found the flavors somewhat lacking in boldness, leaning towards the under-seasoned side. Also, the portions are generous to a fault, making it perfect for sharing. If you have a penchant for mild flavors and an appetite for abundant noodles, this is a spot you might want to try.

I stumbled upon this gem when there was an unusually short queue, with a welcoming lady efficiently managing the waitlist – I barely loitered for 10 minutes before being seated. Opting for a light meal, I chose the shrimp rice roll with chives and a classic HK milk tea. Service was swift, and the dishes arrived promptly, with the ability to sweeten my tea to taste. The rice roll was delectable when enhanced with a dash of chilli oil. Neat, clean, and child-friendly, this spot delivers satisfaction without the pinch on the wallet – my entire experience cost a mere $12. While the 'cash only' policy might deter some, the conveniently placed ATM at the back offers a workaround. I'll certainly return, though my patience for lines has its limits; if the wait exceeds 10 minutes, the neighboring eatery might see my business.

Title: A Bustling Slice of NYC Life at The Suspenders

If you're a follower of mine on Yelp, you know I'm all about uncovering local gems that offer a genuine taste of the neighborhood. The Suspenders is a shining example of just that. Situated a stone's throw from the World Trade Center, this eatery was abuzz with energy at 7pm on a weekday. Picture a crowd of financial district professionals unwinding after a day's work, creating a lively, albeit noisy, atmosphere. Don't be deterred by the din; it's part and parcel of the New York charm!

The Suspenders hits the sweet spot with its casual, welcoming vibe and unpretentious character. Now let’s talk about the food. And believe me, it’s worth talking about. The Beef Barley Soup was a comforting throwback to grandma's kitchen – no shortcuts or artificial flavors here, just rich, home-cooked excellence. As for the Buffalo Chicken Fingers, they were a masterclass in balance – just the right amount of heat and vinegar, enveloped in a light, crispy batter. Perfectly paired with a cold beer.

The star of the show? The Suspenders Burger. It's no mystery why they fly out of the kitchen. High-quality beef in a patty that's flavorful yet not dripping with grease. And for the health-conscious, there’s an option to swap fries for sautéed green beans – a very tasty choice indeed.

Rumor has it, their chicken pot pie is something special, and I'm already planning my next visit. The Suspenders isn’t just a restaurant; it feels like a home away from home. Be sure to drop by next time you're in the Big Apple – your taste buds will thank you!

I purchased a $29 voucher for two with drinks. This deal includes 5 dim sum dishes and 2 drinks. When we showed the voucher, our server told us to wait so he can talk to his manager. We were just awkwardly waiting for 5 minutes. But whatever, it worked and the manager was friendly. We shared: -shrimp dumplings 4p ($6.75) -steamed spare ribs with olive sauce ($5.75) -shanghai juicy pork bun 6p-sticky rice with pork wrapped in lotus leaf 2p ($6.75) -shu mai that consists of shrimp and pork 4p ($5.75) Shu mai and shrimp dumplings were so good to the point we ordered more. Also, the price that they posted online were different than the menu given to us. Prices are higher--roughly a $1 more. Overall, whenever I crave dim sum, this place will do as the food was good and it is close-by.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at a local pizzeria that certainly lives up to its reputation - the pizza here is phenomenal! Service was swift from the moment of ordering, and despite its popularity, the ample indoor seating made finding a spot hassle-free during less busy times. It's no exaggeration to say that this was some of the best pizza I've enjoyed in NYC. Highly recommended for any pizza aficionado!

Title: A Swift Bite in Little Italy - Not Without Its Quirks

I recently decided to take the plunge into the tourist hustle of Little Italy for a dining experience at a bustling hotspot. It's true, the ambience is exactly as you'd expect: loud and lively, with food arriving at your table almost as quickly as you sit down. Efficiency aside, the place isn't winning any awards from me on value for money. The flavors were adequate but not remarkable enough to command the prices, which are steep for what feels like an assembly line meal.

The seating arrangement left a lot to be desired. It felt like a game of Tetris with my water glass precariously close to a candle and not a square inch to spare for an extra dish. Cozy doesn't even start to cover it.

As for the grub, the Farfalle con Rapini e Salsiccia was a highlight—I'm a sucker for any pasta with Italian sausage, and this didn't disappoint, though I was left craving an extra helping of cheese. The Filetto di Manzo con Funghi, however, fell short—especially the sauce, which didn't hit the mark for my taste buds.

In summary, while the pasta might lure me back on a night when I'm feeling less claustrophobic, there are plenty of quieter spots in the city that won't have you rubbing elbows quite as literally.

My dining experience at this quaint brunch spot was a flavorful affair with a wholesome vibe. My friend and I indulged in the Green Shakshuka and Poached Eggs with Grilled Tomato and Haloumi. Priced at $13 and $15 respectively, these dishes offered a refreshing take on brunch classics. The shakshuka remained light and enjoyable, but the poached eggs dish—accentuated by the salty punch of haloumi and balanced with perfectly toasted sourdough bread—won my preference.

While the restaurant presents a healthy and appetizing selection that spans from all-day brunch to dinner at prices that are quite fair for New York standards, be warned: the popularity might not justify the hype. We braved a full hour wait, which seems to be a common weekend brunch expectation here.
