If you've got time to spare, it's worth a visit, but for those with a tighter schedule, this might not be the ideal venue.

Title: Wing Heaven in the Heart of NYC

As a self-proclaimed wing connoisseur with a deep appreciation for the history of Buffalo wings, I made it my mission to visit this renowned NYC sports bar. With its clean interiors and TVs broadcasting the latest games, the atmosphere was ideal for a classic combo of sports and wings.

Now, let's talk wings. The bar's policy of offering sauces in increments of ten was a bit disappointing, as it limits the variety one can enjoy in a single order. However, I was fortunate enough to visit with a friend, allowing us to sample a wider array of flavors.

We went for a selection including Chipotle BBQ, Medium, and Spicy Garlic Parmesan. The standout was the Chipotle BBQ - a perfect fusion of sweetness and spiciness, thickly coating each wing. The Medium wings, while flavorful, were surprisingly more tame than expected, with the heat only hitting after a dozen wings or so - a true testament that sometimes, simplicity reigns supreme. The Spicy Garlic Parmesan brought a delicious twist with garlic-infused sauce and a generous dusting of Parmesan.

The wings themselves were exceptional: lightly breaded, perfectly cooked, and with a sauce that permeated each bite. They rank amongst the best I've ever tasted, and underscore the cultural significance of the Anchor Bar legacy.

In summary, for wing lovers, this place is a must-visit when in New York, although it's set the bar high for my eventual pilgrimage to Buffalo.

We were lucky to get in when we did because it quickly filled up and a line formed outside this small restaurant. The food was really delicious and I practically scarfed it all down. I definitely plan to go back and am so glad it's this close to my new apartment.

My boyfriend and I had wanted to visit a restaurant closer to us for dinner, but unfortunately for us, their kitchen was already closed. So walked around aimlessly and noticed a new restaurant (TSISMIS) and made a mental note to come next time, but one of their chefs was taking a break outside and urged us to go in...so we did! And it was a great experience. Everyone was just so lovely, and our waitress gave us excellent recommendations. We went for the gambas (shrimp with shishito pepper), Jappy's wings (VERY flavorful chicken wings), pancit bihon (rice noodles with vegetables and fried tofu), and a Where else cocktail (for myself).One bite into the shrimp and we could already tell it was fresh and cooked perfectly. Not too much. Not too little. The chicken wings were probably my favorite. Crispy and flavorful. The only thing I'd like to mention about the chicken wings is that it was a little over salted. I love salt, but at some point, it became a tad overwhelming. The rice noodles were yummy, and came in a very generous amount.If you're looking for something new in the neighborhood, this is it!

Title: A Delicious Deal During Restaurant Week

My restaurant week experience at this venue was largely enjoyable, with only a few minor hiccups. I started with the mixed greens, which were fresh, although the dressing was a bit heavy-handed. I recommend getting the dressing on the side for a lighter option. The surf and turf was the highlight of the meal, cooked to perfection with no complaints on flavor but the presentation could have been more attentive. It seems that the special menu offerings sometimes receive less care in their visual appeal during restaurant week.

To finish, the ice cream was an absolute delight, providing a sweet end to an overall satisfying meal. A special mention goes to the wine pairings made available during restaurant week, which enhanced the dining experience and offered incredible value. At nearly half the price of the regular cost, which usually ranges from $125-200 per person, the meal felt like an indulgent treat without the steep price tag. Outside of restaurant week, the regular menu continues to impress, ensuring that this establishment is worth a visit any time of the year.

This place was great. We had a Wagyu beef tartare special, the bucatini pasta dish, the whole squid entree, and the hanger steak. Everything was fantastic although the steak was a little tougher than expected. I would order something else on a second visit. Our server was also excellent and very helpful. I would definitely recommend this place for a nice upscale dinner for a special occasion. One last thing to be aware of is that the overall experience took a bit longer than we had expected. We had a a reservation at 5:30 and assumed we could be out by 7 to meet friends but we had to rush to do so. It was our fault for assuming but just as a heads up as there was a line out the door at 5:30!Would definitely recommend this place and I can't wait to go back and try out the other dishes!

Since the day I first had a JG Melon burger, I never knew that I would crave such a simple, yet amazing burger. I decided to bring my girl friend this time around to bask in this goodness it didn't fail! I got a bacon cheeseburger with cheddar and hot mess fries. The bun was perfectly toasted with a nice char in the inside, the burger cooked medium-rare was perfect throughout. And the fries? Topped with cheese, chili, jalapenos and sour cream. Oh man. I'll let the picture do the talking. 11/10 every since time.

This place is a cute, located in the Parker hotelSo it can be hard to find. The food portions were huge- I got the very berry brioche French toast- tasted amazing and looked very appetizing!! I couldn't even finish the entree because of the portion size. My friend got the chicken and waffle which came with a chocolate waffle- interesting to say the least. The reason for 4 stars instead of 5 is because they don't have unlimited brunch alcohol- one mimosa was $21 and you couldn't even taste the champagne in it. The alcoholic beverages are overpriced for a brunch restaurant. It's definitely worth going to at least once in your lifetime. The servers were great and very attentive.

Overall a great restaurant and bar on Level 7 of the brand new Neiman Marcus flagship store at Hudson Yards.Take the elevator either from the Plaza (next to the vessel) or from the 10th Ave entrance and head to the 7th floor. Walk to the back corner past the luxury jewelry. There is a bar and lounge area, then the restaurant seating. There is a bathroom that is technically outside the restaurant, inside the store, next to Chloé haute couture.Wherever you sit, each guest receives a complimentary popover, an egg based pastry, served with strawberry cream. It was served warm and tears easily for a delicious starter.We had the Frito Misto: delicately fried mushrooms, potatoes and cauliflower ($20). We got 2 drinks: A kolsch beer from Poughkeepsie ($8) and a mezcal cocktail called Urban Sophisticate ($19). Heads up they don't have beer on draft so you'll be offered your canned beer in a glass. The cocktail was very tasty as well.Lots of great app and dinner options, a fully stocked bar, and great service. Would definitely return for a bite after some high end shopping!

Absolutely a must for brunch when in NYC. The food is delicious and tastes super fresh. They also have a great outdoor seating area which is a perfect place to sit and relax for a couple of hours on a breezy Saturday or Sunday afternoon.I went with a friend and we ordered the Veggie burger and the Chilaquiles and both things were absolutely delicious! We cleaned up our plates. The service was great, the location is awesome and the food is delicious!@traveleen_gurl

Visited Sup Crab for a Mother's Day dinner and wanted to share my thoughts on the experience. Booking a table was a breeze - a quick call and we were set for a seafood feast the night before the big day. The place had a welcoming vibe with its bright lights and tasteful decor, a stark contrast to other rowdier seafood joints.

We dove into the Cajun Seafood Combo E but were persuaded to opt for the Spicy Cajun sauce over our initial choice, which was a misstep. The sauce proved too fiery and salty, masking the seafood's natural flavors. Also, the combo's accompaniments felt scant for our party of six. 

However, a pro tip for those who find the sauce overwhelming: take it home! It pairs wonderfully when diluted with noodles and serves well as an added kick to home-cooked meals. 

As for the rest of our meal, the scallion pancake and Crawfish Meat over Noodles were hits, with the latter being a practical choice for those who prefer skipping the hassle of deshelling. The String Beans with Minced Pork was a satisfying pick, staying true to my expectations, and despite a minor hiccup with the Scallops and Vermicelli, it was well-received.

On the downside, we were recommended an off-menu Beer Duck Stew, which was another overly spicy dish with no hint of the promised beer flavor, showing a mismatch between description and taste. 

Service was a mixed bag - from the smooth reservation and a quick fix on a billing error, to pushy recommendations and a sparse allocation of necessary utensils like shell crackers. Payment was another minor inconvenience, with limitations on the number of cards accepted.

In summary, Sup Crab offers fresh seafood with a Szechuan twist that can be intense for those unused to heavy spice. Stand your ground on your flavor preferences and you'll likely have a better experience. Despite the few service flaws and steep pricing, the variety on the menu entices me to consider a second visit, perhaps sticking to the Original Cajun option next time.

Huzzah, hat trick accomplished! I finished my damn ABCs and maybe now I can say I have officially become an adult. That's how it works, right? The Jean-Georges enterprise is a behemoth in the NYC dining scene and the Flatiron trifecta is the perfect example of why it has so much staying power here. All three restaurants are beautifully designed and trendy, with menus that can appease every type of palette. I had been to ABC Kitchen and ABV prior to my Cocina visit, and my expectations for this third venture were pretty accurate. ABC Cocina is a solid, well-oiled machine. While set up slightly differently (the entire menu is tapas-style), the vibe is similar. The menu is large and wide-ranging and all plates are executed with expert precision. No one thing blew me away, but every morsel delivered to our table was respectable at the very least. I highly recommend coming here with a larger party (two is fine, but four and up is best) -- there are plenty of communal tables and with such a lengthy food menu, I think it's safe to assume you'll want to try as much as possible. A little pricy as far as tapas go, but you're also paying for the Vongerichten experience.We came here as a party of four on a Saturday night. Packed, as expected. A big, wide open dining space -- a key feature of all ABC venues. There are a few little, semi-private nooks, but the feel is definitely communal. So here's the situation: double date-blind date hybrid. Bf's friend from high school and her fiancé, who we hadn't yet met. Fingers crossed that we like him (we did, phew). But we couldn't predict our opinions knowing nothing about the chap, so obviously drinks were in order. We stuck with cocktails, which I think was a good choice. The table favorite was theSpiced Pear Daiquiri (ron zacapa rum, ancho reyes, lime, pear), which three of us ordered by the end of the night. I'm not even a rum gal, but this was a perfectly-balanced, perfectly-autumn drink. My second cocktail of the night was the Whiskey Cider (berkshire bourbon, vermouth la copa, apple cider), also quite autumnal. Not *as* good but still solid. While I can't speak to the margarita section of the menu, it was reported to be a force and worth looking at.Cocina is the perfect spot if you're into sharing. It's great for large parties with adventurous palettes, though there's something for everyone here. The menu is long and varied -- snacks, lighter bites (raw fish/veggies), Spanish staples, a substantial taco/empanada section and some more substantial meat-forward plates. I suggest trying something from every section if appetites allow. We ordered more than what I'll review here -- there were a few plates I didn't try to due to dietary restrictions. Everything was great, zero complaints. Our table was slightly removed from the main dining space so I initially worried about being forgotten, but the service was efficient once we put our orders in. Eats, below:Raw shaved fluke with green chili dressing, crunchy rice, herbs: ALight and tasty, a very elegant dish with lots of subtle flavors going on but nothing to overpowering. Nice addition of the crunchy rice for texture.Tuna tartare, chipotle aioli, chilies, chives: APreparation was quite similar to a beef tartare actually -- the cut of the fish and the flavor profile -- but I didn't mind! Richer than the previous dish but still on the lighter side. Served with tortilla chips. Crowd-pleaser, a safe order for sure.Beets, shaved apples, mustard vinaigrette, marcona almonds: AOne member of our party was allergic to apples, meaning I got a second helping of this (praise!). Perhaps the dressing was a bit heavy-handed, but overall I loved this plate. Fresh, sweet and nutty, great flavors. Everything worked together and actually worked as a good palette cleanser before our meat-forward dishes started to arrive.Shrimp with sizzling garlic, chili oil: AHow a tapas bar does shrimp and garlic says a lot about the caliber of the place. It's a simple dish, but a classic that's virtually always a staple of menus like these. Luckily for Cocina, they nailed this one. Fresh, perfectly seasoned with a bit of a kick -- as well-executed as it comes. Maitake mushrooms with goat cheese, fresno pepper vinaigrette: AOne of my favorites of the night. I adore maitake mushrooms and these were delicious. Safe accompaniments here (pretty much always see red pepper and goat cheese/goat cheese adjacent served with mushrooms) but it was very well-done, all seasoned nicely. Octopus, smoked paprika creme fraiche, guajillo vinaigrette: AAs usual, I'm picky about my octopus dishes. I wasn't necessarily enamored with this but it was very, very good. Cooked nicely (that's the priority) and seasoned nicely, grounded in earthy accompaniments that supported the protein well. Overall, very well-executed and highly recommend for octopus fiends like me.

My friend and I recently dined at Wokuni in NYC and were treated to an enjoyable experience. The sushi served was notably fresh, aligning with the energetic and appealing ambiance of the restaurant. While we found the prices to be a bit steep, even by New York City standards, the quality of the meal added some justification to the cost. Our dessert was a visual treat, though the flavor did not quite match its impressive presentation. Service-wise, our waiter, despite not being as attentive as we would have preferred, did provide excellent dish recommendations. Overall, Wokuni offers a vibrant setting for savoring good sushi, albeit with a few areas that could be refined.

Title: A Surprising Treat at a Cozy Hideout

Visited this charming spot late Sunday evening and was greeted with a comfortably half-filled venue, perfect for a relaxed hangout. Contrary to my skepticism about 'Instagram foods', I ordered the Harvest dessert. It turned out to be a delightful surprise, boasting a delectable mix of layers - cake, cream, cookie crumbs, and sorbet. It's a one-time thrill for the taste buds that I'd suggest everyone try. Be warned though, at nearly $15 for a petite serving, your wallet might not find the experience as tantalizing. Nevertheless, I left satisfied with the new flavor adventure.

SO GOOD. I was in NY for the weekend and fo some reason really wanted chicken & waffle....so we came to Sweet Chick! I love everything about the restaurant. The minute we walked in, we were greeted by mini muffins while waiting. The brunch menu has a variety (but not overwhelming) of options and we opted for:- chicken & waffles: absolutely recommend. The chicken pieces were fried to perfection and flavored well. Waffles were crispy and light, paired well with syrup and/or any of the three whipped butter (sweet, savory, and regular) - bacon, egg, and cheese sandwich: super delicious, the biscuit is crumbly and buttery and just delicious - mac & cheese: scrumptious and decadent, perfect portion (not too big or small) We must have done a good job ordering because the table next to us, who came in after us, ordered exactly the same things as us after seeing our food! Overall, I highly recommend sweet chick, whether on a date, catch up session, or just because...

I frequent Taim in the West Village for my go-to falafel salad fix, customizing it with extra tomatoes and cucumbers to my liking. Should I find myself in the neighborhood and not in the mood for Bite or By Chloe, Taim remains a solid choice, consistently delivering on flavor and freshness.

Tucked away in Chelsea Market, Cull & Pistol offers a delightful surprise for seafood lovers. My boyfriend and I dropped in for a weeknight dinner and were seated immediately, diving into a savory clam chowder followed by a Connecticut-style lobster roll and perfectly roasted Brussels sprouts. The flavors were spot on, the quality impressive, and the prices surprisingly reasonable. It's a must-visit for anyone looking for a fresh culinary escape from the usual haunts like Black Barn or the bustling fast-casual joints dotting the market. Thumbs up for Cull & Pistol.

Title: A Slice of NYC – Affordable and Swift!

If you're in the city looking for quick and wallet-friendly pizza, this no-frills takeout spot is your go-to. Come prepared with cash, as cards won't do here. I opted for a whole 18-inch pie for just $10, including my choice of topping – a bargain for the size and quality. If you're fine with something simpler, the $8 plain pie is just as tasty.

The place is a hit; I barely snagged my order before a hungry crowd lined up out the door. It's a testament to NYC's diverse dining scene that you can enjoy a slice here for $1.50. While not quite the iconic 99-cent slice, it's close enough and doesn't compromise on taste.

An added bonus – the friendly staff had no issue accommodating my request for a half-and-half topping pie. For anyone seeking a quick pizza fix without breaking the bank, this spot is a must-try.

Love their happy hour special! They have a 2 for 1 special Mondays to Fridays from 4pm-7pm on drafts, well drinks and house margaritas!! When you order your first drink, they'll give you a token to claim your second one. The restaurant had a very lively vibe with colorful decor. Came with a group of six around 6pm and we were able to get seated right away. It started to get packed shortly after. I didn't really order food and just got some nachos. The nachos were loaded with sour cream, guac, beans and cheese. The portion was also huge and plenty for sharing. My friends ordered tacos which they all seemed to enjoy. The service I'd say could be better. We had to wait a while for someone to come over to take our order or refill our drinks, but they were all very friendly. Overall, this place is a great spot for after work drinks and food!

Title: A Savory Delight for All at Bareburger

I recently revisited the Bareburger chain for the first time since 2016 at their bustling Toronto location. The eatery effortlessly accommodated the Saturday afternoon crowd, signaling its popularity.

The expansive menu caters to a variety of tastes, offering a plethora of customizations for both burgers and chicken sandwiches, with vegan and non-vegan options. I indulged in a Beyond Burger topped with faux bacon and crisp lettuce. The burger was satisfyingly familiar—exactly what one would hope for from a plant-based patty.

Our shared appetizers consisted of French fries and onion rings. While the fries were enjoyable, the onion rings truly stood out, striking a delightful balance between tenderness and crunch, leaving a memorable taste.

Bareburger's warm service and prime location cemented my approval, and I find myself longing for a branch in Buffalo. It's a culinary gem that promises a pleasant experience to both vegans and non-vegans. Highly recommended!

Title: A Delightful Feast for the Senses at This Veggie Haven

My visit to this charming all-day café was a feast for both my eyes and my palate. Catering to the Instagram crowd with its aesthetic appeal, the café boasts a menu that elevates vegetables to the spotlight, offering a communal dining experience accompanied by superb coffee.

The standout for me was the "Sunset Grains" – a vegan powerhouse that defied my expectations of what a dish with kale and mushrooms can be. Hearty and satisfying, it kept me full for hours. The kale was tender, the mushrooms packed with umami, and the overall balance of flavors was impeccable.

My friends were equally pleased with their choices – the "Over the Rainbowl," praised for its flavorful dip, and "The Trails," both receiving enthusiastic thumbs up. We shared a fruit salad that surprised us with its unique twist, where the combination of yogurt and tumeric elevated the simple dish into something memorable.

Not to forget the coffee – it was top-notch, and the inclusion of free oat milk was a welcome touch for the dairy-averse.

I'm already planning my next visit to this delightful spot – it's a true gem for anyone seeking a satisfying and health-conscious meal in a friendly, inviting setting.

Despite the initial hesitance prompted by the 'B' food rating displayed outside, my previous positive experiences with this establishment compelled me to return. Once again, I lined up and ordered their signature shrimp balls and coconut buns, which remained consistently fresh and delightful - a culinary testament to being served straight from the oven. Affordability is another plus; with less than $8, I enjoyed a satisfying meal of six shrimp balls and two coconut buns. A worthy visit for those looking for taste and value.

Saturadas late lunch spot -- was pretty empty. They had a special/ separated menu which has more choice of appetizer or main dish. I ordered a beef donbury out of the menu and they really put a lot of different ingredient in the dish. I know I know, haha, you probably gonna say that I came in for the ramen! But this rice dish will never let you regret. It has tofu, enoki mushroom, onion, pinched egg and also green onion. The tofu combination is the first time that I ever had and it is wayyyyyyyyy better than my expectation. We ordered spicy miso ramen, and it's quite good since we would like some spice but not too strong. To be honest, this is not the best ramen that I ever had, I would give it 6.5/10, considering I have a really high standard for ramen. Pork belly bun is always our to go no matter what, and I really like how Jin Ramen make sure that their pork belly isn't too oily. Ps. I have been too place that their pork belly really need to be cooked/ fire gun a bit longer. Overall great experience, I think this place is quite close to the Columbia forum and campus, so it will be a good place if you would like to have a meal around campus or just chat something a bit formal. Make sure you give a try.

I recently visited a restaurant known for being open late, which was quite convenient for a late-night craving. On this occasion, I opted for the classic meatball dish, paired with bread for about $10. While the food was generally satisfactory, it didn't particularly stand out in a city brimming with culinary delights. The meatballs were decent, containing a good mix of ingredients, though they didn't venture beyond the standard fare. Unfortunately, the bread was a bit on the stale side, which detracted from the overall experience. The sauce, a traditional tomato variety, was passable but failed to impress. In summary, it was an acceptable meal, but with the abundance of exceptional dining options available in the city, this spot wouldn't be my first recommendation.

Their early bird special starts from 5-7pm and my boyfriend and I strolled right by the restaurant as they were just opening up, so we decided to give it a go. The staff there were all so friendly, place was inviting, warm, and clean. We ordered two early bird specials and chose the sashimi appetizer, sushi entree with warm and cold soba. Sushi was meh, no wow factor there, soba was also ok. The only thing that really got my tastebuds going was their green tea pudding that came at the end. That was so good! It kinda tasted like that yellow asian pudding you buy at the market with the brown syrup on the bottom, but this was green tea flavored. Over all, the meal was ok especially for the price. I thought it was worth it.

Located near Grand Central Station, Benjamin Prime opened in 2016 and combines the 'greatest hits' of the menus of both Benjamin's Steakhouse (located on the next street) and Seafire Grill.The ambience and decor is modern with high ceilings and some interesting architectural features (5 wall mounted fireplaces behind glass).Service is very, very attentive with lots of handshaking.  The food is typical steakhouse fare, though well executed and tasty. The restaurant was busy - it says something that the owners have opened two locations in Japan where the current trend is a fascination with the New York steakhouse.Minor grouse, I had a glass of bourbon and thought the ice to liquor ratio was a little on the high side - but it seems the business model in many restaurants is focused on squeezing profit from the liquor pour / wine glass.Dinner was enjoyable, car parking (after 7:00pm straight forward).

I went here for lunch for the first time yesterday and it did not disappoint. I had a salad with mixed greens, Moroccan carrots, curried cauliflower and tomato salad. I loved it! I was happy to see vegan cookies on the counter, too (nope, I am dieting!).The staff were all friendly and helpful and the place itself is lovely..... it felt like I was dining in a country kitchen rather than midtown Manhattan. I will be back!

I went on a weekday with my husband. It is a Two floored restaurant with a cute ambiance. We reached there around 8 when only 2-3 tables were full but later around 8:45-9 it got packed. Recommendations:-mai tai cocktail -lychee martini-pan fried noodlesThey have tons of vegetarian options which makes me want to come back. The menu is quite large. Moreover they also take reservations online.

While the food is very good (for vegan food), service is a bit slow and pricing seems too high for what it is.The biggest issue seemed to be the service. We got there around 2:30 on a Sunday and it was moderately full, but there was just one waiter for around 10 tables. He was doing a great job and there is an iPad app of some sort, but it just seemed the place was understaffed.Juices aren't worth the $10, don't come with ice, and seemed to both lack any sort of sweetness. I was craving some kind of apple/ginger/celery/lemon type drink, but their "green juice" tasted more like cilantro than anything else.The main courses is where these guys really shine. The Caravan burrito is a safe bet, I got mine with tofu. It came with a spectacular hot sauce on the side and was full of rice and beans, cauliflower and fresh broccoli. Still not worth $20. The bbq Tempe sandwich was excellent as well. The Nutella banana dessert was not worth it although the chocolate ice cream was pretty good for vegan ice cream. All in all, we left very full and satisfied, but paid $70 before tip for two juices, two mains and a dessert. Seems excessive, or at least if it's priced this way I'd expect the food to arrive faster. Issue seemed to be lack of servers.

No frills, in and out burger joint. My gf was craving a burger so we went here. The service was fast food quickness. I ordered and before I could think twice the food was at my table. I was left winged and went with a Philly cheesesteak which was very good. I got the curly fries as a side, they were oddly short kind of an afterthought. Overall a fair experience and next I will just get the burger and regular fries.

I can't believe JoJu opened a location in manhattan and I am so happy! I came in a little bit after 1PM and it was not crowded. There are 3 kiosks where you order your food. I only waited about 3 mins and I got my banh mi. I ordered The Sweet banh mi. The pate is super creamy. The Vietnamese ham had good flavors. The caramel pork is really delicious! I think all three were complemented really well with the pickled veggies. The banh mi also had a nice crunch to it. I think you get a great banh mi for a good price. If you are expecting a tradition banh mi from Viêt Nam, this is not the place for you. I think this place does a great modernization of the banh mi. This is the place to try it!

As a seasoned New Yorker, "BBQ's" remains a steadfast choice for a hearty meal without the frills of upscale dining. Despite it being years since my last visit to this location, it's reassuring to see their generous portion sizes haven't changed, and prices, while slightly higher, are still fair. They've expanded their menu, and I must commend their chicken and waffles—a robust and satisfying choice. Their signature #MoscatoMama drink maintains its spot as a personal favorite. Service-wise, our waiter was nothing short of commendable, providing attentive service and adeptly splitting our bill, much to our relief. BBQ's once again proves to be a reliable spot for a great time and a full belly.

Upon entering the elegant and dimly-lit sanctuary of the restaurant at my 7:17 PM reservation time, I was greeted with the unwelcome news of a wait-list; my punctuality seemingly unrewarded as my seat hinged on the absence of others. This initial disservice tainted my experience, though fortune favored me with a swift seating due to no-shows.

I navigated a menu with prices that boasted a $$$ symbol, stretching beyond my budget's embrace. Settling on the Oyaku Ju, my choice did not disappoint. The dish, a beacon of satisfaction in my hangry state, perfectly matched the elegant atmosphere and justified the price, offering a portion just as ample as its flavors. The waiter's pleasant demeanor was a highlight, although not strong enough to erase the initial hiccup.

While I may not rush back given the service hiccup, the memory of tasteful decor paired with high-quality cuisine might lure me back for a future indulgent treat.

Title: A Korean Feast to Remember

I recently visited a Korean restaurant on a friend's recommendation, and it completely blew my expectations out of the water. As someone with a serious craving for Korean cuisine, I could not have been happier.

Right from the start, the restaurant impressed us with complimentary tofu that was fresh, homemade, and incredibly light on the palate. It set the tone for the meal to come.

Our order might have been ambitious, but it was a delicious spread: CDG Fried Chicken, Mushroom Pancake, Bossam, Budae Jeongol, and Galbi Jjim. It's fair to say we ordered a feast, and although it was excessive, we were determined to savor every last bite.

The highlights for me definitely included the fried chicken, which was crisp and flavorful beyond words, and the Galbi Jjim - its rich, succulent flavors are still lingering in my memory. Both dishes are an absolute must-try.

In conclusion, this restaurant is a gem that offers some truly high-quality Korean fare. Whether you're a Korean food aficionado or new to the cuisine, I cannot recommend it enough. Just be sure to bring your appetite – you'll need it!

Title: A Delightful Surprise on a Monday Night

My impromptu visit to this much-anticipated spot on a Monday night turned out to be a serendipitous treat, as the lack of a crowd meant immediate seating—a luxury at a no-reservation venue. My boyfriend and I opted against the pre-fixe menu and dived into an a la carte adventure, with an unexpected chance to sample an exclusive dish from the set menu, thanks to our accommodating waiter.

The star of our table was the Truffle Roasted Mushroom, a dish that wowed with its table-side shaved truffles and robust flavors. It was the unanimous highlight of our meal. The Jeju Chicken Wings, hyped by other diners, were decent but didn't quite soar to our expectations. The Mul Hwe was pleasant, although it didn't leave a lasting impression. Unfortunately, the So Ramyun bowl fell flat with its lackluster taste. In contrast, the Fish Coop was a refreshing triumph that I'm already craving a second helping of.

Despite the one miss, the overall experience earned itself a resounding 5 stars from me. The return trip is non-negotiable—I'm all in for another round of that divine truffle mushroom dish!

Title: A Serendipitous Lunch at a Modest Gem

Today's lunch was a delightful surprise after our original destination was closed. Directed just down the block, we stumbled upon an eatery with a sleek, modern facade, yet serving up traditional comfort fare. Their wallet-friendly lunch specials, a mere $9-$11, started with a choice of hot and sour or miso soup. Both soups passed the palate test with flying colors.

My wife opted for the General Tso's chicken, which was a standout - tender white meat encased in a light, crunchy breading, all drenched in a flavorful sauce, and accompanied by fluffy fried rice. My choice, the roast pork lo mein, boasted a decent, savory flavor, with ample chunks of pork, though the noodles were slightly on the softer side. Nonetheless, the portion was generous and the dish satisfying.

The service added to the experience, proving to be quick without sacrificing friendliness. For anyone seeking a swift and gratifying lunch, this restaurant ticks all the right boxes. A happy accident indeed!

Although this place is not some exquisite high class place, given the price and quality of their food along with their speedy service I'd have to give this place 5 stars! All day everyday Wah Fung has a steal deal where you can order a small rice and stir-fried cabbage with the choice of pork or chicken for only $4.25. The portion they give is definitely large enough to fill you up. I have tried both their pork and chicken, which are both tasty, but I enjoyed the pork slightly better. The meat is prepared very tenderly and is delicious, especially when paired with the sauce, rice and cabbage. I haven't tried their duck yet so I'd like to return to give that a try. This place is just overall a great place to go to when you're not in the mood to cook, want something cheap, but still yummy.*Wah Fung is cash only so make sure you come prepared with a few dollar bills :)

Title: A Delightful Feast Awaits at Wok Wok

If you're in search of consistently delectable Southeast Asian cuisine, Wok Wok is a must-visit destination. My recent Thursday evening visit reaffirmed why it's a cherished spot in the city for my boyfriend and me.

Despite arriving early at 6:15 pm, the restaurant was already buzzing – a testament to its popularity. The Hainanese chicken I ordered was perfectly complemented by a savory chili sauce and aromatic chicken-flavored rice. Across the table, the white curry laksa was met with equal enthusiasm; its broth boasted a depth of flavor with just the right spice kick.

The best part? The prices are as pleasing as the food, promising a satisfying experience for both your palate and wallet.

Pro tip: Utilize Yelp check-ins for complimentary appetizers or a luscious Thai iced tea, and don't miss out on the exclusive deals offered through messenger.

Wok Wok is a gem that warrants a visit. Don't just take my word for it—swing by and taste the magic for yourself!

I recently dined at this local gem with a friend and was utterly captivated by their house special knife cut dry noodles and the fried pork dumplings - both dishes were revelations in their simplicity and flavor. The mere thought of those noodles made me want to return immediately, laughter aside. I can confidently say that I'll be a regular at this spot, eagerly anticipating my next delightful meal. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a mouthwatering experience!

Upon my inaugural visit to Atoboy, skepticism lingered—a Korean palate by birthright, I am a tough sell. Yet, Atoboy defies simple categorization—it is not merely Korean, nor can it be shoehorned into the realm of fusion. It exists in a league of its own, with each dish demonstrating an immaculate execution of technique and an aesthetic of controlled yet vibrant complexity that echoes the spirit of Korean cuisine.

As an aficionado of fine dining, I regard the grumbles over price or portion size with a bemused detachment. Atoboy is about the essence of flavor, the intangible soul that resonates within its offerings. While it may not bottle the soul of traditional Korean food, it draws deep inspiration from it, morphing into something greater—a culinary jazz performance, unpredictable but masterfully controlled.

The menu surprises and delights, marrying Korean foundations with bold accents—uni, fresh cheeses, chimichurri—that elevate each bite to a symphony of the new. To appreciate Atoboy is to embrace a novel encounter of taste, a journey worth embarking upon for those yearning to tread beyond the familiar shores of cuisine.

Tucked away on the Upper West Side, La Salle Dumpling Room offers a tranquil dining experience, complete with tasteful interior design and engaging artwork that complements their exceptional cuisine. A standout choice is their Chicken Dumplings, elevated by a harmonious spicy vinaigrette sauce that also doubles as a fantastic rice dressing. Their Xiao Long Bao and Dan Dan Noodles were also memorable for their authentic flavors and pleasing textures. The consistently attentive and cordial service rounds out the reasons why this spot is a must-visit for a serene retreat amidst the city buzz.

Title: Disappointing Experience at Tang Hotpot

My friends and I were eager to sample the offerings at Tang Hotpot, attracted by their diverse menu. The restaurant presented a clean and modern ambiance, which was a plus. However, the service experience began on the wrong foot when my tardy arrival led to a rushed dining experience – despite visible availability for later seating.

We opted for the ying yang pot, with the 6hr seafood and pork broths delivering on flavor. Regrettably, the delight ended there. The quality of the meat, particularly the beef cuts and beef tongue, was profoundly disappointing, characterized by toughness and substandard taste. It fell short of justifying the premium prices charged, a stark contrast to the superior quality I've encountered elsewhere.

Our meal was continuously interrupted by staff hurrying us, which undermined the leisurely essence of hotpot dining. Additionally, the impractical table setup further detracted from the experience, leading to an awkward juggling of dishes.

Given the rushed service, mediocre ingredients at inflated prices, and inadequate restroom facilities that devolved into an unhygienic state by evening's end, I am compelled to forgo future visits to Tang Hotpot.

We visited this restaurant for our holiday dinner with a party of seven and were delighted by the experience. The service was impeccable, with the waiter being particularly attentive to our needs, ensuring our drinks were always refilled and checking in on us just the right number of times. The culinary offerings were delectable, catering to a variety of tastes and preferences. We all left feeling satisfied and would certainly return for another memorable dining experience.

Title: A Clucking Great Find!

If you're on the prowl for scrumptious chicken paired with delightful waffle cones, look no further! I've dined here twice and am already planning my next visit. The service is consistently top-notch, with friendly and attentive staff that make the experience all the more enjoyable.

The chicken here is a standout — juicy to the core and perfectly lean. Though the buffalo sauce is mischievously mild for something dubbed 'spicy,' it still packs a punch of flavor that satisfies. The cinnamon maple waffle cone is another triumph, leaning into the rich sweetness of maple with just the right hint of cinnamon. It's a combination that's hard to resist.

I'm eager to delve further into their menu, as they've hit the mark on every offering thus far. This spot is a winner for anyone serious about their chicken and waffle cones. Highly recommended!

Title: A Birthday Bash to Remember at the Hot Pot Haven

My Saturday night at this bustling spot was marked by joyous celebrations and the novel experience of Chinese hot pot. Perfect for group gatherings, we reserved a table for our party of eight without a hitch. The lively atmosphere was punctuated by frequent rounds of the Chinese "Happy Birthday" song, complete with a mascot parading desserts—a testament to the venue's popularity for such occasions.

As a hot pot newbie, I found the eatery inviting and was swiftly immersed in the DIY dining experience. Opting for individual broths at an all-you-can-eat rate of $25 each allowed for a personalized feast. From an abundant selection, we chose various meats and veggies, reveling in the freshness and quality of our picks. The thrill of cooking at our leisure added to the charm of the evening.

Verdict: Heartily recommended for the food's freshness, the infectious excitement, and the unique dining experience. A must-visit for a fun and flavorful birthday celebration.

I recently visited this gem of a restaurant with an insatiable craving for tacos, and it did not disappoint! The chicken tacos were nothing short of amazing, bursting with flavor in every bite. I also indulged in a chicken quesadilla that had me instantly hooked with its cheesy goodness. To wash it down, I sipped on their Rose sangria, which was delightful and enhanced the meal.

Do note that they offer happy hour specials on drinks, so plan your visit accordingly to take advantage of those deals. The ambiance of the place was inviting and comfortable, making the dining experience even more pleasant. I highly recommend making reservations to avoid the mistake I made. I'll definitely be making a return trip to this taco haven!

Title: A Delightful Thai Lunch at a Great Value

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this Thai restaurant for a Thursday lunch and was thoroughly impressed. The staff greeted us with warmth, enhancing an already welcoming atmosphere. Service was prompt, with our order arriving surprisingly fast.

We opted for the lunch special – an absolute steal at about $10 for an appetizer and entrée, plus $1 drinks. I chose the pineapple juice, which, while slightly on the sweet side, was refreshing. My companions savored their Thai iced tea and coffee, both of which received nods of approval.

The spring rolls for my appetizer were a hit: perfectly crispy and well-stuffed. The true standout, however, was the basil udon with chicken. This dish was an exciting deviation from standard Thai fare – the udon noodles were perfectly coated in a savory sauce, intermingled with fresh veggies and succulent chicken, all with a hint of delightful heat. This creative twist on the classic Pad See Yew left me both surprised and satisfied.

An additional perk for budget-conscious diners: a 10% discount when paying with cash.

In sum, this restaurant delivers delicious Thai cuisine at prices that won't break the bank. It's a gem I fully intend to revisit.

Tried the beef curry bowl and loved it! There was a mix of tender and tougher beef chunks, but even the tougher pieces were tasty. The curry was savory, fragrant, and had a pleasant kick from the spices. I enjoyed eating the steamed cabbage leaves/carrot slices as a palate cleanser or even mixed in with some of the curry for texture. Definitely a solid lunch choice I'm coming back for.

Title: A Solid Choice for an Early Dinner and Cheesy Delights

I visited this spot on a Sunday around 5 PM and was greeted with plenty of open seats – a rarity that didn't last long as by 6 PM the place was bustling. Pro tip: arrive early or use Yelp to get on the waitlist to save time.

Our table ordered the shrimp dakgalbi for two, supplemented with udon, rice cakes, and gimmari. Although we found the shrimp overly salty and wouldn't order it again, the chicken was the star of the show – juicy, tender, and when smothered in cheese, absolutely delectable. The sides were a hit too, especially the gimmari, although opinions varied, with high marks for the udon and rice cakes as well.

We couldn't resist adding on more cheese dakgalbi and rounded out the meal with fried rice. Portion sizes were generous, making it an ideal setting for sharing amongst a group.

All in all, while not without its flaws, the restaurant offers a satisfying experience for cheese and chicken lovers alike.

I returned for lunch and couldn't resist sharing some of the menu highlights with friends. The Marta Miata salad was a fresh and delightful start, while the Norma pizza lived up to its great reputation. However, the Funghi pizza fell short, lacking the wow factor we expected. Our sweet note, the Peach crostata, was similarly underwhelming. The true star of the meal was the chocolate torte. Its crunchy crust and intensely flavored chocolate were nothing short of sublime. It was a chocolate lover's dream and took the overall dining experience to a level of nirvana.

After a long day at work, my friends and I stumbled upon this charming spot, lured in by their attractive happy hour deals. The decor was impressive, managing to strike that elusive balance of style and comfort. We noshed on the meatball appetizer and Brussels sprouts—both dishes were executed well with flavors that hit the right notes. However, when it came to their pasta offerings, nothing particularly stood out, leading us to skip that section of the menu. All in all, it was a satisfying post-work retreat, and I'd recommend giving it a try, especially for their happy hour and starters.

Stopped in when we needed a quick and cheap bite before heading to Penn Station. They have daily meal specials which are $9.99 for a burger, fries and a drink. The fries are more than enough for two. The burgers are packed with toppings. I'm usually a one napkin kind of girl when I eat, but I used quite a few on my burger. No complaints, I enjoyed every messy bite!  My burger was a little greasy, but that was easily fixed by dabbing it with a napkin before eating. Very small space, there are a couple of bar seats at the window, which was perfect for us to scarf our burgers down. Loved the quotes on the wall, good character for such a small space.

Title: A Chinatown Gem for Comfort Food

I'm a regular at this no-frills Chinatown favorite where speed is the name of the game. Despite the bustle, a table seems to await me every time. My comfort food cravings are consistently sated here, especially with their Beef Brisket Soup Noodles—a savory delight paired with perfectly textured noodles—and irresistible pork dumplings. A companion recently sampled the vegetarian soup noodle, which boasted an unexpectedly generous portion of bok choy, though the vegetable dumplings fell short compared to their pork counterparts. This spot is an absolute winner for those brisk days, promising hearty satisfaction without breaking the bank. Generous portions at low prices make this noodle haven a must-visit.

Title: Hidden Gem Near Broadway!

I had an exceptional experience at this quaint restaurant prior to a Broadway play. It was a peaceful Sunday afternoon at 1:30 pm, the quiet ambiance adding to the charm. The attentive bartender walked us through an impressive selection of infused vodkas – they've got an infusion for every palate! It felt like we had been transported to Eastern Europe, which resonated with me especially after recently visiting Georgia.

The vodka tasting was a highlight, with six shots for a mere $24, offering great value for money. We also indulged in delicious potato pancakes served with sour cream – a simple yet perfect dish. The promise of live piano music on my next visit is exciting. This spot is unquestionably worth a visit, though I suspect it's even livelier when busy. Can't wait to return!

This is a newly opened hand roll sushi restaurant in LES. I'd been wanting to come here for awhile, and finally just made it here on a Wednesday night. I had made a reservation a week or two prior, and it was very easy to make online. The restaurant only has counter seating, and seats to roughly 20 people or just under. Due to this, they only seat complete parties. When my friend arrived, they seated us promptly. From the menu, you can either order a set menu ranging from different numbers of hand roll, starting at three pieces and going up to to as many as six. You can also order a la carte, to make your own set. They also have a small range of dishes which are not hand rolls. I got the Sasa set for $18, which consisted of four hand rolls. My friend got the hand roll set which included six hand rolls. All were excellent, and prepared and served to us quickly. For people with a smaller appetite, four hand rolls is more than enough. For future visits, I would probably order three hand rolls. My friend was content to have six though. The service was friendly and welcoming. They gave us the bill right after they noticed we'd finished our food though, sending the message that this is not a place to eat and linger. Great value for the price, and simple ambience. I'd try this place again for a quick meal, but it's not spectacular, or a must-visit.

Title: Chewy Udon Heaven with a Side of Over-salted Pork

If you're in the mood for some authentic udon and don't mind a cash-only policy, this spot is a solid choice. I went for the ankake egg drop udon and was not disappointed by the quality of the chewy noodles. The egg drop gave the broth a lovely thickness, while the fresh green onions added a bright punch.

However, a word of caution if you plan to complement your carbs with a protein - the miso pork side may not be the best choice. Although it promised to be a savory delight, it was overwhelmingly salty and overpowered with sesame oil, making it a less enjoyable part of the meal. Stick to the udon and you'll leave quite satisfied!

Pretty nice place! I wanted to get food before my journey to the bus terminal so a friend and I ended up here; lady working in front seated us quickly and gave us the paper where we write down what we'd like to order.We got shrimp dumplings (small but yummy), juicy pork (or chicken, i don't recall) buns, and two orders of buns filled with pork, shrimp, and vegetables. I enjoyed all of them and wish my stomach could have held more food. They also gave us a little palette of three sauces- my favorite was the one with the chili flakes. I'd be down to go again if I'm ever in the area! Hopefully I have the opportunity to try even more dishes.

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Bustling Saturday Dinner

Last weekend, I ventured into this much-talked-about restaurant for a Saturday evening dinner with a friend. The place was bustling with activity, and unsurprisingly, not a single table was free. We were offered seats at the bar, which thankfully provided access to the full menu. Opting for the casual bar setting even after a table opened up, we were rather impressed by the attentive bartenders who proved quite helpful in navigating the drink selections and menu offerings.

As someone mindful of gluten, the menu left me desiring more variety; the gluten-free options were limited. Nevertheless, I settled for the Kale & Quinoa Salad, which was a delightful choice—fresh, flavorful, and satisfying. My friend tried the Tuna Tartare Tacos, which, while tasteful, were disappointingly small.

Despite the positives, I couldn’t help but feel that the restaurant doesn't live up to the hype—serving up mediocre food at premium prices. While the service at the bar was a highlight, it wasn't enough to warrant a return visit, especially for dinner. It seems that I might have missed out on what could be a better experience during their brunch services, according to other reviews. But as it stands, my singular visit did not leave a lasting impression.

Title: A New York Slice to Remember

After receiving multiple recommendations for what was hailed as the "best pizza in New York City," my expectations were sky-high as we ventured to this pizzeria post-show at 10 pm. The absence of a waiting line was our first pleasant surprise of the night, a welcome rarity in the bustling city.

Seated near the wait station, our corner spot didn’t offer the best view, but the food commanded attention to itself, eliminating any disappointment over our seating arrangement. Nevertheless, a seat in the main dining area would be my preference for the next visit.

The pizza truly was a revelation. The crust balanced perfectly between a satisfying crunch and the essential chewiness that pizza connoisseurs appreciate. Admittedly, my mother's acclaim of the sauce as "spectacular" was no exaggeration, and the pepperoni eclipsed any we've encountered in Georgia with their rich flavor.

While I can't definitively declare it the best in the city, it was unequivocally the finest pizza I've savored in years. A well-deserved five stars for the food alone. Service was satisfactory, though not extraordinary, yet did nothing to detract from the culinary experience.

The menu offered more than just pizza; my son's chicken parm sub was generously portioned and delicious. And for dessert, the snickerdoodle cookie ice cream sandwich with cinnamon ice cream was a dream come true for anyone with a penchant for the cinnamon-sugar cookie.

In summary, if you’re seeking a remarkable slice of New York, this place should be high on your list. Just remember to request a seat in the main dining area for the best experience.

I ventured into 99 Cents Fresh Pizza a tad skeptical, having had my share of mediocre dollar slices. To my delight, this place was a home run. The regular cheese pizza struck a harmonious balance between gooey cheese and tangy sauce, compelling me to grab a second slice. While the space is compact and seating scarce, it's designed for a quick bite on the move. In essence, for a wallet-friendly, tasty slice, this is your go-to spot. Highly recommended for those craving an inexpensive yet satisfying pizza experience.

I was sad that Keizo had to close Ramen Shack last year, but fortunately he has brought it back!!!Located on Midtown East within the space of Tomiz, Keizo has begun serving some of his signature bowls of ramen once again!  He's got an improved Shoyu ramen called the Future Chuukasoba, and I decided to get the Dirty version of it, which includes a Dirty Niboshi Paste.  I enjoyed eating this bowl and you can taste the freshness of the noodles that he also makes himself.  For now he offers his other signature bowls (Quiet Storm, Sunset, Tan Tan) so other people can try it!  Some of these bowls are limited, so make sure you do not get there too late for some of these menu options.Upon entering the Tomiz location, you order the ramen at the cashiers on the left side and there is a long bench in the back by Ramen Shack's kitchen that is reserved for people getting the ramen.  Check it out and keep up the good work Keizo!

Dined at Maialino last Friday evening with my sister, niece, nephew-in-law, and their son. We were celebrating Sis' birthday. It was a wonderful time! I love everything about this restaurant: the food, service, ambiance--its all top-notch. On being seated we ordered drinks (I had a beautifully prepared Makers Manhattan up, sis had a pinot noir,) and we were served warm ciabatta bread with rich, delicious olive oil and a plate of marinated olives. Sis and I split the Pollo alla Diavola (chicken, black pepper, pickled chili) and the mixed greens Insalata--both exceptionally flavorful. My niece and her husband split a fish dish--truthfully, I was so engaged in my meal I failed to note exactly what they ordered, but they were very complimentary of their dish. We finished our meal with cappuccino and the assorted cookies plate. It was all so delicious! The atmosphere at Maialino is fantastic--while it's a tight squeeze in the dining room, it feels very homey and welcoming. The staff is wonderful. There is nothing whatsoever to complain about the dining experience at Maialino. It's aces!

I had a delightful experience at this restaurant, particularly enjoying the light bites offered. The highlight was undoubtedly the Happy Hour oyster, which was incredibly fresh and remarkably delicious. Additionally, the Caesar Salad paired with Cornmeal Oyster didn't disappoint, proving to be a similarly tasty choice. The service was a cherry on top, with the lady at the bar exhibiting friendliness and attentiveness that made the visit even more pleasant. I'm certainly looking forward to a return visit to sample more of what they have to offer.

Title: A Bustling Weekday Gem with Great Happy Hour

I stopped by this local hotspot on a Tuesday evening post-movie, and to my surprise, it was buzzing with energy — a testament to its popularity, especially considering it was a weekday. The bustling atmosphere was partially due to the happy hour, which runs until 7 pm, offering patrons an excellent reason to flock here.

Our server, Fatima, struck the right balance between attentiveness and giving us our space, enhancing our dining experience. I opted for a frozen Long Island, amped up with an extra shot, which was a delightful treat. As for the meal, the fried chicken paired with mac and collard greens was a standout, combining comfort with freshness. My friend savored the catfish and shrimp accompanied by mac and plantains, which was equally satisfying.

The vibe of the place is perfect for a quick date night or an after-work relaxation spot, although it might be a tad too lively for more profound conversations. With its fresh and flavorful offerings, I'm already planning my next visit to explore more of the menu.

If you're nearby and in the mood for a tasty meal in a vibrant setting, definitely give this place a try. It's a winner for casual dining.

Title: A Memorable NYC Brunch at The Smith

On our final day in NYC, we chose to brunch at The Smith, and the experience was nothing short of impressive. Right from the start, the complimentary sparkling water and the attentive service set a hospitable tone. Our servers kept our glasses brimming without intrusion, striking a perfect balance of efficiency and attentiveness.

The food at The Smith justified the prices. As someone skeptical about ordering hummus, I found their rendition, which avoided the common pitfall of excessive olive oil, delightful. The addition of toasted sesame seeds and thin shallots enhanced the dish beautifully. The spicy salmon tartare was equally noteworthy, reimagining the flavors of a classic spicy salmon sushi roll in an inventive and delectable way.

While The Smith may be on the higher end cost-wise, the culinary experience provided was well worth the investment. It's a pity they haven't expanded to Houston—The Smith would quickly gain a regular in me.

I had seen some rave reviews for this dollar pizza place and kept meaning to try it out. After doing boozey brunch across the street and realizing I can't hang like I used to and the portion sizes of my egg dish being ridiculously small I decided to splurge on a dollar slice. I did just plain and yes - it was good. Yes, I enjoy that additional toppings are only like a dollar extra. The crust is crisp but I'm going to be that jerk and say there wasn't enough cheese and sauce. Everything tasted pretty good. But I've had better dollar pizza in the city. It's perfectly acceptable and just verging on 4 stars. Maybe they were having an off day and I just didn't get the best plain cheese slice. I'd try it again. I feel torn.

**Thai Delights NYC: A Takeout Experience**

Having frequented other branches, I recently tried the Thai Delights' location that was previously inaccessible during my stays in NYC. Craving Thai and too exhausted to dine out, I opted for delivery, choosing the classic pad Thai with seafood, a papaya salad, and chicken with chili & basil sauce.

Mindful of my spice-sensitive stomach and past experiences with the restaurant's fiery heat, I ordered all dishes without spice — a tough call for a lover of all things hot. Despite the lack of heat, the pad Thai did not disappoint; it was surprisingly full of flavor, even if its paler appearance initially raised concerns.

The papaya salad's freshness was undeniable, but it was somewhat overshadowed by the smaller portion size compared to what I'd received at other branches. This discrepancy left me wondering if this was a consequence of opting for delivery rather than dining in.

Regrettably, the chicken dish fell short of expectations due to an off-putting odor that detracted from the meal. 

For those considering Thai Delights, note that the restaurant itself doesn't deliver, requiring the use of third-party services like UberEats or Postmates — the latter, in my experience, being a pricier option.

Despite a few hiccups, friends I've recommended the place to have come back with rave reviews, echoing my sentiment that Thai Delights is a worthy choice for Thai cuisine aficionados in the city.
Ordered the pho bo and the ribs on sugar crane. The soup could be more flavorful and the ribs was mostly fat although the favor is good. Seating was easy and food came fast.

Grabbed dinner with a friend here at La Savane. Even though it's in my neighborhood i wasn't familiar with it (it's super low key). The place itself is not very big and can probably accommodate ~20 people at a time. The servers were attentive and served us quickly. I decided to go for the fish, white rice and side of plantations. The portions were pretty large (i wasn't able to finish it all). The fish was well seasoned and cooked well. I like the sauce that accompanied it. The fish also came with a fish soup that was really good. Plantains were good they cut them up in smaller pieces than I'm used to but cooked wellOverall a cool spot that i will keep on my radar for future dinner spots

I recently dined at a restaurant that, while on the pricey side, delivered a pretty delicious experience. The service was attentive, complementing the elegant ambiance of its active location. Dessert was a highlight for me, particularly the luscious chocolate cake that I absolutely loved. However, the sour cherries atop the cheesecake missed the mark according to my palate. I sampled the crab cake sandwich but found it underwhelming and not quite justifying its cost. On the other hand, the hamburger caught my eye as a potentially more satisfying option. Be advised, portions are modest, so if you're looking for a hearty meal, this might not be the place. Overall, a good spot for those who prioritize quality and atmosphere over quantity.

Had a 6:30 Thursday night reservation for a rowdy team of 16 people. We had a team pasta making class and dinner on the second floor. The ambiance is cozy, warm, and inviting. Italian Province style. White, wooden furniture, dimmed lighting, a fireplace on the second floor, warm hues all around, candles warming the space. Two floors. A bar and dining area on the first floor, and pasta making space and dining area on the second floor. A bit louder on the first floor, although our group made plenty of noise, occupying most of the second floor as well. The second floor is broken out in two areas--the dining area and a small space with a large wooden table, where the pasta classes happen. The price is $35 per person. We also had $35 per person all you can drink wine option, which made the cooking part of the experience bearable for many on our crew.I enjoy cooking, so I had fun making simple pasta using four eggs and four cups of all-purpose flour, that was portionally laid out on the table prior to our arrival. After, we rolled it and put it through the small, hand managed dough flattening machine. We got to keep that dough to take home [many people on our team abandoned their sad looking creations]. We then received pre-made sheets of perfectly made pasta. We cut them into pieces and made different shapes, per our instructor's directions. We got to take that pasta home to cook as well. Our group was drinking, so we took time, prolonging the experience and having way more fun making fools of each other than practicing our cooking skills. PS: I cooked our handmade pasta the next day and it came out better than expected! Simple and nourishing. Definitely will remember the simple egg and flour recipe for the future when I want to sound fancy and hand make fresh pasta for my guests.The service was superb, albeit slow for the dinning portion of our experience. Joe, our pasta instructor was also our waiter and has been nothing but patient, pleasant, sweet, accommodating, and helpful. Most of the peeps on our team have never cooked in their life, so Joe had a tough few hours teaching the class and making sure everyone was enjoying their experience. He taught the class in an easy fashion, always checked in on everyone, and did everything in his power to make our cooking fun. Highly recommend asking for Joe--he's a gem and highlight of our experience. In terming of dinning, we had to wait for our dishes for a while, not sure if that was due to the amount of guests in the restaurant at the time [not many] or to some other circumstances. Now to the dinner that we ate following the pasta making class. The famed, complementary breadsticks were stale and bland.Fried calamari appetizer were rubbery and bland. No one touched them after the first bite. Meatballs were huge and tasty. Well-seasoned and came with plentiful marinara sauce. Wish they had something special to them so I could remember them and recommend to try. They were solid, but nothing outstanding that I'd order again. We got entrees family style. Bowtie pasta with marinara sauce was forgettable at best. The bountiful marinara sauce was my favorite part. Repeating other Yelpers' sentiment: wish all the pasta dishes had protein to them, not just sauce and pasta, as the dish comes out underwhelming. Squid ink linguine in white [possibly garlic?] sauce was the highlight of the meal. It was flavorful and satisfying on that cold, rainy, stormy night. The linguine were definitely on the softer, gooey side, which I like, so I didn't have a problem with them not being aldente.Chicken parm was good, but on the blander side as well. Could've used more seasoning and some oomph to make this dish memorable. You can get this and better parms elsewhere else. Doughnut holes were bland. Do not recommend. Tiramisu was good, but there were mascarpone masses that should've been whisked into smooth consistency for the cream. Overall, the food is good, but you can definitely get better elsewhere. The ambiance and service are what makes this establishment [possibly] worth a visit if you're in the mood for average meal.

I wanted to check out Park Avenue Summer for restaurant week due to the beautiful decor and amazing reviews of food.  My friend and I made reservations for 12:30pm on a Friday.  The restaurant was moderately busy when we arrived.  The interior was nicely decorated, and the summer theme was well done.  However, I did not care for the table spacing.  For a pricey place, you should not be rubbing elbows with your neighbor.  Restaurant week lunch is a prix fixe menu at $26 for two courses (appetizer + entree).  My friend and I both got the corn gnocchi for our appetizers.  For our entrees, I got the pork and my friend got the salmon.  The gnocchi was FANTASTIC.  The pasta was a great pillow-like texture and the sauce had great flavor with mild heat while the truffles took the dish to the next level.  I wish I could say the same about the entrees.  The salmon was cooked medium-rare but lacked seasoning.  My friend enjoyed the accompaniments for the salmon, and said they helped elevate the flavor profile.  The pork was overcooked.  I could tell as soon as my knife couldn't cut into it.  No one should be massacring meat at a $$$ restaurant!  When meat is overcooked, it is dry and lacks flavor.  The veggies on the plate helped a little, but I regretted trying the pork.  Service here was very attentive, and the best part of the experience.  There are a lot of people on staff refilling water, cleaning tables, and checking in.  I would never pay full price for the entrees we experienced.  Perhaps if I found a dish I liked as much as the gnocchi, I would come back.  Overall, I think Park Avenue South is worth checking out at least once for the decor, but it feel short on taste for me.

My boyfriend and I have a special connection with this restaurant as it marks the beginning of our dating journey. We've found ourselves returning frequently, drawn by the delectable vegetarian menu that never fails to impress. Among the many mouthwatering dishes, the Chickpea cake stands out as my personal favorite. The ambiance of the place adds to the dining experience with its welcoming and cozy interior. Highly recommend for both its cuisine and its charm!

Title: A Neighborhood Haunt with an Open-Air Twist

If you're a football fan looking for a spot to catch the game, this local eatery is the place for you. The atmosphere is lively with a youthful vibe, undoubtedly influenced by the nearby international house residents from 155 Claremont, just two blocks away. During the summer months, the restaurant offers an unconventional dining experience with its open windows that directly face the street; a feature that adds an interesting, breezy dynamic to the space, though it may not suit those seeking a more private dining experience. The drinks menu is fairly standard and won't surprise you, but it's adequate for the casual, mostly expat crowd that fills the space. In summary, this spot is a solid addition to the neighborhood, especially for those who appreciate its laid-back, open feel and love for the beautiful game.

I recently grabbed dinner to go from a local spot and decided to try their falafel bowl and butternut squash bowl. The service was swift and the cashier exuded friendliness. While the dishes were satisfactory and flavorful, they didn't quite ignite a thrill for the taste buds. However, considering the reasonable pricing and the healthy offerings, it's a decent dining option in the neighborhood. I'd rate it a solid 3.5 stars.

My husband and I had an impromptu date night at this restaurant and it was a gastronomic delight! The venue intriguingly offers two separate entrances, one for the omakase experience and another for the bar area, where we comfortably landed without a reservation.

We embarked on an appetizer adventure, sampling a variety of offerings. The standouts were the black cod croquette, sourdough crepe, fried chicken, and a sublime hamburger topped with foie gras—the latter two being the stars I'd urge you not to miss. For our entrée, we indulged in the pork shoulder with cold noodles, an ample dish for two, interlaced with a hint of spice and exceptionally tender meat.

To sweeten the evening, we were enticed by the doughnut and a refreshingly unique coconut sorbet paired with what seemed to be hibiscus crunch—both were delightful finales to our meal.

In summary, the food and atmosphere get a resounding thumbs up from us. We're already looking forward to our return, with the omakase section in our sights for the next culinary journey!

Had a wondrous cocktail, and enjoyed the Yellowfin Tuna Crudo VERY much!  Wasn't extremely hungry when we stopped in, so didn't feel like I could do a full entree justice.  My friend had the Shrimp & Grits, and was kind of enough to share a bite (or two...) and it was glorious.  Just LOVED the many and unusual offerings on the menu!  Wish I could come back many, many more times.

I recently took advantage of Ritual's $1 week special at a local restaurant and was pleasantly surprised by the efficiency of the service – my chicken platter was ready upon arrival. The dish itself featured a generous serving of chicken tika masala, accompanied by mixed vegetables, rice, and naan bread. While the chicken tika was quite tasty and the portion size was impressively large, I wouldn't classify it as the finest Indian cuisine I've ever experienced. However, it was a satisfying and enjoyable lunchtime meal.

Title: Mixed Feelings at Amy's Ruth

I finally got the chance to visit the much-talked-about Amy's Ruth on a Sunday evening and was pleased to find a healthy crowd without the hassle of waiting. We were seated upstairs where our server (whose name escapes me) provided excellent service.

The meal started on a high note with warm cornbread and melted butter that was simply to die for. I opted for the fried shrimp with a side of macaroni and cheese and yams, and let me tell you, calling it "beyond delicious" doesn't do it justice.

However, despite the wonderful food and service, I was compelled to give Amy's Ruth only three stars due to an unfortunate observation. A bus boy in the dining area, responsible for clearing dishes and serving water, compromised the restaurant's hygiene with his unseemly nose-picking antics, followed by the unsanitary wiping of his hands on his apron. The absence of any handwashing before he continued his duties was not only disturbing but called into question the overall cleanliness of the establishment.

The experience left me with mixed feelings. While the food and service were exceptional, the concern for hygienic practices is vital in a dining environment. Would I go back? Perhaps, but certainly with reservations.

Title: A Flavor Fiesta at NYC's Culinary Gem

As a self-professed fanatic of this New York City hotspot, I've yet to tire of its culinary magic. Dubbed the crossover of the century, this eatery dishes out an ingenious creation: the naan taco. For a mere $9, you're treated to a lavish helping of succulent meat and fresh veggies, all nestled within a naan that strikes the perfect balance between buttery richness and crispness.

The seasoning of the curry is masterful, offering just the right kick to tantalize the taste buds without overwhelming them. Although they present a commendable variety, my loyalty lies with the chicken curry and chicken tikka masala - both consistently delectable.

On the side, their samosas are an absolute triumph, crammed with flavor and worthy of adoration in their own right.

In summary, this place is an unmissable culinary star in New York City's bustling food scene. Every visit confirms why I'm such a big fan.

Title: A Culinary Adventure at a Bustling Hotspot

From the moment it opens its doors at 5 PM, this place is a hive of activity, with eager diners queuing up to sample its unique offerings. My inaugural foray into the world of gopchang was a delightful revelation, a testament to the establishment's ability to cater to both neophytes and seasoned enthusiasts alike. For novices, I highly recommend visiting with an experienced patron to navigate the menu with ease.

The assorted gopchang platter was a gastronomic gamble that paid off, offering a medley of meats that were succulent and savory, despite my initial uncertainty about the specific cuts. The culinary journey reached its zenith with a serving of fried rice, prepared on a sizzling plate — the perfect encore to an already stellar meal. This experience was not just a meal but an engaging dining adventure.

Passed by the place on a whim. Entered  the food court to get some ice cream and ended up with some fried chicken go figure lol. I ordered the drum and wing combo it was kind of expensive for fast food but it was money well spent. I ordered the soy and garlic based chicken. The chicken was cooked fresh had to wait about 15 minutes for it to be ready. The chicken itself was very crispy, juicy, and filling. I even appreciated the plastic finger tips the restaurant offered so you don't get grease on your hands when eating. Would have never expected that haha. Will come again if I'm in the area

There are several price tiers of sushi to be aware of in Manhattan.  The lowest would be anything that comes with mayonnaise, or features cold tamago egg, imitation crab, or cooked ebi shrimp as one of sashimi choices.  The middle tier is where you start to see hamachi, aji, and various fish and seafood besides just tuna and salmon.  And the upper tier is where the uni, fatty tuna, amaebi raw shrimp and buttery hotate scallops live.  Typically served without shoyu and wasabi, and brushed lightly with sesame oil.This review is specifically for the sashimi lunch specials.  They have a greater menu with other Thai and Japanese items we did not try.  At $15 per order of the Sashimi Lunch and Chirashi Lunch, we received a generous portion of a mix of low tier and lower mid tier cuts.  In my opinion it is worth the price.  You will be sufficiently full.  But does include several bottom tier selections like the imitation crab, and chilled tamago egg.  This is however completed by an equal or greater amount of middle tier selections to round out the dish.The server forgot the included miso soup, which I only realized was missing afterward when reviewing the menu a second time on Yelp.  This is a place one could regularly visit for lunch if you don't mind the sashimi being a day or two behind in freshness.  But in exchange you won't need to pay $20+ per order if looking for a lunch light on your wallet.

TL;DR:  Solid + authentic if generic Japanese food, large portions for entrees, family friendly, very long wait.  Chaotic hostess system.  No tip establishment.It's always been a long wait at any of the Ootoya's around the city, which are popular with families for being stroller/kids friendly.NOTE THAT THEY RECENTLY CHANGED THE MENU (last week I'm told).  In the dinner menu, my favorites are still Kaisen Don and Hanabi Don (both chirashi bowls).  I think the prices are now higher with the new menu?Portions are big (though it seems they're a little smaller than before with the new menu change).  Everything is set based, as in comes in with various sides which seems helpful for people who can't figure out what to order at Japanese restaurants.Food is good and authentic but somewhat generic with a chain resto vibe, as far as Japanese food goes.  (In other cities I would be really happy with it but New York has a LOT of very good choices for Japanese).Service is tolerable, friendly but make sure to come with a lot of time to spare.  The hostess situation at the front is a bit of a mess.  The most recent time I went, it was about 10 minutes before an actual person showed up (despite there being 20 people crammed into the tiny waiting area), only to tell me they didn't have a table even though I had a Yelp reservation that said my table was ready.  Seemed like staff was running around in chaos trying to sort out table situations during my entire meal.... Overall I would say, if there is a compelling reason, do go, but for me, not sure if worth the effort to eat here given the multitude of other choices in nearby St. Marks.

First and hopefully last review of a new business to open during the covid-19 quarantine, this is a new Italian spot from chef Adam Leonti, who has now had several excellent but too short-lived spots in NYC.Obviously only takeout and delivery right now, there are lots of great options of classic Italian dishes to try.
