We picked up a bunch for dinner, but the Focaccia just came straight out of the oven and we ate it in our car out front, and wow, that was some of the best bread I've ever had. Must must try. We also had the Pepperoni Pizza, which was also incredible.Looking forward to seeing a full sit-down menu from these guys once this insanity is over, so go support now as much as possible to get them through this time and eat this amazing bread ASAP.

I love Xi'an Famous Foods, and have been a loyal follower for more than a decade... Quick comment about this location: there are too many seats installed too closely together which leaves no space for the tourists' jackets & backpacks & suitcases & purses & shopping bags: five people can easily take up ten seats... Quick comment about my favorite dish: extra spicy cumin lamb noodles -- they aren't spicy, there's barely any cumin, there's barely any lamb; I'd gladly pay more to receive a satisfying portion, but I understand they're trying to keep prices low, meanwhile landlords keep doubling & tripling rents.

Had a relatively late dinner here after drinks elsewhere beforehand.  I see all the other 4~5 stars review and I'm not getting it...The food was decent, but I didn't think that it was out of this world good...  The steak came out after a really long time and was way on the heavy/salty side.  The pork was also a bit too dry.  Uni was surprisingly only just ok...  The highlights were probably the lamb meatballs and truffle mac, but the rest of the plates were honestly just so so.Sat at the bar, so the service was good.  However, they unfortunately don't have a hard liquor license, so they are limited to those beverages under 20% only.  Tried the makgoli here and it was just bad, so we sent it back.  The other drinks with glowy lights didn't really impress me either.  They reminded me of those kids' sneakers with flashy LED lights back in the 90s...

I met up with a good friend of mine who I haven't seen in 5 years. She recommended this place for some awesome pub food. Finding the place was a bit difficult but it was very cool hole in a wall. Food overall was very good.   It was obvious that my friend was a regular. Service was friendly and knowledgeable. The first dish we ordered was their appetizer special homemade burrata with zucchini to share.  The portion size was ideal for one but we split in half. The dish was a great start and complemented our happy hour drinks. In this case I ordered a cider which was a great portion for the price I paid. We moved along with the main orders. I had the chicken sandwich and fries. The sandwich was a close to perfect balance of bread to chicken and the chicken was breaded and fried to perfection. The fries were definitely homemade and authentic like a true chip British style. My friend ordered the traditional fish and chips which was pricey for the portion she received. She loved her meal but unfortunately they only serve fish and chips as the main entree and she recalled seeing as an appetizer.  Personally I would definitely take my friends here for happy hour. It's a great hole in the wall located secretly below or within a hotel. I want to try their other dishes especially their shepherd's pie and burger.

Title: A Dreamy Dumpling Delight at Buddakan

If there's a dish destined for Food Network's "The Best Thing I Ever Ate," it's undoubtedly Buddakan's divine Edamame Dumplings. These little morsels of bliss are a must-have and a recurring dream of mine, compelling me to make a beeline for Buddakan upon setting foot in the city. Beyond the dumplings, the food is consistently impressive. The restaurant exudes an air of chic sophistication, justifying its higher price point.

The dim sum selections shine brightest for me. The soup dumplings burst with flavor, and the rock shrimp is another crowd-pleaser. While the sizable Lobster Egg rolls are satisfactory for sharing, they lack a certain je ne sais quoi. In contrast, their covertly excellent lychee martini—a secret gem not listed on the menu—is a thrilling diversion from the usual.

Be prepared for a vibrant ambiance; Buddakan's energetic buzz makes it a prime spot for celebrations. It might get loud, but the people-watching opportunities are an entertaining perk. Despite the decibels, Buddakan remains an illustrious culinary hotspot that's worth every decibel for those delectable dumplings alone.

Title: Decent Food, Disappointing Delivery from Local Spot

I've recently experienced delivery from a neighborhood restaurant that's left me with mixed feelings. On two separate occasions, the delivery time stretched well beyond the acceptable, clocking in at over an hour and a half despite follow-up calls and living just a few blocks away.

Despite these delivery woes, the food quality itself paints a brighter picture. The grilled chicken was a pleasant surprise—lean, mild in flavor, and generous in portion, allowing for personal seasoning preferences. The large tostones provided a hearty serving but suffered a bit in texture, hinting at oil that perhaps needed refreshing.

The steak encebollado's consistency wasn't reliable; one time it arrived with a perfect savory blend, while another was marred by over-salting and an unfamiliar taste profile. As for the red beans, they offered a satisfying medium thickness and didn’t skimp on the beans, outshining other Dominican places that often lean too heavily on broth.

All things considered, the food aligns well with what you’d expect from a casual Dominican/Hispanic establishment in terms of taste and quality. However, I’d be hesitant to suggest their delivery service. If you're craving their dishes, you might be better off opting for pick-up—though I can't vouch for that experience personally.

Title: Cozy Dumpling Delights at Tiny Shanghai

Rating: ★★★½☆

Nestled in the bustling heart of Chinatown, Tiny Shanghai proves to be a delightful spot for those with a penchant for authentic dumplings and noodles. A must-try on each visit are their signature soup dumplings, which do require a bit of patience; give it 15-20 minutes for these little pockets of joy to arrive at your table, possibly because there aren't enough steamers to expedite the process.

The shared experience of their menu offerings was generally good, with the Fried Tiny Buns being commendable, albeit not the best I've savored compared to nearby Shanghai 21. The Beef and Broccoli dish left me wanting with its rather stingy beef portions, but it was tasty nonetheless. On a brighter note, the Beef Lo Mein was brimming with flavor, making up for earlier shortcomings.

Their soup dumplings are the true stars, with both crab & shrimp and black truffle & pork variants hitting the mark. Although I'm on the fence about the extra charge for the truffle enhancement, it was a unique experience worth indulging in at least once.

Overall, while Tiny Shanghai dishes out some worthy Shanghai-style cuisine, it may not top my list of favorites in Chinatown, given the time it takes for their specialty to be served. Still, it's a good place that merits a visit, especially for those dumpling cravings.

'm a sucker for Xi'an Famous Foods. I previous reviewed the restaurant in Flushing, which is the original one so I was excited to try the Midtown location. This restaurant is very close to the Empire State Building and gets a lot of foot traffic from tourists so I was a little weary that the quality of the food would go down. To my surprise, it didn't! I came here on a Sunday night around 7/8pm with a couple of friends (3). One of my friends order the Spicy Beef Noodles while my other friend and I both ordered the Spicy Lamb Noodle Soup. We were able to grab some of the last lamb dishes before they sold out! When we got there around 8pm, most of their cold vegetable dishes were already sold out such as their spicy cucumber salad, which is a shame because that would be perfect as a side for the noodle soup. I would suggest if you have specific dishes you want to eat, to go here early. They also have slightly different items based on the restaurant location- so I wouldn't be surprised if your favorite side dish isn't at this one/or vice versa.The Spicy Lamb Noodle Soup was delicious. Great flavor that wasn't washed out with the soup. Great cumin seasoning on the lamb and the noodles were great. I prefer the noodle dish on a cold winter day- it will really warm you up.The place is pretty small and you seat yourself. With that being said, a lot of people do take out so there is a lot of foot traffic so be sure to check the back. I can see this place getting a little hectic during lunch hour if people are trying to sit down and eat. I would suggest no more than 4 people groups when coming here for a sit down. Great location and will be sure to come back for more. It's a bit closer to Flushing so this is a great spot to eat Xi'an Famous Noodles.

I recently visited this restaurant for their dim sum and was pleasantly surprised to find that they've standardized the price for dishes of all sizes at $3.25 each, making it an affordable dining experience. This place becomes bustling by noon, so it's advisable to arrive early to avoid the rush. The quality of the food didn’t disappoint; it was delicious. Coupled with rapid service, the overall experience here is definitely worthwhile. It's a great spot to enjoy a meal with family and friends. Highly recommended for dim sum lovers!

Tucked away as a culinary gem in NYC, this restaurant remains a personal favorite. The chori burger, with its savory beef longanissa patty, consistently delights my taste buds and stands as a testament to their menu's excellence. A friend recently savored their brunch special, a unique Filipino twist on classic eggs Benedict, which came in a generous portion that echoed the restaurant's commitment to hearty meals. The staff's friendliness only enhances the dining experience, making every visit as enjoyable as the last.

I recently visited a once bustling burger joint that's now easier to navigate without the long lines. Deciding on the American burger, I was pleasantly surprised by its taste and would certainly order it again. The peanut butter milkshake, shared between us, was satisfyingly sweet without being excessive, though I'm eyeing the Oreo milkshake for my next visit. My companion enjoyed his bison burger in quiet contentment.

The menu is on the pricey side – $60 for two burgers and one milkshake feels steep, especially when considering the size and presentation of the milkshake, which was more elaborate than substantial. Opting out of the extra candy garnish didn't diminish the cost.

In summary, while the food was enjoyable, the restaurant would benefit from more competitive pricing to complement its quality offerings.

This felt to me like a corporate bakery/pastry place. The croissant came in a pre-packaged box, like at the airport or a Starbucks. When I ordered it, I was told to grab it from a display of boxed goods. Everything was OK. The outdoor seating and service were nice.

Title: EN Japanese Brasserie - A West Village Gem

Review:

Discovering EN Japanese Brasserie in the West Village has been an absolute delight. Perfect for everything from a business lunch to a friendly catch-up, this modern Japanese eatery boasts an interior that blends sophistication with warmth, making you wonder if you've walked into an upscale furniture gallery. With attention paid to every detail, including the elegant dishware and a shockingly pricey yet enchanting bathroom diffuser, the ambiance is undeniably inviting.

When it comes to dining, opting for the lunch menu is where the best value lies. The fried chicken lunch set is exemplary, priced at $19, and includes a range of sides from soup to obanzai, complemented by a surprisingly delectable, cloud-like soft tofu and the pièce de résistance, succulent fried chicken thigh meat that needs little more than a lemon wedge—or, upon request, a refreshing dip in savory ponzu sauce.

For those exploring the a la carte offerings, the flounder karage presents as an innovative standout. Priced at $24, this fusion of textures and flavors combines crispy flounder with a vibrant scallion salad, served with ponzu for an extra zest. A dish best shared due to its generous portion.

Seasonal treats like the visually stunning cold soba noodle with warm duck broth make for a special summer experience, while the hot duck soba caters to winter cravings. Though the duck is sparingly served, the flavorful broth more than compensates, particularly with the cold version's unique presentation and taste profile.

In sum, EN Japanese Brasserie excels in creating memorable meals with a touch of luxury. While a la carte dining may climb in price, a visit here, especially for the lunch set or special dishes, is an indulgence worth savoring.

I don't want to sound fickle or hastyAny more than I like to look pastyBut the Pancakes at DumplingAre as dreamy as HumpingWith Barbie, and almost as Tasty!Get: THE PORK AND CABBAGE PANCAKE. IMMEDIATELY.Don't get: Anything else. Dumplings meh. Just do what I said.So I've been told that my dumpling is pretty tasty. But it's kinda expensive these days if you want to taste it.My dumplings are another term for all the short girls I've dated and broken up with over the years. Yes there are many.But I'd never dump Tasty Dumpling.Ever.Even though their actual dumplings are very dumpable, honestly. Their pork and cabbage pancake though is one of the. Best. Things. I've eaten in NYC. Seriously.This is one of those places that Yael recommend that I try - and honestly I wasn't expecting much. I mean we're talkin about a cheap little back-street savoury Pork/Cabbage stuffed pancake at a hole in wall place with mixed reviews in Manhattan - and even though a lot of the stuff that she likes is stuff that I really like, there's also a lot of stuff that she thinks is great which doesn't really blow me away.However this blew me away more than almost anything else I've ever eaten in New York City. Absolutely spectacular amazing delicious stuff here. WOW.Not so friendly... kinda didn't want me to use their bathroom but I did anyway. Didn't mind them being iffy in the service department after I tasted the amazingness.It literally ended up being one of the very best things that I've ever eaten in NYC. Not even exaggerating. Yael now has the claim to fame of having recommended a whole host of the "best stuff I ever ate" in NYC. Probably 10 of my top 50, probably 3 or 4 of my top 20 even. And I've eaten hundreds if not thousands of good things in this town.It's so damn cheap that I bought two of these Pork/Cabbage pancakes - even though I knew I didn't want to eat two of them. They turned out to be a huge as well as cheap - and I ended up eating all of them, because they were just so f**king good.And if you get a rash on your butt from sitting in a dirty taxi, there's a name for that."Cab-itch."

Title: A New York Slice Surpasses Italian Roots

Having feasted on pizza in the heartland of Italy for a month, I thought I had experienced the zenith of this saucy, cheesy delight—until I encountered the bustling scene of a New York pizzeria that challenged everything I knew about a good slice.

The line stretched out the door, but the recommendation from a local with a hearty New York (or Jersey?) accent was simple: "Get a plain or a sausage...everything is solid here." Taking his advice to heart, I opted for three varieties: cheese, Diavolo, and potato.

The cheese slice was a marvel—enormous, fresh, dripping with glistening cheese oil. The sauce was a revelation, sweet and vibrant, as if the tomatoes were just plucked from the vine. Despite its size, which made folding it almost a Herculean task, the taste was worth the effort.

The Fra Diavolo was a spicy square of perfection, loaded with crisp pepperoni and fiery sausage on an audibly crunchy base. Each bite was a testament to the balance of heat and flavor.

The potato slice, a creamy concoction of potato and onion, was a unique and satisfying departure from the norm. Alas, after the cheese and Diavolo, I was already deep in pizza paradise and couldn't do it full justice.

This joint is a must-visit whenever I find myself back in New York—a testament to the city's ability to take a classic and raise it to a whole new level of deliciousness.

I recently dined at a local Malaysian restaurant that truly impressed me with its offerings. The highlight was the curry laksa, which was absolutely delicious – a perfect blend of spices and flavors. Despite the bustling atmosphere, it's surprising that this gem seems to maintain a low profile. Service was efficient, no-nonsense, and the menu prices were very reasonable. This spot has all the makings of a great go-to for a casual weeknight dinner.

This review i for this tender greens location as i am a frequent customer of tender greens because I'm from California and would go often and i have NEVER dealt with this before.So starting out the customer service was cool the young lady who helped me was nice but the food was horrible!! My chicken was pink and undercooked and i also found a piece of steak meat/bone in my mashed potatoes!! I do not eat red meat so I'm completely disturbed right now.

This place is good but not amazing. But there's no denying that they're still very busy and popular. You'll still have a difficult time getting a reservation here. The wings are delicious and I would definitely do it again. I believe they're sprinkled with Chinese five spice which is delicious. The egg rolls were different but enjoyable. But the star of the night was the Hainan crab rice. The flavor was absolutely on point. They only comment is that it wasn't hot enough, temperature wise. The mapo tofu had too much mala going on. To the point where it wasn't even tasty anymore. I would skip that next time.

On a recent Tuesday evening visit to Cucina Bene in the Financial District, I found both the pizza and the establishment underwhelming. The pizzas on display lacked visual appeal, and unfortunately, the taste did not redeem them. The crust was overly hard, the sauce too salty, and the toppings meager – the Buffalo Chicken Slice suffered from greasy, underheated chicken with no trace of buffalo flavor, while the Ricotta and Spinach Slice was the only mildly redeemable option, thanks to its departure from their standard fare.

Portion sizes were typical of New York pizza slices, priced at $3.00 for a Cheese Slice and $4.00 for specialty slices like Chicken Cutlet or Ricotta and Spinach, which is reasonable but not justified by the quality served. 

The ambiance did little to uplift the experience; despite its proximity to the NY Stock Exchange, Cucina Bene is easily overlooked, with a cramped interior exacerbated by unkempt tables littered with debris and an unclear waste disposal area.

During my visit, the shop was nearly empty, save for another customer engaged in a loud phone conversation, contributing to an already less-than-pleasant atmosphere.

Staff seemed disinterested in attending to cleanliness, with no effort made to tidy up the dining space. To top it off, expect to be challenged by the parking situation if you're driving. In summary, Cucina Bene failed to impress on all fronts – from pizza quality to cleanliness and service.

Came here for brunch on a Sunday. They take reservations and it gets quite busy, so I'd recommend it! They have two deals, one for $21.95 (a dish + coffee/tea) and $31.95 (a dish + bottomless mimosa/blood mary). The ambience is lively and laidback.  We got the tunisian eggs (baked eggs with spicy tomato, feta cheese and capers) and the eggs scandinavian (poached eggs with smoked salmon). I enjoyed the tunisian eggs which were a decent size and came with a great spicy tomato sauce. They also come with a side of baked potatoes. The bloody mary was a little watery but decent.Overall, decent spot in the east village especially if you're looking for a bottomless brunch option!

Nestled within the Gramercy Park Hotel, this Italian gem is a culinary treasure trove in Manhattan. My experience? A flawless 5/5. 

The adventure began with a Pignocco wine, a delightful nod to my Nonni's roots in Le Marche, each sip as refreshing as the last. The antipasti—salami etna and an exquisite blue goat cheese—set the bar sky-high, with both earning top marks for their extraordinary flavors.

Pasta courses followed suit; the spaghetti vongole boasted an ample serving of fresh clams, nestled within al dente pasta, all swathed in a savory sauce. The fettuccine bolognese, a harmonious blend of pork ragu and pasta, provided a robust and satisfying symphony of flavors.

Ambiance? The restaurant's minimalist art aesthetic served as a quiet yet elegant backdrop to the meal. Service? Impeccable. Both waiter and server emanated warmth, impressing with their attentiveness and expertise.

In sum, this dining experience was exceptional from start to finish. I'm eagerly anticipating my next visit.

I recently visited a local restaurant for happy hour, which runs from 4-7pm, offering $6 drinks and appetizers—a real steal. It was the perfect spot to unwind with coworkers after a nearby work event. We arrived at 4pm to find the place welcomingly quiet. The quick service was a highlight; there was hardly any wait for our orders. The wings definitely hit the spot, although the potato skins were a bit underwhelming. All in all, a great choice for an affordable post-work gathering.

Pretty good food here! I would give 3.5 star more likely. But it's definitely worth more than 3 stars. BBQ here is good, I really love the side dishes here today, fish cake, jabchae, yummy!They have lunch specials which is good value, should come back some time here during week day!Service is quick and good here too, recommend

Absolutely loved this place. It's a fusion of Chinese and Cuban food. If you check in on yelp you'll get yucca fries served with gochujang (Korean red pepper) ketchup. Bottomless drinks for 90 minutes and there are quite a few choices beyond the typical Bellini and mimosas. There's a guava and caipirinha drink and these drinks are strong!!!I got the pulled pork Benedict and my friend got their avocado smash. Both were pretty good. Service was amazing starting from our server to the bartender. The place opens at 11 and there are plenty of seats but it quickly fills up.

Manhatta was the place -- sight unseen -- where we celebrated our 25th Wedding Anniversary. Considering that I would never win the 'Husband of the Year' award, I really needed these folks to come through and help me out. And did they ever. First, I made reservations here weeks in advance (online from Houston). Whatever system they use is clutch, because I received a number of automated messages about my evening and also was afforded the opportunity to text back and let them know that I wanted to impress the hell out of my bride. It all worked like a dream.We showed a little early and sat in the lounge, with its comfortable lounge-style seating and telescopic lookout stations with a gorgeous view of the city. The lounge area is staffed by an attentive server who made sure that the wine and beer flowed ... and anything else we wanted. Outstanding.We were seated, by request, in a corner with a view. Wow. My wife was so enamored with the setting. Admittedly, I was too. We've had tables with a view in a number of American cities, but this one took the cake. After all, New York is the capital of the world. And when you have such a view -and- a staff that is truly interested in helping you make memories ... there's nothing better. Though the food here became secondary, it was fabulous. Foie gras was succulent -- even my wife (a non-organ meat eater) tasted a sample and was won over. The beef was melty. The veggies were crisp tender. But forget about all of that.Want to impress your date? The Dom Perignon is available by the bottle here, and it works like a charm. But truly, it's the service and atmosphere that impresses. Thank you, Manhatta, for making our 25th Wedding Anniversary so much more memorable (with plenty of brownie points to boot) than I could have done on my own.

Title: Decent Spot in UES, But Chinatown Holds the Crown

If you're hunting for exceptional dim sum, you may want to keep looking beyond this UES restaurant. While the ambiance is quite pleasant, and the service is reasonably prompt, the food doesn't quite hit the mark. The soup dumplings lacked the promised "soupiness", and the duck roll, albeit tasty, was disappointingly petite. A severe letdown was the turnip cake; imagine an undercooked dough with bits of turnip—far from appetizing. On the brighter side, the dandan mian and siumai were satisfactory, with the pork BBQ bao being decent, though it hinted at being previously frozen. All considered, the experience was underwhelming, particularly when you factor in the cost, which seems inflated for the quality served. Great for atmosphere, but your taste buds might vote for a trip to Chinatown instead.

Title: Authentic Mexican Flavors Shine at Los Tacos, NYC

If you're on the hunt for authentic tacos in the Big Apple, look no further than Los Tacos. While New York City may not be synonymous with Mexican cuisine like Los Angeles is, this bustling joint tucked away in Chelsea Market is a gem that rivals the best.

Los Tacos has earned its reputation, with lines of eager patrons at any given time indicating just how beloved it is. Don't let the queue deter you; it's a small price to pay for what awaits. The variety is commendable – from the succulent grilled steak to the zesty marinated pork, every option is a powerhouse of flavor wrapped in a soft corn tortilla.

The true standouts are the juicy meats, perfectly marinated and brimming with spices, especially when loaded with all the fixings like onions, cilantro, guacamole, and salsa. A personal recommendation – don't miss out on the grilled cactus taco for a unique twist.

The restaurant's efficiency in handling the crowd means you'll be sinking your teeth into these vibrant, flavor-packed tacos in no time. For those spice aficionados, the roasted chili peppers at the condiment station are a must-try addition to your meal.

Returning countless times, I've yet to be disappointed. Los Tacos is not just a place to satisfy your taco cravings; it's a culinary experience that keeps you coming back for more. Whether you're a local or just passing through Chelsea Market, this is the go-to destination for some of the best tacos in the city.

The best thing about this restaurant are it's amazing views! If you have out of town guests, this is a great option for dining. Our group was placed in the PDR because we had 10+ people, and were a little upset that we couldn't experience the dining room menu. The Wagyu beef was incredible, but our pasta was extremely undercooked. While our waiter was very attentive, we wish we were treated less like a catering group than diners of the restaurant.

I was starting to lose hope that there were any good Ramen joints in the Lower East Side. It was a rainy cold day and I knew I needed some noodz to warm up my soul. This spot is super small and it was packed when I arrived. In order to get in the queue, you have to order and pay. Once a table opens, the host will get you. Very interesting way to make people stay lol.I ordered their new toyko style shoyu ramen. At first sip, my faith in the ramen gods were restored. The temperature was just right and the the broth was flavorful and the perfect consistency. The broth is made with Chicken, Truffle, and porcini. The noodz come with Chāshū Pork, Chicken Breast, Bamboo Shoot, Shiso, Egg, Mushroom Paste, Pork Fat. Each meat was delish and the egg was cooked perfectly. I have to say that Ramen Ishida is my favorite bowl of ramen in the LES so far. It's not your traditional ramen broth, but it's bomb. Highly recommend if you are in the area and want noodz.

Hummus and Falafel was delicious, the falafel was not dry and it's tasty. Chopped Salad was being chopped salad. Branzino was good, a but heavy on the butter or oil whichever they used. Shrimp Risotto was meh, the shrimp was good just the sauce was weird I didn't get it. Outdoor seating perfect for the summer time!

I stumbled upon this gem while hunting for a bite to eat and decided to give their grilled chicken salad a whirl. The server promised satisfaction, and boy, were they right! The mix was so tantalizing that, despite my usual aversion to tomatoes, I found myself enjoying every last piece. If they’d tossed in some red onions, it would have been absolute perfection for my palate. It was so delicious I contemplated taking leftovers home, but alas, the generous portion left me satisfyingly stuffed with no room for more. Would recommend and return!

Food in a museum can go 2 ways... this one went right where I wanted it to! YUMMY & beautiful! I didn't think that the portion would be big enough for the price but it satisfied my hunger for a few hours. The food inside is gourmet so definitely step in and just go to the cafe, bypass the museum like we did (just for this trip) and then go across the street and go shop at the Moma store! soooooooooooo much fun stuff inside the store.

Title: A Lit Brunch with Vibes and Beats

I recently had the pleasure of attending a friend's birthday brunch at this lively spot, and the venue certainly lives up to its name - it's lit, both figuratively and literally. The DJ kept the energy high with an excellent mix of hip-hop, borderline techno, and R&B that ensured a buzzing atmosphere throughout our celebration.

The interior design strikes the perfect chord between minimalism and artistic flair, boasting striking art pieces and ambient globe lighting that, alongside the tasteful flora, create a laid-back vibe. It's a space that caters to a stylish and mature crowd, primarily 25 and older, where everyone seemed to be in their best attire and radiating positivity.

As for the space, it's ample, allowing for plenty of room to move and dance without feeling crowded. The highlight for me was the food – I savored the shrimp and grits with an added touch of cheese, and it was a delight. The shrimp was notably fresh and seasoned to perfection.

Service was generally satisfactory, but an encounter with a rather surly bartender slightly marred the experience, hence the slight deduction in what would have been a full five-star review. On a brighter note, the unlimited mimosa or sangria offer for $25 an hour per person was the cherry on top of this enjoyable experience. Overall, despite the small hiccup in service, I'd recommend this place for anyone looking for a great brunch spot with energy to spare.

Title: A Hot Pot Haven for Traditionalists

If your taste buds yearn for the authentic hot pot experience, then rejoice, because this place has mastered the art of traditional hot pot, especially their standout dry hot pot. What sets it apart is the DIY element—handpick your favorite ingredients to craft the hot pot bowl of your dreams. A combination of 4-5 items is ample, leaving you satisfied with leftovers to spare.

Personal favorites that are a must-try include the delicately cooked quail eggs, succulent sliced rib eye beef, tender enoki mushroom, perfectly cut fish fillet, and the star of the show—Fuzhou fish balls. These delightful orbs pack a surprise with their savory meat filling, and they're divine.

For those who enjoy a culinary kick, opting for the spicy level is a game-changer, as it infuses the pot with an explosion of flavors. The mild is palatable but pales in comparison. Adventurers and heat seekers might dare to try the super spicy level—but be warned, it's not for the faint-hearted. This restaurant delivers on all fronts for hot pot enthusiasts.

Title: Lackluster Service Overshadows Decent Breakfast

I stopped by this spot for a late breakfast and was immediately struck by the indifferent welcome. The hostess wordlessly ushered me to my seat and the staff seemed devoid of enthusiasm for their work. The service was lacking—my waiter disappeared after taking my drink order and only reappeared after a lengthy wait.

I ordered an egg burrito and had to flag down the waiter again for guacamole. Observing the floor staff's interactions, they were more akin to stoic guards than welcoming hosts—an odd vibe for a restaurant. The manager and hostess maintained the same stony demeanor, barely acknowledging patrons unless prompted.

When my burrito arrived, there was confusion over the side dish; I had expected french fries, but it came with home fries. The waiter seemed bothered by my question but offered to correct it. Meanwhile, I found solidarity with neighboring diners over the palpable tension from the staff.

The food itself was satisfactory—the burrito was flavorsome though heavy on potatoes. Despite the cool ambience of the restaurant, the overall experience was tarnished by the distant staff.

As I departed, the hostess's sudden warmth felt disingenuous after the initial cool reception. While the restaurant appears to thrive, I left feeling uncertain about a return visit. The takeaway—decent food can't compensate for a lack of genuine hospitality.

Restaurant Review: Jungsik, TriBeCa

In the chic enclave of TriBeCa, Jungsik offers a modern Korean cuisine experience that's nothing short of sensational. The ambiance of the space pairs well with the innovative dishes, making it the perfect spot for an unforgettable high-end meal.

Eschewing our traditional birthday omakase, we dove into Jungsik's full tasting menu ($235 pp), a veritable feast that proved to be worth every penny. Noteworthy among the many delights was the Foie Gras Mandoo, a divine combination of rich dumpling and soothing bone broth, joined by tender raw beef. The Octopus was another star, its perfect frying technique delivering an irresistible crispy exterior juxtaposing a succulent inside, amplified by a spicy, heat-packed aioli.

A reimagined Tuna Kimbap was a revelation in textures and flavors, turning the familiar snack into a gourmet highlight, while a modern take on a traditional Korean birthday soup added a personal touch to the occasion, transforming it into a creamy delight.

Desserts at Jungsik are in a league of their own with the signature Baby Banana being a pièce de résistance—artful, edible white chocolate craftsmanship paired with coffee ice cream. A return visit confirmed their standalone dessert tasting ($75) as one of the best.

Jungsik excels not only in food but in service, with a welcoming environment and attentive staff ensuring your meal is exceptional from start to finish. For anyone questioning the price, rest assured it's a resounding yes—absolutely worth it. Jungsik doesn't just serve meals; it serves memories that linger long after the last bite.

Title: Trendy Bites with a Side of Patience

Upon entering the bustling, compact space of the restaurant, my party of four was swiftly seated despite the presence of two large parties. The atmosphere radiates a vibe that’s perfect for a lively happy hour.

Our culinary journey included an array of dishes—succulent fried chicken, savory duck wings, and the inventive Fries with short rib. The beef and avocado tacos, with their crispy wonton-like shells, offered an enjoyable Asian twist, while the well-seasoned Brussels sprouts impressed with their difficult-to-achieve deliciousness.

The slow arrival of the wagyu buns, however, tempered the experience, contributing to a three-star rating. While the flavors across the board were vibrant, particularly the short rib that featured in both the fries and the buns, timely service could have elevated the meal.

The smoked ramen received nods of approval from my companions, but it was the wagyu buns—despite the wait—that were the standout for me.

In conclusion, while the restaurant tips towards the pricier end and patience may be required, the promise of tasty bites makes a potential Happy Hour return an intriguing prospect.

Cheap, decent Chinese takeout place that is good for lunch. The owner is friendly and accommodates requests. I ordered chicken and eggplant in garlic sauce since so it was in all the reviews. Isn't on the menu but he was willing to make it. The garlic sauce wasn't very garlicky and it was a bit sweet, but it was still good. There was a lot more eggplant than chicken. There was enough for two meals. Cash only.

I recently savored the flavors of Tiny Shanghai on the recommendation of a friend and was not disappointed. Arriving at a quieter time, 1:20 PM on a Friday, the sparsely occupied restaurant offered a calm dining experience. We embarked on a culinary journey with sliced beef in scallion pancakes – a delightful mix of savory and fresh – followed by tangy Szechuan style wontons. The hearty Shanghai lo mein with beef was a feast in itself, leaving us more than satisfied. Yet, the highlight was undoubtedly the pork soup dumplings; their perfect preparation could easily turn them into a daily craving. Service was brisk, but a heads up for credit card users: they only accept American Express, though debit and cash are fine. Despite this minor hiccup, the tantalizing dishes and prompt service ensure I'll be returning to Tiny Shanghai for another serving of authentic Shanghainese cuisine. If you're in Chinatown, do give it a try!

Food is good but pricey for what it is, aka izakaya food which is supposed to be cheap.  I also found the menu to be a bit limited.  I understand there's not a whole lot of Japanese in this part of the city (K-Town), so ok you pay a premium for authentic Japanese.Overall experience reminded me a lot of Ootoya, set menus, large portions, authentic and decent but slightly generic food, excessive wait, a bit pricey.  Popular place so you may like it just fine, but just wasn't my cup of tea.

I recently dined at an impressive spot that's a haven for vegan cuisine lovers. The portions are generous, ensuring you get great value for every delectable mouthful. The food itself was seasoned to perfection, from the savory BBQ "riblets" to the satisfyingly tasty chopped "cheese" sandwich. The waitstaff added to the positive experience with their delightful and friendly service. However, the only drawback was that the dishes were served lukewarm rather than hot. Despite this, the flavors were so amazing that I'd still highly recommend a visit.

I recently discovered a fantastic spot for seafood thanks to Yelp, which came in handy when my cousin was craving seafood for her birthday. We decided to try something new, venturing away from our usual haunt, Claw Daddy, and thank goodness we did! This hidden gem really delivered on flavor.

While the appetizer plate left a bit to be desired—aside from the perfectly fried fries, which were a standout—the rest of the meal was excellent. The highlight for me was the crab legs; they were cooked to perfection and tasted divine.

Service-wise, our waiter could have been a touch more attentive. However, his charming English accent added a pleasant touch to our dining experience, somewhat compensating for any lack of attention.

Overall, this place has won my stamp of approval for a seafood feast. I'm already looking forward to my next visit!

Title: A Mixed Bag with a Worthwhile Ending

Despite needing to wait over an hour for our table despite a reservation, my dining experience at the restaurant turned out to be quite enjoyable, mostly thanks to our chef, Manuel. His pleasant demeanor and entertaining cooking skills made up for the initial inconvenience.

The delay from being seated to Manuel's arrival felt unnecessarily long, but once he began, the meal flowed seamlessly. The array of dishes, especially the steak and colossal shrimp accompanied by six other courses, was commendable. The Mai Tai I ordered was notably strong but enjoyable nonetheless.

For those considering a visit, my advice would be to avoid Saturdays – the chaos of the crowd detracts from the experience. However, the food and service do tempt me to return on a quieter day.

Title: Disappointing Visit to the Hyped Red Lobster

After being lured in by a celebrity-filled YouTube video and a craving for Red Lobster's iconic cheddar bay biscuits and strawberry lobsteritas, my friend and I decided to try our luck at the usually bustling location near the movie theater. The restaurant, surprisingly uncrowded, greeted us with a friendly hostess and a swift seating time of under ten minutes – a promising start that quickly took a downturn.

Our initial thirst left unquenched, as our server took an unusually long time to appear. When we finally placed our drink orders, confusion ensued; my iced tea was delayed, and the drinks brought to us didn't resemble the ordered lobsteritas – the server’s flustered response and hasty pivot to food orders did little to reassure us.

The food that followed was underwhelming: the much-anticipated biscuits arrived lukewarm, losing their usual comforting appeal. The lobster tacos were a letdown with off-tasting seafood and stale tortillas, and while the shrimp was passable, its accompanying broccoli had been overcooked to an unappetizing mush. Even though the incorrect margaritas were enjoyable, they were not what I had been eagerly anticipating.

In the end, most of our meal remained untouched, and we declined the offer for takeout boxes. A final note of caution to fellow diners: check your bill closely, as ours included an 18% gratuity – a common practice in Times Square eateries that could lead to unintended excessive tipping.

In summary, despite the celebrity hype and a promising start, this Red Lobster visit failed to deliver on the food and service fronts, leaving us with deflated expectations and a reminder to always peruse the receipt.

Tried to come here during my first NY visit about 2 years ago, only to find that it was closed. Now, I went back on my second-to-last day on my next trip, determined to finally try their giant xiao long bao (小籠包). Their giant XLB consists of crab and pork meat mixed together. Told it'd be a 20 min wait to prepare, which was fine by me, since I could just do some catch up work while waiting.When they brought out the Giant XLB, a straw was also served to the drink soup. The waitress told me to be careful because it's really hot. I admit, even with that warning, I ended up burning my tongue a bit, but that's how I know it's fresh! If anyone wants to know how much the Giant XLB weighed, I weighed it with the food scale I brought. With the basket, it weighed a total of 22.57oz, and when I finished the XLB, the basket on the plate weighed 10.90oz. The Giant XLB itself weighed 11.67oz.Really enjoyed this bit of a novelty!

A great new addition to the West Village. Anton's is Danny Meyer's veteran Nick Anders first independent project after working with Meyers on numerous Italian inspired spots. Anton's is still very much a work in progress, lots of great aspects but it's potential is much more. The food, drinks and wine were all good. The service was spotty. All could use some refinement, but one hopes and expects that they will get there and Anton's becomes a go to spot in the neighborhood.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at New York's first pizza joint, and it was an experience worth sharing. Don't let the petite size of the venue fool you; the ambiance is undeniably cozy and welcoming. The pizza exceeded my expectations with its mouthwatering flavor, ensuring that every bite was savored. The service complemented the meal perfectly; it was prompt, attentive, and genuinely friendly. I'm already looking forward to my next visit. A small tip for future patrons: remember it's a cash-only establishment.

Last week, my dining experience at Dukes was disappointing before it even started. Arriving around 6:35 PM, we were promptly informed that no tables were available. The reason, as the hostess indifferently explained, was the anticipation of a crowd for games scheduled much later in the evening, potentially not freeing up space until 11:45 PM. Despite visible empty tables, it appeared the restaurant prioritized game-watchers over walk-in customers. It wasn't just the lack of availability but also the dismissive service that struck a sour note. It seems Dukes has the luxury of turning away eager patrons. We left without even considering the bar, disheartened by the unwelcoming response.

Really cute place in the UES! Cozy dining area, delicious food, and attentive staff. The first time I came here, I made a reservation for 7:45pm on a Monday night and were seated immediately. The place had decent amount of people there. We were given menus and after ordering, received complimentary bread. I was quite delighted by my first visit and made a reservation for a party of 10+ a few weeks later. We had almost the entire upstairs to us, making for a very intimate gathering. The restaurant staff was attentive throughout our dinner. For dinner, I had the lamb chops ($30) good medium-rare; it was such a delightful meal and cooked perfectly. During my second visit I got the pre-fixe meal (as well as everyone in the party) which was such a great deal with appetizer, entree, and dessert for ~$28! I had the duck confit for my entree and the passion fruit ice cream for dessert. The prosciutto wrapped asparagus for appetizer. Everyone was very pleased - I heard that the salmon was tender and wonderfully cooked. Atmosphere is wonderful - I was able to have good conversation with my friend and in a big group setting. I definitely will be back here again. Gem of UES, I am delighted to say.

Been meaning to try the empanadas here for years, since my boyfriend moved to the area... no better time than today, weeks into self-quarantine and the fact that almost all of the other local businesses in the area have completely closed down. Plus, Allset offered $5 credit today (very generous), so we had to use them somewhere. Perfect excuse to finally check them out.We ordered 4 different empanadas between the 2 of us to share - BBQ Pulled Pork (corn flour), Ground Beef (oven baked), Desayuno Colombiano (wheat flour) and Shredded Chicken (corn flour). They were $3.99/each + tax, which is worth it if you're looking for a small snack/meal, and depending on which flavor you get. The shredded chicken was a bit too dry and its corn flour a bit too thick - wouldn't recommend/order again. The other 3, however, were bangers. BBQ Pulled Pork was probably our favorite - sweet & savory, perfect textures. Ground beef is a good classic (similar to a Jamaican beef patty) and the desayuno colombiano is obviously a solid breakfast item. Don't forget the green sauce - it's *chef's kiss*Only tiny hiccup is that we had originally ordered El Ruben empanada (oven baked) through the app and paid, but they told me they had ran out and replaced it with the Ground Beef instead when I went to pick up the order... Not too big of a deal, we were just a lil disappointed but guess we'll have to return one day to try it! Hoping this spot will remain open through these tough times.

As soon as you approach, the mouthwatering aroma of baking dough lures you in, hinting at the culinary delights that await at this gem of a pizzeria. True to its tantalizing promise, this might just be some of the best thin-crust pizza I've ever enjoyed. Masterfully balancing textures, it boasts a light and flaky crust with a surprisingly chewy center—a testament to the owner/chef's dedication to his craft. He shared that the secret lies in a meticulous three-day dough rising process, which is a compelling reason in itself to pay a visit. As if the pizza weren't enough of a draw, you're likely to be welcomed with the warmth and charm of the chef's wife, making the dining experience feel just like home. An absolute must-try!

Title: Hype Overload at the Local Pizzeria – A Mixed Experience

My evening at the highly-talked-about pizzeria left me with mixed feelings. Arriving at 8:30pm on a weekday, I was surprised to find a line still snaking out the door—a sure sign of popularity, or so I thought. As a fan of Joe's Pizza, however, the anticipation didn't quite pay off.

The thicker crust pizza isn't my usual preference, and that seems crucial at this spot. If you're a thin crust aficionado, you may want to reconsider the wait. My boyfriend, ever the optimist, overestimated our appetites with three hefty slices each. A word to the wise: these slices are a meal in themselves, so two would suffice for most.

On the upside, the pepperoni topping hit the mark—thick, flavorsome, and perfectly sized on their square slices. Sadly, the cheese didn't sing to me, and a scant tomato sauce left the pizza wanting.

Rating it at 3.5, the experience was average; the long wait and crust preference make it a discretionary choice for fellow diners. Joe's Pizza might still be my go-to for a quick, satisfying slice.

I returned to this gem of a restaurant to celebrate Lunar New Year and was delighted to indulge in their beef dishes once again, alongside the enchanting lychee hot cocktail, which stole my heart. However, the pinnacle of my craving, the beef Gyu Katsu set, had vanished from the menu, leaving me engulfed in disappointment. This dish, an exquisite blend of eggs, beef, and an irresistible sauce, was the very reason for my visit. I implore the management to reconsider its absence; its return would guarantee my patronage every week—such is the allure of this delectable cuisine.

I visited South Of The Clouds on Sunday evening around 7:30 pm. The restaurant was half full and we were seated immediately. Enjoyed my experience and the food. Ambiance: Very decent ambiance and gives a strong vibe about the Asian ethnicity of the place. Absolutely loved it!Recommendations:Little pot- Amazing noodles cooked in a very flavorful spicy chicken broth. Very delicious and opens up your tastebuds. Lovers of spicy food will absolutely appreciate the little pot. Tomato beef soup- Very spicy, flavorful and sour (in a pleasant way). If you like tomato based soupy noodles, this is the perfect option!

Where to start? This place has a great vibe, yummy food, and good drinks. I love coming here. It's a good spot for brunch, dinner, or just to grab drinks. The weekends bring in a nice crowd and the DJ is always good. Price wise, I think they are reasonable. Some of my fav food items to order are the guava BBQ wings, Mac n cheese, crab cake salad, and the braised oxtail with chicken. I've never had an issue with the food when I'm here. I would highly recommend.

I was here early for dinner so there was no wait. Only one table had people but by the time I left there were a few others. As per most other Singaporean/Malay places, I ordered a teh tahrik to drink. My main chosen was Char Kueh Teow, a noodle dish I commonly have at a lot of other spots. The waitress recommended either beef or shrimp and I went with the former. After a good while, she brought out a rather large bowl and my drink surprisingly with my order and she quickly left. The noodle dish while large (it should be for 20$) lacked the charred flavor you find in most other places. Even the egg was a bit off. I almost think they forgot to add the dark soy sauce. Some pieces of beef had some gristle as well. The spices were alright though I would have requested chili sauce but the waitress didn't show up again.The flavors of the teh tahrik were good but the drink was unsurprising lukewarm instead of hot. It was probably ready for a while but they brought it out with my main dish for some reason  I would excuse if the place was crowded but the place was quite empty. After finishing, I waited a good while for the check. The waitress oddly never asked whether I wanted dessert though that probably would have taken a good while also.This place was in many worse ways opposite of Laut Singapura; their sister restaurant. There the service was almost too talkative and the spices were nice and strong. Even the beef was nice and tender by comparison. I wouldn't have minded this so much if I wasn't paying so much but frankly I prefer the gruff service in Chinatown because at least they get stuff done and the flavors are right. Just go to Rasa or Nyona or their newer restaurant.1.8.

Swear I had a spiritual awakening in eating this Pho.WOW.Come hungry, no come RAVENOUS and order the classic Madame Pho with Short Rib. They give you an ungodly amount of meat- every meatball or morsel of beef and pork I still found left in my soup was more surprising than the next. The short rib does indeed, fall off the bone. I was balancing maybe four different utensils at once to take down this monster of a dish. Like really, for serious eaters only. Joking aside, the noodles are deliciously chewy and long, the broth just right in flavor, with plenty of mushrooms, scallions and onions, as well as basil/bean sprouts/jalapeños on the side. (Key to any great pho).Yeah...there's no doubt I'm coming back again. Felt lucky to grab seats at the bar right at 5:30 PM on a Sunday. Make sure you snag a reservation, or come early.

During a recent visit for a late lunch at this well-situated eatery, we sampled both the beef tartare and tuna tartare, complemented by an impromptu side of truffle fries. The tartares impressed with their complexity; the beef was flavorful, while the tuna's freshness was accentuated by a citrusy drizzle, crisp cucumber slivers, and a touch of sesame seeds, all of which created a well-balanced dish. Unfortunately, the truffle fries, although tasty, were disappointingly greasy. Despite the somewhat steep prices, the restaurant's prime location helps to mitigate the cost. Overall, a satisfactory dining experience with a few hiccups.

Another great Izakaya spot, similar to Udon West Midtown which we reviewed a few days ago.Highlights:- Open Late (4AM)- Best food prices (most items under $10)- Wide variety (endless ala carte options)- $1.50/glass for Asahi and Sapporo.  $8 pitchers.Lowlights:- Motsunabe is closer to a Dwaenjang Chige (Korean Miso Stew) than it is to a traditional Japanese nabe in terms of broth and ingredients.  We were disappointed to not know this prior to ordering.  Still a good dish, just inaccurate representation.- Very crowded if you dislike sitting shoulder to shoulder with other guests.- May be a wait time, as restaurant is overtly popular with the younger crowd.I'll briefly explain my thoughts on each dish we ordered.The Maguro Salad ($8) was a very uniquely prepared item.  It is reminiscent of Big City Diner's 'Ray Chan's Ultimate Poke' in Hawaii.  Slabs of maguro tuna over a bed of greens, dressed with a light sriracha and ponzu sauce.  Enough for 2-3 to share.The Ankimo ($7), or chilled monkfish liver, would be a close cousin to foie gras.  Not as fatty or difficult to stomach as its cousin.  Very flavorful with a savory profile, but not salty at all.  Topped with a dollop of tobiko flying fish roe and dressed in ponzu sauce.  Great as one of several appetizers for any table. Serves 1-4.The Karaage Chicken ($7) was as one would expect Japanese Fried Chicken to taste.  Meets all the stops an Izakaya goer expects: crunchy, served hot and fresh out of the deep fryer, signature mirin taste without being overpowering.  Single order serves 1-4.The Motsunabe ($29) was my most conflicted dish of the night.  I expected a Japanese style dashi broth but was not expecting a Korean miso stew.  Nothing else on the menu indicated that Kenka served Japanese-Korean fusion.  Still, the hot pot was prepared with fair portions of meat and veg, served on a tableside gas hot plate to keep warm throughout our meal.  If you are a fan of Korean soups like Dwaenjang Chige, Soondubu, or Kimchee Chige you will enjoy this selection.  Easily serves 3-6.  Comes as a large portioned item.Overall experience was fantastic.  Staff work as a team, service is speedy, and restaurant is clean.  Kenka sits on my toplist for late night, cheap alcohol Izakayas in Manhattan.

Title: Charming Village Gem with a Minor Service Glitch

Nestled in the West Village, Phillip Marie stands as a quaint and charming culinary delight. The ambiance of the location adds a touch of serenity to the dining experience. I was particularly enticed by the scallop appetizer, which, although small, packed a punch of flavor, perfectly accentuated by the chef's exquisite sauce.

The main courses maintained the high standard set by the starters, offering a seamless dining experience. However, the true star of the meal was the cheesecake—remarkably light and finely balanced in sweetness, it left a memorable impression.

While the food was nearly flawless, our service experience did waver. Our waiter, though friendly, had a knack for disappearing acts that led to some frustration. The need to request our check multiple times was a hiccup in an otherwise delightful meal.

Despite the service misstep, the sublime cheesecake—and indeed, the overall quality of the cuisine—persuades me to give Phillip Marie a strong recommendation. Consider this a four-star experience that narrowly misses a full five due to service alone.

Title: A Magical Thai Feast at Top Thai Vintage

My evening at Top Thai Vintage was an unforgettable foray into authentic Thai cuisine. Right from the entrance, the ambiance transported me to the heart of Thailand with vibrant tuk tuks, custom tiles, and colorful shutters, creating the perfect backdrop for a girl's night out.

The eatery was abuzz with a diverse crowd by 6:30 pm. Eric, the heart behind Top Thai, personally welcomed us with his infectious warmth, guiding us through the menu with expertise. Meanwhile, the bartender intrigued us with Thai beer and drink specials that didn't disappoint.

The culinary journey began with a dumpling platter that was swiftly devoured, alongside an appetizer platter featuring sublime fried calamari, curry puffs, and a delectable fried chicken concoction. Each dish spoke of the careful consideration for diners of all preferences, notably with a fully halal menu.

The star of the main course was the 3 Spices Red Snapper. It was a dish I insisted on, and it lived up to every expectation with its crispy exterior and tangy tamarind sauce. While I skipped the duck noodle dish, it earned high praise from my companions, with none left for the kitchen.

Regrettably, we skipped dessert, but this only means a return visit is necessary. Top Thai Vintage, thanks for a spectacular dining experience. Your meticulous attention to detail and sumptuous flavors have set a new standard for Thai dining in my book.

**Title: A Tsukemen Revelation in the Lower East Side**

**Rating: 5/5**

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this hidden gem in the Lower East Side, renowned for its exceptional tsukamen. My experience was nothing short of spectacular. Opting for the Tonkotsu Cha Siu Tsukamen, I was delighted by the generous portions of succulent cha siu in both the noodles and the dipping sauce – a true testament to their dedication to quality and flavor. 

My husband's choice, the equivalent ramen, did not disappoint either. He particularly enjoyed the option to add extra noodles with a hot stone, enhancing his meal's warmth and enjoyment. Both of us were impressed by the melt-in-your-mouth cha siu, the hallmark of their dishes.

The noodles were thick and had just the right bite, while the umami-rich broth, distinct with a hint of shoyu, set the tsukamen apart from its ramen counterpart. A special mention must be made of the egg – it was a marvel, marinated to perfection, with a creamy interior that spoke volumes of their meticulous preparation.

We couldn't resist trying the karaage, which was a crispy delight, tender on the inside and a perfect accompaniment to our main dishes. The vibe of the restaurant captured the essence of LES coolness, with good music and an inviting bar setting complementing the dining experience. The attentive and friendly service, punctuated by attentive water refills, was the cherry on top.

We are already planning our next visit, and I wholeheartedly recommend this place to anyone in search of the best tsukamen around.

I recently visited this restaurant for lunch and opted for their weekday Lunch Burger special at $8, to which I added bacon and smoked mozzarella for an extra $2.50. While the add-ons didn't significantly enhance the flavor—the smoked mozzarella, in particular, seemed to get lost in the mix—the burger itself was a standout. It was well-seasoned and utterly delicious as is. In my opinion, the standard burger is a solid choice without the need for extras. I'll certainly be returning to this spot for another satisfying meal.

I recently visited a fabulous spot that was brimming with energy and excitement, and I just have to share! The happy hour specials were absolutely incredible, offering great value that elevated the experience. The ambiance was brought to life with some fantastic music that set a vibrant tone for the night. The staff were a delight, contributing to the cheerful atmosphere with their pleasant demeanor. Oh, and let's talk about the food – the sliders I ordered were deliciously tasty, hitting all the right notes for a casual yet satisfying meal. All in all, it was SO MUCH FUN, and I can't wait to return!

The most amazing lunch I've had. This restaurant is also so so spacious and gorgeous. We came right at opening and were seated immediately even though we didn't have a reservation. My sister and I got the wokuni don and the sashimi. Both had similar fish but the wokuni had shrimp tempura and tamago. While the sashimi had uni and a generous bowl of rice on the side. Every piece of fish tasted so amazing. You can really taste the quality. There's also a private room in the back that's quite spacious as well.

Is there an option to give zero stars?I had a pickup scheduled today at Macbar with MealPal. When I arrived to pick up my meal, I was told they were out and had given away the last one for that slot so I would need to wait about 10 minutes.I asked if it was ok for me to run an errand and be back in around 10 to pick up instead of waiting there. They said that was fine.I came back afterwards and asked if my meal was ready and after a few minutes, they'd given that meal away to someone else, indicating a guy who just walked out door.They asked me to come back at a later time but that wasn't going to work for me. I asked if they didn't have another meal ready--after all, presumably you know how many people are coming to pick up lunch and at what time--but apparently they didn't.I asked if they had anything else ready to go? No. Cool. Welp, I wasn't going to hold my breath and wait for a meal that was messed up twice.So long Macbar, your incompetence is staggering.

Title: A Staple for Soontofu Lovers in K-Town

BCD Tofu House remains a top choice for authentic Korean cuisine in K-Town. Their soontofu is a standout dish, served piping hot with a hearty portion of rice and a variety of tasty side dishes. While the prices may be on the higher side, the quality and flavors justify the cost. Be prepared for a wait, especially on weekends, as this bustling spot is rarely without a queue. Opting for a weekday visit might save you some time. Despite the crowds, BCD Tofu House consistently delivers a satisfying culinary experience.

Ippudo never disappoints and is definitely my favorite ramen place in the city, despite the ~$18 cost! My only reservation about this place is that there is always a wait here, no matter if its for lunch or for dinner which makes it annoying since you can't call up in advance...I always go for the miso ramen here and add a soft-boiled egg, it's amazing! I enjoyed mixing in the miso paste together and the chashu pork was great. What missed the mark for me at this location were the pork buns - I didn't see the hype about the buns considering the pork was marinated in a thick, gelatinous bbq sauce. I would skip these and try anther appetizer like the kara age that comes with shishito peppers.

Very good deal and lots of food to share. Portions were bigger than I thought and my friends and I are stuffed. We had five people and did two sets (each set is recommended for two people) and added one extra starter.Most of the dishes are great and delicious. I loved all the mushroom dishes. Some were a bit on the plain side like the yu choy. Thought they would do something different with it than a regular Chinese restaurant but it was pretty similar. It was not packed at all surprisingly when we went. Lots of empty tables.

Delicious Thai food and friendly staff. The restaurant is small and the tables are very close to one another. It starts getting crowded around 6pm, even on a weeknight, and can get loud especially during happy hour. I would recommend setting up a reservation. I had the kua gai noodle which is broad flat noodle with squid and chicken. It was delicious and tastes a bit like pad see ew. It comes with a tangy sauce which was also very good. My friend has the beef thin noodle soup which he said was very good and filling. Yelp has a $1 tea iced tea offer for checking in. It was good, but I wouldn't pay full price for it since the glass was rather small and had a lot of ice. I believe the normal priced tea is larger. Pay with cash and get 10% off.

Title: A Hip Vegan Spot Near Radio City

I recently dined at by Chloe before catching a show at Radio City and was pleasantly surprised by the experience. Arriving at 6pm, my group of four found ample seating in the trendy and clean interior, although the single bathroom did lead to a bit of a wait.

The entirely vegan menu impressed us, especially the quinoa taco salad with convincingly delicious chorizo – though a tip for fellow diners would be to request extra dressing. The Thai salad also received praise from my companions. The burger, while average and lacking accompaniments like fries, fell apart easily and the Mac n' cheese was noted to be underseasoned.

Salads are the standout here, offering both substance and satisfaction. We all enjoyed the kale artichoke dip we shared, which made for a tasty communal starter. Service was exceptional, as the staff were attentive, helped us with cleaning up, and kindly took a group photo for us. If you find yourself in the area and in need of a quick, friendly, and vegan option, by Chloe is a solid choice. Just make sure to lean towards the salads for a more fulfilling meal.

Title: Unbeatable Sashimi Value in the Heart of NYC

I recently had the pleasure of dining at what I now consider the pinnacle of sushi/sashimi value in NYC. Despite its high-end status, the restaurant offers reasonably priced delights, particularly their sensational sashi bowls. I opted for the coveted wokuni set, a favorite among patrons – and for good reason. Be warned, though; they offer a limited number of sets daily, so arrive early to avoid disappointment.

What sets this place apart is the fish, sourced directly from Japan, ensuring unparalleled freshness with every bite. I'm a tough customer, usually only enjoying salmon sashimi, but they graciously accommodated my request to swap out other fish without additional costs, a rarity in my experience.

The service was impeccable, and the ambiance matched the quality of the food, though the "club" music seemed out of step with the otherwise sophisticated atmosphere. This is a minor quibble in what was an exquisite dining experience. I'm already planning my next visit!

I recently dined at an exquisite Chinese restaurant that captivated my senses and tugged at a nostalgic string. While the menu leans towards the expensive, every dish served is a testament to its value, meticulously prepared and bursting with authentic flavors. The elegant chinaware adds a personal touch that harkens back to cherished memories of family meals in a beloved San Diego eatery during my childhood. Additionally, the BYO-Wine option is a delightful bonus, allowing patrons to pair their favorite vintages with the rich cuisine. In conclusion, this establishment is a true gem for those who appreciate the finer nuances of Chinese dining.

I had an amazing experience at this eatery where a mere $4.50 gets you a beautifully crafted falafel sandwich. Despite a bustling atmosphere, the line was swift and the food was served promptly. I highly recommend this place for a quick, delicious, and affordable meal.

Title: A Flavorful Fiesta at Taco Haven!

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this gem of a restaurant, renowned for its diverse taco menu. Each taco is bursting with bold spices and flavors, yet they're perfectly balanced so that even someone like me, who typically shies away from spicy foods, found the kick enjoyable and manageable.

The joy of sharing a variety of tacos with friends added to the experience, allowing us to savor a little bit of everything. Impressively, the service was swift, which meant we weren't left waiting to indulge in our delicious choices.

The ambiance of the restaurant is the cherry on top, providing a chill and relaxed environment that's just right for a laid-back meal. I'd wholeheartedly recommend a visit for anyone looking to enjoy a great meal in a great atmosphere.

Incredible experience at this gem of a restaurant! The starters set the stage, but the mains truly steal the spotlight. The Toasted Rye Cavatelli and Fried Chicken are culinary masterpieces not to be missed—unbelievably delicious with every fresh, savory bite. Their curated wine list complements the meal perfectly, and the desserts provide a solid, satisfying finale. An evening here promises no disappointments, just pure gastronomic delight.

On February 13th, our group of eight visited this lively eatery and our experience was mostly delightful. Tucked away in the backroom, we had an absolute blast, cocooned in our own little world. The cobb salad was a standout dish - enormous in size and evidently the best I've savored in recent memory. Sports enthusiasts would appreciate the array of screens featuring various sports channels, adding to the vibrant atmosphere. However, the music volume was quite overbearing, infringing upon our conversations. If not for the need to shout over the loud tunes, our dining experience would have been near perfect.

After walking back and forth in the mobbed marked, we settled on this eatery randomly (by looking at the reasonable lines).It was busy during a Friday lunch hour, but not so badly that there weren't any seats. The wife and I found a spot at the bar next to the dishwasher window. Steam was coming out of it, but it was atmospheric.They have this gimmicky dish, the baked whole cauliflower, that was extremely and surprisingly good. We are going to replicate it when cauliflower is in season!The kebabs/pita sandwiches were fine. Nothing in particular stood out, nor was it anything offensive. Overall, it is a good place to have a meal while in the market. I gave it 3 stars because the value proposition is not good. $10 for a baked cauliflower? You do the math. The pitas were pricey too for the portions and type of meat. I know this is NY, but still.Shout out to the attendant behind the bar; he was very helpful with our additional order of the cauliflower; he took our order instead of having to line up at the cashier again.

Title: Delightful Dining with Minor Hiccups at [Restaurant Name]

My dinner experience at [Restaurant Name] with my boyfriend was certainly a memorable one. The standout for me was their cold soba with mushrooms and grated radish, which showcased the bouncy, chewy texture of their house-made noodles. The chirashi set was an impressive array, boasting nearly 20 pieces of sushi, creating a sense of great value. Although the octopus was a bit on the tougher side, the rest of the sushi did not disappoint.

A slight mishap occurred when we were uninformed of the unavailability of uni until overhearing a conversation between staff and another table. After inquiring, the waiter did attempt to remedy the oversight with complimentary ice cream, which, despite the kind gesture, fell short in compensating for the mishap, especially considering the price/value disparity. Additionally, the black sesame ice cream proved too sweet for us.

For those seeking a warm beverage, do note that the restaurant offers complimentary hot tea upon request—a detail my boyfriend particularly appreciated on his solo return visit a few days later.

Contrary to other reviews, our experience with the service was more than satisfactory, as the staff conducted themselves with considerable courtesy.

All in all, despite a couple of setbacks, [Restaurant Name] provided us with a culinary experience that was both enjoyable and worth recounting.

Title: Lively Vibe with Mixed Culinary Hits and Misses

Review:

Nestled in the bustling heart of the city, this snug and vivacious eatery presents an ambience that nearly hits perfection at 4.5 out of 5; the lively energy is palpable without being overwhelming, particularly in the comfort of the back booths. Our arrival, slightly tardy, was met with understanding as our table awaited us, a testament to the accommodating service rated 4 out of 5.

The front bar can feel crowded, but the swift and attentive drink service ensures your glass is never empty for long. Now, onto the culinary journey: the Big Eye Tuna Saisi and Jumbo Lump Crab Beignets were the stars of the night, scoring a 4/5 and a perfect 5/5 respectively. The Halibut, expertly cooked with a delicate texture, fell short on flavor, earning a 3.5/5. Disappointment emerged with the switch from Tagliatelle to Penne in our shrimp pasta, leaving a fishy taste lingering for a 2/5 rating. The Steak au Poivre divided the table with its heavy peppercorn crust; it earns a middling 3/5 as some found it enjoyable while others, myself included, noted the lack of tenderness. The Brussels Sprouts gained a solid 4/5, rounding out the meal pleasantly.

In summary, while the food had its ups and downs, the draw of the spirited atmosphere and the promise of a potentially great burger have me willing to return.

Title: A Warm Birthday Celebration Despite the Bustle

My recent dining experience at this local Mexican eatery was a delightful rush. Despite our time crunch and the restaurant's packed setting, the hostess's welcoming demeanor and efficiency were commendable. She managed to seat us promptly, ensuring we didn't miss our subsequent show.

The restaurant's ambiance struck a balance between energetic and cozy, with warm lighting that complemented the familiar, yet perhaps clichéd, Mexican décor. While portion sizes erred on the smaller side, the quality of the food compensated. The shared fruit salad plate with honey and ricotta was a hit, creating a fresh and delectable start to our meal. Tacos brimming with flavor and a particularly memorable margarita added to the satisfying culinary experience.

A highlight came at the end of our meal when the staff, having taken note of the birthday occasions, presented the guests of honor with complimentary ice cream complete with birthday candles. This thoughtful gesture imbued our dinner with a personal touch that was both surprising and heartwarming.

Although prices veered towards the high side, the overall experience at this establishment was overwhelmingly positive. It's a place I'd recommend for those special occasions when the little extras truly count.

Title: A Mix of Highs and Lows at a Michelin-Starred Spot

My recent visit to this Michelin-starred restaurant delivered a truffle pasta that easily ranks among the best I've experienced. The dish was a sensory delight, notably with the live truffle grating, which lent an air of culinary theater to the meal. The pasta itself was cooked to perfection, maintaining the ideal balance between firmness and tenderness, and the sauce was rich with flavor without tipping into excess saltiness.

However, the visit was marred by several minor setbacks. Despite assurances of walk-in friendliness, we were initially quoted a wait time of 45 minutes to an hour - a surprising disconnect from my pre-visit research. This was quickly followed by a premature notice that our table was ready, leading to a rushed and unnecessary expenditure at a nearby coffee shop.

Upon return, we were seated at the bar, which would not have been an issue if it weren't for the overpowering fishy smell wafting from the raw dishes - a smell intense enough to detract from the overall ambiance. Additionally, a minor spill accident involving our server and my personal belongings went unacknowledged, which, while not disastrous, certainly detracted from the service experience.

The meal itself was mostly commendable. While the truffle pasta stood out, my husband's ssam bop was satisfying, balanced by the punchy saltiness of the accompanying kim. A pleasant surprise was the lemonade - a bottled variety from the UK that provided a refreshing and floral counterpoint to the meal's richness. It was a highlight that I wouldn't hesitate to recommend.

Despite the negatives, the strength of the culinary offerings makes a return visit tempting, especially to try the ramen. An advisory note for fellow diners: the restaurant has a single unisex bathroom, a quirk that's not uncommon in New York establishments. With adjusted expectations and a bit of planning, one can still look forward to a meal that showcases why this place has earned its culinary accolades.

Title: A Flavor Explosion at Booing Ramen!

If you’re on the hunt for top-tier ramen, look no further than Booing Ramen, nestled on the 3rd floor of the Time Warner Center, just past Bouchon. My taste buds were in heaven with the Spicy Beef Ramen, which packed a punch while showcasing the undeniable quality of fresh ingredients. The Chicken Garlic Ramen was equally impressive, offering a fragrant and flavorful experience.

But the star of the show? The Shrimp Stick Bun. Imagine a crispy piece of perfectly battered shrimp enveloped in a cloud-like stick bun, accompanied by a zesty spicy mayo. This dish was nothing short of bombastic!

Adding to the ambiance, their roaring specials menu displayed behind the bar captivates and engages you the moment you settle in. In short, Booing Ramen is totally worth a visit for anyone craving an undeniable explosion of flavors.

I recently dined at this charming midtown eatery for breakfast and can confidently say it's a great spot for both breakfast and lunch. The spacious interior allows for comfortable dining and they conveniently accept reservations. Prices are quite reasonable, especially considering its central location.

The service was prompt and friendly, contributing to a pleasant dining experience. When it comes to the food, their French staples are of decent quality. I highly recommend the Crepe Nutella, which was absolutely wonderful – a true highlight of the meal.

However, I'd suggest passing on the Endives Salad, as it failed to impress and was rather unremarkable. Overall, this restaurant holds its own with good service and tasty French fare, making it worth a visit.

Title: Seamless Gem for Noodle Enthusiasts

My latest go-to spot for delivery on Seamless has to be this exceptional noodle haven. With a solid 4.5 out of 5 rating for their food, they've managed to make each meal a hit, not only for me but for the many friends I've introduced to their menu through large orders. No complaints have surfaced - a testament to their consistent quality.
