The Khao Soi Ramen is a personal favorite, even stacking up impressively against some of the city's best. The Tonkotsu and Miso Ramens also stand out with their perfect balance of flavor and affordability, each priced comfortably between $13 and $16.

Their noodles are sublime, and the broths are rich and savory without tipping the scales towards overly salty. Another star on their menu is the crispy chicken – it's always cooked to perfection and satisfyingly light.

What elevates my experience further is their attention to detail with delivery orders. Everything from individual labels to accommodating special requests, like swapping pork belly with chicken in my ramen, is handled with care. Their punctuality and thoughtful packaging, ensuring enough utensils for everyone, make the experience seamless.

In summary: Phenomenal food, seamless delivery, and all at a great price point. Highly recommended and will definitely continue to order from here.

On a bustling Friday morning before work, I swung by Two Tablespoons for a quick breakfast pickup. The staff handled my order with remarkable professionalism and speed. I opted for their distinctive breakfast sandwich featuring eggs, pesto, sweet potato, and a refreshing kale/cabbage salad. Presentation-wise, it was a feast for the eyes, and the taste did not disappoint. It was an extraordinary rendition of a breakfast staple and stood out from any other I’ve encountered in the city. For anyone in search of a healthy, satisfying morning meal, Two Tablespoons is an essential stop. Highly recommended!

Convivial Italian spot with super accomodating service that falls somewhere between old school and new school. A longtime hotspot with two rooms and mostly four top tables that are separate like old school type joints. This staff will literally move tables for you or hang up your coat or store your umbrella. It's like that. It's a great date spot and despite some reviews these guys know how to run a restauarant- they've been here a long time.Food:Spicy olivesCrusty breadAntipastiSalmone in mustard sauceChicken with sweet sausage Tiramisu Food here tastes good and feels authentically Italian, the vegetable antipasti is great to share and they always have a good Cornish hen and my salmon was generous and haricot vert perfectly cooked. If you want to eat well and be treated well, not like some spots this is the spot!

Tucked away in Harlem, this charming Thai spot has quickly won over my colleagues and, as of my recent visit, myself. The decor strikes a delightful note with its super cute aesthetic and the live plants on each table add a touch of warmth and natural vibrancy. 

Upon entry, the tantalizing aroma from the kitchen had me indecisive with a diverse menu tempting my palate. Although I only sampled the spring rolls on this occasion—which were, by the way, perfectly crisp and flavorful—I noted the lunch and happy hour specials along with the invitingly fresh salads.

Service was nothing short of friendly, contributing to an overall welcoming experience. I'm eager to return soon for a deeper dive into their offerings.

Nestled in the bustling Chelsea Market, this charming bakery greets you with an irresistible aroma of fresh baked goods as you step through its doors. With the convenience of both indoor and outdoor seating, it's a perfect spot for any weather.

My visit was a delightful experience, highlighted by a decadent mocha cappuccino paired with a selection of their offerings. The cheese straw stood out—crispy, fluffy, and full of flavor. It's a must-try for any patron. The egg benedicts, a staple for a hearty brunch, did not disappoint; each bite was as tasty as the next.

The chocolate pudding, while adequate, didn't match the high bar set by the other items. Nonetheless, I would still highly recommend this bakery for anyone looking to indulge in a weekend brunch in NYC. The standout dishes and the warm coffee are more than enough reason to pay this spot a visit.

Title: A Love Affair with Flavor at Las Lap

If Las Lap keeps this up, I might just have to move in! The moment you enter, a wave of warmth greets you, reminiscent of those Sunday dinners at grandma's. The service is top-notch - with a hostess and server so welcoming you'll feel right at home.

Let's talk about the real star here: the jerk chicken spring rolls. They're the kind of delight that warrants a 'hands-off' alert around the table; so good, you'd guard them with your life. Ordering a second serving was non-negotiable. And the sauce? Let's just say I wouldn't be surprised if a chef named Roy is the secret weapon in the kitchen.

Even the drinks hint at a mastery that makes choosing just one a feat. And while I'm hesitant to share this gem of a spot, fearing the inevitable change that fame might bring, it's a find too good not to celebrate.

In short, Las Lap is a must-visit. I know I'll be back - probably sooner than my waistline would like.

Some actual Chinese BBQ in Manhattan!I got two chicken, two lamb and one mushroom. I like the chicken and the mushroom but was not a fan of the lamb - not very fresh so it got that special taste of lamb, which I don't enjoy.The way they cook is traditional. The seasoning they used was right. The food was a little burned on the outside but they cut those parts off before handing the food over(wrapped in alumni foil if you ordered a bunch). Price is cheap, and no seat.Overall a nice surprise.

If you love Thai food and are also an indecisive eater, Taladwat's gotchu.  Think of them as your stand-in Thai grandma; she's always got something cooking even though her fridge is already packed with delicious dishes she's already made.  Help yourself to anything and everything because, you know, she's gotchu.Just like at Grandma's house, just show up because they don't take reservations.  We arrived around 7pm and were told it would be 20 mins.  Worth it.  We were seated at one of the long, communal picnic tables.  These tables were annoying because anytime your neighbor would shift or move, the bench beneath you would move along with him/her.  But I guess that's part of the charm.We started with the Thai Omelette, which, for something made only of eggs and herbs is surprisingly flavorful.  For our entrees, we ordered from the Pick N Mix menu (2 half-portion entrees for $22).  We had the Panang Curry Beef, Crabmeat Tom Turmeric, 5-Spice Pork Belly, and the Ginger Braised Short Rib.  The Pick N Mix also comes with a basket of lettuce and your choice of Jasmine or red rice, so we got one of each.  Everything was so, so tasty. And just like at Grandma's, you'll leave feeling full, happy, and with leftovers.

I celebrated a friend's birthday at this charming restaurant, which boasts adorable decor perfect for photo ops. Opting for the lamb kebab, I was treated to a generous skewer of meat paired with vegetables and a side of pita-like bread. Though it appeared simple, the dish was remarkably satisfying, and the accompanying sauce complemented it perfectly, creating a delightful, deconstructed Mediterranean sandwich experience. Highly recommended for both the food and the atmosphere.

Visited this Little Italy restaurant over the weekend. The standout was definitely the Shanghai soup dumplings, with their delicate skin and generous broth, rivaling those found in Chinatown. Disappointingly, the rest of the meal didn't measure up. The Shanghai stir-fried rice cake was drenched in oil, the scallion pancake suffered a similar greasy fate, and the wine chicken had an interesting flavor but was undercooked to the point of bloodiness at the bones. With better culinary experiences just blocks away, a return visit seems unlikely—the heavy-handed oil and inconsistent seasoning marred the dining experience.

I might have to make an exception to my general dislike of tapas-style eating after all because Atoboy was bomb. $46 for three dishes. If you come in a big group, you could probably hit the whole menu which is mostly Korean but with some interesting twist or flair. What I liked about the menu is that it definitely has something for everyone - veggies, fish, egg, meat. You can customize it to whatever you're in the mood for. Everything we ordered was delicious. If I had to choose, my favorites were the sunchoke with mushrooms (first time eating this), the radicchio with burrata and pecans, the yellowtail, and the galbi. They also give you two kind of kimchi (some kind of green pepper and eggplant), as well as house-made seaweed chips (which were amazing and should be sold in stores). The portions might seem on the small side but we actually felt pretty satisfied once we were done eating. They have some a la carte items (like fried chicken with spicy peanut butter) and they'll also offer a refill of your rice bowl. My one very small ding is the ginger/grapefruit/soju drink I ordered. For $14, it somehow managed to taste both watered-down with zero trace of ginger or grapefruit on the first sip while finishing with a very powerful punch of soju. So, in other words, a giant shot of soju. Definitely make a reservation especially on Fri-Sat nights, place was hopping.

Atmosphere: 4/5 Food: 3.5/5Atmosphere: This is a beautiful NY restaurant that is bigger than it initially appears. The vibe is classy but also fun, with a mix of residents that are getting off work to tourists that are in awe. The spacing between each table was less than I'd like but seems to be standard for NY. Food: They start you off with a variety of breads that tasted freshly baked. The clam chowder was very yummy for starters. The Surf and Turf wasn't as good as I'd expect for the price. The steak had no flavor and the lobster was chewy and over cooked. My dad like the Branzino but he too expected more. Finally the lemon drop was extremely too strong for my first drink, but I'm sure others might not mind that!

I ordered French toast for my breakfast. I tried this place for the first time. Toast came just warm and they didn't delivered exactly what I ordered. I requested them to extra jam and I payed extra $3 for that but they didn't give me any of extra jam what I payed extra for. I was a bit annoyed and didn't contact them to ask for delivery my extra jam or refund money. I just choose wrong place for my French toast. I wouldn't never try order this place again. They said give me fruit salad but they only gave me slice of orange. Not same anything's. Toast tasted ok and Bread was little bun. Orange tasted not fresh too. I only ate one of them and I had to throw that out at the garbage. I am not sure I wrote review about this place with only once delivered experience but I ordered a lot of foods for delivery before, and I thought I could get to know about they service or foods.

Restaurant Review:

Absolutely worth the hype! Pro tip: Book your table online to cut down on the wait. Don't miss out on the off-menu delights like the rich and savory pork buns with perfectly tender meat wrapped in impeccably steamed buns, complemented by the crunch of fresh cucumber. And while the spicy rice cakes are a flavor bomb, they pack a serious punch - hot enough to keep your water glass in constant use.

We managed to snag seats a bit ahead of our 9:15 reservation - the staff was accommodating despite our early arrival. Opting to share, we indulged in the sizzling flat iron steak. It arrived pink and succulent, cooking gradually on the hot plate. Paired with a velvety sauce and delicate enoki mushrooms, it was an unforgettable dish, though the decorative leaves on top may be better left untouched.

In short: Highly recommend booking a table and trying the pork buns, rice cakes (if you can handle the heat), and the sizzling flat iron. Definitely a dining experience to remember!

I happened across this nice, quaint, tasteful Italian restaurant in Grammercy. They had so many specials which all sounded great, but I ordered the Gramigna alla Carbonara and the Vitello alla Milanese listed on the menu. I was not familiar with gramigna pasta. It's like bucatini but thicker. The carbonara sauce was rich and creamy. One minor nit is that the bacon was a bit dry. Overall, I enjoyed this dish. The veal was cooked nicely, crispy and tender, but I felt it was underseasoned. It also came with leafy greens and chopped tomatoes on top, which I wasn't expecting. In the end, Novita has pretty good food in a classy setting.

I had decided to give Patrick's a try one afternoon and was very happy with my choice. I walked in and was seated immediately to one of the high top tables facing the street. it is a large venue with seating at the bar as well as multiple options for table seating. There are multiple food options-salad, burgers, a raw bar, etc. I waited a while until the server arrived but had already made my choices. i decided on a cheeseburger, medium well which arrived with lettuce, tomato and onion and was delicious! I also ordered a small side salad but which arrived in a bowl that was too small to accommodate the salad, making it difficult to eat. A bigger bowl would be more appropriate. The server, Milot was attentive and had stopped by to see if I needed anything from time to time. Some may feel it is a little pricey but it is not for midtown.  it was an excellent meal and i would recommend and return

Title: A Soup Dumpling Delight in the Heart of the City

I recently visited this unassuming spot on a quest to satisfy my soup dumpling cravings, and it did not disappoint. Service was notably swift, which was a pleasure, especially since I arrived during a quieter time. The space is compact and efficiently arranged to accommodate as many diners as possible without feeling cramped.

Don't expect to be wowed by the decor; it's pretty basic with a no-frills vibe that caters more to diners seeking a brisk meal rather than a lingering dining experience. The simplicity of the setting, however, took nothing away from the star of the show - the soup dumplings.

These little pockets of joy were spot-on in both size and flavor, and the pricing felt just right. While the place might not be the go-to for ambiance seekers, it's definitely a gem for those in pursuit of delicious bites. I'm already planning a return visit to indulge in the dumplings again and, perhaps, to explore more of the menu with friends. If you're in the area and in need of a quick, tasty meal, this is your spot.

AMAZING! Can't rave about this place enough!Wonderful customer service (Amy you're the best server ever!) and good food; it'll feel like your grandma cooked you home cooked food. The decor is beautiful and the plating is superb. They serve the lunch special 7 days a week...you heard me right: SEVEN DAYS A WEEK!! The prices range from 9.95 to 13.95 (might be higher for some dishes) depending on the protein you get. It includes an appetizer and an entree. With the lunch special, you can get thai iced tea, thai iced coffee, and other heavenly sweet drinks for only $1! A DOLLAR! And the serving size is perfect for one person. I honestly have nothing bad to say except maybe you'd be doing a great disservice to yourself if you don't come here! My new favorite thai spot

Title: A Mediterranean Delight at Savann

As a Mediterranean cuisine enthusiast, Savann caught my eye on UberEats during my post-study hunger pangs. I opted for the chicken kebab, which was paired with rice, red cabbage, and onions, plus a side of naan. The delivery was prompt, under 30 minutes, and I received my food warm and clearly prepared with care.

Each bite was flavorful, authentic, and left me feeling satisfied without being heavy. The portions were generous enough to provide two meals, a pleasant surprise. Savann nailed my order, ensuring that when the Mediterranean cravings strike again, they'll be my go-to spot.

Title: A Delightful Korean Feast

My sister and I chanced upon this Korean gem during a recent venture and were promptly seated despite a bustling dining room. The complementary side dishes set a welcoming tone with tasty offerings like kimchi and miso soup. The highlight, an assorted BBQ meat platter, did not disappoint, with the chicken and bulgogi outshining an already stellar lineup.

Accompaniments like scallion pancakes and dumplings further elevated the meal. The service was attentive without being intrusive, ensuring a seamless dining experience. This place won us over, and we're both eager to return for another round of Korean culinary delights.

In the shadow of the Manhattan Bridge, in the Two Bridges nabe on an unassuming side street, is this tiny pizza place with maybe 4 stools. So it may be better to take out if you are going to order more than a slice. Friendly prompt service greets you. Reasonable prices, to boot, especially considering you are in Manhattan, after all. I had the meatball parm hero, that was over a foot long! Mangia!I will return someday for pizza.

I wouldn't give this plaCe any star for the food or ever visIt this place again. One of my colleague loves this place so I decided to give it a try again as the last time I had visited was like 4 years ago. However I do remember not liking the food then so I was kind of expecting it. We were a party of 3 and they have a lunch buffet or you can order from the ala carte menu. I ordered rava masala dosa which came highly recommended to me from the manager. My colleagues ordered the thali which was horrible.The dosa took a lil longer to come as they had to make it and serve. I thought the wait would be worth it but it was not great. The masala which came with it was not good, also the sambhar tasted horrible. The only saving grace to my dosa was the white chutney with which I could eat half of it atleast. Never coming back again.

I recently dined at a local restaurant as part of a team offsite event, which allowed us a rare opportunity: the freedom to explore the menu without concern for cost. We indulged in a variety of dishes, including an array of shrimp preparations, a whole fried fish, garlic and Hainanese chicken, duck, numerous desserts, and several types of roti.

The meal was enjoyable, thanks largely to the vast selection and the fact that it was on the house. Among the plethora of tastes, the garlic chicken—with its tender meat and perfectly balanced flavor—was a standout dish, as was the coconut pudding, which ended the meal on a high note.

However, I must be candid in my review. While the food was good, it wasn't exceptional across the board. The standout dishes were memorable, but others faded into the background. Also, considering the hefty price tags coupled with a cash-only policy, I would have had some reservations about the value for money had I been paying.

In summary, while the experience was made better by the lack of a bill, if I were to rate the restaurant based on its full prices, the overall impression would be that of a satisfactory meal with a few highlights, but perhaps not one that would pull me back eagerly for a second round.

Title: Cozy Spot for Chicken & Waffles - Sweet Chick

Rating: 3.5 Stars

Having recently transplanted from California to New York, Sweet Chick was a welcome discovery just around the corner from my new residence. Yelp led me here for a Tuesday lunch, and I was pleased to find no wait – a stark contrast to the bustling weekend brunch lines I've noticed.

As a connoisseur of chicken and waffles, I hold high standards for this sweet and savory delight. I opted for the chicken paired with bacon and cheddar waffles. The chicken, while perfectly fried, fell short on flavor. However, the waffles were spectacular – fluffy, loaded with hearty bacon pieces, and utterly satisfying.

Service was a bit lackluster; flagging down a server was necessary. Still, the interior exuded a relaxed vibe that’s hard not to enjoy. While Sweet Chick may not see me queuing for brunch, it’s certainly on my radar for those chicken and waffle cravings.

Title: A Mixed Bag of Flavors at Local Eatery

I recently dined at this establishment and had a chance to sample a variety of dishes. The highlight for me was the tuna ceviche; the sauce accompanying the fish was delightful, although a finer chop on the fish would have been preferable. Unfortunately, the chicken tostadas didn't hit the same high note - the chicken was on the dry side and in dire need of a flavorful sauce to liven it up. It's a dish I'd suggest skipping.

On a brighter note, the quesadilla boasted impressive size, resembling a thin-crust pizza more than a traditional quesadilla. While tasty, the execution could be improved with better-melted cheese. However, the yucca fries were a table favorite - perfectly crispy on the outside and wonderfully fluffy within.

To round off the meal, the molten chocolate cake was sinfully good, though the ice cream's flavor (perhaps cinnamon) wasn't to my liking. All in all, the experience had its ups and downs, but certain dishes like the tuna ceviche and yucca fries would definitely lure me back for another visit.

This was excellent. We had talked about going here for years, and finally got around to it. We got the charred Japanese eggplant, petit salad, and west coast oysters to start. We enjoyed all three, but the oysters really stood out -- if they weren't the best oysters I've ever eaten, they're definitely on a very short list. That was followed by the spaghetti neri and the burger. I really liked the spaghetti -- I'm a sucker for squid ink, and the octopus was excellent. The burger is the thing we'll be coming back for, though -- there are lots of great burgers in New York, so it's hard to say this is one of the very very best, but it was still amazing. We finished with three desserts -- the apple tart (special), the dark chocolate, and the ice cream sandwich. Of those three the latter two are the ones I was excited about, but the apple tart was what I'll remember. This was probably the best apple pie I've ever eaten.I will say -- I don't really put that much weight on service, but it was very slow. Our three courses took almost three hours, all in. That said, we had two babies with us and they were incredibly accommodating about that.

Gotta support my mans Eddie Huang! I'm a huge fan of his - love and respect his writing, loud/hilarious opinions, food, brand, content, etc. - so my review may be a LIL bias but hear me out.As a fan, I've attended a couple of his free, public speaking events here in NYC. One at Macy's for APAHM and the other at the Google Hardware Store pop-up. Hearing him drop wisdom is always a treat. The icing on the cake at these events, however, was that they were catered by his very own BaoHaus. How dope! I'm sure he didn't have to do that, but he hooked us up and I still SO appreciate that. It truly elevated the overall experiences. I've had the Chairman (classic pork belly gua bao), Birdhaus (fried chicken) and Uncle Jesse (tofu) baos, minced pork stew on rice, Ten Ren teas and AiYu jelly lemonade - all on the 8th floor, Home Dept of Macy's and/or the Google popup in Soho last year. Of course free food is always more delicious, but... that doesn't take away from the fact that everything really is so good. This is food that accurately represents us as first generation Asian Americans.In between these fun events throughout the past couple years, I've dropped by the actual restaurant a few times to happily pay for anything and everything. Unfortunately one time they were closed temporarily to prepare for a catering event (ironic!) and another time we came by around midnight on Saturday to find that they only had tofu left. But there were a couple of more successful ventures, where I picked up the Manager's Meal (~$14) and taro fries (~$4.50). Can be a bit pricey but the Manager's Meal is 100% worth it. It comes with a HUGE slab of pork belly, minced pork AND fried chicken - 3 proteins and veggies over rice! Again, an Asian American version of the classic Taiwanese bento box which I can get behind. Super filling and yummy. I always recommend Baohaus to friends and I have to come back soon to try the fish bao... getting so hungry thinking about it all.

Found this gem near our hotel and went every day of our NYC strip! My 10 yr old nephew is a very picky eater and convinced himself that he only could eat chocolate chip pancakes on this trip. Turns out, this place has 'the best chocolate chip pancakes I've ever had!'Great breakfast, fast and friendly service. New York typical prices. We were seated almost immediately every time.

Gato is a great spot for NYE dinner in NYC! My husband and I have wanted to come to Gato for quite some time just due to the fact that all of my friends at work have raved about how good the place is. So we decided to make a reservation for New Year's Eve and boy we were not disappointed.We started our meal with a few cocktails which were great! For an appetizer we had the burrata and the scrambled eggs. The burrata was definitely good with the little flakes of garlic shavings all over; however, the show stopper was the scrambled eggs for sure! The confit toast that the eggs are served with was delightful, while the eggs are so full of flavor and the boucheron cheese really pulls the whole dish together. For our main dishes I had the kale and wild mushroom paella, while my husband had the rabbit. The paella was cooked to perfection and the server mixes the dish for you right at your table which is super fun to watch! My husband said that the rabbit was fantastic and that he would definitely recommend anyone dining at Gato to try the dish.We also had a side of the crispy potatoes which were awesome and very crispy; the poached egg was cooked perfectly and we literally consumed the dish in a matter of minutes!I cannot say enough about Gato and definitely plan on returning in the near future.Gato - I really appreciate the hospitality and amazing dinner. I could not think of a better way to spend NYE!

Title: A Delightful Find for a Quick Lunch in Chelsea

I stumbled upon a charming gem during a casual stroll and decided to stop by for a quick lunch. It turned out to be a delightful decision. The interior exuded warmth with its pristine cleanliness and the vibrant masks adorning the walls caught my eye instantly.

The lunch menu presented a plethora of choices and, after some helpful guidance from the friendly server, I settled on orange chicken with vegetable fried rice, accompanied by a spring roll and a can of coke.

The spring roll was notably non-greasy, a pleasant surprise from the usual fare, setting a positive tone. The main course, orange chicken, was bursting with flavor, beautifully complemented by crunchy broccoli and red peppers, adding a visually appealing pop of color to the plate. The fried rice, often a dish I'd rather skip due to its oily nature, was a revelation here - light, flavorful, and an absolute joy to eat. I'd definitely order it again without a second thought.

In conclusion, I've found my perfect spot for a satisfying Chinese lunch in Chelsea. It's simply delicious!

Interior -- this place has two parts to it. One coffee booth area with bagels, and a dining area for Chinese food. The dining area mainly serves Chinese dumplings, which were delicious!! You can see the chef making dumplings live in the lobby.Service -- pretty decent! They are fast with their service and workers here are bilingual.Food -- all plates are a bit on the sweeter side with generous portion. The plates (other than dumplings) came with a bowl of rice on the side. The dumplings are filled with meat, definitely satisfying. This place provides a lot of convenience for Asian students like myself on campus, and it's not dramatically pricey for decent Chinese food.

Title: A Spirited Evening at Becco with Hits and Misses

My latest dining adventure led me to Becco, where the atmosphere buzzes with a vibrancy reminiscent of a Brazilian BBQ and waiters whirl around with seemingly endless bowls of pasta. Opting for the all-you-can-eat pasta trio on a bustling Saturday evening proved to be both a hit and a miss – one selection wowed us, two satisfied, and one fell short.

Becco keeps diners on their toes with a rotating lineup of pastas, though it's worth noting that their website’s offerings didn't align with what we were served. For future reference, a quick call ahead might be the best bet for those particular about their pasta choices.

In essence, Becco delivered a good—not great—meal. Nevertheless, the convivial setting and novel service style made for an enjoyable experience. It's not an everyday affair, but Becco is certainly on my list for an occasional fun night out.

This is an enjoyable midtown lunch spot, especially for large groups. The food is pretty authentic -- from thin flaky scallion pancakes to spicy chicken to casserole soups. Due to the large family portions, it's an affordable meal for office parties.

Solid restaurant to have a meal in Flatiron. If possible, go with at least one other person and get a chicken for 2 with sides. It is truly a good tasting bird and we got the Plymouth Rock whole bird. The fries and salad were both excellent. Also tried the duck breast with fig, poached egg with escargot, slow cooked duck egg and foie gras (although there will be a ban on this item soon). Would only get 1 of the egg appetizers, so pick whichever one you like the sound of, both were good. The flottante was a nice way to end the meal. Definitely recommend the chicken and fries!

Title: A Culinary Gem Before Apollo's Amateur Night

My recent dining experience at this hidden gem was nothing short of AMAZING! It's not just the food that'll have me returning; the staff's friendliness and their tasty recommendations added to an already delightful visit.

A group of four, we ventured in before hitting amateur night at the Apollo. The Lemon-crusted nuggets were a refreshing twist on the usual vegan fare, bursting with a bright, citrusy flavor. The Stuffed avocado was a hit, fresh and flawlessly sharable. As a New Orleans enthusiast, the Po'boy with fried crawfish met my high expectations, creating a little taste of the Big Easy right there in the restaurant.

Our mains – Smothered chicken and two Crawfish entrees smothered in BBQ sauce – came with an array of sides, including a standout sweet potato soufflé that blended sweet and savory to perfection. The mac and cheese evoked nostalgic BBQ memories, and even the rice with capers and broccoli sides were a hit.

However, the pièce de résistance was the dessert. The Salted pecan chocolate chip cookie ice cream sandwich with praline crunch ice cream was a sublime end to our meal that had us ordering seconds to take home.

I can't endorse this place enough; every dish was memorable, and the ambiance was warm and welcoming. This spot is a must-visit – and do save room for dessert!

Ocean, an upscale international seafood restaurant situated at the bustling corner of Park and 19th Street, offers an impressive dining experience with its grand high ceilings and panoramic windows. With a capacity to host approximately 70 tables and 220 guests within a spacious 14,000 square-foot area, Ocean is more than equipped to handle a crowd.

The restaurant boasts an extensive wine collection, housing around 10,000 bottles, and a full bar, ensuring a perfect pairing for every dish. A highlight of Ocean's offerings is its diverse seafood selection, sourced from the Pacific, Atlantic, and Mediterranean seas, complemented by fresh produce from the renowned Union Square Green Market.

The expansive menu can only be described as a gastronomic journey through the oceans, featuring sections like a Raw Bar with fresh oysters and shrimp cocktail; Nigiri and Sashimi with choices such as Hamachi and Uni; various Rolls including Spicy Tuna and King Crab; and Small Plates like a decadent Crab & Shrimp Salad and Charred Spanish Octopus.

Main courses extend to Sea selections with the likes of Hawaiian Walu and Madai Snapper, and for those who prefer turf over surf, there are "Land Walker" options such as Free Ranch Chicken and Wagyu Beef. Ocean also caters to whole fish enthusiasts with offerings of Black Bass and Turbot grilled to perfection.

Dessert is no afterthought, with standout items like a 16 Layer Lemon Cake, and sides such as Truffle Fries and Brussels Sprouts round off any meal. The culinary journey at Ocean is a testament to its commitment to variety, quality, and the freshest ingredients, providing an exceptional dining experience for seafood lovers and gourmets alike.

This place just blew me away. Prices were real cheap. But food was very flavorful and tasty. I will keep going back to this place. Only problem is seating. There are very few seats and there are always a crowd of people trying to get one. But taking out and eating somewhere else is a good option. Sesame pancake was really good. The bread as such was very soft and flavorful. I went for the one with Szechuan style beef sauce. There was not much meat, but still it was very tasty. Chicken boiled dumpling with spicy sauce was good too. The spicy sauce and the oil gave a nice kick. I dipped every other item in the spicy oil. It boosted the flavor of everything. Chili flakes irritated my throat and made me cough for a while. But still I love it. Basil & chicken boiled dumplings were good too. Chive and pork fried dumplings were very flavorful. I loved the flavors Chive added to it.

I gave the OTHER Kikoo on 9th Street about 2 or 3 stars. This one beats it by a long shot. I do admit, the menu is somewhat more extensive in the 9th street Kikoo, but this one beats it in service, crowd, and most importantly FOOD QUALITY. One of my biggest gripes I had about 9th street Kikoo was the quality of food. The fish was not fresh and the shrimp tempura once came out stale. THIS Kikoo does it right! Fish is WAY more fresh, my shrimp tempura was CRISPY, and the balance of vinegar to rice is perfect here. **Sashimi is limited 30 pcs.**This crowds at this restaurant is also much smaller and I love it because it is more lowkey and quiet--perfect for a date spot. My food also comes out much quicker because of the smaller crowd and the server is much more attentive and was nice enough to inform us when the credit card terminal had problems and when it started to work again. If this Kikoo decides to incorporate more items into its menu WITHOUT compromising quality in its other items, it deserves 5 stars.

Title: A Winning Game Day at Benson's

I stumbled upon Benson's during the Women's World Cup's second half and got more than just a seat with a view. Though they had just one screen, the atmosphere for the game was vibrant, with a cozy crowd of around 10 people. The highlight was the Avocado Smash, generously topped with ripe avocado, perfectly poached eggs, and fresh greens - a steal at $15, given its sizable portion that puts other pricier versions to shame. Washing it down with a $6 draft stout was also a treat. Service was top-notch, thanks to our attentive bartender, Dave. And don't miss out on the check-in discount — a cool 10% off your bill. Benson's is definitely on my return list for a casual hangout with great vibes and food value.

Located in Harlem right by the George Washington bridge and Hudson river, this sports bar is super chill. Came here last night (Saturday before Super Bowl Sunday) around 830p and it was on the empty side. As the night went on, the crowd began to pack in and the security guard was checking IDs at the front door. The bar has many seats and tables for groups of friends to sit and enjoy themselves. The food is typical, mediocre bar food. The price of the food and drinks is the main reason why people come to 123. Sliders are $1 (must order minimum of 3), shots $2, and beer $3. I was with a group of 4 people and we spent $40 each. I personally suggest trying their Rum Hooch punch its Delicious!Negatives I would add are the bathrooms are unisex in the back of the bar, and the music was pretty terrible lol.

Meeeehhh. Stopped in here for an early dinner after the Museum of Natural History. Was craving just a few pieces of sushi and that's what I ordered. No one was inside when we came (granted it was just a bit before 5pm) and the server was just super on top of us, like staring at us and a bit pushy and loud. Sushi quality was okay. Ginger dressing was good. Wouldn't come back though, too many other great options in the neighborhood.

My boyfriend and I recently decided to enjoy a cozy meal at home and ordered delivery from [Restaurant Name] through Uber Eats. We had an exceptionally positive experience. To celebrate Burger Day, we opted for The Essential Burger, which was the special of the day, and paired it with delectable waffle fries and their renowned Colony pizza.

The food arrived with minimal need for reheating, which was no hassle at all. The flavors and quality of the meal made our evening delightful. We're already planning our next order – I've got my sights set on their chicken Parmesan for the future culinary adventure. If you're contemplating a hassle-free, delicious meal at home, [Restaurant Name] is a choice you won't regret.

I recently satisfied my Korean fried chicken cravings at a friend-recommended spot and it didn't disappoint. For those ordering in bulk, bring cash for a rewarding discount. We opted for the boneless meals, which were generous in portion. A must-try is the spicy Pelicana sauce; get it on the side to control your heat level – it's a taste sensation. As a beer skeptic, the strawberry beer was a delightful surprise, offering a decent and refreshing twist to the usual brew. Highly recommended for a flavorful experience!

My friends tried making reservations Saturday morning and the earliest reservation they had was 2:45 pm. I recommend making a reservation earlier in advance. There unlimited boozy brunch ends at 3:30 pm. I got the Hang 10 Burrito ($14), which was okay. The steak wasn't very tender, so it was hard to bite into it without having to eat the whole piece of steak. If the steak were cut up into smaller pieces, it would be better. The burrito itself was a little bland, and I needed to add hot sauce to every bite to add some flavor. The Queso ($13) because we added chorizo for ($3) was good. When you get the Queso it comes a little liquidy and with little hold, but once it cools down the consistency is better. The taste of the Queso overall is pretty good though and it comes with a heaping pile of homemade warm tortilla chips, my favorite. The Buffalo Cauliflower Bites ($8) were tasty, what you would expect from ordering them. My friend ordered the Mexican Benedict ($14), and she said it was good, but nothing special. Unlimited boozy brunch is an added($18) per person, and they serve the mimosas and sangria by individual carafes, which causes the waiter to do a lot more work and for the drinks to get to you slower. If you had someone go around with pitchers, it would be much better for the customer and the staff. Granted our waiter worked really hard to get us drinks as fast as possible. Overall, a large restaurant with bright colors. It is a Cali themed restaurant, so don't expect authentic Mexican food. For someone who has lived in San Diego, the food does not compare.

- feels like you're stepping into Harlem right in midtown. Love the authenticity. - loyal fan base. Everyone sitting at the counter clearly comes here regularly. - they have specials everyday, and everything is cooking already, so they'll bring it to you immediately. - cod was a little too salty for me. Shredded beef was good, but it's your standard ropa vieja dish, nothing memorable. Both come with yellow or white rice. I recommend the yellow, because it comes with beans. - the plates are majorly rice and about a scoop of meat. The food is tasty, but I wish it'd be less rice and more meat. For the price of a plate, you could get something way more filling a stone's throw away. - they bring you complimentary avocado and sweet plantains! - the old ladies running the place are straight-up bosses. They barely speak English, but they still know what you're ordering and they welcome everyone with a smile. Lovely addition to the area!

I ordered the extra spicy ramen with pork, and it was pretty good! The spice is delivered on the side, so you can put it in accordingly. It definitely wasn't one of the best ramens I've had, but it was solid and did the job of filling me up. The broth was flavorful and I liked the spice they used. The pork wasn't great though..a bit too hard. My noodles were thin and straight, but I like the curly and bouncier noodles with my ramen. Should've asked for those instead since they serve that type of noodle with some of their other ramens. Thin noodles don't grab onto the broth as well. Overall, I wish the ramen came with more toppings like bamboo shoots and an egg. For the price, they could've definitely added more ingredients to the bowl. The further I get into this review the more I realize I would actually give this restaurant a 3.5 stars. Because there are so many ramen shops in the city, I probably won't go out of my way to come again but would be willing to go if I happened to be near it.

Title: Lively Ambiance but Priced on the Higher Side

My group of 10 had an enjoyable dinner at this lively spot that's perfect for those looking to avoid the club scene but still seeking a vibrant atmosphere. The service was impeccable, thanks to the attentive hostesses and staff, and the bar did not disappoint with its impressive selection of drinks.

Appetizers here are the real stars; the octopus, egg rolls, and tuna tartare were particularly noteworthy. However, the main course fish dishes were fairly standard for a Mediterranean restaurant, without any accompanying sides to elevate the experience.

The major downside was the pricing. At approximately $125 per person, considering the number of drinks we ordered, the value proposition just didn't add up. For a special dining outing, I'd recommend considering Barbounia over this establishment, as this place doesn't quite hit the "must-visit" mark for its cost.

Rating: 3/5

Title: A Flavorful Foray into Breakroom's Taco Trio

After a glowing recommendation from my friend Gabrielle, I recently tried out Breakroom with another friend, Katie. The eatery's small space made for a cozy atmosphere, though we did share a table with a fellow diner.

Upon Katie's suggestion, I chose the Taco Platter, which lets you mix and match any three tacos for a reasonable $10.95. A quick chat with the attentive cashier ensured my Tempura Fish Taco was prepared without avocado due to my allergy, with a fresh glove change for safety.

The standout for me was the Pork Belly Taco, its crispy skin reminiscent of Chicharrón and delightfully savory. The Tempura Fish Taco also impressed, making it a popular choice at our table. Unfortunately, the Carnitas Taco didn't quite hit the mark, coming across as dry and lacking the rich flavor of its counterparts.

Despite the one miss, my overall experience was positive, and I'm eager to return to Breakroom for another round of their tasty offerings.

Cozy and enchanting is SAAR. A modern Indian bistro located right at the heart of Time Square. Michelin Star Chef Hemant Mathur has uplifted today's home dishes to pure culinary enjoyment.  Savoring still of my bites of tantalizing "Tandoori Tiger Shrimp & Kitchri", "Salli Boti", "Saag Paneer".Impeccable was the service. Will definitely make a reservation here again prior to a Broadway show.CHEERS!

It's so good that when my family came to visit for a weekend, we willingly chose to eat in separate stalls rather than catch up over a normal meal.  When you arrive at Ichiran, you wait in line (can move slowly or quickly depending on the hour) then get seated individually. You can choose to get seated next to one another, but the wait may be a little longer to do that. Once you get seated, the menu and instructions are all laid out for you. You push a button on the counter when you're ready to order. Basically every part of the ramen can be adjusted to your liking. The ramen was so good - the broth was rich, and the noodles perfect. It was relatively expensive for ramen, but I felt like the brand name warrants it and felt like the experience and food was generally worth it.   The hype is real. I think other NY ramen holds its own against Ichiran, but there's no denying how good Ichiran is.  I'm intrigued by the ramen sets you can purchase and make at home. I've actually heard pretty positive things about it, so I may purchase a pack next time I stop in.
Nice little place to have a great cocktail.  Is not as packed, and the sitting is confortable.  The drinks are great and the names of the drinks are great.  Nice place to relax!

Title: A Fair Assessment of a Hyped Seafood Spot

I arrived at this much-talked-about seafood restaurant with high expectations, given its popularity and the rave reviews it had received. Being a visitor from the south, where seafood boils are abundant, I was eager to see how this place would measure up.

Straightaway, there was a notable inconvenience: the establishment is cash-only. While they do provide an ATM, it's a point worth mentioning to friends who might be accustomed to card payments.

Upon ordering, I discovered that all shrimp, including those in the shrimp cocktail, are served with heads on – a new experience for me. My choice was a combo of snow crab and crawfish, flavored with Old Bay and a 'hot' spice level, alongside a side of mac and cheese.

Unfortunately, the service had its blunders: my cocktail order was mixed up, my mac and cheese was forgotten, and the restaurant didn't offer boiled eggs as a side, which was quite surprising.

When it came to the food, while it was enjoyable, the 'hot' spice level was underwhelming, lacking that fiery kick I anticipated. The atmosphere, on the other hand, was delightful, buoying my overall experience. Additionally, some delectable oysters shared by a friend stood out as a highlight.

In summary, this New York-based spot billing itself as offering a New Orleans vibe fell short of my moderate expectations. It's a solid 3 out of 5 for me, with its saving graces being the ambiance and those delicious oysters. Would I make a return visit? Unlikely – the experience doesn't compel a second round.

Entering with expectations of a soba-centric experience, my visit to this establishment took a surprising turn with its izakaya-style offerings. The menu was diverse, featuring chicken skewers, pork, chicken thighs, udon, and sashimi don. Unfortunately, the skewers fell short, lacking the anticipated crispy exterior and tender, flavorful interior.

The sashimi don was a highlight – not up to par with an omakase joint but commendable for izakaya fare. As for the soba noodles, they were passable; though, I attribute my lackluster response more to personal taste than the dish's quality.

This place is a jack-of-all-trades, master of none, which in a competitive culinary city like New York, might not be enough to carve out a niche. If you're in the mood for variety and decent food, this could be your spot. But if you're seeking a standout dish to remember, you might want to keep looking.

I frequently visit this restaurant specifically for their chicken tortilla soup, priced at a reasonable $6.80. The soup is served with nachos and packs a delightful blend of flavors and the right amount of spice. It's hearty with generous portions of chicken and corn - certainly a dish I'd recommend. The tacos, however, can be hit or miss; I’ve encountered some with overly greasy pork. Also, the requirement to purchase a minimum of three tacos is a bit disappointing when one or two would suffice for a snack. Despite this, the food generally feels fresh, and I would still recommend this dining spot.

This has got to be my new favorite Thai spot in Hell's kitchen. It's my second time visiting, and both times I have been blown away with the quality of their food and service! The interior is very unique - a bunch of seating separated by sliding doors. Cool wallpaper all around makes it feel like you've transported to Asia. Their menu is vast and everything looks so good! I've tried their salmon coconut noodle soup before (AMAZING!!), and so this time I went with the traditional Chiang Mai noodle soup and their Thai iced coffee. The chiang mai noodles were also the perfect mix of texture and spice - regular noodles in the creamy broth mixed with the crunchy dry noodles on top. You can tell they care a lot about presentation as well. If you're hungry and looking to catch a meal before your show, give Qi a try!

Title: A New Go-To for Korean Takeout

My quest for the ultimate Korean takeout may well be over. I'm thoroughly impressed with the generous portions and the flavors that pack a punch in every dish. While the pork was satisfying, it did lose a bit of its initial moistness over time; a common occurrence with delivery foods, so not a dealbreaker.

The presentation took me by surprise - a bountiful bowl of meats and kimchi, thoughtfully separated from the rice, preserving the integrity and volume of each component. It's a nice touch that sets this place apart from others that might try to conceal smaller servings beneath a bed of rice.

The fried chicken deserves its own fanfare. It's simply the best fried chicken that has graced my doorstep - miraculously maintaining a crisp and tantalizing skin through the journey from kitchen to table.

I'm already planning my next order and contemplating a dine-in experience to compare. Highly recommend!

Yiwanmen is an ideal choice for those seeking a casual yet satisfying dining experience. The menu smartly divides into three enticing categories: Noodles with soup, jianbing, and baos. For the particularly ravenous, I recommend the hearty noodles or pairing a jianbing with baos for a fulfilling feast—all at wallet-friendly prices. 

My selection, the N1 Chongqing Red Oil Noodle, was exemplary of their offerings. The broth was rich and flavorful, boasting the ideal level of spice to complement the noodles. The dish struck a commendable balance of noodles, meat, vegetables, and soup, ensuring each bite was as delightful as the last. Especially on a brisk winter day, Yiwanmen provides the perfect culinary embrace to warm the soul.

Title: Heavenly Flavors Worth the Wait at Ippudo

Ippudo, you have my complete, unadulterated praise—and my money. With a $40 toll on my wallet and an hour of anticipation, I have zero regrets. The chatter about overpriced ramen is just that—chatter—because the bowl you're served here transcends the ordinary. The umami-packed, rich broth alone is worth every penny, but I must urge you to dive into the spicy Karaka-men. Adding the red pepper sauce is akin to culinary nirvana, like your taste buds being serenaded by angels.

Do not skip the pork buns—yes, they’re fatty, yes they’re tender, and unequivocally sensational; a prime appetizer that sets the stage for the main act. While Ippudo’s price tag might err on the side of indulgence, it's the kind of treat that makes any evening out in the area a memorable one.

Rating: 5/5, without hesitation.

Pro tip: Arrive early, get your name on the list, and they’ll text you when your table is ready. In the meantime, the surrounding locale offers plenty of watering holes to make that hour-long wait part of the experience, rather than a test of patience. Go in knowing there's a wait, and you'll walk out utterly satisfied. 

Would I return? In a heartbeat.

Despite an unplanned visit to a neighboring restaurant instead of Tavola, the mix-up turned out to be a pleasant surprise in terms of cuisine. The food certainly met expectations, suggesting potential shared ownership with the intended destination. Nevertheless, the ambiance fell short of what I was seeking. The highlight, though, was the modern top 40 playlist, which provided an enjoyable backdrop to the meal.

Came for a birthday celebration, Jean-georges delivered a pleasant fine dining experience overall.Interior - this place has been around and still remains sparkly clean with their modern decor. I love that the dining area is in a private setting, separated with the lounge.Service - at first it was just okay.. they seemed very busy when we first walked in, had to stand there a bit to wait for them to be done with their calls and finish running around. The reception table locates outside the lounge and is in the main lobby. There's coat check but no bag check. Our server was delightful though! Georgia was very thorough throughout our entire dinner experience. She was funny, chill and friendly. Loved the vibe! 10/10 service. Every course was delivered right on time, no rush at all. Taste - interesting vegetarian tasting menu, and you can really see the work they put into details. The corn ravioli was also in their other menus, which indicates that it's a must-have, and I agree!! It was the tastiest plate out of all. The dessert was also the highlight of the menu, filled with fruits and really did deliver the tropical theme to the patrons. With the price I kinda did wish I was receiving some kind of meat plate though (lol), so I felt a bit limited with my options there.Overall, it was a solid experience and they do try to make everyone feel special!

**Restaurant Review**

I recently dined at a bustling spot where the crowds were a testament to its popularity. Despite a hiccup with the Yelp waitlist not updating our reservation status promptly, we were seated fairly quickly upon arrival – a minor inconvenience that the staff handled efficiently.

The food, albeit with longer than expected wait times, was delectable across the board. Each dish we tried was packed with flavor and perfectly prepared. A slight mix-up had our appetizers arriving post-main course, but it didn't detract significantly from the overall experience. The standout for me was the Tom Yum hotpot soup – a richly seasoned delight – and the always reliable Pad Thai did not disappoint.

With an extensive menu offering a plethora of tempting options, I'm already planning my next visit to explore more of their culinary creations.

I stopped by Chinatown yesterday driving around trying to find a new place to try during the covid times.  Luckily I came by this place which was still opened at around 6:30pm.  Because of the time, the kitchen in the back was closed but they at least have noodles selections and cooked meat for sale.  So I got the wonton noodle soup while my wife got the fat rice noodle with roast pork.   We also picked up a portion of squid and soy chicken.  While the food we acquired was very simplistic in nature, the flavors were spot on and it just hit that sweet spot after scouring for a place yesterday.  They packed everything very well and separated the noodle and protein from the soup itself.  Definitely worthwhile to try and you won't be dissappointed.

Came here solo on a Friday night when I was in town for a night and was able to get seated immediately which was fantastic as they had quite the wait. I loved everything I got. Started with the sake flight which was on the pricey end but also had some excellent sakes on there and a perfect way to start out a night. For appetizer I had the kakuni bao. Excellent. For the ramen I had the tantan ramen with ground pork. I was insanely full afterwards.Ambiance - lively. Great for a small group of people. Overall - pricey but I wasn't trying to depend conservatively and it was worth it. Would definitely recommend it!

My boyfriend and I visited the restaurant for a weekday breakfast and were pleasantly surprised to be seated immediately upon arrival. We opted for the Shakshuka and Challah French toast, which can be described as decent but didn't quite meet our expectations, especially when compared to favorites like Jack's Wife Freda and Reunion in Williamsburg. The coffee, unfortunately, was a letdown – weak and lacking any robust flavor. While our overall experience wasn’t negative, we had hoped for a meal that would stand out a bit more.

Last night's visit to Remedy Diner was nothing short of legendary. Despite the late hour, the place was alive with energy, feeling more like the hottest club in town with its pulsing music and vibrant crowd. An unexpected film added to the unique atmosphere. We may have gotten carried away and ordered a feast, but every dish was a hit, reinforcing the diner's status as the G.O.A.T. It's hard not to adore the staff here; their charm and efficiency never fail to impress. Observing their late-night delivery hustle, it’s clear they've got the game nailed down. For anyone in the vicinity, I can't recommend Remedy Diner enough. It's a must-visit spot for a memorable dining experience.

From the moment I stepped into this stunning restaurant, its beauty struck me—pristine white decor that radiates a light, spotless interior. The staff added warmth to the ambiance, with Brooke standing out for her exceptional service and spot-on recommendations. Each dish was a delightful fusion of health-consciousness and flavor, served with an aesthetic appeal. The atmosphere buzzed with excitement, a testament to its popularity evident in the eager queue that forms even before the 11:00 am opening. A must-visit for anyone looking for a fun vibe and a delicious, healthy meal.

My husband found this place while on vacation for Valentines in NYC with our twins girls. Tbh we were hesitant about trying it out but boy were we glad we did! The ambiance was great and the food was delicious. It's a bit pricey but definitely worth it. I highly recommend you try them out for breakfast when in NYC!

Although the restaurant was located inside of Trump Tower, this michelin star restaurant exceeded our expectations. Not sure why it went for 3 to 2 star, but it definitely felt like 3 star. From the folks who work there to the ambience to the food, the overall was wonderful and beautiful. Food was amazing and quite delicious. Service was top notch and amazing. Folks really genuinely did everything to make our anniversary special. From welcoming us in, to incredibly professional and courteous service to walking us out. I REALLY appreciate the ladies in the front taking time to take a picture of us under the Jeans George restaurant name so we can capture an unforgettable, memorable night in New York. It really brings a special ending to our last night in New York. The experience, food, and ambience was totally priceless. I really can't stop thinking about it!!My girlfriend and I spent our anniversary here and we will never forget this memory. I wouldcome back again for another Michelin star experience.

Title: Fresh Fish Fiesta at Summer Salt

If you're on the hunt for the crispiest, freshest fish in the Latin/Mexican quick-service game, look no further than Summer Salt. This delightful spot puts the standard rock-hard salmon to shame with its tender and flawlessly cooked fish that can be savored in tacos, bowls, or burritos. I've indulged in all three options and find myself constantly craving more. For those working nearby with a penchant for a top-notch fish taco, Summer Salt stands out as the go-to lunch destination.

On a scorching summer day, I found my oasis in the form of this quaint restaurant famous for its mool naeng myun. The chilled, savory broth with perfectly tender noodles provided the much-needed respite from the heat. To my delight, the meal came with an abundance of ban chan, those delightful small side dishes that add variety and depth to Korean cuisine. As a bonus, we were treated to a complimentary egg souffle that was airy, fluffy, and just the right touch of warmth. A must-visit spot when the temperature climbs and you crave something refreshing yet satisfying.

A quaint location that's hard to spot from the street. There is a very low amount of seating (a handful of tables, seating along the wall for around 10 people), but my party beat the rush by going between 5-6pm. The food was tasty; I had the curry udon and the fried chicken. Be sure to bring cash because they don't accept card!

Title: Late-Night Gem with Speakeasy Charm

Tucked away behind an unassuming facade, this restaurant truly commits to the speakeasy aesthetic, making the initial challenge of locating it part of its allure. Once inside, the ambiance hits full stride, transporting you to an era of hushed decadence.

The prime rib here is not to be missed—excellent in both quality and preparation, with a fat-to-meat ratio that ensures each bite is as sumptuous as the last. Complemented by a zesty horseradish cream and a tantalizing house seasoning, it's a dish that commands attention.

Service is a standout, with Brandon providing recommendations that elevate the experience. His tip on the off-menu French onion dip was spot on—a sandwich replete with succulent meat and a savory dipping sauce. It's hearty, satisfying, and travels well for leftovers.

The English cut prime dip also left us impressed. The thin cuts were skillfully cooked, enhancing the beef's natural flavors, and the horseradish cream served as an ideal accompaniment.

However, the Cacio e Pepe Carbonara Pasta fell short of expectations. While the pasta was perfectly al dente and the tableside mixing added a touch of theater, the dish lacked the peppery bite one anticipates from a cacio e pepe. Despite this, the sunny side up egg and chunky bacon added layers of texture and taste that were enjoyable.

A late reservation at 12:15 am is not for the faint of heart or stomach, as our party discovered. While we left with leftovers, they reheated well the next day—a testament to the quality of the food.

Bear in mind, bookings are exclusively managed through Resy, and they open up 30 days in advance. For those who prefer dining at a more conventional hour, foresight is key.

In summary, if you're seeking an immersive atmosphere with delectable fare and attentive service, look no further—just make sure to plan ahead for the best experience.

Upon the promising buzz on Yelp, we timed our visit to coincide with the opening at 5pm and, to our surprise, were met with an empty restaurant - a quiet dining experience ensued. We dove right into the uni toast, which, albeit petite, was a burst of flavor and is a must-try item. The yuzu clam mazeman, while enjoyable, was unexpectedly filling; I barely managed half the serving. However, the star of our meal was the bone marrow ramen, featuring a robust broth that outshone the mazeman. In summary, make a beeline for the uni toast, and if available, the bone marrow ramen is a winner.

Visited a local ramen joint that turned out to be quite average. The ramen, particularly the 'Lava men', had the heat but lacked depth in flavor. Ingredients used in the dishes were nothing out of the ordinary. Service left much to be desired; a forgotten request for the check resulted in an unnecessary wait, subsequently leading to an unpleasant walk in the rain. With superior options available, I find it hard to recommend this establishment for ramen enthusiasts.

We walked into Benjamin Prime and they immediately earned themselves five stars. Wait what!?! Yeah, their SERVICE is top notch and I was sold before even seeing a menu. Both the two hostess and barman were gracious, friendly and professional and I felt as though I was being welcomed into a friend's home instead of a restaurant. We didn't have a reservation (suggested) but was seated in the balcony (our choice) almost immediately. For my appetizer I chose a dish off the bar menu instead of their main menu. Good selection because my fillet crostini was so good! It was three pieces of beef, I cannot remember which cut but they were individually covered in peppercorn, brunaise and blue cheese. Even though they were all tasty, next time I'd have them all in blue cheese. Our mains and desserts were equally delish and I would recommend here anyday. The first floor was a bit jovial. I realized many were celebrating birthdays so it was nice to dine in the balcony where it was quiet but you're still able to enjoy the festivities downstairs. I only saw male waiters but ladies!!! Those men will have you eating out of their hands! (Pun hahaha). Did they deliberately choose (exotic looking) male models as servers??? Thank you! Picture it, dinning surrounded by all this fine art both restaurant AND STAFF. Woooooosah, hand me a fan because I AM a fan! Yes lorsh. Back to earth....And once again, I must reiterate how wonderful the service/staff, venue and food here was. Beautiful all around. I'll be back. The End.

Best place to come if you have a dog!! It's such a nice restaurant with nice decor, and the food is very decent!! Avocado fries are a must!! The regular fries are so good too!!The best part is that they have a dog menu, so your doggy can eat with you! I personally tried the Grilled Chicken Breast that I ordered for my dog, it's really fresh and perfectly cooked chicken - just without any seasoning!It's THE place to come with other dog parents!!

Title: Consistently Excellent - Upland Delivers

My experiences at Upland, especially during group brunches, have been nothing but remarkable. The menu caters to all, straddling the line between classic breakfast and hearty lunch offerings with finesse. Visiting last Saturday with six friends, we collectively savored the gastronomy - notably the al dente bucatini and the savory quiche.

Portion sizes strike the ideal balance, leaving you content, not overstuffed. Simplicity is elevated here, with the chef transforming standard American dishes into culinary jewels, largely thanks to the freshest of ingredients.

Dinner service mirrors the quality found at brunch, underscoring Upland's commitment to consistency. The attentive waitstaff and well-timed service only enhance the dining experience.

Upland is my go-to for those in search of a reliable feast in an ambiance that complements its modern American cuisine. It's a rare gem that makes every visit worthwhile.

During my recent dinner visit to the restaurant, I opted for the wagyu dish with a personal twist—swapping out asparagus and arugula for a Caesar-like salad, which was notably enhanced by delicious bacon bits. The wagyu steak itself was cooked to tender perfection, although marred by excessive saltiness. Accompanying potatoes were served nice and tender, and the chimi churri sauce provided a flavorful kick without the heat. While the food was passable, the standout was the service. Despite a slight delay due to a temporary backup, the staff was attentive and compensated for the inconvenience with a delectable cookie, which was a delightful end to the meal. Their customer care has earned them another visit from me.

After eagerly anticipating my visit, I was immediately greeted by the tantalizing aroma of fresh pizza upon entering the expansive dining area. My attention was caught by a couple enjoying the renowned Nona Marie, its steam signaling irresistible freshness. I opted for a Sicilian slice and it did not disappoint - a harmonious balance of cheese and tomato sauce with each ingredient standing out, particularly the impressively sourced tomatoes. The generous cheese portion elevated it from a mere slice to a gourmet experience, served up quickly. It's a place I'm excited to show off to visiting friends. However, it's worth noting the lack of a water spigot at the soda machine, necessitating a bottled water purchase.

Came in last weekend with my boyfriend for brunch. We made reservations for 10:30. It wasn't too crowded when we got there, but it definitely filled up and there was a wait by the time we left! They have a pretty good menu with options for just about everyone. The coffee was pretty pricey but was unlimited so can't complain too much. We both ordered the broccoli scramble and a side of cheese grits. The scramble was delicious! So creamy and perfectly cooked. It also came with a biscuit. I have high standards for biscuits and have been on the search for a good one in NYC. This one was decent. I didn't like the jam they had very much. The biscuit had a good taste but wasn't very flaky. The cheese grits were awesome! I don't think I've ever had any like that before. Very flavorful but not too cheesy. A good place to bring parents for brunch.

Love this place! I made a reservation here for my boyfriend's birthday a few months back. Upon arrival, we were seated right away. Couldn't have gotten a better spot. We were seated upstairs in the corner so we had a bit more privacy. The interior is so classy and romantic. The vibes here were truly wonderful. Everyone was so relaxed. The service was impeccable. The waiter was very informative and always eager to help. Both of us ordered steaks, of course. They were cooked exactly how we had asked for them to be prepared. We ordered mac and cheese and mashed potatoes as our sides. Mashed potatoes were good, super creamy. The Mac and cheese was incredible! One of the best I've had. Super cheesy, crispy on the top. Ugh, if only I could eat that everyday. They brought out a complimentary dessert plate which had cream puffs, tiramisu and a chocolate mousse cake. So sweet of them to do for my boyfriend's birthday! At the end of the night, we got our photo taken by one of the hostesses and were given a copy to take home with a letter from the business which was a great touch. We also got to talk to the owner--he was walking around talking to his guests and thanking them. He stopped at every table. It is a pleasure knowing that the people who run this place truly care about the guest experience and appreciate the patronage. We will be back for sure!

Nope. Never. I'm glad I tried this for free, because it's not worth paying for this in NYC with so many good options around. The crust is thick and chewy in a stale way, inedible once it's cooled. The sauce is disturbingly sweet. The cheese is oily. I mean, it's not Little Caesar's or Papa John's, but that's not good enough in this area.

During my recent visit to the restaurant, I decided to try the vodka sauce pizza with sausage and onion. The vodka sauce itself was a delightful surprise, bursting with flavor and a standout on the slice. However, the distribution of the sauce was uneven, leaving parts of the pizza rather tasteless, which was a letdown.

The sausage and onion topping left much to be desired, as it came with an unexpected addition of maple syrup. This sweet twist was off-putting, as it clashed with the savory elements that one typically expects from a pizza. The combination was reminiscent of breakfast fare and, in my opinion, did not mesh well with the pizza.

Another downside was the temperature of the pizza. It arrived in a lukewarm state, which suggested it hadn't been adequately heated. This was disappointing, as a properly heated slice would have undoubtedly elevated the experience of the vodka sauce.

In summary, while the vodka sauce was a hit in terms of flavor, the overall experience was marred by the peculiar sweetness of the sausage and onion, as well as the lackluster temperature of the pizza. A few adjustments could turn this into a much more enjoyable dish.

Dining at Atera is an investment in an ethereal experience, with each successive course surpassing the last in a symphony of culinary mastery. The price, while notable, pales in comparison to the unforgettable journey of flavors and impeccably-timed service that elevates you far beyond the humdrum of Worth Street. With an ambiance that cradles you into a realm of gastronomic bliss, Atera doesn't just serve meals; it ensures that every penny is transformed into a moment you'll cherish.

This is one of the stalls inside the Food Gallery 32 food court. They serve traditional Korean food here such as bibimbap, kalbi, etc. The plates here are not too pricey at about $10 each and most of the items do come with rice and a soup. Everything tasted fine too. However, they are pretty stingy with the meat. It is mainly rice and vegetables. And the "soup" is basically just flavored water.

Title: A Hidden Gem Amongst NYC's Halal Carts

If there ever were a Holy Grail of Halal carts in the city, this unassuming spot near Bryant Park might just be it. Despite the fierce competition from acclaimed chains like Halal Guys and Rafiqis, and standout carts such as Kwik Meal, this pioneer of Halal carts - possibly the first in the city according to Grub Street's deep dive - reigns supreme.

Every day for weeks, I was drawn to their superior quality and consistency without the hassle of enduring the long lines you find at other midtown locations. Their lamb, which I indulgently ordered on repeat, was nothing short of succulent, paired with flawlessly seasoned and veggie-punctuated rice that outshines the commonplace overcooked alternatives.

The cart's Caribbean-Muslim roots weave a delightful cultural tapestry into their offerings, with curry goat and jerk chicken upping the ante - though I confess, the lamb has my loyalty. However, straying from tradition with their tamarind sauce alongside the classic white sauce spun a new twist on a well-loved favorite and is a pro tip not to be missed.

While Yelp might have mistakenly listed this cart as closed, recent visits and contradicting reviews confirm it's thriving, debunking the claim. It remains, undisputedly, one of my favorite places in the city. The day it truly closes (if it ever does) will be a somber one for New York's culinary scene, but for now, it stands as a testament to the rich, diverse, and delicious offerings this metropolis holds.

Have a heart. No really. Have a chicken Heart. They serve that here. And it's pretty darn tasty!I remember as a kid being coerced into trying it. I couldn't get past the mental block. But this time I was determined to triumph. No problems here. All the skewers were tasty. Pork Belly was my favorite. Of course you come here for the boil. Tips 1. Wear gloves 2. Put that bib on. Right now3. Medium is hot AF. Don't be fooled. You gotta have a good tolerance for spicy. We were crying. I should have learned last time. But it's the good kind of spicy cry. 4. Don't wipe your face. 5. Stay away from your eyes. 6. Change gloves and ask for more water. You'll need it. Follow these rules and you'll be on your way to success. The potato and lotus root taste absolutely AMAZING in the boil. They soak up all that seafood and base flavor. Unreal. I will be back again for sure. And again I will order the medium spice. And again I will cry. But that's okay. That's how good it is.

Title: Timeless Elegance Meets Classic Chinese at Mr Chow

When Mr Chow first opened its doors, it made waves by juxtaposing white tablecloth service with noteworthy Chinese cuisine in cosmopolitan hubs like London, New York, and Beverly Hills. Years later, it steadfastly offers that same blend of sophistication and culinary delight. While adventurous foodies might crave more innovation, Mr Chow's dedication to a "fancy" dining experience paired with quality Asian dishes remains its distinguishing charm.

The Beggars Duck, a standout and delightful twist on the traditional Peking Duck, continues to please regulars and newcomers alike. And for those in search of the perfect sip to complement their meal, Mr Chow's lychee martini reigns supreme in the city, adding a touch of fruity elegance to the dining experience.

In essence, Mr Chow is a classic; it doesn't strive to redefine the genre, but rather to perfect the upscale classic Chinese dining experience.

I recently visited a local restaurant where I ordered the beef pan-fried noodles and was pleasantly surprised by the generous portion size, which was ample enough that I couldn't even finish it. The dish was particularly impressive for its abundance of beef, a refreshing change from the usual serving sizes at other establishments. The quality and quantity of food provided definitely ensure my return, especially considering the prices are on par with what you would expect from most Chinese restaurants in Chinatown. Highly recommended for those seeking hearty and satisfying meals.

I recently had the pleasure of trying the Cauliflower Schwarma Pita wrap at a local eatery, taking advantage of a fantastic Dollar lunch deal through the Ritual app. As a newcomer to vegetarian pita options, I was pleasantly surprised by the flavorsome experience. I opted for the full array of toppings – although I'm still curious about what s'rug is. Despite skipping the extra-cost hummus, it found its way into my sandwich, which was a welcome surprise. The pickled toppings were a standout, complementing my love for pickles, and contributed to the wrap's satisfying and hearty nature. My order, placed via Ritual, was ready in a mere 10 minutes, and the staff was notably welcoming and efficient. The seamless service paired with the delicious pita has made me a definite repeat customer.

Title: A Pappardelle Paradise

From the moment I walked in, the warmth of the staff made me feel right at home. Their flexible seating policy allowed me to choose the perfect spot to enjoy my meal, a gesture that did not go unnoticed. The highlight of my experience was undoubtedly the pappardelle with mushrooms and sun-dried tomatoes, all swathed in a delicate cream sauce that was both satiating and delectable. It's rare to find a restaurant that serves up such a perfect rendition of this dish. For anyone with a penchant for pappardelle, this spot is a must-visit. A resounding two thumbs up for excellent food and service!

Yeah, I'm not too happy with how this place has gone.Similarly to Benita -- it used to be pretty good. Though it was always overpriced, at least the quality was somewhat OK.Came him for lunch with a friend, I was excited to show her this place because she is basic posh.We got guacamole - Fantastic Tacos - Average.Drinks - Pretty good.Everything wasn't that that bad, until we got our bill.We were told it was "Happy Hour." and ended up being charged full price. When we asked about it, our waiter said, "Yes. That's happy hour."How is Happy hour the same price as what's on the menu......And why are you lying about it......Avoid, get real mexican food outside of  Chinatown and save your money

I visited the restaurant during the weekend and was surprised to find it not bustling with patrons. I opted for the tonkotsu ramen, and while the option to add extra toppings was appreciated, the use of thin noodles didn't quite hit the mark for my personal taste. I've certainly enjoyed better ramen at other establishments. Additionally, the seating was a bit cramped, which might be uncomfortable for some guests. However, the thoughtful touch of a designated spot to hang coats was a nice convenience.

I recently visited this Korean restaurant for lunch with a colleague and was thoroughly impressed by the authenticity of the cuisine. The flavors were delightful, truly capturing the essence of Korea. Service was outstanding; our waiter was exceptionally friendly and welcoming, which enhanced our dining experience. Additionally, the speed at which our food arrived was perfect for a lunch break, with little waiting time. Highly recommend for anyone seeking a delicious and efficient midday meal.

Came here on a weekday for lunch with coworkers. Was craving comfort food so I got the short rib and mashed potatoes. We shared the cheese plate, thin crust pizza and escargot. This was my first time having escargot and it was my favorite thing I tried here! I was wishing there were more of them.My coworker knows the owner and they have us a complimentary apple crumble!I had some of my main course left over and I asked them to pack up my short rib and potatoes.
