When I got home, all they had packed up only the meat, no potatoes or gravy! I had more potatoes than meat left on the plate. It did feel a bit light...next time I'm going to ask to pack it myself!

**Yummy Wood Fired Pizza in Midtown**

Located in the heart of Midtown, this restaurant offers a gourmet twist on traditional wood-fired pizzas. The establishment favors a more refined approach compared to the classic New York-style pizzerias in the vicinity, presenting an impressive variety of toppings. Patrons can either craft their own pizza or select from the signature pies featuring thin, artisanal crusts.

Service was straightforward: order at the counter and wait for the pizza to be served at the table. On my visit, I sampled the "Impossible" vegan pizza and the "Tartufo." The former boasts a 'sausage' that remarkably emulates meat, paired with a vegan cheese that's more akin to American cheese in texture when melted. Despite the middle of the crust being slightly soggy – an exception, I'm told, to the usual crispy standard – the flavors were nonetheless satisfying.

The Tartufo pie was my favorite, perfectly balancing arugula, mushrooms, truffle oil, and mozzarella on a crispier crust, sans the traditional red sauce. While eating a whole six-slice pizza solo is a bit of a stretch, I managed five slices without much trouble.

Also on offer are intriguing options like vodka pizza and a honey with prosciutto variant that I'm keen to try on my next visit. The pomegranate lemonade, while refreshingly sweeter, could have benefited from a more pronounced lemon tang. Overall, if you're looking for a pie with a bit more finesse in Midtown, this place is well worth a visit.

Title: A Tasty Fusion with Authentic Flair

From the moment I walked into the restaurant, I was enchanted by the inviting ambiance, a fusion of modern charm and comforting warmth. Admittedly, the seating arrangement left little to be desired, presenting a slightly cramped experience. However, the culinary offerings quickly overshadowed any discomfort.

The roast duck tacos were a revelation, each bite bursting with flavor and perfectly cooked to delight the palate. Similarly, the softshell bao was a delectable treat, its contents enveloped by a soft, pillowy embrace that simply melted in my mouth.

Craving a taste of nostalgia, I ordered the Tsukemen, a dish I fondly remembered from a trip to Kyoto. The noodles were flawlessly executed; their texture and flavor were spot-on, a testament to the kitchen's attention to detail. Dipping them into the broth was a joy, although the broth itself didn't quite meet my expectations. While savory and palatable, it lacked the scalding temperature and the crucial viscosity needed for the noodles to carry its full essence.

In summary, the restaurant tantalized with its delicious fusion offerings, though a tweak to the Tsukemen's broth could elevate the dish from good to exceptional.

On a brisk day that called for comforting fare, my visit to 2nd Ave Deli hit mostly high notes. Opting for the half soup, half sandwich combo, the corned beef sandwich was satisfying, but the matzah ball soup, despite a stellar matzah ball, had a broth that was lackluster. Sharing amongst ourselves, the pastrami sandwich stole the show with its remarkable flavor, overshadowing the corned beef.

The potato pancakes were a twist on the expected, leaning more towards flour than potato, yet still enjoyable when complemented with applesauce. The coleslaw and pickles, often a meal's unsung heroes, were notably great here. A hiccup with our order meant the kugel was a no-show, but the staff amiably removed it from our bill without fuss.

Heed the warning of prior diners: your wallet will feel the weight of this experience. Though the prices at 2nd Ave Deli might induce a mild case of sticker shock, if you're prepared to splurge, the food will mostly live up to the expenditure.

Fun order at the counter spot inside Chelsea market! Recently moved here from California and I'll be honest the Mexican food hasn't really compared, until I found these tacos! I ordered the pollo asada and carne asada tacos and they were delicious. They give you a ticket then you tell the guys on the line whether you want corn or flour tortilla and what toppings. Will be back!

Title: Disappointing Return to a Once-Favored Spot

Two years ago, this ramen joint captured my heart, but my latest visit left it aching for the flavors of yesteryear. The extra spicy paitan ramen which I looked forward to turned out disappointingly bland, lacking the depth that once made it stand out. My girlfriend's mega ramen shared the same fate; a creamy broth and well-cooked noodles couldn't mask the absence of flavor. The real letdown, however, was the meat. Both chicken and pork were so tough and dry they detracted from the overall experience. It pains me to declare this encounter as one of our least enjoyable ramen meals to date. On a positive note, the staff was as cordial as I remembered. Unfortunately, in a city with no shortage of ramen spots, it's unlikely we'll return unless we hear of a major turnaround.

Title: Serene Ambiance with a Unique Vegan Twist

Nestled in a serene corner that blends modern aesthetics with a touch of nature, this charming eatery is the quintessential date night refuge or a cozy spot for small gatherings. The vegan menu is a breath of fresh air, offering a variety of tantalizing choices. 

We started with the mushroom gyoza, which was delightful, followed by the avocado tikki—bursting with flavor, although paired with a slightly overdone flatbread. The plant burger, albeit a tad basic and dry, could benefit from an extra drizzle of sauce. A standout was the side of truffle potatoes, a dish so divine it could easily be the sole reason for a return visit.

In summary, the restaurant delivered a pleasing experience with the promise of more culinary exploration—especially for those irresistible truffle potatoes. Definitely worth another visit.

I tried Ichiran for the first time and was mightily disappointed. I don't mind the dining set up that's intended for people to enjoy the ramen solo. But the ramen I had was mediocre at best! The noodles were a bit overcooked, the broth without character, the toppings not worth mentioning. I'm not sure how they got people to line up around block when it first opened up in Brooklyn but this is one of those joints that are all hype. Don't go! I recommend Ippudo or Totto instead.

Title: A Pleasant Nautical Dining Experience

I must say, after seeing some unduly critical reviews, my recent visit to the boat restaurant provided a refreshing perspective. The culinary delights may not have been extraordinary, but the overall quality was certainly satisfying. Plus, dining aboard a boat grants a unique charm that should be taken into account.

The establishment's modern approach as a cashless venue resonates well with those of us who have embraced a cash-free lifestyle. Despite a slight hiccup with our large group struggling to secure outdoor seating without an additional reservation fee, we managed an agreeable compromise by dining indoors – a wise choice given the balmy weather – following up with an enjoyable outdoor drink session.

The star attraction, a Bacon Lobster Roll, came at a premium ($24) and though generous with lobster, the accompanying cold bacon detracted slightly from the value. A side of fries might have justified the cost. Nevertheless, the overall food experience lands at a solid 3.5/5.

Drinks, albeit on the pricier side – my classic margarita was noteworthy at $16 – were both delightful and potent. They were a hit among my companions, as well, who sampled a range of beverages throughout our two-hour cruise.

A standout aspect was undoubtedly the service. The staff demonstrated exceptional patience and agility in accommodating our large party, ensuring our experience was comfortable and convivial. Our waitress, in particular, was a gem, providing timely and attentive service that greatly enhanced our outing.

The vistas on offer were spectacular, contributing significantly to the venue's allure. Whether you're basking in the afternoon rays or soaking up the sunset views, the restaurant promises a visual feast.

In conclusion, this boat restaurant is a fantastic option for groups seeking a distinctive dining experience. While the 'summer pass' isn't something I'd invest in due to infrequent visits, I am already looking forward to another enjoyable outing next year.

I've been consistently impressed with this gem of a restaurant I discovered on Uber Eats. It's now my go-to spot for lunch. The menu strikes the perfect balance between health-conscious and indulgent flavors — truly a rare find. Every meal is a delight for the taste buds without the guilt. Highly recommended for a satisfying, wholesome lunch!

Fresh food in a dark smoky modern house. I read that dim restaurants make you eat more. This is not a problem with what's being served at Locanda verde. Each dish had fresh ingredients and were obviously sourced from high quality markets. I particularly enjoyed eating the prosciutto with Asian pear which was a different touch. My tagliatelle although vegetarian was hearty but the best pasta dish was truly the ravioli.The high ceilings don't seem to detract from the intimate atmosphere here. Definitely a nice place to just have a drink as well. Our server had excellent knowledge of the wine options here and what to expect.

My friend initially recommended Thursday Kitchen for their Capri sun drinks so we headed over after dinner. Although it was a Monday evening, the restaurant was packed and our party of 4 waited approximately 45 minutes to be seated. Our server was very energetic and attentive which made our overall experience all the better. We ordered a wide variety of drinks and entrees to share. I had the lychee reach rich and my friends ordered the blah blah blue, Ruby the gf, pure strawberry, Ms. Cutetini, and the yuzu tonic (nonalcoholic). I definitely thought that the lychee and pure strawberry drinks were on the stronger side. The lychee drink tasted more like mango than anything but I enjoyed it. I personally loved the lychee, strawberry, and Ruby gf drinks. I wasn't expecting much as for the entrees, since I'm not the biggest fan of Korean fusion food. However I was seriously blown away by each entree. The truffle mac and cheese was incredibly delicious and despite the truffle oil, it wasn't too heavy or rich. The ugly potato dish was also really good. The potato slices had BBQ seasoning and were topped off with feta cheese. The steak was hands down my favorite dish. The steak was cooked medium rare and the meat was very tender. The kale was crunchy and well-seasoned and complemented the steak really well. We finished off our meal with one of their desserts: popcorn ice cream. Their popcorn ice cream has caramel popcorn in thick vanilla ice cream, topped off with caramel drizzle. I'm not a huge fan of caramel but this dessert was so good, I couldn't pass it up. I absolutely recommend going to Thursday Kitchen for their drinks and their entrees. I would go on a weekday since their wait times on the weekend can be up to 2 hours.

The restaurant itself is pretty small but what they lacked in space they made up in the food! I got there around late dinner time and managed to snag a single table for me and my friend. I got the beef stew noodles as recommended by the waitress, and my friend got the mala noodles. The moment I took the first bite, I was in LOVE. I usually can't take much spice in noodles, but this spice hit different. It would make me cough if I inhaled too fast, yet it didn't burn my tongue. The noodle dishes all came with plenty of noodles, bok choy, and scallions. Broth was also amazing and mixed really well with the spice. The only qualm I had with my dish was that the beef stew was a lot more tendony than I expected. This made it a little chewier than I would have liked. My friend really enjoyed his mala noodles on the other hand (consisted of ground pork) and was also a fan of the spice. Overall, a good noodle spot to try in Hell's kitchen area.

Caviar House & Prunier takes your typical airport meal experience and turns it on your head. Treat yourself during strenuous delays and immediately improve your travel experience! My visit was in July 2018 but I still think back fondly on this spectacular experience. I definitely forgot I was in the middle of the international terminal as a sipped on champagne and stuffed my face with caviar. This is truly an experience you need to have once and worth the price point!

Came here to hang with my coworkers/friends. Loved hanging at this place. The huge halls and wooden furniture really brings together the German beer hall vibe. The waitresses were all very attentive and nice, we were seated fairly quickly and had our orders taken. Their menu had a variety of different beers and classic German food. We got a few of their huge pretzels and a couple different sausage dishes, all of which were phenomenal. They also had a good assortment of sauce to dip both the sausage and pretzels. I would definitely return here to hang with friends, the atmosphere and food definitely make it a fun place to visit. Sausages - Bratwurst and BautenwurstUber pretzel

During our visit to the restaurant, we were treated to fantastic singing performances which certainly enhanced the dining experience. However, the culinary offerings were merely adequate, not quite living up to the excitement of the entertainment. 

One notable downside was the aggressive tipping culture. The establishment strongly encouraged patrons to "fill up the bucket," creating an uncomfortable environment for those who don't carry much cash. With only a $20 and a $1 note on hand, I felt compelled to leave a $20 tip to avoid the shame cast by the insistent passing of the tip bucket, which seemed excessive given the already lofty prices.

In summary, while the atmosphere was delightful thanks to the talented singers, the push for tips dampened the overall enjoyment of our evening. We would have appreciated a more subtle approach to gratuity that respected the changing norms of cashless transactions.

Cute spot, the menu at this establishment is what brought me here. Funky burgers and treats my type of place on Friday night. I ordered the southwest burger which was the burger with street corn on it. Yummy! I also ordered the buffalo chicken nachos, they weren't my favorite. I would have preferred the cheese on the nachos to be melted. Now for the sweet treats !!! Deep fried Milky Way and dough bread. Sweet treat attack both were so delicious. The noise level was a bit too high for me, overall my experience was good! Service was good as wel

This review is entirely based on the pesto meatball sub, because, that's the only thing I need to taste to write it! Absolutely must-have. Something I've been craving ever since I had it. The pesto has a nice savory flavor, some sort of mozz drizzle brightens it up, and the meatballs are some of my favorites anywhere.

If you're looking for authentic szechuan food, look no further! I think the biggest give away is when I stepped into the restaurant, I saw a busy restaurant packed with locals who knew what's up. Every table surely had a huge hot pot filled with yummy spicy goodness, and I knew at that point this was the place to be!We started off with the beef tendon with chili oil which is a cold dish. The dish had layers of thin slices of beef tendon soaked in chili oil - for those who never tried tendon, it almost reminds me of al dente noodles, but more tender. It was a nice mild spice and didn't feel too oily. The real winner and apparently their most popular dish is the grilled whole fish and I can totally understand why once this masterpiece was set on our table. First off, this pot was HUGE - easily feeds 3-4 people at least. You get a whole grilled tilapia stacked upon layers of lotus root, seaweed, noodles, mushrooms, fried tofu, bok choy, potato and the spices marinated extremely well together - especially in rice. It is a little bit more tedious with the bones but I would definitely recommend this dish. I love grilled fish and when the crispy skin is soaked in the spices, it really enhances the flavors. The chong qing spicy diced chicken is another winner. Don't let all the chili peppers scare you - this is a classic szechuan dish, and one I always love to get. The pieces of crispy chicken has so much flavor and a kick of spicy numbness from the szechuan peppercorns, and I couldn't stop eating them! Overall, I think this place is excellent and would definitely recommend it. Come in a bigger group so you can try a little bit of everything, I guarantee you'd want more than just 2 dishes here. The service was great - super attentive servers who always came back to refill water (which I'm so thankful for with all the heat from the food).

We came in here just because we wanted to check it out no food first time around just had drinks. Decent specials on beers from $5-8 by the glass or $16-20 by the pitcher. We had a pitcher of the Sapporo beer great tasting beer not a bad deal. Next time around gave the Hot Sake a try not bad taste wise. Appetizers we had  the shrimp Shu mai nice tasting great w the soy sauce. Main dish I had the Chicken Ramen added some spicy garlic oil , very good ramen a little odd the poached egg never had it like that but it pretty good taste wise, realized I prefer the egg to be hard boiled, great tasting ramen & soup.Decent size place, good amount of seating & bar area. Price wise drinks not bad , ramen dishes typical prices to the area. Interesting fun decor, u get ur check in like a Lilly's comic book .. nice touch! Service can me slow but it's not bad I'd rather it be a bit slow than be rushed through my meal.

Not the place to go if you're looking for a reasonably-priced dinner.  But if you're looking for a place that changes its menu almost daily using the freshest available ingredients, and plates and flavor combinations that will impress even the most picky foodie, then this place is for you.  We had the extended tasting menu, which included 3 different amuse bouche, and each course was better than the next.  One of the duck dishes had some sinew, so was a little tough, but the rest was a home run!

Title: A Taco Haven in the Heart of Chelsea Market

If you're roaming through Chelsea Market and your stomach begins to rumble for Mexican fare, follow the throngs of enthusiasts to this bustling taco spot - a clear favorite among locals and visitors alike. Arriving at opening time, we were greeted by a queue, evidence of its popularity.

Ordering is a two-step process: first, you place your order and pay, then move to the pickup window, ticket in hand, where the magic happens. The communal vibe of the market means finding a spot at a standing table isn't an issue. And let's talk about what you're really here for - the tacos. At $4 a pop, expectations are high, and rightly so. The tacos I sampled were nothing short of perfection, brimming with flavors and ingredients that satisfied with every bite. 

Even amidst the cornucopia of culinary delights in New York City, this taco stand holds its own as a must-visit. It was the only taco spot I patronized on my trip, and I can say with confidence – it’s well worth your time.

Stout NYC strikes a satisfying chord for those looking to unwind with a well-crafted beer and some solid grub. The dark beer aficionados will feel at home here, with a commendable lineup of stouts and porters like the velvety Breckenridge vanilla porter and creamy Left Hand milk stout - both standout Colorado brews. The bar's system of sub-categorized cans and bottles is particularly user-friendly.

While the food doesn't venture far from pub fare expectations, it rarely falters. I recommend diving into the appetizers or daily specials for a reliable treat; their buffalo calamari, for one, is a surprisingly palatable twist worth a try. If you're up for it, inquire about the rotating $6 craft drafts, they rarely disappoint.

Despite a minor hiccup with some beers from the list being unavailable, the bartender adeptly navigated us to satisfactory alternatives. It's easy to make a habit of visiting Stout NYC, given the consistent comfort it offers no matter which of its three locations you're at - from the vibrant flagship near Madison Square Garden to the cavernous, almost romantic vibe of the FiDi spot in the wee hours.

In short, Stout NYC is a solid pick for a casual night out, especially if you fancy a quality stout and some dependable eats. My girlfriend and I will certainly be back for more.

Well for starters this was the second time in about years I had the pizza with having a " night out" in nyc and it's not as good as I remember. That being said when I have the pizza at 1:00am it is amazing.. the service is fast and they have very creative pies.... the line moves fast but make sure you know what you want before you get online... the sauce is on the sweet side and I'm not down with that.... but it's a go too!!! Plus the beers on tap are $3!! And they are to go!!

I love this place. It's been around forever! I loved coming here when I lived in BK and recently gathered friends for some holiday shopping. It's authentic, welcoming, and delicious but you need to put in your name and come back in an hour (if you are lucky). We snagged some seats at bar after 30min.  We still had another 40mins to go for a table. We toasted with Bellinis and hard ginger kombucha (tasted like a cider & similar alcohol content). We opted for classic shakshuka, mushroom omelette, and Israel breakfast. We were all happy with our choices.It's worth a visit if you are in neighborhood but have a plan so you aren't surprised by the wait.

Came here for restaurant week to get a taste of the restaurant and their winter menu.Some things were a hit or miss here:Majority of the food was delicious, but a quality restaurant delivers delicious food from beginning to end. We had the pumpkin ravioli which was creamy and savory (to die for). I had the yellowfish tuna crudo which definitely could've used some extra acidity. Our entrees were good, but nothing stand out-ish. The desserts were probably the best part of the meal - I could not stop despite how full I was! Since the most expensive part of the menu is the entree, I expect it to be the most unforgettable. However, the appetizers and desserts were the ones I remember the most.We also ordered brocoli with flaming hot cheetos on the side. We finished every last bite, however, I think if they chopped up the cheetos it would've given the extra finesse it needed. As for the walk downstairs, the route to the bathroom oddly had a strange sour note wafting along your steps. This restaurant leaves you full, and I am certainly intrigued to come back for the other seasons. I think to get the best experience, you ought to do your research and see which dishes are the best to order.

Great food but a tad expensive and VERyyyy loud. Friendly and fast service - tuna poke ($20/eh): not a huge fan of the tuna, was a little chewy. Came with tortilla chips and lots of avocado- side of kale salad and avocado ($9/ YUM): so much yum avocado and sweet potatoes- catch is the day, hake ($25/ YUM): super tender, perfectly cooked and served with sautéed bok choyTLDR: great food, fast service, healthy options

The best ramen I have ever had! I came here during a particularly sad day and it was just the right comfort food to cheer me up. I also pleasantly found out after I came in that iron chef Morimoto was the chef - though he wasn't there I when I went. We started with the gyoza and boy what a treat! It was cooked to perfection and the ginger scallion sauce on top gave it just the right amount of onion yumminess to set it apart. The tonkotsu ramen was the star. Rich and flavorful with a real pork flavor. I added the Kakuni The waiter did make suggestions on what to add to amp up the flavor even more but I'm afraid I dont remember what they were. Also it's served with chopsticks but don't be afraid to ask for a fork if you are chopstick impaired like me.

First time I had ichiran in the US. I compared this place to Hong Kong's ichiran. First thing I gotta say, IT'S TOO DAMN EXPENSIVE. They're charging $18.90 for a bowl of ramen? A glass of tea is $4? The dessert is around $10?? Come on. Ichiran knows they don't have to charge that much for a bowl. It may be a touristy, well-known chain ramen joint, but the price is too much. Anyway, on to the taste. I did NOT order the recommended set. I believe that is another scam from Ichiran trying to make money. I ordered:- Medium dashi- Rich Richness- 1/2 clove of garlic- With scallions- With chashu- 10x spiciness- Firm noodle textureRegarding taste, it was a good bowl of ramen. I enjoyed it quite a bit. It was quite spicy, but not enough to make me cry (lol). I am a bit salty that I forgot to get my free noodle refill. I didn't get the most out of my $20. Regarding the quality, the broth was great, but it tasted a little like instant noodles soup (maybe because there was so much spicy powder). The noodles were fantastic. The chashu seemed a little old and could be more fresh.Regarding service, the wait was around 10-15 minutes at 6:30 pm on a Thursday. But I got lucky because a whole bunch of people made the line a lot longer behind me after I arrived. The service was quick and efficient. They seem to not have very many seats, which is why they hurried people out the door when they were done eating.Overall, 5/10 stars. Good bowl of ramen, but way too overpriced. Not the best bowl of ramen I've ever had, and I doubt this is the best ramen in the US. Would maybe recommend to tourists, but if you want better ramen, go to Hong Kong or Japan.

A good place to enjoy some Malaysian fare albeit $$$We enjoyed the appetizer pancake which is like an elevated roti canai (but with beef!). Curry puffs are, as always, welcome to my belly.The server was very honest about the expectation of the chili crab dish. No it's not the same as the O.G. Singaporean dish but it's decent. I never turn down fried dough. The sauce however was a tad too sweet, almost like sweet and sour sauce.I have a special place in my belly for nasi lemak but I tried something different here today which I'm not sure I have the loves for as much... The rice was blue and the fish was fried crispy, bone-in.The shaved ice dishes are a welcome refreshing end to the meal but in mid January also gives a little extra chill inside.

The overuse of ponzu sauce was so evident in their Trust Me set. I would have been perfectly fine if they only placed ponzu sauce on the tuna sashimi but then they used it for several other pieces. Only the salmon sushi, toro handroll, and crab hand roll were good. Not sure if this set is worth the $40 price tag, but there's no tipping at the end of the meal. I really enjoyed the warm sushi rice...if only it didn't break apart so easily.

Came here to try the legendary falafel, and they were awesome! We split a side of falafel which included 4 falafels and came with a side of white garlic sauce. They were super crispy on the outside and deliciously herbaceous and fluffy on the inside. To finish with something sweet, we each got a piece of baklava which was equally as delicious. Overall, definitely lives up to the hype and I'd recommend!

Can't believe this unique restaurant is in the heart of Times Square! Local to many Broadway shows and classic New York tourist spots which makes it an ideal restaurant for someone looking to get a more unique but laidback dining experience in Times Square. And I can't believe after all these years, I've finally made it a point to try this place! We had a great experience here. This restaurant is beautiful adorned with unique Victorian trimmings, it could honestly keep you entertained for hours just admiring the decorations. Surprised that they blast mainly Top 40 hits from today and the past, given the theme, but it is a bar after all. The music made for a fun environment; we ended up bonding with the people next to us about the music. Our waitress was super friendly and outgoing and knowledgeable about the menu, which helped in my ending deciding factor. I ended up going with the shepherds pie. The portion size looked tiny but it ended up being so filling that I couldn't finish what was left on the skillet! The meat was seasoned just right, the mashed potatoes were nicely done and evenly coated and it was a hearty meal overall. Dessert was okay, I honestly can't remember the name of my cake on the menu but it was chocolate. Nothing to write home about. My one issue was that the majority of the tables at this spot are mainly high top tables. I'm short, and I had a lot of trouble getting onto the seats, especially the booth that we were seated at. Oh well, this was just a small hurdle to cross over to enjoy my dinner here. Really enjoyed it here and would love to try their high tea. And I'd definitely come back for a casual brunch or dinner as well!

A favorite top spot upper east with a fun energetic vibe great for some games and sport watching. This is the go to spot for kids at heart.  Have been here many times with friends and my son to enjoy the fun atmosphere and good casual food. Atmosphere. Comfortable and spacious with a bar and large space with wood beer garden type community tables. - several TVs throughout playing sports / games - board games on the tables- ping pong tables and pinball games- popcorn machine with free popcorn Service.  Always extremely friendly and attentive servers. Food.  We've not been disappointed with anything we've ordered - even my picky son - including:- Giant pretzel adorned with mustard cups as eyes to make a smiley pretzel - sausage sampler with sauerkraut - schnitzel with egg on top - tasty chicken wings - looong (foot long) hot dog - pork tacos - delicious - pork nachos - so good and a must try - avacado on sourdough - so good - burger- my son eats the entire thing - heaping zucchini fries - fantastic - giant bacon strip - also a must try for bacon loversDrinks.  Large selection of beers but the bartenders have also made great cocktails.Definitely recommend for casual, very good food with friends and family in a fun restaurant watching or playing some games!

Up Thai earns its place among my top Thai dining destinations in NYC. The only slight mar on an otherwise perfect experience is the occasionally mediocre service; the servers sometimes appear disinterested, with a focus on turning tables rapidly that can leave one feeling rushed. However, the sublime flavors of their dishes single-handedly redeem the dining experience, ensuring that any service-related shortcomings are easily forgiven. A high recommendation with a minor caveat.

Kinda like a hole in the wall place and extremely difficult to find if you are just randomly walking around K-town. Completely different setting once you enter the restaurant. The elevator takes you directly to the restaurant and the ambiance is amazing. Pros: Happy hour (even on Saturdays) from 5 to 8 pmRecommendations: The drinks are great, especially the fruity cocktails! Try the apple mule, smoky manhattan and their amazing variety of lychee based drinks (including lychee martini). Also they have an amazing variety of soju, try the passionfruit one. Also, their fried chicken and tacos are a must try!

You should Definitely enjoy some food here! If you're at Chelsea Market or in the area near 15th Street and 9th Ave, enjoy a fish taco.  Or order the shrimp cocktail, served in a tall glass like you'd see an ice cream soda served in.  Someone at my shared picnic table ordered it, and it looked amazing !! So, my next visit, I'll have to try it.  It is $12.  I can tell you that the fish taco is ALWAYS DELICIOUS , so definitely get a fish taco, and see whatever else appeals to you.  AND PLEASE PUT SOME MONEY IN THE TIP JAR.Drinks and beers are also served here and quite popular, too.There's also an after-work type crowd for drinks and guacamole or salsa.  Place your order, hold on to your paid receipt, and listen for your number shown on your receipt.  Service here is friendly, helpful, and just plain old NICE!!  The staff works hard here, they are really nice , so please remember to show your appreciation and put something in the TIP JAR please.  The food here is fresh and delicious and very reasonably priced.  Enjoy!  A nice place to get a bite between learning sessions at Apple OR Google.  See my photos!

Things that are scary in life: working a block away from the WV location of Emily because you can easily go and pick up pizzas ft. a brussel sprout salad and then convince yourself that because you had the salad, you were healthy that day, so you can skip the gym and then this pattern continues on and on and then it's summertime and you're whole entire body is just like pizza: doughy.

All the dishes we had was really tasty and prepared with care. The flavors were all bold and well integrated with the dishes. The noodles were firm and not gummy. The protein all cooked and seared to perfection. The only bad thing was the service wasn't friendly. We were only a party of 5 and it wasn't terribly crowded until the end. The wait staff need better training.  Would definitly come again though for the food..

Came here for the first time with two friends around 6pm and it was already pretty packed. However, we were seated right away since we were a smaller party. The waiters were very attentive and helpful, which was great. For starters, we ordered Cajun fries. It came with a sauce that I am not quite sure what it is, but it reminded of a truffle aeoli sauce. Next, we ordered two pounds of clams and two pounds of shrimp with the "Boil" special sauce. Everything tasted wonderful. Everything was flavorful. The fries were crispy and tasty. All the seafood were huge! Definitely don't see that often at different seafood spots. Both the shrimp and clam bags had so much sauce in it that it made the seafood taste so good. When you order 2+ pounds, they put a potato and corn in the order as well, which is great. Overall, the Boil is definitely a place to return to.

Come here for brunch! Their food consisted of the most unique blend of different flavors. The nori carbonara was my favorite but the Japanese curry shakshuka was a bit salty. The endless flow of complimentary iced tea helped

Walking in there is a sign that said it's one of the best Korean BBQ in town and it did not dissapoint. My colleague and I came in for lunch and shared a meat package for 2 and a few sides and it was more than enough. The do cook it for you and they use a piece of fat to oil the grill vs. oil. The best dish in the house was the amazing Kimchi Fried Rice. It was unbelievable with flavor and comes with an cooked egg on the side.  Definitely would come again!

Very clean, looks new.   Mushroom miso soup was exceptional.  House green salad was very good as well.  Dressing had a strong citrus note.  Avocado  fries were tasty, but slightly oily.  Presented very well though. Sushi was very tasty, and even though the menu is small, they will make whatever you like.  Overall great experience

Title: Hidden Space, Mixed Experiences at Local Chinese Eatery

Upon entering this seemingly compact restaurant, we were promptly led to an additional seating area downstairs due to the crowded main floor. Unfortunately, the charm of the hidden dining space was overshadowed by the lackluster service. It seemed as though the staff were less attentive to patrons seated below, leading to a stretched-out mealtime of 90 minutes that could have easily been halved.

The food offered a mixed bag of traditional Chinese flavors. The highlight was the pan-fried hand-pulled noodles, offering a satisfying chewiness and a burst of flavor, especially when paired with the roast duck—albeit fatty. The fish ball with meat-filled noodle soup was mediocre, lacking the punch I had hoped for, and the noodles in the soup were notably softer than their pan-fried counterparts, losing that desirable texture. Steamed vegetable dumplings met the standard expectations without fanfare, while the xiao long bao was passable but not exceptional.

Overall, despite the service falling short and some dishes not hitting the mark, the pan-fried hand-pulled noodles alone merit a visit. Worth a try for those curious about authentic hand-pulled noodles, but set your service expectations accordingly and be prepared for a wait.

Café Mofongo is a hole-in-the-wall restaurant that serves up tasty and inexpensive food.Food: Very Good (4 of 5).I stopped by for lunch to take out a Pollo Guisado (chicken stew), with yellow rice and a cup of black beans for $7.50 total. One gets to choose yellow or white rice, and red or black beans. The chicken was tender and delicious (although I wished the serving had slightly more because of bones), with the beans and their sauce providing additional flavor and saltiness.Atmosphere: Could Be Better (2 of 5), but it's great that Café Mofongo has chosen to focus on quality, low-priced food. Although eating in is possible, it is best to order out. Customer amenities are sparse -- there no customer bathrooms or regular tables -- but there is a ledge that rings much of the restaurant for eating while seated on bar chairs, or while standing. I look forward to returning.

Title: A Rare Gem in Murray Hill – A Love Letter to Rare

I must confess, Rare has stolen my heart and it's high time I shout it from the rooftops – or at least in a review. Tucked away in the charming streets of Murray Hill, Rare is not just a local favorite of mine; it's a culinary revelation.

Why, you ask, does Rare deserve a gleaming five-star accolade? The answer lies in the extraordinary blend of exquisite food paired with prices that defy Manhattan's steep cost of living. But wait, there's more – an honest-to-goodness happy hour graces the bar daily from 5 to 7 pm, a true unicorn in the Big Apple.

Let's talk about the pièce de résistance: the lobster burger. This isn't your average seafood sandwich; it's a divine assembly of pure, hot lobster goodness sans the usual mayo and veggies found in a lobster roll. Served alongside mouthwatering Mexican corn and a pool of melted butter – it's a seafood lover's dream.

I'm not one to exaggerate when I say every burger I've tried here echoes the same level of culinary prowess. Even my particularly discerning parents left with their taste buds dancing in delight. And should you crave a side, let the French fry basket be your indulgence. With a seemingly endless portion of their cottage, sweet potato, and regular fries, complete with an array of dipping sauces, it's a feast. Do yourself a favor and try the cottage fries – they are nothing short of spectacular.

A brief note for the realists: yes, I encountered a mouse trap on a recent visit. It's New York, after all, and these critters are part of the scenery. I choose to see it as a sign of proactive pest control rather than a drawback.

In conclusion, whether it's for the ambiance, the food, or the value, Rare remains unmatched in my eyes. It stands as a testament to what a Manhattan eatery can and should be. Five stars without a doubt.

Title: Cuban Delights with a Side of Service Woes at Asere Que Bola

Asere Que Bola swept me off my feet with its authentic Cuban flavors, transporting me straight back to my roots with dishes that resonated with my heritage. The highlight of the night was undoubtedly the 'Ropa Vieja,' a dish I can only describe as obsession-worthy, even for someone who grew up on the traditional fare. Cooked to perfection, it was not oily and boasted a sauce that sang with flavor. Regrettably, the 'Plátano Bowl' it was served in fell short, tasting overly oily and detracting from the dish’s excellence.

The live band set the tone for the evening with an irresistible beat, making the cozy confines of the restaurant hum with vibrancy. The hostess embodied the warmth of Cuba itself, greeting us with open arms both over the phone and upon our arrival.

However, the service left much to be desired. Despite our large party of 12, including three eager children, the expected bread and butter to pacify our growling stomachs were notably absent, prompting an additional order. Our waitress seemed to vanish into thin air at times, with our table, seemingly her sole responsibility, often left unattended. This resulted in long waits and the disappointing sight of later arrivals tucking into their meals before us. While our food was prepared correctly, the drinks stumbled, diminishing the satisfaction of our dining experience.

The 'Paella' suffered from a lack of authenticity, echoing the sentiment of a boxed meal, with the seafood element more decorative than substantial. In contrast, the bartender shone like a polished glass, mixing Cuba Libres with a liberal hand and ensuring our spirits remained high.

In sum, Asere Que Bola offers a culinary journey worth taking for its delectable Cuban dishes. I find myself eager to return, hopeful that the service will rise to meet the high bar set by the cuisine and the convivial atmosphere.

During Resy Off-Menu week, I visited a restaurant that featured the Tumpeng platter, an impressive array of dishes priced at $68 per person, which seemed a bit steep. The platter showcased a variety of items including roasted baby chicken betutu, beef short rib rendang, lamb satay, prawn tamarind, and eggs balado, centralizing around a large cone of rice. Unfortunately, the beef rib was slightly over-charred and tough, though not inedible. The prawn tamarind stood out with its flavor, and the eggs balado were exceptionally soft and well-seasoned. However, the lamb satay was just passable. We added a side of corn fritters to our meal, which proved to be quite a delight. The restaurant's ambience was indeed pleasant, contributing to an enjoyable dining experience. Overall, while the food had its highlights, the high cost leaves me inclined to explore other dining options in the future.

Title: A Mexican Haven in the Heart of NYC - MAD Dog & Beans

From the moment I stepped into MAD Dog & Beans, the New York City frenzy melted away, replaced by the festive vibes of an authentically adorned Mexican eatery. The ambiance is vibrant and promises a lively happy hour, though my lunchtime visit was quieter, allowing for prompt seating and service.

The staff was notably accommodating, navigating our group through moments of menu hesitation with grace. We started with chips and a fresh pico de gallo-style salsa, a simple yet satisfying kick-off.

I indulged in a chicken burrito while my companions chose tacos, both dishes earning enthusiastic approval for their flavor and value. Adding to the allure is the restaurant's prime location, a short stroll from Penn Station, making it a convenient culinary escape for travelers and locals alike.

MAD Dog & Beans isn't just a meal; it's an experience I've eagerly shared with friends and one that I'm keen to repeat on my next city adventure.

Title: A K-Cuisine Gem Amidst the Urban Jungle

My quest for authentic K-cuisine amidst the bustling streets lined with karaoke and BBQ joints led me to a spot that’s been all the rage according to fellow food aficionados on Yelp. With no reservations, their nifty system managed wait times, and a handy waitlist via Yelp made the 70-minute anticipation bearable.

Entering the place was akin to stepping into a K-pop music video—a stark contrast to the homey Virginia eateries I'm familiar with. The hipster vibe was palpable, and I couldn’t help but feel a tad out of place amidst the urban chic crowd.

Opting for a combo, the food service was a whirlwind of efficiency—a delightful spectacle of small plate appetizers and meats sizzling away without the need for us to lift a finger, save to transport mouthwatering bites from grill to palate.

Missing rice on the menu threw me for a loop, but the carb-free experience didn’t detract from the overall delight. A standout was the seafood pancake—crispy, flavorful, and served in a generous portion that guaranteed leftovers.

For a taste of Korea with a dash of city flair, this NYC spot is a culinary adventure not to be missed.

Title: A Slice of Parisian Heaven at Our Favorite French Bakery and Cafe

Review:

There's a little piece of France tucked away in this charming bakery and cafe that has won our hearts. The menu offers a delectable range of classics, from perfectly assembled sandwiches to a sumptuous eggs Benedict that can only be described as a masterpiece. The quiche, too, is not to be missed, with its flaky crust and rich filling, each bite transporting you to a quaint Parisian bistro.

But the real stars of the show are the coffee and bakery items. The aroma of fresh pastries and bold coffee is a siren song you can't ignore. Each pastry is a work of art, and the coffee is nothing short of outrageous—in the best way possible. It's clear why this spot has become a beloved go-to for us. Whether you're a connoisseur or simply in search of a cozy spot to indulge, this French bakery and cafe is a must-visit.

Title: Underwhelming Experience at Toledo

I had high hopes for Toledo, keen to see why it was a favorite of my friend's, but was met with disappointment. The cuisine was unremarkable, lacking the vibrant flavors I anticipated. The only saving grace was the jamón, which was acceptable but hardly a culinary challenge. Service was overbearing, though the sparse patronage could make one more forgiving. The wine selection does earn some praise and contributed to the second star in this two-star review. Regrettably, with so many other establishments offering fine wine and more, I won't be returning.

The food is quite good. A bit pricy but hey it's Manhattan!I like especially the duck Lu feng, the Hunan charcuterie and winter melon. Very flavorful but not greasy! The pigs trotter was not what I imagined. There were more peppers than pork...the lotus meatball was also just ok. The flavor was good though just that the texture is a bit soft to my taste.

My first time having Detroit style pizza and I have to say that I am a fan of it! I don't know how authentic is it, but they definitely serve really good slices here. Each slice actually feels more like a retangular pie, which is cut into 4 squares. They are also thicker than your average New York style pizza. It almost feels like a in between of New York and Chicago style pizza. It's definitely something you can share with a friend or if you are truly hungry, it can be a large meal in itself. The classic is the pie that definitely gets you your bang for your buck because it's only $5, while the other specialty pies run about $10-$12, which is not bad for the amount you get. The first time I went, I got the pepperoni pie and they did not skimp on the pepperoni. You get a bite of pepperoni with each bite. The only downside was that it was a bit on the salty side, so I definitely needed water. I also wish there was a bit more cheese with it to balance out the saltiness. When I ordered my slice, they popped mine in after my friend's, but they took it out at the same time. It didn't come out as hot, so I should have had them put it in a little longer to get it more toasty. My friend ordered the mustard pie and that was definitely unique. It also has corned beef tucked under the cheese with a layer of mustard. Never would I have thought I would enjoy this, but it was very good. The mustard cuts some of the heaviness of the cheese since there isn't any sauce to it. The corned beef added some meatiness to it and balances it out a bit since mustard is quite sharp. We had never had so much mustard in one sitting, but it was definitely good. I came back a second time and this time tried the classic and the mushroom. The classic is a nice starter if you never really tried detroit style pizza and if you don't want to be fancy with the toppings. It's more sauce than cheese for the pies that have red sauce. They also put cheese first before sauce. The mushroom was definitely more heavy since it was just cheese and large pieces of mushrooms. This time when we went, the guy who took our order actually gave us the marinara sauce and vodka sauce to try, even though he said they are good on its on. They added more flavor to it which is nice to change it up, especially if you are eating 4 slices. I think it definitely helps with the pies that don't have sauce. The tang from the tomato sauce helps brighten up the pie when it feels a bit heavy on the palette. So if you go, I would suggest asking for sauce on the side so you can try to mix it up if you like. Aside from the food, the workers there are super friendly and lively. They definitely have a lot of character and make the whole experience more fun and inviting. They talk to you like they are your friends and I'm sure they are even more fun with regulars. The guy who took our order even told me his instagram handle and said he also likes to make videos with customers at time. The space itself isn't very big and there are only 3 standing tables for you to eat on, so if you want to sit and relax, you might want to take the pizzas to go elsewhere. If you haven't tried Detroit style pizza and want to give it a try for a decent price, try Lions and Tigers out!

Last evening at 5:30 pm, my boyfriend and I ventured out to celebrate his birthday at this establishment. The experience was largely elevated by the service provided by our server Gregory, whose attentiveness and warm birthday serenade earned our genuine appreciation.

We bypassed the weekend special, a 3-course delight for $49, in favor of the more expansive Prix Fixe menu at $85 per head, granting us a 4-course journey that promised much. The Tuna Tartare and Pastitsada as starters came highly recommended and did not disappoint. An additional splurge on the Astakomakaronada introduced a surprising sweetness to the squid ink linguini that was brimming with flavor. 

However, the journey hit a snag at the mains. The Xtenia Me Panseta (scallops with pork belly) suffered from an overzealous salt hand, and the Fileto Moscharisio (filet mignon), while generous, felt a tad underwhelming due to mild seasoning.

Redemption was found in the form of desserts. Both the walnut-infused Karidopita and the rich Sokolatina Xanthia were standouts, ending the meal on a high note. Despite the main course hiccups, the ambiance and impeccable service made the evening one to remember. We are enticed enough by the overall experience to plan a return visit.

Having long anticipated a visit to this local gem, my boyfriend and I finally seized the opportunity to dine in one evening before a film at Metrograph. We arrived at 6:30 PM on a weeknight, snagging the last available table in what I now realize is a deservedly popular spot.

The highlight of our meal was undeniably the spicy beef brisket huimei. The dry hand-pulled wide noodles had an authentic kick, perfectly complemented by tender beef that made the dish a standout. Equally impressive were the soup dumplings, each a delicate parcel of pork encased in a gossamer-thin wrapper that burst with savory broth upon the first bite. I find myself reminiscing about their impeccable balance of flavors and textures.

Portion sizes struck an ideal balance, satiating without being overwhelming, leaving us comfortably satisfied. This culinary experience has left me eager to return, next time with a group to share in the joy of the big tray chicken, which I've heard is not to be missed.

Place-  2 StarsFood-    2 Stars Staff-    5 starsDrinks- 5 Stars I wanted to love this place, especially since we came right after the Bettlejuice play, but was left kind of disappointed. We made reservations for 6:30pm on a Sunday night and were seated right away. When I say this place is tiny. I mean like really tiny. It's very uncomfortable because people are always bumping into your seat and there is no space to really relax. The decor is cute. Lots of wall art that pay homage to Tim Burton films. Staff was amazing from the waiter to the characters. When we went Jack Skellington and Mad Hatter were there. They were funny and friendly. They walked around and interacted with everyone. Ordered the Coco Skellington drink and it was amazing. I would return just for that drink. They make you get a pre-fix meal where you have to get an app and a entree for $40 which is not bad if the food was better. Half of the things on the app menu were sold out so we ended getting the Jambalaya and the Frankenstein fries. Jambalaya was okay. Lacked flavor. The fries were crispy and the best thing I ate through the entire meal. It came topped with blue cheese and a side sauce that was good For the entree my friend had the mac and cheese. That was better than I expected. I had the scissor burger and didn't care for it. No dessert options so we went to get ice cream near by afterwards. This is one of those places that you go to for the experience and that is it. Go for the drinks too. They are really good and worth the visit. I honestly wouldn't recommend the food. Also, they sell lipsticks that are named after some of the characters in the movies. A lady came by showing them to us which was a little weird for me as you are eating.

Title: A Refined Taste of Vietnam at Ginger and Lemongrass

Ginger and Lemongrass offers an elevated dining experience, pairing the authenticity of Vietnamese cuisine with a touch of modern finesse. The move to their more spacious locale hasn't diminished the charm and warmth that regulars cherish. The menu, reasonably priced for its upscale vibe, boasts an impressive selection of pho, each with a unique and deeply satisfying flavor profile.

The fried spring rolls with shrimp are an essential start—crisp, well-seasoned, and the perfect prelude to the heartier mains. As a seasoned patron, I can't help but recommend the BBQ pork pho, a personal favorite. Meanwhile, my husband swears by the richness of the beef bone marrow pho, a must-try for newcomers.

While the sparkling iced ginger lemonade errs on the spicier side of ginger, the beverage selection is commendable. Lastly, street parking is a breeze, especially on Sundays, adding to the overall convenience and enjoyment of the experience. Ginger and Lemongrass is a culinary gem worth a visit for anyone craving authentic Vietnamese fare with a contemporary twist.

My friend and I ate dinner here one Saturday evening right before our Broadway show. The restaurant was clean with a cool decor. The staff were amazing and super friendly.  The owner came out and introduced himself and took pictures with me and my friend. My friend and I ordered the same entree and I was pissed because I always like to try other food from others plate,  lol. We both ordered the fried chicken with mash potatoes and biscuit. Before our meal came we were served these yummy sliced apples with a sauce. My chicken was good, not the best I've ever had and not the worse. The mash potatoes and biscuit were delicious. I was concerned that I wouldn't eat all of my food because I usually have leftovers and I didn't want to take a bag to the theater. However,  not this time,  I ate everything on my plate and my belly was satisfied. Lol. I would definitely check this place out again to try some other menu items.  Oh and I loveeeee the fact that they had electrical sockets by most of the tables,  woo hoo. You know we always need to charge something. Lol

Title: A Late-Night Delight in China Town: Noodle Soup Nirvana

Last night's adventure led us to a culinary gem in the heart of China Town that caters to the night owls. Boasting a minimalist and impeccably clean interior, this restaurant specializes in a tantalizing array of noodle soups. Vegetarians need not worry, with thoughtful options like tomato, spicy, spicy pepper, and coconut curry broths—all pork-free and customizable with veggie sides.

The extensive side dish offerings are impressive, but the star of my meal was the Original YunShang Rice Noodle bowl. Laden with an array of toppings from pork slices to shrimp and quail eggs, the experience of crafting my soup in a steaming clay bowl was as satisfying as it was delicious. The spicy broth variant I sampled packed even more flavor, both light and devoid of excess oil, allowing the ideal consistency of the rice noodles to shine through.

Not to be missed, the Salty Crispy Chicken with its spicy mayo dip was an absolute knockout—perfect for sharing. Portion sizes are generous, providing great value for the price.

Service was exemplary, accommodating my vegetarian friend with ease and patience during my moments of indecision. All in all, this spot is a must-visit for a delightful and affordable feast served up with care.

Title: Late-Night Comfort at Cozy Soup 'n' Burger

After a night of laughs at the Broadway Comedy Club, my boyfriend and I found ourselves at Cozy Soup 'n' Burger around 2 am on a Sunday. The place was bustling, yet we secured a table immediately. Cravings guided our order towards breakfast staples - eggs, rye bread, home fries, pancakes, and English muffins. To our delight, service was speedy without sacrificing quality; our hot, fresh meal arrived promptly.

As an onion enthusiast, I requested them in my eggs, and the chef obligingly diced them. However, the onion-to-egg ratio was overwhelming, which slightly marred an otherwise satisfying dish.

The highlight was our server who deftly advised us on menu choices, ensuring we got the most bang for our buck. Cozy Soup 'n' Burger offered a warm, welcoming experience with just a minor hiccup. Would recommend for anyone seeking a hearty meal into the wee hours. 4/5 stars.

Highly recommend coming for Happy Hour! The sangria is $9 a glass, and both the red and white were delicious and stronger than you'd think! As for the tapas, I had the Cojonudo ($6, chorizo/quail egg on little toast pieces), Tortilla Espanola ($8, quiche-like potato omelet), Patatas Bravas (fried potatoes with salsa and garlic aioli), and Escalivada ($8, eggplant/red pepper with flatbread). I also added an entree order of the Albondigas ($16, lamb meatballs). The garlic aioli on the Patatas Bravas was amazing, but my favorite tapas dish was the Escalivada because of the warm, soft flatbread! The Albondigas was also delicious, although pricey for a small dish. The happy hour specials are a steal though!

I stopped by for a regular slice, anticipating a hearty New York-style portion. Unfortunately, it was surprisingly undersized, feeling about half the size of what's customary. Given the $4 price tag, I was expecting something exceptional, but alas, it didn't hit the mark.

Title: A Disappointing Venture into Vietnamese Cuisine

I was left utterly disheartened after dining at what I can only describe as a poor representation of Vietnamese culinary tradition. With cost as its only redeeming factor, the restaurant failed to deliver on the intricate flavors and authenticity that Vietnamese food is celebrated for, serving instead a diluted, Americanized version that missed the mark considerably.

Our meal consisted of a Pork Meatball Banh Mi and Spring Rolls. The banh mi was a letdown, leaning on sriracha for heat in place of the customary jalapeños, devoid of the refreshing crunch of cucumbers, featuring lackluster pork meatballs, and enveloped in bread reminiscent of a common hoagie, stripping away the delight of a true Vietnamese baguette. The spring rolls fared no better; they were a bland assembly of noodles, lettuce, and shrimp, glaringly absent of the essential fresh herbs that epitomize the vibrancy of Vietnamese rolls, accompanied by a dipping sauce that could only be described as watery soy sauce.

The service did offer a glimmer of warmth with a pleasant lady behind the counter, and the establishment did sell an array of Chinese and Vietnamese goods. Sadly, this did little to compensate for the overall disappointing culinary experience.

Came here on a Tuesday evening with a reservation at 7pm and was seated right away. The service here was truly great, and I'd say efficient. Food came out in an orderly fashion, taking the time to clear the plates and silverware every time. The venue a was pretty big and nicely decorated as well. For food, I tried the tasting menu. Price-wise, it is definitely worth more than getting the dishes separately. That said, I would say this place is pretty contemporary and modern. The presentation was really nice. I thought the taste profiles were interesting, and mixed different flavors and textures. I think it worked well in some cases, but not so much. My favorite of the night would probably be the beet dish. The dessert on the other hand wasn't for me. It was super tart that I couldn't really eat it sadly.

Title: Charming Italian Essence with a Touch of Moonshine

Review:

Upon entering the restaurant, I was enveloped by an authentically Italian ambiance that promised an immersive dining experience. The waitstaff were knowledgeable and offered excellent recommendations, although the bus boys could improve on the prompt clearing of plates.

The location on the ground level boasts a quaint yard, perfect for warm weather dining, which was an unexpected setting as I anticipated a rooftop view. This, however, did not detract from the overall charm.

Culinary-wise, the meal commenced with an array of appetizing starters; baked clams, scallops, octopus, and meatballs, each bursting with perfect flavor. The breaded veal main course, while fresh, fell a little flat in taste, but the ravioli special filled with shrimp, lobster, and calamari dazzled as the best ravioli experience to date.

A delightful surprise was the serving of Italian moonshine with dessert, a unique offering that quite literally added a spirited finish to our coffee and complemented the three bottles of wine savored during our extensive lunch.

In conclusion, the restaurant delivered a memorable Italian encounter, complete with exceptional food and a unique twist on tradition. I eagerly anticipate my next visit, ideally on a sunny day to fully enjoy the idyllic outdoor setting.

If you're on the hunt for a charming brunch spot with affordable fare, this is the place for you. The cheese grits are a highlight—expect them to be exceptionally flavorful and creamy. It's also refreshing to see turkey bacon on the menu, a thoughtful alternative for those who skip pork. Their French toast is another delight, tender and infused with fruit, topped with fresh strawberries for an extra burst of flavor. Plus, the fact that it's open 24 hours is just the cherry on top. Highly recommend for a satisfying brunch experience!

What great addition to the neighborhood.  This cozy spot has been open since September 2019, which still makes them the new kid on the block, but their food and service are making a big impact and creating regulars already.  Alison is not a bottomless brunch spot, but the quality of the food is a reminder that you do not need a boozy brunch to enjoy a good meal.  They do offer brunch cocktails such as your typical mimosas and bloody marys but also offer a grapefruit spritzer, that includes cava.  Alison is a place where I would brunch with my girlfriends to catch up, dine alone, and dive into a good book while awaiting my food, or an excellent place for families.  What I love about Alison is it is a place for everyone, due to the diverse food menu, welcoming waitstaff, and beautiful open space.

Title: Bubbly Brunch with a Side of Mediocrity

My latest outing to this spot marked my second visit, a testament to the convivial atmosphere that makes it a magnet for group gatherings. Their boozy brunch, a lively affair reminiscent of a day club, is worth noting for the sheer volume of choices available at a reasonable price point. Be prepared for a dimly lit space where the music drowns out conversation—a small price to pay for the revelry.

Service is a high point, with attentive yet unobtrusive staff ensuring a flowing supply of food and drink. Speaking of drinks, the vast selection for brunch entices, but be wary; options like the sake sangria and margarita disappoint with their diluted flavors.

Food, unfortunately, doesn't quite live up to the establishment's lively ambiance. While the crispy potatoes shine, other offerings range from lukewarm Korean fried chicken that fails to replicate past glory, to a forgettable chicken chilaquiles. Soggy duck buns, insipid kimchi fried rice, and rubbery fish chicharron exemplify missed opportunities, and one is better off avoiding the sushi rolls with their off-putting texture. There are some redeeming plates, like the well-executed plantains and the warm, tasty Thai chicken empanadas, but these are exceptions in a sea of mediocrity.

In summary, this place offers a raucous good time with capable service but is let down by its less-than-impressive food and drink options. It seems the more you indulge in their bottomless beverages, the more forgiving your palate becomes—a detail worth considering before diving into their culinary offerings.

I recently visited this restaurant with high hopes, but left feeling underwhelmed. Initially, the service was attentive; however, my experience was marred when my sweet potato fries arrived cold and needed to be replaced. To make matters worse, I discovered what appeared to be a beard hair amidst my fries, which was off-putting. On a brighter note, the guac burger was decent, offering a taco-like flavor that provided some redemption. Unfortunately, the seasonal lemonade, which was matcha-flavored, failed to impress and was quite unpalatable. Overall, the visit was a letdown due to the issues with both the food and beverage.

Title: A Nostalgic Bite at Tad's Steak in Manhattan

In the heart of Manhattan, where culinary sophistication often reigns supreme, Tad's Steak stands as a testament to a bygone era. Forget the grass-fed, hormone-free buzzwords, this is a place where simplicity and nostalgia take center stage.

Walking in, you are greeted with wood paneling, red walls, and cozy stained glass lights. New York City's iconic photographs adorn the walls, reminding you of a different time. The front area, complete with a visual menu over the flame grill, invites you to order with ease.

At Tad's, a no-frills meal awaits. Your plate will be laden with a satisfactory piece of steak or chicken, a baked potato, an ample slice of garlic bread, and a simple salad with your choice of dressing. The garlic bread, ready to sop up the beef stock and onion flavors, is a highlight, as unconventional as that may sound. And if you feel like it, a pre-poured glass of wine, amusingly sealed with plastic wrap, is there to add a touch of 'fancy.'

Word to the wise: order your steak a notch below your desired doneness—I learned this the hard way with a well-done prime rib instead of the medium rare I anticipated.

Seating is spacious but not particularly comfy, and the ambient temperature seemed unusually warm. Yet, you'll find all the necessary condiments at your disposal on the no-nonsense tables.

Tad's Steak doesn't promise a gourmet experience; rather, it delivers a slice of New York City's less polished but more affordable past. However, time is running out to savor this nostalgic eatery, slated to close its doors soon. Tad's is more about the memory than the menu, and if you're yearning for a taste of old New York, this is your chance.

Stopped by for a couple of slices while waiting for our train... The employees were friendly and the pizza was pretty good as well, the only problem was that we took a seat at the counter to eat our slices and we were approached by numerous people asking for money. My fiancé actually gave his pizza to a woman who said she was hungry. I mean I do feel bad for anyone who is in need but after he gave the pizza away a man then approached and when we said we couldn't help him out with any money he got rather aggressive and started saying all kinds of rude things... I couldn't wait to get out of there... Now I know this isn't the businesses fault but it really puts their patrons in an uncomfortable situation.
Food was fresh. Service was real fast. Price was good. So this is a place I would come back to if in the neighborhood and feeling like having poke.

Title: A Slice of Heaven in NYC

If you’re on the quest for the ultimate pizza experience, look no further. This gem has skyrocketed to the top of my pizza hierarchy, not just in New York City, but globally. The craving for their slices is real; I’d happily indulge daily if I could. The sauce is the standout – rich, plentiful, and utterly delectable. Combine that with the melt-in-your-mouth cheese and the crust that strikes a divine balance between thick, crispy, and tantalizingly chewy, and you've got a pizza that renders you speechless.

Each visit leaves me eager to return, with the ambition to conquer every variety they craft. Considering the transcendent experience thus far, I trust each slice is a taste of the divine. This isn't just pizza; it's an edible revelation.

My friend and I recently visited this restaurant for Sunday brunch and were greeted by plenty of open seating. The atmosphere was pleasant, and while the service was competent, it failed to stand out. I opted for the vegetarian plate, which unfortunately did not meet my expectations in terms of flavor or freshness. Furthermore, the condition of the seating left something to be desired, as we noticed some chairs were notably damaged. However, I must commend their guacamole; it was the lone highlight in an otherwise unimpressive meal. With a myriad of superior dining options available in the city, I'm inclined to explore other venues rather than return here.

In recent months to the past year, the Midtown East area east of Park Avenue started to become somewhat of a hotspot for diverse (even if namebrand) food trucks.  On 3rd avenue itself, you'll get the likes of Neapolitan Express (which I remember eating way back in 2013 or so) and even Cousins Maine Lobster (yes the one Barbara Corcoran invested in on Shark Tank).Tibetan Nomad Momo finally makes its Midtown East debut.  For anyone who doesn't know what Momo is, it's basically South Asian dumplings.  Simple as that.  The truck itself is very self explanatory. The momo itself comes in different varieties:  traditional, pan fried, deep fried, steamed gravy, and fried gravy.  You can also get the Tibetan's own Shapaley too.All the options above can be made with beef, chicken, or veggies.  It's $6 for the traditional momos, $7 for the pan fried/deep fried momo, $8 for steamed gravy, and $9 for fried gravy.  Not bad pricing.  I went with the pan fried momo this time around although my unhealthy side of me preferred the deep fried one lol.  For 8 pieces, $7 is not a bad deal.  And it also tastes pretty damn good for a truck.  You get a variety of different sauces including chipotle, an avocado mayo, and sriracha.Enjoy it while you can!

Title: A Delightful Tapas Feast at Hao Yummy!

Review:

Hao Yummy is a gem for group dining, with tapas-style offerings that invite sharing and sampling. Expect to be satisfied with 2 to 3 plates per person. My husband raved about the Hotpot Beef Noodle Soup, praised for its freshness. The kids were taken by their Fried Noodles with Eggs and Vegetables, not a morsel left behind. 

The stars of my evening were the semi-spicy Jellyfish Salad, a harmonious blend of texture and heat, the Pot-Stewed Pork Intestines which were rich in flavor, and the Dandan noodles, perfectly balanced in spice. 

While the Lapsang Souchong tea's presentation might strike some as extravagant, the deep, smoky essence was utterly transporting—albeit quite abundant in volume. 

The restaurant's minimalist decor enhances the dining experience, allowing the vibrant dishes to take center stage. Service was attentive without exception.

Additionally, Hao Yummy accommodates all guests with wheelchair access and gender-neutral restrooms. Note that there’s a limit of two credit cards per table for payment. 

In summary, Hao Yummy is your go-to for a deliciously eclectic meal in a welcoming, modern environment.

My boyfriend and I reserved a table at this predominantly walk-in restaurant for our anniversary dinner, and it didn't disappoint! The staff went above and beyond to ensure our celebration was memorable, with special kudos to our server, Sarah, who was nothing short of amazing. The highlight of the meal had to be the scallops – they were simply divine and a must-try for any future patrons. We're already excited about our next visit!

Title: A Pleasant Lunch Special with Mixed Impressions

I recently opted for a pickup lunch from a local eatery on a Saturday and came away with a mixed bag of impressions. Ordering their $12 lunch special, an efficiently prepared package surprised me with an included serving of white rice, not mentioned online.

The standout of my meal, a pair of chicken and shrimp dumplings, shone bright alongside a soy sauce concoction. The accompanying house soup was unremarkable yet comforting with its standard broth, glass noodles, veggies, and a few tofu morsels. A side of roti delivered with a flaky texture that added a nice variety to the meal.

Unfortunately, the "housemade" garlic bread was a letdown, a creation I could easily surpass in my own kitchen, lacking any unique twist I had hoped for in a Thai restaurant. On the other hand, the coconut sticky rice was an absolute highlight, served as a delightful mini-log wrapped in leaf, offering a sweet and well-infused coconut flavor that could pass for dessert.

As for the main dish, the green curry, it was packed with chicken and a rich ensemble of coconut milk, Thai eggplants, string beans, bell peppers, bamboo shoots, and basil. However, my request for a "very spicy" dish felt unmet, barely tickling my heat tolerance. The curry was tasty but far from the authentic Thai spice I anticipated.

Overall, the experience was decent, with some hits and misses. Next time, I'm tempted to challenge the chef's spice game with a direct request for "phet mak," in hopes of achieving the fiery kick I crave.

People love this place and I have come here once before so had to bring my wife this time. We ordered a bunch of different slices. The vodka square tastes like there is a parmesan crust. The texture is quality and the flavor is good.  I don't think I could eat more than 1 because it is a little heavier but nothing wrong with that.  The upside down slice is also solid. The regular slice was also top notch. The crust on the regular slice is very good. We also tried the sausage onion slice as a little curveball and the flavors worked. The square could be offputting for some because of the heaviness and the unique flavor of the crust.  In terms of NYC, this is a top 10 place for a slice!The kicker here is the great customer service.  The one guy working the register there is very friendly and does a good job of making the place feel welcoming. 4 stars all the way!

Title: A Hidden Gem with a Twist on Thai Cuisine

Upon approaching the bustling scene outside this cozy eatery, it's immediately clear why it's a local hotspot. The informal waiting system, a simple notebook for info jotting, adds to its charm. Seating was prompt post-ordering, and the food arrived swiftly thereafter.

The menu breaks tradition, inviting diners to select a protein and pair it with inventive bases like pad Thai or basil udon. The appetizer platters, a value at $23-$25, are a must-try. In fact, the platter alone sufficed as a hearty entrée for some in our group, with the standout being the sublime 8oz grilled skirt steak.

The crispy duck udon earned its reputation with a flawless execution, while the crispy crab pad see ew, though an innovative concept, lacked the punch in flavor I anticipated. The crab and egg amalgamation didn't resonate with my palate; I found myself longing for more robust crab chunks.

A top tip: Utilize Yelp's check-in for a Thai iced tea at a mere dollar. And for those who prefer to pay with paper over plastic, you'll be rewarded with a 10% discount.

Verdict: This spot is a testament to culinary creativity and value—an experience that's undeniably worth the buzz.

I recently visited this spot for a weekday lunch and decided on the steak and fontina panini. Priced around $10, it was fairly aligned with my lunch budget—not exactly a bargain but worth it for the substantial portion served. The sandwich was expertly heated, maintaining a consistent warmth all the way through, a detail I greatly appreciated as many delis tend to skimp on the toasting time, leaving you with a lukewarm center. It was a satisfying meal that truly hit the spot. While I'm enticed by the variety of lunch options nearby, I would consider returning here for another solid sandwich experience.

Title: A Toast to Good Times and Tasty Bites

My experience at this spot has been truly satisfying. The drinks, notably the bulldogs, are a must-try, especially during happy hour when they steal the spotlight with their perfectly balanced kick of alcohol. Swift seating on both my visits meant I dove into the vibe without delay.

The staff are attentive, ever-present to meet your needs with just a wave. On to the food – simply put, it's delectable. The freshness is undeniable; you can't miss the buckets of plantains making their rounds, a testament to their kitchen's commitment to freshness.

The sancocho stole my heart with its rich flavors. It's a thick, hearty soup that begs for a side of rice, an ideal duo in my book. And if you're planning a group outing, grab one of the large tables in the back and maybe bring some games – it's the perfect setup for a night of fun and feasting.

Tucked away in the basement level of the bustling Dekalb Market Hall, Han Dynasty's NYC offshoot offers an intriguing dining ambiance. With its open layout shrouded in darkness, punctuated by vibrant, flashy lights, the atmosphere here diverges into a more casual realm compared to its Philadelphia counterparts.

Although it still categorizes itself as a sit-down restaurant, don't expect the same level of attentiveness you might have experienced in Philly; the service here leans more towards the fast-casual end of the spectrum.

For those familiar with the delights of Han Dynasty, their signature dishes like the succulent Dumplings in chili oil, the ever-comforting Dan Dan noodles, and the fiery Dry Pepper Style fish continue to please. These favorites certainly scratch that itch for genuine spicy Szechuan cuisine, making Han Dynasty a convenient and satisfying choice right in NYC.

This is the first time I am trying kimbap. I went with the beef one. The old couple make it fresh when you order it. It was nice. I think I will have to eat kimbap a couple more times before I get used to the taste. Banana milk drink was also nice.

Overall a very solid spot with plenty of delicious cocktails plus food options. Picked this spot during Restaurant Week but it turns out Sundays were not included. Located in a trendy part of the UES, there are plenty of delicious restaurants in the surrounding area so please read this review bearing this in mind. 3 stars here for their inconsistency of dishes. We ordered the chicken parmigiana dish (mixed with pasta & marinara sauce) but most of the dish was taken up by cold pasta. But then turning around and ordering the mussels: delicious.
