Very well seasoned in a bowl of soup perfect for scarpetta (italian term used for dipping bread in sauce).Our cocktails were good but not amazing. Their side dishes were killer (especially the mac 'n cheese) yet their service was only average - being checked on by our waitress only once. Ultimately, a decent spot for plenty of cocktail / food options in the American-style cuisine arena, but don't expect fireworks when sitting down for a meal here.

Title: A Brunch Experience that Turned into an Impromptu Dance Party

I recently visited a restaurant that managed to exceed my expectations, not just with its solid food and cool rustic decor, but with an atmosphere that was nothing short of electric. The service was good, and the "Bashment Punch" was a delightful brunch beverage.

But let's cut to the chase: the music is the heartbeat of this place. My friends and I attended a birthday brunch during their special "Caribbean Sunday," and DJ Fragg had us captivated. His mix of Dancehall hits, Afro Beats, Reggaeton, and Soca was impeccable, with smooth transitions that kept everyone's energy up – the entire table couldn't resist standing up to dance!

It's one thing for a restaurant to be "lit," but this was "LIT LIT!" There was talk amongst the patrons about converting the restaurant into a full-blown "Bashment" party, and honestly, I wouldn't have objected.

In short, if you're the type to enjoy a side of dancing with your dining, don't walk – dance your way to this place the next chance you get. It's a must-visit for anyone looking to eat, drink, and groove.

To be quite honest, I liked Woo Lae Ok better than The Woo. When I was in elementary school, I'd go to Woo Lae Ok and it was such a homey and nice restaurant. The Woo is a modernized Korean restaurant that's trying too hard to be fancyI'm giving it 5 stars though because it is a nice restaurant. It's a bit upscale looking but I enjoyed my meal. The meat was great, but the service isn't there to cook the meat for you, which could be a pro or con depending on your take.

FAB FILIPINO FOOD!!!I've been dying to dine here since it opened, but sadly never made it until this past Saturday evening. Being a Filipino living in the City, it was long overdue, but well worth the wait. I made a rez online & the host was going to seat us at the bar counter right at the entrance of the restaurant. It was date night with my hubby so we decided to wait for a table in the dining room. The host had said we should have called to make the rez bc we could have given our preference over the phone as making a rez online doesn't let you know that bar seating is a possible option. We waited about 20mins from our 8:30pm rez and we got a table half way back by the bathrooms & the window to the kitchen. Tables are tight especially if you order 2 apps and 3 entrees plus 2 small bowls of rice like we did. We also ordered specialty drinks that the friendly bartender had recommended. Our waitress was friendly & gave great suggestions on the food which was all spot on. We ordered ketchup pork ribs & lumpia shanghai to start and chicken adobo, mussels, & short ribs entrees. Everything from drinks, apps, & entrees were PERFECT! All flavorful & cooked to delicious tenderness. I was raised on this cuisine, so I would know! I HIGHLY recommend a fun & fab Filipino dining experience here!

Title: Decent Experience at a Bustling Korean BBQ Spot

My partner and I visited this Korean BBQ hotspot on a Sunday evening and found ourselves amidst a throng of diners, leading to a wait time that exceeded the estimated 30-40 minutes by quite a stretch—we clocked in at over an hour and 20 minutes before being seated. The draw for us was my boyfriend's eagerness to try Korean BBQ for the first time.

Once seated, we ordered the USDA marinated platter which was satisfying, although the meat portions were notably smaller compared to other venues I've frequented. That said, the smaller portions suited me fine as I'm not a big meat consumer, and the reasonable pricing made this less of an issue.

Service was a mixed bag. Our waiter was attentive to the point of feeling overbearing; his constant presence gave the impression he was hurrying us along, overshadowing our dining experience.

The venue was neat and ran like a well-oiled machine, aspects I greatly appreciated. However, a concern arose regarding accessibility—the bathrooms were incredibly cramped, seemingly not accommodating to individuals with disabilities.

Overall, I'm inclined to rate this restaurant three stars. While the cleanliness and efficiency were commendable, they will need to address the lengthy wait times and over-zealous service. And of course, ensuring proper accessibility is crucial.

I came here for the $1 oyster happy hour deal and that turned into having dinner here. They have some awesome deals with their oysters which included getting 6 oysters with a glass of wine for $13.I got the Cajun Lobster Roll with french fries. This came with what I think is Tartar Sauce along with ketchup and I used up the entire tartar sauce as dipping sauce for the fries as it was just that good. The lobster roll is really good with a nice amount of lobster meat on delicious toasted bread. I also got to try some of the Creamy Seafood Pasta which was pretty light on the cream and tasted pretty good as well.

Stumbled upon this gem after some errands and couldn't resist the allure of fresh sushi. The ambiance is sleek and spotless, complemented by the warm welcome of an informative greeter who champions their ethos of freshness and speed. To celebrate National Avocado Day, I indulged in a shrimp tempura roll and a salmon avocado hand roll; both surpassed expectations. A helpful tutorial on unwrapping the hand roll's clever packaging preserved the crispness of the seaweed, a testament to their attention to detail. This establishment outshines the standard pre-packaged sushi experience by leaps and bounds. Highly recommend a visit for an elevated quick sushi fix.

After many failed attempts, my gal pal and I finally did a restaurant for NYC Restaurant Week, and for whatever reason, we can never seem to try other places besides Butter.  It's a trustworthy staple if you're a reoccurring RW fan like us, but sadly, I don't see coming any other time but for RW.  Expect to shell out $42 per person to partake in the RW Menu selection, and it's three choices for the appetizers and entrees, and only two desserts to decide on.  I would've liked a little more variety since it was very heavy on the fish.   This brand new location though, was well worth the move - it's absolutely gorgeous and pales in comparison to their previous location.For appetizers, I started with the Sea Bass tartar, while Marilyn R. got the short ribs.  Out of the two, I personally think the short ribs were the way to go to get the most bang out of your buck.  My tartar was yes, small, but the fish was fresh and the minced vegetable mix that came with it was very refreshing.  It was a snack, not really an appetizer.Entrees, I decided on the duck breast, which was, again, sparse, but was very flavorful.  The duck was not gamey at all, and over the bed of sauteed kale and other greens, it was a perfect compliment.  Again, I could've definitely loved a bit more, but alas, it's Restaurant Week.The millionaire shortbread should be the only dessert you really bother with.  It is like Christmas Day with melted caramel, chocolate, and the shortbread.  It's oven warm and it will soothe your soul.  This is scrap the plate kinda need this more in my life - kind of a dessert.  It was the clear star of the whole experience.90 minutes from start to finish, and they really were eager to take our plates, even if we weren't done, and did have to tell them so more than once.  I like the 5 star feel, but there was too much hovering of the wait staff; let me lick my fork in peace.

JeJu Noodle Bar was actually amazing and lives up to its Michelin star. We ordered their prix fixe set for $45 per person. I was initially skeptical that this would be enough food for two, but it was quite filling and really delicious. The dishes came one at a time and we were started off with Pork Pyunche Seasonal Salad. This came with pork, roe, and various seafood such as octopus and even scallop. It was so good and seasoned perfectly. Then came toro ssam bap with the seaweed in a different container so we can wrap the toro in the seaweed ourselves. This was not only interactive but equally good. Honestly, the two are tied for my favorite dishes out of everything we tried from the set.Next up was the jeju chicken. The inside was so tender and the outside was very crispy. Afterwards, we had the hot stone rice which was similar to clay pot with salmon on top. You're advised to mix the salmon up with the rest of the bowl. Our last dish of the set was the ramen we chose at the beginning. We went with Jeju Bibimmyun and were mistakenly expecting something with broth. Unfortunately, we did not enjoy it as much as the other dishes. The noodles were hidden underneath the vegetables and egg and it reminded me of a more elevated version of the ramen from spicy ramen challenge. All in all, the experience was a really good one and I would love to go back for another ramen that has broth and reorder their appetizers.

Title: A Delightful Dinner at 2nd Deli

My recent visit to 2nd Deli proved to be a delightful experience. From the moment we entered, the welcoming greeting and swift seating set a positive mood. The matzo ball soup was a tasty start to our meal, bursting with flavor and comfort.

The main course didn't disappoint, with a pastrami sandwich that was both hearty and succulent, while the chicken tenders and grilled chicken sandwich were equally satisfying, each dish evidencing the kitchen's attention to taste and quality. The French fries were a scrumptious side, perfectly complementing the mains.

Service throughout the evening was attentive without being intrusive. While the prices were slightly above average, the quality and overall dining experience justified the cost. In summary, 2nd Deli offers a warmly recommended culinary adventure for those in search of great food and a welcoming atmosphere.

Came here for birthday dinner and was excited to try their omakase menu, it was easy to make reservations and there was plenty of seating when we got here. Biggest highlight of my night was spotting Sara Ramirez( Callie Torres in greys anatomy) here anyways... I was too shy to say Hi and I thought it might be rude to interrupt someone enjoying their dinner so I decided to just admire from afar.The appetizer was decent I wasn't a fan of the shrimp it was wayyyy too sweet and the hamachi in truffle was meh, didn't really stand out. The avocado fries however was different in a good way, I've never had fried avocado and I actually don't mind it! The mayo dipping sauce could have used a little lemon or a little Siracha kick but it was still good. The omakase for amount of food is really worth it for $75 you get ALOT of food, however I think this type of omakase is suited for people who like traditional omakase where there isn't much frills to the sushi peices, I on the other hand prefer truffle and yuzu and jalepenos and gold flakes twist to my omakase and found this a little bland. The wasabi is in the sushi already so they don't offer that on the side. Service was friendly and the waiter came around the introduce the fish and refill our water. If traditional omakase is what you like then I would recommend this.

Having buzzed through social media with rave reviews, the anticipation for the opening of Pepper Lunch in New York was high, and it didn't disappoint. Mimicking a fast-food service model, you're greeted by an efficient ordering process - select your meal at the entrance, receive a number, and within minutes of sitting down, you're ready to play chef at your table.

I opted for the Sambar Pepper Rice and wasn't let down. The combination of rice and sauce hit the mark, though the beef component lacked a bit of the punch I was expecting. That said, the overall experience was satisfying, and Pepper Lunch warrants a return visit next time I find myself in the neighborhood.

Title: A Valentine's Day Delight at Olio e Piu

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Olio e Piu, and despite a Valentine's Day hiccup on my part (I walked in without a reservation), it turned into a five-star experience. The staff advised a later return for available seating, and after killing time nearby, we were seated at the chef's counter with a bustling kitchen view. The atmosphere was enhanced by the authentically warm and attentive service, particularly from Maya, who made us feel exceptionally welcome.

The real showstopper was the food. I'm no pasta expert, but Olio e Piu has converted me. Each dish showcased perfectly al dente pasta, justly highlighting the freshness and skillful preparation. In sum, this gem has won me over. If you're undecided on a date night locale, look no further — Olio e Piu is a must-visit.

I recently visited a charming, cozy spot for an afternoon lunch that truly impressed. The highlight was the Tropical Storm drink—a delightful, flavorful concoction that set a high bar. Meanwhile, the appetizers didn't disappoint, offering a tasty prelude to the meal. An interesting twist was the option to add bacon to their guacamole, a combination that I found both unique and delicious. Additionally, the prices were quite reasonable for the area, making it a great value for a midday treat. Highly recommend for a casual dining experience with a touch of inventiveness.

Title: Burger Bliss at its Best

If you consider yourself a burger aficionado, then prepare to meet your match. This place serves up what may very well be the most delectable burger you'll ever sink your teeth into. The star of the show is a perfectly cooked patty, nestled between a buttery bun, accompanied by caramelized onions, fresh tomato, and a crisp leaf of lettuce. Though I typically pass on pork belly, this burger might just convert me; my friends can't stop raving about it. The complementary side of fries and a tangy pickle round out this gustatory delight.

Just today, I had burgers delivered to the office for myself and four colleagues, and the gratitude was overflowing—everyone was thoroughly impressed. What's more, the kitchen nails the cook on the meat every time, whether you're a medium-rare enthusiast or prefer it well-done.

Not in a burger mood? Opt for the dinner pasta—a savory mix of rigatoni, pancetta, green garlic, fennel, and parmesan that's simply irresistible. And to wash it all down, the "Diplomatic Immunity" cocktail, with its fusion of rum, ginger, and honey, is a must-try.

The restaurant itself exudes a fantastic ambiance paired with a killer playlist. Don't just take my word for it, though—treat yourself to a meal here and experience the hype firsthand.

Hatsuhana falls into an awkward category of sushi where it's a bit too corporate and austere (and pricey) for a fun, casual sushi gathering with friends, yet not indulgent/high quality enough to be meant for a splurgey celebration dinner. It's the "radical middle" of a sushi dinner.The thing that they're really known for is the Box of Dreams ($48) which has 9 squares of various sashimi (about 2-4 pieces each) over beds of rice. It's more food than it looks, and I was pretty stuffed by the end of the meal.Service is out of your face (in a good way) yet effective (e.g. water always re-filled). The ambience is very quiet and filled with business dinner types, making it a weird spot for a weekday date night (maybe better on a weekend).

Schnippers presents a bit of a conundrum with its interior—caught somewhere between fast-casual, chic, and industrial vibes. Nonetheless, it offered us a much-needed respite from the heat and a spot to refuel. I opted for the fresh market salad with chicken, maintaining my usual health-conscious choices. I was pleasantly surprised by the generous chicken portion. Meanwhile, my companion chose a burger which took a bit longer to arrive. Taking our time to peruse the menu was no issue as the place wasn't crowded, although the menu board's tiny print proved challenging; thankfully, an attentive associate provided us with readable menus and helpful suggestions. While I enjoyed my promptly-served salad, the wait for my friend's burger was slightly awkward. In all, Schnippers caters well to various tastes—even if the decor is a bit of a puzzle.

Title: A Sweet Spot with Some Room for Improvement

I recently visited a notable dessert bar renowned for its great desserts and was pleasantly surprised by the table service as opposed to the self-service system at their K-town location. Despite a prime-time visit at 10pm on a Thursday, our party of five only faced a brief wait of about 15-20 minutes before we could delve into their sweet offerings.

The standout for me was the Matcha Waterfall, an intriguing dessert that's not only a treat for the palate but also a feast for the eyes, thanks to the delightful pour effect when you cut into it. Paired with a scoop of condensed milk ice cream, the flavors were rich and well-concentrated, far from being watery or diluted.

My boyfriend enjoyed a Grapefruit Beer, which, despite its name, had a refreshing soda-like taste that complemented the dessert experience well. He also tried the Monkey Bread, which, while tasty, didn't quite hit the mark for him next to my stellar Matcha Waterfall.

The one drawback noted was the pricing; portions appeared somewhat small considering the cost. However, the service compensated for it, being efficient and friendly. For our next visit, the cookies are on our radar to see if they match the appeal of the rest of the menu.

Jeju Noodle Bar offers a Michelin-starred experience that's unique for its category. The ambiance is delightful, with a bright, spacious setting, sturdy wooden tables, and an eye-catching chandelier—reservation recommended.

We ventured into the truffle mushrooms, which although steep at $24, provided a memorable tableside truffle shaving that added a hint of luxury. The dish had well-balanced flavors, albeit slightly on the salty side. For a hearty choice, the Gochu Ramyun ($18) with added Bansuk ($2) brought together a symphony of spice and rich pork broth. However, like the mushrooms, the saltiness was pronounced. The pickled veggies offered a refreshing counterpoint, and the pork belly was a tender treat with a crispy edge, although the egg didn't quite rise to the occasion compared to others I've had.

The Miyuk Ramyun ($16), a vegetarian option, surprised us with a broth robust in flavor, which is quite a feat. A dab of chili oil enhanced it with a nice smoky kick that's highly recommended for the spice aficionados.

A notable quirk of Jeju is the dual role of cooks as servers. This unconventional approach resulted in less than ideal service; interactions felt more transactional with a lack of personal suggestions and awkward communication, specifically concerning menu queries.

In summary, while Jeju provides an enjoyable dining experience with reasonable prices for its status, it might not surpass the expectations one might have for a Michelin-starred establishment. The absence of a cocktail menu is also a minor letdown for those seeking a complete dining experience.

Title: Disappointing Experience at an Overrated BBQ Spot

Unfortunately, my recent visit to this NYC BBQ restaurant left much to be desired. Despite the pulled pork and brisket being extremely tender, they were surprisingly devoid of flavor. The absence of seasoning or a flavorful sauce to complement the high-quality meat was a significant letdown. The sauce options available on the table did little to enhance the meal, only adding to the disappointment.

For the price point, the portions didn't measure up, contributing to the overall sense that the experience was overpriced. Service was another low point; the staff seemed slow and inattentive, which put a damper on the evening.

The margaritas were another misstep – overly sweet, undersized, and lacking the traditional salted rim. This was a surprise as the restaurant boasts a nice selection of beers, served in charming mason jars, which was one of the few highlights.

The venue's rustic, southern charm did create a pleasant atmosphere, but ambiance alone isn't enough to compel a return visit. In a city brimming with culinary options, it's a shame that this BBQ joint misses the mark where it truly counts – the food and service.

Whenever le boyfriend asks me what do I want to eat, and my response is "I don't know". This spot has been our fail-proof "I don't know". Their ramen always hits the spot (I always get the Yuzu Kosho or Ajitama ramen), but the thing that keeps me coming back every time is their takoyaki. They're served piping hot and I've learned my lesson of not popping these bad boys into my mouth right after they're served (they're steaming hot). I tried their Karaage (fried chicken) for a change the other day, it's still pretty good but takoyaki is the winner got me.

Title: A Flavorful Oasis for Diverse Tastes

I recently dined at a charming spot that impresses with its well-crafted and delectable menu, suited for vegans, vegetarians, and carnivores looking for a plant-based twist. The standout dishes included the airy and crispy air fries served with a unique beet ketchup and an irresistible aoli sauce, which I preferred slightly more due to its texture. The taco salad, with its overly spicy yet flavorful seitan "beef," crispy tortillas, and scrumptious quinoa, is a healthy yet hearty choice.

The kale Caesar salad, surprisingly delightful even to someone who isn't keen on kale, takes the crown as my favorite, blending vegan parm, a creamy Caesar dressing, maple croutons, and salty shiitake bacon in a symphony of taste.

However, the soba noodles fell short, lacking the zest one would expect from a fusion of Japanese flavors and creative veganism. Despite this one miss, the pickup process is a breeze with their efficient app ordering system, ensuring your food is hot and ready upon arrival.

The ambiance of the restaurant adds to the experience, exuding homeliness with cozy swing chairs and a serene vibe amidst the city's hustle. Whether you're picking up or enjoying the tranquility onsite, this gem is worth recommending across the dietary spectrum.

I found this place on doordash when I wanted to switch up my usual Thai food routine (i.e. Up Thai). The delivery was exactly on time, and the food was very good. My only complaint is that the spicy fried rice with tofu could have been a little more generous on the tofu. It was a little spicy, but I'd probably request extra spicy next time. The sautéed Asian eggplant and tofu was very good. It's really more like mixed vegetables than eggplant, which is fine by me! It comes in a satisfying garlicky brown sauce. I would definitely get that dish again.

Upon an impromptu visit to this eatery, I sampled their ramen rice with chicken and a shrimp okonomiyaki. Pleasing to the palate, each dish, however, erred on the side of greasy, which might not appeal to everyone. A departure from tradition caught me off guard when I noticed the absence of bonito flakes atop the okonomiyaki; a staff member explained they incorporate it into the batter, an interesting twist but not quite to my liking. In comparison to the renowned Otafuku, this place falls a little short, especially when it comes to their okonomiyaki. Overall, a decent dining experience with room for improvement.

My recent visit to this restaurant left much to be desired, leading me to lean towards not returning. Attending with a large group exposed disorganization among the waitstaff, contributing to a less than smooth dining experience.

Our meal commenced with an assortment of appetizers, among which the Asian glazed wings were the standout, offering a well-executed combination of a crispy exterior with a sweet and sour glaze, topped with sesame seeds. The Mahi Mahi tacos, on the other hand, were unimpressive and forgettable.

The French Onion soup was a pleasant surprise, arguably the highlight of the menu. Its savory broth, semi-crunchy croutons, and delectable melted cheese provided a satisfying experience.

However, the main course did not maintain this standard. The classic burger with cheddar was disappointing. Despite its generous size, the patty was under-seasoned and lacked the depth of flavor one would expect.

In a city brimming with culinary options, I would suggest exploring other venues rather than settling for the mediocrity of this establishment.

Came here for dinner with my cousin, sister and fiancé. It was a short wait and definitely worth it. We ordered calamari, salt and pepper shrimp and the vegetable spring rolls for appetizers. The calamari was banging!! So much flavor! I ordered the pad see iew which was delicious. My cousin had pad Thai, my fiancé had the fish and my sister had curry chicken. I was impressed with the fish too! The presentation was so cool! They used a flavorful sauce on the fish. My fiancé also ordered a spicy drink which he enjoyed. The service was great. Someone continually refilled our waters without us asking despite how busy it was. We received our bill shortly after finishing. The turnover was really quick since there were other people waiting. Great service and great food! My only complaint was that the shrimp was not cleaned - I had to spit the shrimp shell out of my mouth. The taste of the shrimp was good but it was not enjoyable to eat since the shell was still on the shrimp. Overall, we loved this restaurant and would definitely return!

Nestled in the financial district lies a fantastic tavern that feels like a well-kept secret among locals. The staff, brimming with friendliness, and an exceptional bartender, create an inviting atmosphere that draws you in. Clearly a hotspot for regulars, the camaraderie is infectious, compelling newcomers to join in the lively exchange of drinks and stories.

The bar snack menu doesn’t disappoint, with their wings deserving a special shout-out - they're simply awesome. A night at this tavern isn't complete without the unspoken tradition of buying rounds for new and old friends alike, blurring the line between first-timers and long-time patrons. The sense of inclusivity here is unparalleled; you arrive as a guest but leave feeling like a part of the tavern's fabric. A highly recommended spot for those seeking a slice of local charm and delicious bites.

Title: An Unforgettable Feast for a Special Occasion

Our group of 33 gathered at this charming eatery for a momentous celebration, and our experience was nothing short of splendid. Planning was made effortless thanks to the ever-efficient Sophia, who helped us craft the perfect party package, complete with an irresistible steak add-on that elevated the evening.

Upon arrival, we were ushered to our cozy corner at the back, where two expansive tables awaited. The restaurant's flexibility shone when they graciously delayed our dinner service to accommodate latecomers.

A parade of family-style appetizers set the tone, with the stuffed mushrooms emerging as the star—guests couldn't resist sopping up every ounce of sauce with the complimentary bread. The calamari, with its satisfying crunch, was a close second.

The pasta offerings were a symphony of flavors: the seafood-abundant linguini, the rich rigatoni with eggplant and mozzarella, and the spaghetti with its towering meatballs.

As for the mains, the steak pizzaiola, in its cook-perfect glory and the tender chicken parmigiana, were the undisputed favorites, while the salmon held its own.

The sweet finale featured a dessert platter that was the talk of the table—the cannoli and tiramisu were particularly noteworthy, and the light cheesecake balanced the indulgence. Complimentary beverages flowed throughout the meal, ensuring we were well-hydrated as we dined and laughed into the night.

Alan and Mario, our servers, were the embodiment of exceptional service, matched only by their colleague whom we believe was named Mike. Their attentiveness was a significant contributor to the evening's success.

Despite an initial hiccup with a less-than-welcoming greeting, the rest of the night was faultless. We left with not only leftovers but cherished memories, eager to return for the simple pleasure of a good meal or another grand occasion.

Ikinari is an amazing steak place if you're running on a budget and want a decent customized/well-cooked steak. I've been here several times now, and to several locations and have never been disappointed. I usually always order the Ribeye (medium rare) and I swap out the free corn for broccoli. They always cook it to order and I'm always satisfied. I've also tried their chuck steak (average - obviously tougher than the ribeye) and their rice with steak (soo good - but really filling with the rice).Their beer options are also pretty affordable - I would definitely try if you can!Side Note: I think several of their locations are either changing names or shutting down and I'm really sad about this. Hopefully this location/establishment stays!!

Wow!! Blow me away! Westville showed up today and brought our hospital test-tent a team lunch!! We were tired and hungry (one of us may have been Hangry! Lol!) and here they come to the rescue! It was absolutely DELICIOUS! My friend and I both received the Market Plate (we think). The chicken was grilled and had great flavor and was nice and moist. With this was sticky rice and a dressing that had a great flavor and a little bit of sweetness to it. And to top it off - fresh vegetables that were cooked PERFECTLY!! Just thr right amount of crispness. I am totally ordering from here next week or later this week to take home for dinner. Thank you for loving on us healthcare workers!! We  you!

A great experience was had by all. I've passed by this place many times and wanted to visit, but it always seemed to be really packed and really loud. I was probably was not in the mood for really loud even though I'm really loud. We ending up at Bait & Hook during a random Sunday Funday excursion, and we were pleasantly surprised that the restaurant had a very generous happy hour even on Sundays. Some of the happy hour items include $1 oysters, $3 tacos, $6 well drinks, and draft beer specials. During our visit, we had a spread of food that included oysters, fish tacos, the kung po calamari, and I know that I'm forgetting the last item. All of the food items were pretty great, especially the kung pao calamari. I highly recommend the kung pao calamari. The bar and service staff, especially Mykayla (sp), were pretty nice, charming, and funny. We stayed for our food and a few rounds of beverages. Although the restaurant has a great weekend happy hour special, the restaurant was somewhat empty with a few folks at the bar and at a couple of tables inside and outside of the place. Perhaps, we arrived after the main brunch rush, but before the dinner rush. I look forward to visiting the Bait & Hook for another Sunday Funday excursion. Note (as of Apr. 2019): A Yelp check-in gets 10% off of your bill.

This is a solid Indian Restaurant. I went with three friends who all had different opinions. The ambience of the restaurant is modern and welcoming. I really like the murals on the wall. The food took a bit long to arrive (so I docked half a star) but the drinks arrived pretty quickly. For the table, we ordered the Garlic Naan, the Chicken Tikka Masala, the Paneer Makhani and the Chana Masala. My friend thought that the chicken tikka masala was too sweet. He also said that even though he ordered it spicy, it wasn't that spicy. They did do a good job on the garlic naan, though. The seasoning was perfect, it wasn't overly greasy, and it was fresh and just the right balance between soft and crispy. The paneer makhani was also really good. The paneer tasted fresh and not too soft. The gravy was slightly sweeter than average but still tasted quite yummy. The chana masala wasn't bad, but it also wasn't among the best I've had. I'd say this place is worth a visit for the food, but it's best not to dine in if you're in a hurry.

Toloache Thompson is the downtown outpost of a mini-chain of quality Mexican restaurants here in Manhattan. Toloache, unlike most Mexican eateries, has an actual star chef -- Chef Julian Medina -- who creates flavorful dishes based on classic Mexican food. Chef Medina once faced off against Chef Jose Garces on Iron Chef. Toloache Thompson has a casual vibe appropriate for the Village. Great margaritas, good food, nice service and a casual ambiance make for a pleasant evening.

My recent visit to this restaurant was far from satisfactory. The wait time was inordinately long, which was particularly frustrating given my hunger. Upon arrival, I was seated in an isolated area separated from other guests, which made the experience uncomfortable. It felt as if my presence was unwelcome, potentially due to my race and the fact that I was dining alone.

Service was slow to the point that I considered leaving before my order was taken. While the karaoke provided some entertainment, it was not enough to redeem the overall experience. Unfortunately, I found the establishment unwelcoming and cannot recommend it based on my visit.

We enjoyed our brunch! Our server was super sweet and helpful. I don't remember her name but she was awesome. I had the green bowl and it was super healthy and large portion of veggies. My husband had ground chicken burger and loved it to. Restaurant is super relaxed casual vibe. We went about 10am on Saturday and they were just starting to get busy. They take reservations which is nice too

Honestly, a pretty average Korean BBQ place. If this place was in LA it probably wouldn't even make it on the radar for most people. But given we're in Manhattan, the options for good KBBQ are much more limited. Still, I'd rather go out to deep Flushings and get something extra good if I was in the mood for KBBQ.They come in a variety of meat combos, and the servers here end up doing a lot of the cooking for you when it's not too busy which is nice. Everything else though was pretty standard, ranging from average banchan, average seasoning, and typical meat quality.Service was quite top notch when we went, but it wasn't too crowded at that time, so the servers were extra eager to help out. They refilled my lettuce basket before I was even half way through, which was super awesome.

Seemed very trendy, and looked like a cool place, but the food was pretty average.  I had the eggplant parm appetizer and gnocchi bolognese.  Both were good, but lacking in seasoning.  I added salt and pepper to both dishes, which I rarely do.  Other cons: Went with a group of 7 and they wouldn't seat us until the entire party arrived even though we had a reservation and the table remained empty until our whole group showed.  They also served us bottled water the whole time, and when the check came, we realized that no one in our group asked for bottled water.  They never asked us what we preferred.  This seemed really shady to me, but they did take the $30 water charge off our bill when someone complained.  Also took forever to get some of our drinks.  All of that said, the restaurant looked really cute - I kept seeing well dressed girls taking pictures on the stairs leading up to the restaurant- seemingly for posting on Instagram.  I'd return if I needed a cute place in the area, but I certainly wouldn't make this a destination for good Italian food.

Came here for brunch and I fell in love with the place. From start to finish, I felt like I was on vacation because the vibes and ambiance were amazing! The music was on point which made me love the place even more !Appetizer: Ricotta Fritters - Requeson Doughnuts, Sugar and cinnamonMains:Tres leches French Toast -  Brioche bread topped with mixed berries, pomegranate and maple syrupCantina Hash brown Benedict - Pork Carniats Hash (opted out of the pok), 2 poached eggs, avocado, potato with Hollandaise sauceDrink:La Gran Manzana - Jack Daniels "Apple", pear puree, lime juice cinnamon, syrupI was a bit disappointed with my dish since I don't eat pork, I was hoping they would substitute the meat for chicken or beef burger didn't give me that option even tho I paid full price for my dish. But no the less it was a great place & I just can't wait to be back.

Came in on a Tuesday with a resso for three people at 6:15. Place wasn't too packed. There are a lot of menu options so it's a good idea to take a peek at the menu online beforehand. We started with the gyoza, which you should avoid. It was soggy and I've definitely had better frozen gyoza bought from the Asia n supermarkets. I ended up going with Azuma Gozen set, which comes with noodles, dipping sauce, a piece of shrimp tempura, two pieces of veggie tempura, sashimi, rice, "seasonal side dish" (which was this pickled veggie with egg thing), and ice cream. You have the option of getting a small, medium, or large portion, which are all the same price. So if you start with small, you can get two more servings. Medium, you'll get one more serving. Large, those are all your servings up front. I totally get why they would do this for the hot soba, so that the noodles don't get too soggy. But I'm not quite sure I understand the point of it for cold soba. Maybe for people who are trying to eat smaller portions?I haven't had soba noodles too many times in life but I think I discovered this time that I don't love it. The noodles are too dry/wheaty for my taste, even with the dipping sauce. I probably wouldn't come back for the noodles but there are a lot of other apps/menu items I want to try - like the Katsu don. Will return for that! Hopefully next time, our waitress won't ignore us too much like this time.

**$15 CREDIT CARD MINIMUM!** My friend and I visited Tasty Hand Pulled Noodles II on a Friday evening around 5:45pm.  As others have mentioned, the shop is on the smaller side and can probably seat 5-6 small parties comfortably.  Throughout the time we were there, it never got fully packed, but was always more than half full.  If you come during a peak time, you'll probably need to share the table with another party.I ordered the pork dumpling noodle soup with regular hand pulled noodles ($8.95) and my friend ordered the Fujanese pork wonton noodle soup with the big wide hand pulled noodles ($8.95).  I will say that this is one of the cheaper dinner options you will find around Hell's Kitchen, and the no-frills environment and simplicity of the dishes are aligned with the pricing.  For me, the soup was good, but nothing special.  My favorite things about my soup were the dumplings.  They were jumbo, juicy, and well-flavored.  It was sad that there were only a few of them in the soup!  The noodles tasted fresh and had a nice chewy consistency that I expect from hand-pulled noodles.  However, the ratio of noodles: broth: other stuff was very noodle heavy.  And one thing about hand-pulled noodles is that they don't intrinsically have a ton of flavor.  So once you finish the bites with the dumplings and veggies, you're just left with lightly flavored noodles and broth.  So yes, it is a filling portion for under $10, but 80% of that portion lacks taste without dousing with condiments.  For that reason, it just didn't hit it out of the ballpark for me.Aside from taking our order and bringing the food, there was no form of "service" here, so I can't comment on that.  There is a pitcher of water on the table that you refill yourself.  Overall, if you're looking for a cheap meal in the area, I would recommend getting those dumplings.  However, the soup isn't something that would have me coming back again and again.

Title: A Quick Bite in the Heart of the Buzz

After a day of city exploration, we ducked into this Times Square pizzeria seeking a quick and convenient slice. True to its prime location, the place bustled with energy at 6:45 pm, teeming with patrons and lacking a discernable line for service. Despite this, we managed to snag the attention of the staff and pointed out our choices through the display glass.

The menu wasn't clearly posted, which could be a challenge for those with dietary restrictions, but we weren't deterred. I chose a white pizza topped with fresh mozzarella, beans, and greens. While the flavors were satisfying, the lukewarm temperature after a quick oven reheat was a slight letdown. My husband opted for a pepperoni slice that also fell into the lukewarm territory, though his contentment with tasting "real" New York pizza overshadowed any temperature concerns.

Price-wise, the slices were on the steeper side, which didn't surprise us given the prime real estate of Times Square. In summary, while the experience wasn't without its flaws, this spot delivered a decent, albeit pricey, slice for those seeking the quintessential New York pizza experience amidst the city's hustle and bustle.

Title: A Spectacular Birthday Seafood Feast at [Restaurant Name]

My husband's birthday celebration at [Restaurant Name] was nothing short of marvelous. Their seamless reservation system and warm hostesses set the tone for the evening.

Despite the bustling crowd, the attentive service was immediate, complete with a detailed run-through of tempting specials. As seafood aficionados, our expectations were high, and the restaurant more than delivered.

The server's recommendation of a sweet Merlot proved delightful, complementing our appetizer choice beautifully. The grilled calamari, a first for us both, was a revelation with its smoky sweetness and savory notes—a clear indicator of the quality to come.

For mains, the salmon with its smoky crust and tender flesh was a standout, enhanced by the unique black rice and a sublime yogurt honey/dill mustard sauce. Across the table, the Maine lobster's succulence shone through, whether savored on its own or with the classic lemon and butter duo.

Capping off the meal, the crème brûlée was textbook perfection. Its creamy interior, crackling sugar top, and the refreshing addition of strawberries and mint left our palates thoroughly satisfied.

While prices are on the higher side, the exemplary flavors and overall dining experience at [Restaurant Name] justify the cost. A top recommendation for anyone in search of premier seafood offerings.

Now my 2nd time here, but the first time was yearsss ago. Happy to say, nothing has changed, same excellent taste!Not sure why people say the portions are small...these are NORMAL portions and far sufficient to feed someone!Started with the garlic fried chicken and spicy rice cakes, delicious and juicy! We couldve just had this all night! And the pickled dikon was a nice refresher.Also had the kimchi stew and kimchi fried rice, flavorful and had great depth! Buyer beware: very hot! Will be coming back to enjoy the seasonal menu some more
Very nice space for all occasions- romantic, family, friends, business. They have a nice social hour until 7pm. I had the tanquery gin and tonic. Service was great and we enjoyed our time here.

Easily my favorite breakfast and lunch place in New York. I've never had a bad meal here. Everything always taste fresh and homemade. They only use fresh ingredients. I love their pancakes and bacon. The pancakes are the best restaurant pancakes I have ever tasted. This visit I ordered a hamburger and it was great. The meat tasted so fresh and tender. It was a very good burger. The prices are around $20 a plate, but when you taste the food it is worth every penny.

Title: A Mixed Experience Close to Highline

Located near the enchanting McKittrick Hotel and a stone's throw from the Highline, this quaint restaurant exudes a charming ambiance, perfect for a post-stroll dinner. On the plate, the branzino promises flavor but is unfortunately overshadowed by an excessive greasiness. Similarly, the ribs disappoint with their lackluster taste, and the grease factor doesn't help.

For those with dietary restrictions, gluten-free options are marked, but those with severe allergies, such as celiac disease, might want to think twice. Although the staff is outwardly friendly, there seems to be a lack of understanding or consideration for the seriousness of cross-contamination – a concern that's particularly alarming when even a simple request for clean utensils is met with an eye roll.

Despite the allure of its location and interior, my return to this spot after years, especially with heightened dietary needs, was regretful. This establishment has the potential for a pleasant dining experience but falls short in both culinary execution and accommodating service.

I love Max Brenner and I completely forgot they have one in NYC - their Vegas location closed a few years back. I wanted to come here yesterday for my birthday, for dessert.A friend and I split their s'mores crepe, which is gigantic. My second choice was their Make Your Own s'mores thing which also looked really good. I've been to this location before, too, and had their chocolate pizza.If you're a chocoholic like me, this is a must stop when in NYC. They also serve lunch and dinner, and I believe breakfast or brunch too.

This tastes just like street food I had in China! The crepe on the outside was perfectly crispy and thin, and the sweet bean sauce tied all the ingredients together. I've never found another place in the US that serves such authentic jian bing. If you're in the NYC, this shop is a must-go.

Fantastic service and food!We got the meatballs as an appetizer and oh my they were divine. I really wanted to try the lasagna but they had run out for the evening. Instead I got the pappardelle which was a good choice--fresh pasta with mushrooms and a creamy cheesy sauce. The atmosphere was perfect for a date night.

Pricey but good!I had the Thai noodle salad and it was excellent. The beef was super tender and the sauce was sweet and tangy. I enjoyed the touch of peanut in the salad though I do wish there was a lime wedge on the side and more spice in the sauce itself. I also tried my friend's French dip and it was really good! The prime rib super tender and the au jus is well seasoned. This is definitely a good for a date or company dinner. Very classy.

I ordered the yasai itame. The green curry base itself was rich and felt a little oily. I think the toppings were over cooked, the vegetables were quite mushy and the deep fried tofu was a bit hollow/empty on the inside. There were also an overwhelming amount of peanuts in the dish, which added a good texture but was a powerful flavor. It was a decent meal but I don't think I would order this again.

I headed to a charming spot for a pre-theater lunch on Wednesday before catching the matinee showing of "Gary" at the Booth Theater—a must-see, particularly for Nathan Lane's brilliant performance. Though initially the restaurant appeared quiet, it quickly filled up, justifying our decision to make reservations.

We started with a refreshing Greek beer, complemented by warm, delightful pita bread. We opted for the Pilikia combo, featuring a trio of tasty spreads paired with succulent stuffed grape leaves—a standout choice, especially since the pita basket was generously replenished. While the spread assortment was impressive, the grilled sausages truly stole the show. Unfortunately, the Spanakopita was a tad on the dry side.

The service was top-notch and the tables were comfortably spaced. Overall, this eatery on restaurant row is a solid choice for a pre-matinee meal.

Located in the shops and cafe complex under Rockefeller Plaza. It's a decent spot for a nice hearty Sicilian slice. Sorta wished they had a veggie pie but ended up w/ Margherita slice which was quite satisfying consider it was nicely warmed up and it was a cold day. This spot is great for a quick bite on the go.

Title: A Little Slice of Italian Heaven in Greenwich Village

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this gem of an Italian restaurant in the heart of Greenwich Village, NYC, and I am already planning my return visit! From the moment we arrived, the experience was exceptional. The outdoor seating allowed us to soak in the vibrant street atmosphere, adding to the restaurant's great ambiance.

The service was attentive and prompt, impressing us with complimentary appetizers that included pillowy soft baked bread, artichokes, and olives – a simple yet delightful beginning to our meal, though a small tip for the restaurant: pitted olives would be much appreciated.

Our starter of a cheese and meat platter did not disappoint; the meats, particularly the non-salty mortadella and the aptly named Sweet Copa, were cured to absolute perfection, and the Burrata was the epitome of freshness and creaminess.

As for the mains, my carbonara was truly a dish to be sung about – the pasta was al dente, the creamy egg beautifully coating each strand, and the balance of cheese and pepper was spot on. The Bolognese, ordered by my dining companion, was tasty but didn't quite hit the high note of the carbonara.

In short, this restaurant has set a new standard for Italian dining for me, and I can't wait to come back – not just for seconds or thirds, but for fifths! A definite must-visit for anyone craving authentic Italian in NYC.

A quick stop here after a long day (3.5 star, 8/10/2019). Im not sure how crowded this place usually is. However, there was no line at 8:30pm on Sat. We got brewed ice tea, lemonade and one red velvet. Every item was reasonably priced even though many places in this neighborhood usually are. I loved non-sweetened ice tea which doesn't give a typical after taste. Lemonade was unique, and not too sweet (that's how I prefer). A red velvet cake was very dense and heavy. The cake was unfortunately not my favorite. I'd come back here though if there's no wait!

AMAZING FOOD! The brunch menu is a particularly wonderful deal, with $32 for a brunch prix fixe and $15 for 2-hour unlimited drinks. The menu changes seasonally, and we went in for the Summer menu.The corn gnocchi is probably my favorite dish from the entire menu! The gnocchi is perfectly cooked and soft, and the flavors in the corn gnocchi come together so well! The burrata is another favorite appetizer, and it is served with some greens and peaches. So fresh all the time. From the main entrees, the branzino, shakshuka, and meatball are all excellent choices. For dessert, the basil ice cream was so delicious and unlike any other ice cream I've ever tasted before!The service here is always impeccable, and the interior is gorgeous!

I loved this place. Very awesome atmosphere for late night bites. I recommend getting the corn in a cup appetizer. You cant go wrong with what you order here because everything is delicious. The manager is very friendly. He walks around and greets each and every table to ensure service is timely and food is on point. That was a good differentiator between this place in comparison to others. Have some micheladas or tequila shots.
Good pho and quick service. Staff was pleasant, especially since we were the last ones still eating after they closed. The salmon soup was also pretty good.

Stepping into this restaurant, you're immediately transported to Japan, thanks to the authentic food, immersive ambience, and welcoming staff. Despite a wait list, my friend and I were pleasantly surprised to be seated quicker than the estimated 10-15 minutes.

Watching chefs at work in an open kitchen added to the excitement. I opted for the sukiyaki don, which, despite its chewy texture, was a letdown. My partner's yakiniku don, contrastingly, was absolutely delicious. The inclusion of miso soup and pickled vegetables with our rice bowls rounded out the meal, providing a satisfying set that left us full and happy.

Despite the hiccup with the sukiyaki, the experience was overwhelmingly positive. I'm already looking forward to my next visit to try the katsu and dessert. This place is a must-visit for anyone craving a slice of Japan.

Title: A Modest Foray into 'Nirvana'

On a whim, we ventured to dine at a place ambitiously named Nirvana, curious to see if it could possibly match its lofty moniker. To our satisfaction, the Chicken Tikka Masala I ordered was quite palatable, accompanied by a generous portion of well-executed Naan. My wife's choice, the Biryani Chicken, was deemed acceptable, though it didn't inspire rapture.

The ambiance, reflective of the restaurant's age, had a worn-in charm, but don't expect it to dazzle. Service was unremarkable, efficient yet lacking that special touch of warmth one might hope to find in a namesake of paradise. In short, Nirvana provided a decent meal without the celestial experience its name might suggest.

I think this place is a hit or miss and I will try over next week for a better review. So I came in and we ended up getting a quesadilla and a choclate martini. Somehow I was thinking that the martini would be a extremely sweet taste beacuse of course, it's choclate. I absolutely loved the display but it was kind of a bitter taste in my mouth. I took a few sips then handed it over to the gentelman that came in with me. The quesadilla was vibrant and colorful with great presentation too but diddnt exactly fit my standards of what a quesadilla should be like. The service was great and the atmosphere is amazing. I'm actually going to give this place another shot and order something different before i go to try and get alittle more out of this though. I dont think its fair to fully assess this place based off of two items!

I've been craving Shakshuka ever since I  saw Chef Aarti  making it on Guy's Ranch Kitchen..the poached egg on the rich tomato sauce..yum! I was so excited that I was finally actually going to be able to try it out at Hummus Kitchen! It was insanely delicious!! The sauce of rich and the egg yolk gave this delicious dish a balance of creaminess. I also ordered  the Hummus Shakshuka and omgg it's like the best of both world! It's truly a must! Our Server Noy was simply amazing too! He recommended the THE KITCHEN KADIF with is a Halva parfait on shredded filo dough topped with halva & silan...you have to order this dessert!!! It's out of this world delicious!! I truly can't wait to go back for more!!They truly have an amazingly delicious brunch!!

Title: My Uptown Chinese Cuisine Staple - Lotus Express Review

If you find yourself in Washington Heights craving Chinese cuisine, look no further than Lotus Express. As a true connoisseur with stringent standards for Chinese food, having loyalty only to select spots in Brooklyn and the Lower East Side, I can confidently say Lotus Express has earned its place as my uptown sanctuary.

The menu's extensive range has been thoroughly tested by my palate – from the comforting classic of chicken wings and fries to the virtuous choice of healthier shrimp options. Each dish I've sampled has been nothing short of perfection, both in flavor and preparation.

Notably, the attention to detail extends to their packaging – ensuring that every order arrives intact and ready to satisfy.

For locals and visitors alike seeking a reliable Chinese eatery, Lotus Express stands out as a must-try destination. Without a doubt, this spot gets my seal of approval and a hearty recommendation.

I had a really good time at Hama! The service was great and the fish was so fresh! I ordered the Kaisen Chirashi which contained an assortment of fish, including white tuna, salmon, masago, tuna, and clam. It was surprisingly filling and I gave up towards the end and left a ton of rice in my box.I love how the restaurant is clean, bright and open! It makes it easier for me to trust that the sushi is top of the line.

Title: A Gem in Midtown: Niles Delivers Delight

Having dined at Niles three times in the past month, my experiences have been consistently excellent. The lobster bisque, a steal at $9, is a must-try—each serving is replete with succulent lobster and the flavor is impeccably balanced. The portion size is just right.

Niles boasts an enviable location across from LIRR and MSG, making it an ideal spot for pre-event drinks or a meal. The decor strikes an upscale note, and the atmosphere is enhanced by the professional demeanor of the staff.

A bonus is the low noise level during both lunch and dinner services, contributing to a comfortable dining environment. The drink selection is impressive, featuring a fine array of beers, wines, and cocktails.

In all, Niles offers solid food at great value for an establishment of this caliber in Midtown Manhattan. It's a versatile venue, perfect for anything from a casual lunch to a polished team dinner. Highly recommended for a satisfying meal or a round of drinks when you're in the area. Cheers to Niles for consistently great experiences!

I happen upon this place during one cold lunch hour. This place has legit flavorful broths with Chinatown-level quickness in service. The price is on par with all other lunch places in the area but even with tips for sit down it's still so reasonable. Definitely worth a visit alongside other restaurants on the block and recommend adding to your rotation if you live/work in the 'hood.

An excellent spot for the modern ramen eater! It's the perfect place to get ramen customized exactly to your preferences. You order on an iPad when you walk in before being seated. I got the hippie ramen made with veggie broth. It can be either vegan or vegetarian (depending whether they add butter to the broth). The noodles are curly and good. The best part was probably the tofu, which was soo flavorful. (Am I the only one who's sick of having their vegetarian ramen topped with squares of completely unflavored, uncooked tofu?) And I appreciated that they provided a side of chili oil at no extra charge. (There are also cloves of fresh garlic available on the table accompanied by garlic presses, if you're into that!) Overall, this is one of the best spots I've found for veggie ramen in New York City, and it comes at a reasonable price.

This is delivery! I can't imagine how awesome this could have been if I visited the restaurant! The empanadas were overstuffed with chicken and just the correct spice. So juicy when I took a bite they leaked! Wow! I loved the fresh garnish too! Red cabbage and frisee. Not pictured are the steamed mixed vegetables which are fresh and not bagged with asparagus, carrots, zucchini and peppers expertly seasoned. Nice! Now this Chicken. It is a Chicken Cordon Bleu but way off the scale (see pic)! Got to be the best I've ever had! And the most different! Fresh chicken breast, ham and a smooth gooey cheese but with a delectable tomato portobello mushroom sauce! Damn! I'm staying at the Doubletree hotel and the order said 30-45 minutes, but I met my delivery guy in 20! Super! I highly recommend!

Title: Savory Unagi Experience with Exceptional Service

I recently visited a Japanese restaurant that has mastered the art of unagi, with a menu that celebrates this delicacy in almost every dish. Opting for the western-style unagi don, I was treated to crispy skin and slightly chewy flesh, all brought together with a special sauce that was both delightful and complementary to the eel and rice. While not the best I've ever sampled, the dish was undeniably tasty.

The set not only satisfied my craving for eel but also included a fresh salad and a delectable Yuzu jelly dessert, rounding off the meal beautifully. The service was impeccable – the Japanese staff were the epitome of friendliness and politeness, although their English was limited. For those eyeing value, I recommend visiting at lunch when the unagi don set is more economically priced at $55, compared to $65 in the evening.

Title: A Spicy Surprise with a Hint of Price - A Review of My Szechuan Experience

My culinary adventure at this Szechuan restaurant was sparked by a friend's recommendation and what an experience it was! As soon as we stepped in on a lazy Saturday afternoon, the spacious and tastefully decorated interior set a welcoming vibe.

Our culinary journey kicked off with the Fish Filet in Numb and Spicy Peppers. The serving was surprisingly generous and the fish itself swam in a perfectly spicy and numbing broth that was lifted by the hidden treasures of bean sprouts and lotus roots at the bottom of the bowl - a delightful complement both in substance and texture. 

We quickly continued with the Spicy Cumin Lamb, which arrived promptly. Each bite of the tender, sizable lamb chunks amidst the aromatic blend of chili peppers, onions, and cilantro was a testament to the chef's expertise in harmonizing flavors.

To balance the heat, we opted for the Sauteed Shredded Potato with Chili Pepper. Although marked spicy, it was rather tame but wonderfully crisp, with a pleasing touch of acidity from the vinegar.

While the dishes dazzled, the pricing did give us pause, leaning towards the higher end of the spectrum when compared to other Szechuan offerings around the city. The additional cost for extra rice felt slightly restrictive, given the robust and spicy flavors of the cuisine that typically call for more than a single bowl of rice per entree.

Despite the price point and the rice policy, the meal was highly enjoyable. I'd recommend this spot to any spice enthusiast, and suggest coming in a small group to indulge in a variety of dishes. Just be prepared for a slightly higher bill and consider your rice ration!

Title: An Unforgettable Dining Experience at The Ragtrader

Review:
The Ragtrader doesn't just earn five stars—it deserves a constellation. From the instant I inquired about bar seating, I was met with the antithesis of the stereotypical New York attitude: pure politeness, beaming smiles, and infectious positivity.

The ambiance was set by a fantastic soundtrack that had me grooving all the way to the bar, where a phenomenally personable bartender greeted me (though her name escapes me, her drink-mixing prowess and flawless makeup won't). The sangria I ordered was a masterpiece—far from the watered-down imitations out there—bursting with fresh fruit and a robust, soul-satisfying taste.

I dived into the crispy salmon, perched atop nutty black rice and swimming in a heavenly curry sauce. Each bite was a flavor revelation, so much so that I saved half to savor the experience again the next day.

The grand finale was the Sticky Toffee Pudding, enhanced by a theatrical pour of Grand Marnier set aflame, captivating both sight and taste.

Thanks to the ever-vigilant bartender, not even my leftovers were forgotten. The Ragtrader delivered stellar service, exceptional food, and an atmosphere that guarantees my return. It's the perfect spot for any occasion, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

Title: A Carnivore's Delight at the Heart of the City

If you're searching for a spot to indulge in a fun night out in the city, look no further. The rodizio here is simply finger-licking good, making it an ideal destination for meat lovers. The service is exceptional, with attentive staff ensuring your table is spotless and your needs are met promptly.

Do not overlook the salad bar – it's a treasure trove of fresh, tasty options that perfectly complement the meaty mains. However, pacing yourself is key; it's tempting to dive into the salad offerings, but you'll want to save room for the rodizio experience.

The ambiance strikes a delicate balance between relaxing and chill, setting the stage for a perfect date night or an enjoyable evening with friends. Be warned, though – you might leave the restaurant a bit heavier, but your taste buds will thank you for it.

I came here with my colleagues and had a great experience. I didn't have dinner, but I did have dessert, champagne and some bread that they left for the table. The bread was like a loaf of Challah. We had to cut it ourselves, but that was fine, since everyone wanted different amounts. The bread itself was really good and was topped with what I perceived to be carmelized onions. The outside was smooth, and the inside was soft. There were no crispy edges like the bread at other places, but it still tasted good. The butter that came with the bread was whipped, light and perfectly salted. I could eat it all day with the bread. For the champagne, we ordered two bottles of the Ruinart Blanc de Blancs brut (it was a large group of lawyers, and we were there for a celebratory dinner). The servers poured the champagne for us perfectly, and my glass never empty unless I wanted it to be. For dessert, I got the creme brulee upon the recommendation of our server, and it was also incredible. The creme was smooth and sweet, and the sugar on top was even, cirsp and bruleed to perfection. I also liked the garnish of raspberries and mint on top. Service was excellent. From the moment we walked in and they took our coats and bags, until the moment we left, we felt very well taken care of. The servers were patient and answered all of our questions. Even though our party was there for a while, we never felt rushed, and were comfortable taking our time. I docked one star because there were very few vegetarian options, if any, on the entree menu.

Upon my recent visit to 2nd Ave Deli, I found it to embody the quintessential charm of a traditional Jewish deli, with its noteworthy sandwich selection. The culinary experience offered both highs and lows; while the brisket was unfortunately a tad dry, the pastrami stood out with its delightful flavor. Additionally, the bread served was notably fresh, and I highly recommend indulging in a side of their fries.

However, I must say that the encounter with the deli's manager slightly marred the experience. His rather brusque and discourteous demeanor during our arrival and seating was unwelcoming. In stark contrast, our server was excellent, shining with great service that one would expect. Despite the food's merits, the management's approach to customer service regrettably led to my lower rating for 2nd Ave Deli.

Looking at the menu, the triple sampler is definitely a better deal but we came for the lobster and got only that. We got two lobster rolls, one was the winter special white truffle roll, which I enjoyed more than their regular one. I highly recommend the winter special before they stop serving it! I think it was $18 for one lobster roll, which was pretty pricey considering how small the roll was. You can eat the whole thing in like 4 bites. But still definitely worth it as it was the best lobster roll I ever had. Such big pieces of lobster in that buttery toasted bun. I wanted another roll as soon as we finished those two. Since there's so many locations around NYC, there's no excuse not to try this place out.

Title: A Taste of Old New York at Puffy's Tavern

During a recent trip to NYC, my husband and I had the pleasure of visiting Puffy's Tavern in Tribeca, a recommendation from a friend familiar with the area. Though Puffy's exterior may raise an eyebrow, stepping inside is like a nostalgic trip to the New York of yesteryear—a true local hangout rather than a tourist hotspot.

We arrived early for lunch, welcomed warmly into the nearly empty tavern, with the liberty to choose our seats. Puffy's exudes an old-school charm with its tin ceiling, wooden tables with copper accents, and a stately wooden bar. The floor, resembling pristine vintage tile, added to the authenticity of the ambiance.

True to its reputation, Puffy's delivered on its promise of delicious sandwiches. Their menu offered a variety of options, complemented by a choice between "crunchy" or "soft" bread—we both opted for crunchy ciabatta. The Gladiator, stacked with Italian cold cuts, mozzarella, and olive paste, was a triumph of flavors, both fresh and satisfying.

While Puffy's boasts a full bar, it's more a haven for lovers of classic cocktails, beer, and wine rather than those seeking fancy or blended drinks. Not there for the libations, we were nonetheless impressed by the reasonable prices and the congenial bartender, hailing from Croatia, who shared that the tavern becomes quite lively at night.

Though the unisex bathrooms showed signs of wear, they were clean, and for those inclined, there's a dartboard to pass the time.

Puffy's is a relic of the good-old-days in NYC—authentic, wallet-friendly, and with a big heart. I left feeling well-fed, cared for, and decidedly happy. If you find yourself in Tribeca, make it a point to visit Puffy's Tavern. It's a gem that will make you a regular, even if you're just passing through.

I recently dined at a local restaurant that offers a unique take on halal cuisine. Unlike my usual spot, the meat here was served in larger chunks, providing a different but delicious texture to the meal. It was a pleasant surprise to see that they still serve lamb, a beloved option that has unfortunately disappeared from the menu at the halal guy near MoMa. Occasionally, I find myself craving a not-so-healthy combination over rice, and this place certainly hit the spot with their flavorful, satisfying offerings. Highly recommended for those looking for a tasty twist on traditional halal dishes.
Luke's lobster is a must anytime you come out to New York. It is pricey but well worth it.  I can easily spend over $100 whenever I go here.

What a fun treat! It's good chicken for the hustlin New York life style. You can buy one and get in and out within a couple minutes. What's fun is that you can grab the cone then walk and eat around town.

Barolo East shines as a cozy Italian haven in Midtown, bustling with energy even on a typically quiet weekend night. Welcomed by a fully stocked bar and the promise of a comfortable white-linen-tabled dining experience upstairs, the restaurant sets a tone of class and warmth.

As a solo early arrival, I was swiftly accommodated by a considerate waiter, armed with both dinner and an impressive wine menu, perfect for oenophiles with options by the glass or bottle. The authenticity of the menu, presented in Italian with helpful English subscripts, adds to the charm.

Our table savored the burrata appetizer special followed by a divinely shared truffle risotto and chicken sausage orecchiette, which managed to be indulgent yet not overly heavy. A highlight of the evening was the complimentary bread accompanied by a mouthwatering tomato spread—a simple pleasure that could easily overshadow the main course if indulged in without restraint.

Barolo East, with its embrace of Italian cuisine in a cozy atmosphere, ensures that even a carb-centric menu can deliver a delightful dining experience without the post-meal heaviness. A Midtown gem worth visiting.

Came here on the recommendation of a good acquaintance (who happens to own the place with his wife). Was not sure what to expect since I'm admittedly not well-versed in Thai cuisine, but I'll be damned if I wasn't thoroughly impressed with the presentation/deliciousness of literally each dish.I'll post pics of some of the delicious food I had because I mostly do not remember/cannot pronounce their names. But mad props to chef Bat. You da real MVP.Basically, have some self-respect and stop ONLY eating pad thai, ya BASIC. There's a whole plethora of Thai dishes out there! Exercise self-love and bring yourself here for some of the best new Thai in the city.Go here!

Title: A Decent Attempt at Beef Noodle Soup

I recently visited a highly raved-about noodle joint, hoping to be wowed by their specialty: beef noodle soup. Opting for the wide noodles without any add-ons, I found the soup to be hearty yet lacking in robust flavor and certainly in need of salt. The abundant cilantro, not a favorite of mine, didn't help matters. My dining companion, on the other hand, enjoyed the meal's heartiness. The texture of the noodles stood out as a highlight in an otherwise average dish. Considering the steep price of nearly $20 per person, I left feeling underwhelmed and with the notion that there's ample scope for refinement in their signature offering.

I came in on Christmas Eve around 6:15PM with 2 other friends - we were early for our 6:30PM reservation. We asked for The Poni Room and they walked us downstairs to the izakaya which wasn't crazy packed. Unfortunately, that night there was only 1-2 waitresses working in the speakeasy area. Service took a really really long time which contributes to losing a star. They told us about the Christmas Eve "7 fishes tasting" and that there was a happy hour special for wine and Christmas punch for $25/2 hours if the whole table participated. Our friend (who happened to be the birthday girl) was sick and couldn't drink and the waitress told us she'd get back to us to see if we could make an exception - took 15 mins came back to tell us we can help ourselves but will probably be charged for the first glass and then we can renegotiate after - took another 20 mins to confirm. The Christmas punch was a good thing to try since I am a sucker for all things fruity especially when the base is yuzu vodka - yuzu is a Japanese citrusy sweet lemon. We also ordered 30 mins before... drinking on an empty stomach was not the greatest and we were hungry but opted for the 7 fishes tasting $49pp. Here's a rundown of the dishes:- Umami custard broth shooter: this was so smooth and good, there were lobsters bits and fish roe.. they provide a spoon to scoop from a glass- Salt & Pepper squid & coconut rice with fish roe: very nicely seasoned and not too fried - acceptable amount of chewy, the portion of fish roe could have been a bit more but the coconut rice was aromatic and delicious, not overwhelming - Coconut Laska: served in a tea pot into tea cups and after drinking, you see bits of seafood and cilantro inside - really appropriate especially when cold out- Salmon belly skewers & green tea soba noodles: the salmon belly skewers were charred to perfection and medium rare (not overcooked!) dipped in yummy garlic sauce - we each had 2 skewers and the green tea soba noodles were nice and chewy, al dente!!- Clams: very flavorful because of the broth- Taiyaki dessert with vanilla/chocolate ice cream, a pirouette, and chocolate covered strawberry oreo (?): this was really sweet, we kind of gobbled the ice cream and left the taiyaki pastry to eat what we could without a sugar overload - the bottom of the pastry has the red bean and more cake pastry which I ate since the top portion gets overwhelming!!We really enjoyed the food, but I was not impressed with the service since we ended around 9PM (could have gotten a 5 star) - nonetheless I'm open to coming again in the future to try some of the other menu items like the sugar pumpkin and octopus! Just be warned the portions are on the smaller side so you'll need 3-4 per person to feel full, we actually kind of questioned if they skimped out on our collective portions since we were a party of 3. We saw a table for 6 near us with more food.

I've only been to this place when they had a live band. With the band, it's extra enjoyable, so really it should get an extra star for atmosphere when there is a band. No cover! There is a small floor for dancing. So if not dancing, you can just watch and enjoy your beer and/or meal.They have a decently priced beer that comes in a boot. Highly recommended as the boot glass is adorable. Also, I've had there spiked apple cider with Jack Daniels. Mmm.. They have a big pretzel with spicy or sweet mustard. 50% off discount on Yelp for the big pretzel. Had tried their chicken wings, latkas and biercheese dip. I recommend the biercheese dip and chips. The chips are potato pieces. The chicken wings were okay, not too impressive. The potato latkas were good. Highly recommended. Overall, it's a decent bar.

A very cute restaurant with nice decor, so naturally I had pretty high expectations, especially after seeing the pricey menu. The Atlantic Salmon was actually quite good, it was tender and flavorful. However, the pasta and risotto didn't look quite right - the consistency isn't right and it just didn't taste good. The Lemon Lobster Risotto had way too much lemon in it and it feels like eating a porridge that has already turned bad (the acidity from the lemon). It was a pretty disappointed meal for such a nice and cute place.

We had a tasty, very filling lunch here, though the arepas themselves were generally thinner, crispier, and a little drier than I'd prefer. Don't let them sit too long or the bottom half will get very soggy! Also, two arepas was way too much, even though I was crazy hungry. 1.5 would have been perfect.This is a tiny space that fills up fast, the tables are close, and there is one server. It's also cozy & homey there.THE WAIT: None on a Sunday at 12:11pm, but within 20 minutes it'd filled up and there was a wait outside!THE FOOD: La del gato with black beans (4.5 stars), followed by De pabellon (4 stars). The Miss PIggy was more soggy and less interesting (3.5 stars).See my photos for additional details!

I'm definitely sold on Camellia's ramen after catching their BOGO ramen deal for the month of October. Ramen enthusiasts, go get yours now!Once you step inside, you're greeted by a large restaurant space with casual seating and ample tables. There's no table service, but that's ok, because the staff are so friendly and helpful. You order at the counter, then pick up your ramen once your number is called. When looking at the menu, the build-your-own ramen option might immediately catch your eye. The noodle options are very unique: matcha, carrot, beet, cuttle fish paste, butterfly pea flower, and rainbow flavors.Although I was initially tempted to order a rainbow ramen for the gram, I realized that it was only offered as Tsukemen. Instead, I ordered the Ma-Yu Ramen, a bold ramen with heavy overtones of black garlic oil seasoning. The Ma-Yu was delicious, but just a little too salty for my liking. It's definitely very savory and rich, perfect if you like bold flavors. The big bowl of noodles comes with chasu, fish cake, mushrooms, soft boiled egg, and scallions. The chasu was cooked perfectly, allowing you to enjoy the tender meat and fatty rim.Another charm of Camellia's is their house-made gelato with daily flavors. Where can you find another ramen shop that also serves up delicious gelato with unique flavors? That day I went, they had flavors like Rose Lychee, Cinnamon Pumpkin, Lemon Cookie, White Rabbit, and Strawberry Shortcake. I sampled many of them before deciding that Lemon Cookie and Cinnamon Pumpkin were my favorites. I enjoyed 2 mini scoops of gelato for free with my Yelp check-in.Camellia is a great spot for well-priced, tasty ramen and gelato. I'd love to come back and enjoy another bowl sometime.

When I came to New York for the first time last week, I was set on being able to try Lombardi's Pizza. After all that I had read on the history of this restaurant, I knew I had to get some pizza. I came in with a group of three and one of the people had a dairy allergy. I know that obviously that's a difficult allergy to have in a pizza restaurant, but I figured that there would be at least a couple different items they could order regardless. I was wrong. FOOD: Aside from a few salads and some small appetizers, there was nothing else on the menu besides the pizza. Don't get me wrong, I'm game for some pizza, but we needed something for our person with an allergy.SERVICE: I then asked our server if there was any possible way that we could order one of the full pizzas, and just not put cheese on half of it.
