He went back and forth with me on trying to say that the pizzas are the way that they are and ultimately it was frustrating. I tried and tried to explain it, and for some odd reason he just didn't understand. This was the last conversation that we had before I ended up asking for the check for our drinks so that we could leave and go somewhere else. I also was disappointed to see that 90% of the people working at this restaurant weren't even Italian. This doesn't seem like a big deal, but for relying on authenticity, it sure doesn't sit right with me. OVERALL: I spent about 25 minutes inside Lombardi's before we left unsatisfied and disappointed. I was extremely excited to try this restaurant, but I will not be returning.

Absolutely enamored with the plant-based Mexican cuisine at this gem of a spot! Lunchtime brought us through their doors, and the experience was nothing short of exceptional. The chips and guacamole set a high bar, perfectly prepping our palates for the main courses: mouthwatering enchiladas and a chile relleno that delighted with every bite. The service matched the high quality of the food, attentive and efficient. Complemented by an inviting ambience and a great music selection, this restaurant comes highly recommended for anyone craving delicious, plant-based Mexican fare.

During a recent outing with friends M.Y. and N.S., I was delighted to discover that the local dumpling house had updated its menu with exciting new options. Although not ravenous, we shared a modest yet satisfying selection of dishes, including pork and kimchi soup dumplings, pork and chive fried dumplings, beef fried rice, and a beef and scallion pancake.

The pork and kimchi soup dumplings, while steaming and succulent, fell short in delivering the robust kimchi essence one might anticipate. Nevertheless, they remained a pleasurable treat. The fried dumplings set a high standard for future dumpling experiences with their delightful taste and texture.

The standout of our meal was the beef and scallion pancake, which exceeded our expectations with its perfectly prepared thin slices of beef, lightly pickled cucumbers, and an artfully assembled pancake enveloping the savory fillings.

Given the overall positive experience and the allure of unexplored menu items, I'm holding back the final star, offering a solid 4-star rating for now. I'm eager to return, explore further, and potentially bestow that perfect score. Until then, I'm looking forward to my next visit!

Title: A Satisfying Bite at Thunder Buns

During my stay in the Financial District, I followed a fellow Yelper's recommendation and strolled to Thunder Buns, nestled on the lower level of New York Plaza at Water and Broad St. This counter-style burger joint caught my attention with its array of burgers and sides.

I indulged in the Crimini Mushroom burger paired with a side of onion rings. The burger didn't disappoint—the buns were delightfully soft, rivaling those of Shake Shack, and the creamy mushroom and cheese topping was a flavorful hit. Overall, the burger was truly satisfying.

For anyone in the Financial District looking for a quick, wallet-friendly meal, Thunder Buns is worth the visit. Their tasty offerings hit the spot without breaking the bank.

Title: A Cozy Brunch with Room for Improvement

I recently visited this spot for a Saturday brunch and found the atmosphere quite relaxing, ideal for a weekend morning. However, I must mention that the portions left me wanting more. My Canyonland poached egg on an English muffin, priced at $15.75, was tasty but insufficient, and even my $4.50 cappuccino couldn't fill the gap.

My companion opted for the intriguing egg n apples Benedict on French toast with bacon, which set them back $19.25, accompanied by a unique bowl of hot chocolate – a whimsical touch to a standard brunch beverage.

While the ambiance scores high, the food was unremarkable in flavor and quantity. Perhaps with heartier servings and a dash of culinary creativity, future brunches could truly satisfy the palate and the stomach.

Made a reservation for brunch for 4 on a Saturday. It didn't seem all that crowded once we got there but I could see how it could get crowded quickly.Ordered the tonkatsu sandwich and first off, it's *thicc*. Between the two hearty slices of milk bread and the whole pork cutlet, it's close to "unhinge your jaw" levels. I understand keeping the cutlet the size it was allows it to fit the bread better, but I think I was expecting something closer to a typical katsu thickness, or thinness rather. It could've also used a little more sauce. Looking back at the menu it says there was an aoli, and looking back at my picture it seems there was probably a little katsu sauce but both were barely noticeable. The pickled onions were a welcome addition to add balance to the carbs of the breading and milk bread.Seems like other reviewers had some issues with service but I didn't notice anything exceptionally negative or positive. Overall it's earned a spot on my list of tasty brunch spots.

This is by far the best Thai food I have had I the NYC area and my brother and sister and law agreed. Both have also visited Thailand and felt this place could compete with the food there! Not only is their food absolutely delicious but the atmosphere and service is GREAT.4 of us shared 3 appetizers and 3 entrees. We had the following:- chicken wings- calamari- chicken dumplings- skirt steak with Thai seasoning- pad see ew with shrimp- green curry with chickenWe finished all of it and absolutely loved it!! One week later we've still been talking about how great the food was and how we cannot wait to go back as we enjoyed everything so much.From great service to wonderful food this is a place you must drop into! What's even better is you can make a reservation on yelp :)

Title: A Late Night Gem with Flavorful Delights

My recent visit to this unassuming eatery was a revelation for my midnight hunger pangs – the food is simply delicious! We feasted on three standout dishes: the grilled beef tongue, which was succulent and flavorful, the Katsu curry, with its comforting warmth (although I wouldn't mind a bit more curry next time), and a scrumptious beef rice dish that was both generous in portion and rich in taste. It's quite the surprise that such a small kitchen can produce such well-rounded flavors. This place is a must-visit for those looking to satisfy their late-night cravings with some truly satisfying fare.

Very authentic Thai restaurant, serving family style dishes in an informal setting with bright yellow tables which make food look tasty. Very friendly staff who will always give you a recommendation if you are not familiar with the menu. I like turmeric chicken and Pad Prik Khing Pork Belly but most items are very delicious. Ginger lemonade is very refreshing out of non alcoholic beverage options. It's a sister restaurant from Pure Thai which is located a few block up but serves a completely different atmosphere and no wait unlike at Pure Thai. I highly recommend this place for all Asian cuisine lovers!

Randomly stopped by this place enroute to an Indian restaurant. The interior design is very modern and cute for a date.I ordered the sesame tofu that came with bento flakes and sesame sauce. This is so so good! Its very flavorful and its aesthetically pleasing.Next is the pork knuckle over rice which was a little salty but very tasty as well.

Came here for a private social event. The restaurant sectioned off the end area of the restaurant for our party to stand and mingle. Great sangrias served, not too sweet and just right punch. There were small bites served as well. My favorite was the cheese croquettes. These came out fresh from the fryer and in bite sizes. So dangerous for my diet. I also had their version of bruschetta. I was amazed to hear they import the bread from Spain - it is half cooked and they finish it here in NYC! My night got much better when the churros came out. Again, piping hot, fresh with warm chocolate sauce to dip it into. I will definitely be coming back here again to try out the rest of their offerings. I came here on a Thursday night at 6:30pm and the restaurant was half empty FYI.

HK Wonton Garden is my go-to spot for anything involving wonton noodle soup. Eat-in or take out, this is the place for piping hot noodle soups. You can add spruce up your wonton noodle soup by adding toppings such as roast meats (duck, pork chick), beef (tripe, tendon, stew, balls), fish balls, or veggies. Pro-tip is you can order frozen wontons to take home. As others have said, the service here is nothing to write home about but the food well makes up for it. I'm hoping this establishment never goes out of business!

I recently visited a lovely wine bar in our neighborhood and was thoroughly impressed by their offerings. They have an excellent selection of wines, with glasses starting at an affordable US$6 during happy hour. The food menu also provides good choices that pair well with their wines. Highly recommend for a cozy evening out.

Title: Brunch Delight with the Girls at [Restaurant Name]

I recently visited [Restaurant Name] for a brunch gathering with my friends and it was a delightful experience. Kicking things off, we enjoyed a shared pitcher of screwdrivers that set a fun and relaxed tone.

The brunch menu impressed with its variety, catering to all our cravings. A friend opted for the super healthy shrimp sauté, a choice for the health-conscious. I, along with another friend, savored the steak and eggs. The steak was succulent, paired with perfectly scrambled eggs – just needed a touch of seasoning.

An unexpected joy was the complimentary tiramisu they brought out, a sweet nod to the friendly and attentive service we received throughout our meal. The restaurant space is generously sized, boasting both upstairs and downstairs dining options. Its airy, well-lit ambiance enhanced by natural light made for a comfortable setting.

Clean restrooms are conveniently located on both floors, echoing the attention to detail found throughout the establishment. For anyone looking to indulge in a satisfying brunch experience, [Restaurant Name] is a must-try. Don't forget to follow my foodie trail on Instagram at @SaltandSavor for more tasty adventures!

Rating: 4.5/5

Title: Comfort Food Haven by Bellevue – Moonstruck Diner Delights

My recent visit to the Moonstruck Diner near Bellevue Hospital on 1st Ave and 28th St was a testament to classic diner charm. Sharing the same ownership as its 3rd Ave sibling, this spot maintains the genuine diner spirit, catering to those of us who appreciate simple, well-executed comfort food.

The menu offers everything you'd expect from a diner, but what stands out is how consistently the food meets those expectations—served up promptly, with dishes arriving at the right temperatures, whether it's a steamy stack of pancakes or a crisp Caesar salad. With pricing that's a notch below the usual midtown east fare, your wallet will breathe a sigh of relief without compromising on quality.

Service here is both efficient and courteous, and the dessert roster is worth lingering over. The banana cream pie hits all the right notes, and while the fruit pies are also a delight, the cakes are respectable but not standout.

The ambiance is unfussy yet pleasant, with cleanliness that's immediately noticeable. The bonus feature of booths with park views adds a touch of tranquility to your dining experience. Whether it's a day of dealing with hospital matters or just a neighborhood jaunt, Moonstruck Diner is an inviting spot that'll lift your spirits with a good meal.

After work, my fiance picked me up and just wanted to roam the city and try something new.  We like to do that together.  We were driving around to places we rarely go to and we decided just to park and walk into a restaurant we both agreed on.We parked across the street from this restaurant and decided to give it a shot.  I'm glad we did because it's probably the best steak I've had in a really long time.  Usually, Ikinaris are where you stand to eat the steak quickly right after it's been made.  Here, though, they have high chairs and tables.  We came on a weekday after I got out of work so it wasn't busy.  That was nice.  Here's what we ordered:-  (2x) Ribeye 10oz - one medium with onions and corn, one rare with onions and broccoli-  Garlic Pepper Rice-  Amabuki Strawberry - you get to keep the glass-  Amabuki Sunflower - you get to keep the glassIt may not seem like a lot, but this was enough food for 2 people.  It was delicious and hope to try this again real soon!

Bubbys, I love you!We added ourselves to the wait list on Sunday and showed up around 5 minutes before our seating time. The place was packed, which was expected for 1pm on a Sunday. We ended up waiting another 10-15 minutes before we were seated. There are a ton of good options so it was definitely hard to decide. We ultimately went with mac & cheese to share, while I got biscuits and gravy and my boyfriend the banana walnut pancakes. The food came out super quick and everything was delicious! The biscuits and gravy were super delicious but there was barely any sausage. The home fries also weren't really that good. The pancakes were so soft and fluffy, and the toppings weren't too sweet for the whole dish. The mac & cheese was very cheesy but a little on the bland side. They have a super friendly wait staff and play some really good hip hop. Overall a great brunch experience and I'll definitely be coming back!

I found this place on yelp as I was searching for a place for valentine's day dinner. I dint know that this restaurant is in the back of Eataly until I went inside. I usually come to eataly to have a pizza slice or some desserts from their bakery but never went inside the restaurant area. But it is surprisingly a very big area and the view is amazing. This area is also shared by other restaurant LA pizza and LA pasta.I had a reservation at 8 pm but we arrived early around 7:30 and they checked our coat as the table was ready. We started with some complimentary bread with extra virgin olive oil. Their were 3 different types of bread and 2 slices of each. I really liked the tomato focaccia bread. We ordered gnocchi sorrentina and Maialino from the Dinner menu. They also had a special valentine'd day menu. Our waiter told us that our order will take 15-20 mins and we were fine by that as we were on a window seat and the view was amazing, was seeing the WTC with all the colorful lights. Our order came in 15 mins, and both dishes looked amazing. Gnocchi - 4/5I was craving for a pasta but as soon as I saw gnocchi in the menu, I knew its going to my dinner. It came with melted burrata on the top, tomato sauce which was tasty but very less, should have been more on the plate. Gnocchi without sauce and burrata was bland, there was very little seasoning. Overall I liked it, with little more seasoning and more sauce it would have been perfect.Maialino - 4/5The grilled pork and the pork belly was really good but my husband dint like the vegetables that it came with. Their dessert menu looks really amazing but we were so full that we dint order any dessert. But they gave one fennel cookie and one small chocolate crisp as complimentary desserts. I had a great time, service was very good. Its ambiance is very fancy, a good place for a date. Restrooms are very clean and spacious.

Title: A Taste of Authentic Persian Delights

My recent visit to this unassuming eatery, cozily sharing space with a pizza joint, proved to be a delightful foray into Persian cuisine. The food, contrary to expectations, was authentically flavorful without an overwhelming spice profile.

I dined in with a bowl of ash-e-reshteh soup, which offered a mild yet satisfying experience, primarily thanks to the aromatic fried onions and garlic. Accompanying the soup was a sesame bread that, while unremarkable, did not disappoint.

Taking home a beef kabob and a celery artichoke beef curry proved to be an excellent decision. They retained their delightful flavors, with the beef kabob being notably succulent and delicious even the next day.

Whether opting for a sit-down meal or takeout, this place is a solid choice for those looking to explore the subtleties of Persian cuisine.

I loveeeee this place! May be my new favorite Mexican spot after work! The place is decorated beautifully! The food was delicious. I highly recommend the table side guacamole if you're a fan because it is soooo good! I had the taco Assad and loved them. My friends had the short rib which was very soft and well seasoned. My other friend had the ceviche assortment and she loved the spice on them. There is also something for everyone here which is even better even for picky eaters. Also the cocktails were great but wish they had olives for the martinis!

I've visited this gem of a spot twice for their happy hour and both times, I've left thoroughly impressed. The happy hour menu is outstanding, offering a variety of enticing options that are sure to delight. With a vibrant bar atmosphere complemented by top-notch service, this place has quickly become one of my favorites. While I've only stopped in for drinks and appetizers, the experience was so positive that I'm eager to return for a full meal. Don't pass up the chance to enjoy their offerings; I can't recommend it enough!

I recently discovered a quaint eatery while wandering near NYU looking for a quick bite. The service was impressively swift and the staff was exceptionally cordial, which I greatly appreciated. However, one downside was the temperature of the pizza; it was not quite as hot as I'd hoped for, especially on the chilly day when a steaming slice would have been perfect. Despite that, the overall experience was favorable.

On a recent frigid visit to my one-time local haunt on the lower east side, I indulged in my all-time favorite 'Wolf Attack' – a heartwarming pile of tater tots topped with meat sauce, gooey cheese, sautéed onions, and the kick of fresh jalapeño. It's a dish that never disappoints.

However, nostalgia aside, the restaurant's menu has hit a stalemate. Years ago, their wraps, bursting with fresh ingredients, seemed inventive, but the novelty has since worn off after sampling three or four similar varieties. Their saving grace has been the delectable beet salad with its rich goat cheese and aromatic dill, which has kept my palate interested.

I rate this spot as A-OK – the food quality remains high, but the lack of variety has made the experience rather monotonous for a loyal, returning customer like myself. It's time for this place to spice up their menu with new creations that live up to their initial inventiveness.

Title: A Fiesta of Flavors at My Go-To Margarita Haven

Review:
This margarita bar has firmly established itself as my favorite, serving up what I boldly claim to be the best Mexican cuisine in town. Each visit guarantees a culinary delight; I’ve yet to be disappointed by a meal, with its remarkable high-end quality consistency. Be prepared for a vibrant atmosphere, as its popularity means it's always bustling and lively—a testament to its reputation. If you're seeking top-notch Mexican fare and tantalizing margaritas, look no further.

The meal I had here was amazing! We had the following:-tuna tartare: this is one of the best that I've had at a restaurant. The sauce that comes with this is just amazing.-burrata: this came with a strawberry compote and the combination was so good and original -sea bass: this was cooked perfectly and the sauce that came with it was amazing. I also loved the roasted artichoke hearts that came with it.-prosciutto wrapped pork chop: my husband loved this dish-mashed potatoes: so good and creamy. I would definitely recommend. This restaurant was great!

Very large venue with lots of tables!  The steak deserves 5 stars and the service was great-the sides however are skippable. I shared the porterhouse steak for 2...I wish I didn't have to share! The flavor was delicious, unbelievably tender, and the cook was perfection! Side of sautéed asparagus wasn't good. The flavor was lacking, it was oily, and they didn't remove true ends-it was very stringy and chewy at the ends that I actually couldn't chew it. I had to spit those parts out. The side of mashed potatoes was also not very good. They were very bland and not as creamy as I was expecting. The slice of carrot cake was very small for the cost and it was not good. It was dry, crumbly, and lacked that decadent, sumptuous taste I look forward to in a carrot cake. I'd absolutely come back for the steak. Skip everything else!

I'm gonna be honest: you always hear so much about barbecue but I felt like it was always overrated! I'd give the obligatory nod and smile when people would rave about brisket or ribs but it was more to appease them. Never a true reflection of the cooking that we were addressing. Until now. Oddly enough, deep in the heart of New York City lies the best barbecue anywhere. Hill Country Barbecue Market changes the game when it comes to barbecue. Let me tell you how. First off, they utilize market pricing style. For those who don't know what that means, it means you pay for what it weighs. I love this concept. But for those of you who are indecisive, they also have specials. For us, we split the 2 meats for $23 which featured a third of a pound of two meat entrees (with the exception of 3 items, but still left plenty of options) and 2 sides. When you order your meats, you get two choices: moist or lean. If you're a true foodie that eats for your heart, the answer is easy. But with the rise of all these diets and preferences, lean was also a necessary addition. But boy oh boy if you get the moist meat you are in for a treat. It is literally dripping. The brisket was the most impressive when it came to being moist because the meat followed the every command of your fork. It was beautiful. Now let me run down the food. We tried the Brisket and the Pulled Pork. Thanks to my best friend I was also able to sample the sausage. The sausage was very unique. It was well done, very meaty and mildly smoky. A worthy nod to its southern origins. The pulled pork was something mouthwatering. Extremely moist, flavorful but not overbearing and filling. The thing that I always judge a barbecue place by is their brisket. And if this place was to be solely judged by that, they'd be second to none. The Brisket meat itself was a very good quality. I opted for the moist, so there were no other utensils required. I was able to dive in to any piece at any point, simply by using my fork to divide it. It was heavenly. If you wanted the best bite simply get everything attached. Gather a good hunk of meat and be sure to get some skin along with it. The skin adds an element of seasoning that helps complete the taste. This is truly the way barbecue is supposed to taste. So if you're one of those who is like I was (a carnivore with no idea why people think barbecue is so good when it's just ok) then I'd direct you to the city. I know, it sounds counterintuitive to me too. But trust me, this is why barbecue is so coveted and so good.

Had such a great time at this authentic Japanese restaurant! We started out with the sapoon lemon drink which was my absolute favorite! So fresh and curated perfectly. The decor was nice and you have the option to take off your shoes and sit on the floor like traditional Japanese style and eat your food! We started off with edamame and a tuna avocado salad. Both were as expected! Then we ordered the crunchy stone crab roll which was so delicious and I would definitely order again. The tofu roll was a bit off for me texture wise and flavor was average. The miso cod could have had a little more sauce on it, but it was cooked nicely. My absolute favorite out of everything would have to be the beef cooked on a hot stone! It was Devine and I would come back just for that! Absolutely delicious. Service was a little slow due to possibly how busy they were.

Went here after work with a group of coworkers on a Friday night. In order to make a reservation I had to give my credit card because there was a minimum that we had to spend. Upon arrival I was expecting a little more in decor and customer service so I was a little disappointed in that but it was cool. Our waiter almost argued with us because we needed another table to fit our group but eventually he agreed. The tables are so small. The drinks were good the food was good. It did get crowded really fast

Title: A Hidden Gem Just a Stone's Throw from Port Authority

Review: I stumbled upon this culinary delight quite by chance and oh, what a fortunate discovery! Nestled conveniently closer than its downtown sibling, this spot is a godsend for those of us trekking in from Jersey. I swung by around 3:30 PM to find a serene setting, ideal for a quick service, which I indeed received with a warm welcome. Within mere minutes, the lady at the register served up a tender combo that set my taste buds alight. The chicken tenders were a masterful blend of flaky, seasoned crust and succulent meat, while the fries struck that perfect balance between crispy and tender. And the sauces? Each one was a match made in heaven with the chicken. Counting down the moments until my next visit!

I went to this place because One Bite Everyone Knows the rules claimed this was the best slice he has ever had. I say the slices were just OK, it was hot in temperature but I did wish the pizza was crunchy, I think all slices should be crunchy. All the regular slices had major flop and that was a major issue for me. I visited twice to make sure I wasn't crazy and I was disappointed both times.The food:Upside Down Cheese Slice- Slices of mozzarella, Pecorino, tomato sauce, wild Sicilian oregano, breadcrumbs. I enjoyed the Upside down over the Cheese slice, I think this was my fav of the three but it the slice was crunchy then I would have enjoyed it a little more. yelp.com/user_local_phot…Cheese Slice- Tomato sauce, shredded mozzarella, Parmesan. Just an OK slice, it was actually a little bland and the crust wasn't crunchy. Heritage Sausage Slice- Tomato sauce, mozzarella, homemade sausage, garlic, Parmesan, olive oil. The sausage slice was good but the onion and garlic were a bit too overwhelming. yelp.com/user_local_phot…Al Pastor Square- Mozzarella, tomato sauce, pineapple sauce, jalapeno, pickled red onion, roasted pork, cilantro, pecorino. I tried this just for the sheer silliness of it. The Al Pastor tasted very Americanized and I felt the pineapple was way too sweet. The dough was too airy, it felt too much like Detroit style pizza and I wasn't crazy about it. yelp.com/user_local_phot…

I used live in this area and I didn't know Japanese steak place around this area. I passed by this place early summer and we talked about try this place when we have time. Finally we've tried this place. Stopped by early dinner. The staffs were very welcome and there's only few peoples. We sats immediately and our waitress asked us to try this place before. We never been this place and we didn't know how to order. She explained us how to order. She was super nice and it made us felt very special. You have go to front of kitchen for order your food after you choice what to order and you have tell to the staffs if you wanna salad or rices or etc. It's little confused us when we ordered. I thought it would be better if I can order it once, not a separate. (Rate 2star because of that point, I would give 3star for their food) We ordered wagyu steak cube with soup, salad, rice. I wanted try cauliflower rice but unable to order. I choose onion dressing for my salad and it really yummy and my friend choose pepper dressing(it's good too). I accidentally put J steak sauce a lot and it made very salty my steak. Please be careful when you try add steak sauce. Miso soup was pretty decent but salty for my licking. I always eat well done for my steak anywhere else but this place wagyu was very soft even my steak was well done but oily for my licking. Totally it was good experience. I will stop by this place for try to their lunch menu. I personally thought you wouldn't disappoint this place with their lunch special menu.

It's very possible that I just didn't order the right items or that the dishes I tried didn't align with my personal tastes, but I was not wowed by my experience here. I came with a friend for dinner and did the pick n' mix, which lets you try the half size of two different entrees for $18. I thought some of the dishes I tried were pretty good but did not enjoy some of the others, and prices were on the high side for servings that were not very large.Service was very friendly. Seating is at communal tables.Recommended:-Turmeric Curry Chicken - it's good, very tender and flavorful.-Tepo Curry Pork Belly - flavorful curry but the amount of pork belly is very small.OK:-Braised Short Rib - I didn't try this but my friend said it was good, though he preferred the pork belly.Not recommended:-Thai Omelette ($9) - very average omelette, tastes like something you can make at home. I definitely did not feel was worth the price.-Stir Fried Kabocha Squash - way too sweet. We couldn't eat this.

Title: A Happy Hour Delight at [Restaurant Name]

My fiancé and I ventured into [Restaurant Name] for happy hour yesterday and were greeted by a buzzing crowd. Despite the challenge of navigating through the packed space, we managed to snag some enticing deals at the bar – $6 margaritas, $5 Sam Adams seasonal drafts, and irresistible $1 empanadas.

The highlight of our visit was undoubtedly the empanada trio. I savored a mix of chicken, shrimp, and the intriguing Viejo ropa (steak), while my fiancé, content with chicken, agreed that each flavor was exceptional. A special nod to the hot sauce available at the bar; it was a fiery delight with a kick of flavorful authenticity.

As the clock struck 7 PM, the atmosphere relaxed with the close of happy hour. Through the hustle, our bartender was the epitome of friendly efficiency. A pro tip for future visitors: arrive early to sidestep the wait.

Eager for another round of those shrimp empanadas, [Restaurant Name] has certainly secured a spot on our "must-return" list. Service and ambiance aside, it's the tasty bites that beckon a second visit.

So good! We had the 14 piece omakase option. It's very reasonably priced for the quality of the sushi and ambiance of the place (quiet with jazz music). The waitress was also very attentive and friendly. The sushi chefs looked skilled and spoke Japanese. Can't wait to go back.

Upon stepping into this hidden gem, one is immediately transported to a high-end establishment reminiscent of Thailand's finest. The restaurant's interior exudes elegance, setting a luxurious backdrop for the dining experience.

Starting with the Ray Rai Nah Phu, this appetizer was a delightful surprise, serving up a creative mix of crab and noodles adorned with a scrumptious coconut curry sauce. The King Pad Thai followed, offering a traditional flavor enhanced by a generous use of tamarind and spices—a familiar dish executed with finesse and presented with an artistic twist, wrapped in an omelet.

The Crispy Catfish Salad, while not groundbreaking, was a solid dish, meshing the familiar notes of spicy lime chili sauce found in Thai cuisine with the satisfying crunch of fried catfish. 

Though not the most adventurous Thai food I've tasted, the meal was satisfying overall, with particularly high marks for the appetizer and the visual presentation of the dishes.

This is a very charming restaurant in "little Italy". Their decor is very cute and it feels just like you are in Italy when you are inside. They have fresh pasta made daily and brick oven pizza. We ordered pizza and eggplant Parmesan. The pizza had a thinner crust with a nice crunch, it was pretty good. Eggplant Parmesan is one of my favorite dishes in general. Theirs is decent, but was not my favorite. They are also supposed to bring us bread with our meal, but we didn't get any. Apparently they forgot, so make sure you ask for some. We liked this place, but it was not anything out of the ordinary or extremely special. I more than likely wouldn't go back. Not to mention the prices for anything other than pizza, are kind of high.

Title: A Little Slice of Cuba Near Washington Square Park

I serendipitously stumbled upon this Cuban gem while looking for a dining spot near Washington Square Park. The anticipation for my visit was fueled by alluring Yelp photos and a craving for authentic Cuban cuisine.

Upon arrival, I was immediately captivated by the vibrant decor that seemed to transport me straight to Havana. Following the recommendation of online reviews, I opted for the seafood paella and, despite my usual aversion to squid, found myself enamored with the flavors of the dish. I deftly navigated around my tentacled friends, but I still reveled in the well-seasoned, oceanic tapestry of rice and seafood.

The staff elevated the experience with their exceptional service, bringing the warmth of Cuban hospitality to the heart of the city. While I may not have become a squid aficionado, I left with a satisfied palate and a resolve to return. This restaurant is a must-visit for anyone looking to savor Cuban cuisine with a side of ambiance.

Definitely one of the omakase places in the places worth trying. What I like about this experience is that they also offer tables as well as the sushi bar. Came on a Tuesday night and they were pretty busy! Sushi bar reservations were all taken. They have 3 options for omakase, a lighter option, they regular which is $60 and their third option which is $85. I like this idea because it caters to people who might not be super hungry and people who have a higher appetite. I was decently full with the regular. It was 12 courses I believe. It starts with  salmon tataki and fish miso soup. When you're at a table and not the sushi bar, the sushi pieces come out 3-4 pieces at a time and ends with a choice of handrolls (I got the toro with radish) and a piece of egg on the side, not exactly tomago but more a cakey texture? Not sure how to describe it but I enjoyed it. The scallops and uni stood out to me amongst all the pieces, I guess this depends on your taste preference. I thought the idea of radish and toro in a hand roll would be weird, but I surprisingly enjoyed it. They give you sushi on the side here and they don't put it between the fish and rice for you like a lot of places, which is good for people who don't enjoy wasabi.

I haven't had a lot of Filipino food in the city, but this place did satisfy my craving! My friend and I shared the pork sisig and the tosilog. The flavors were good and the eggs were cooked well. The pork was slightly over cooked and the dishes were a bit salty for me, but I'm generally more sensitive to salt than the average consumer. The sweet pork paired well with the garlic rice and I liked that the sisig actually came out sizzling! The staff was kind and we ordered at the counter first and the food was brought out to us. It was a homey place and if you're looking to satisfy a craving I would suggest this place.

Why has it been 3 years since I've been here ?!?Depressing !! This place is awesome sauce, I must come frequently. Came on a Sunday night for the live Cuban salsa band. The place was so packed!! Was lucky to get a table along the side pretty quickly. Order first round of lychee martinis without even looking at the menu. I don't play games!! The lychee martinis are just rocking. Everyone knows this by now. The staff was so attentive, always asking if anything was needed. Loved how it was a few people always checking up on the tables. Service at its best. Ordered calamari and honey ginger salmon. The calamari was the best calamari I've ever had. The fact that it was so crunchy yet the calamari itself was not chewy was just amazing. Dunk it into the sauce and you have a glimpse of heaven. It's a must try please! Would drive from central jersey any time to have that. The honey ginger salmon was delicious. Salmon was so fresh, tender and seasoned well. The coconut rice is a staple here as well, just too dang good. Four lychee martinis later and I was up dancing to salsa music, who would have thought!!! First for me :-) I will 100% be back and totally recommend this place.

Winter weather calls for a warm bowl of spicy ramen.Karakatta has been on my to-do list for a bit, and it was worth the wait. It's definitely one of my top ramen shops in Manhattan!It's not the biggest place. About the same size as Minca, but somehow feels lot roomier. I walked in around 7:45 on a Friday and there was no wait (but by the time I was getting done, there was a line out the door). I grabbed a seat at the corner of the counter, perfect for solo dining.I ordered the "jumbo" pork gyoza and the spicy ginger stamina. I would've gotten the butter ramen, but wanted to save room in my stomach for heavy drinking later on. And so I could try out the gyoza.The gyoza was as advertised - jumbo. Two big ass gyozas, each heavily charred on one side, with two dipping sauces - a soy and a chili one. Pretty good, but more of a novelty than anything.The ginger stamina, however, was awesome! I don't think I've ever seen/had ramen where ginger was so heavily featured. But it adds a nice complexity to the flavor, especially with a different type of spiciness. The bowl also came with 2-3 large pieces of smokey pork belly, half of a perfectly cooked egg, and the broth was FULL of minced pork. Like... a LOT of it. You definitely get your money's worth for just $15.50! The noodles were also thick and springy. So good!The only thing I can fault them on is that the food took a bit to come out, and the gyoza and ramen basically came at the same time, rather than coursed out. It looked to just be 3 guys in the kitchen making everything, so it's understandable.All in all, I definitely recommend Karakatta!

Title: A Hearty Feast at a Local Gem

I recently dined at a spot that's earned the approval of 2555 other satisfied guests, and I'm excited to add my own recommendation. For seamless entry, assemble your full party and use the 9th Street entrance.

Upon arrival, expect a brief wait outdoors before being seated. I indulged in the deluxe meat plate, a generous serving priced at $20, loaded with an assortment of traditional delights: a choice of meat, potato, sauerkraut and mushroom pierogi, meat stuffed cabbage drenched in a savory mushroom gravy, perfectly grilled kielbasa, and a zesty side of sour cream & beet horseradish salad. Opt for the borscht – a warm beet soup enriched with a dollop of semi-sweet sour cream and accompanied by a hearty slice of bread – it's a must-have!

Every bite was a celebration of flavor, especially when enhancing the cabbage with horseradish and adorning the pierogis with a mix of sour cream and buttered grilled onions. Despite the tempting dessert menu, I was thoroughly satisfied and capped off my meal with a refreshing bottle of Obolon.

The sight of latkes on a neighboring table caught my eye; rest assured, I'll be returning to sample those. If you're looking for a hearty meal that promises to both delight and satiate, this is the place to be.

One of the most famous pizzerias in New York.I just wanted to see what the hype was about, so I got one regular slice ($3). I was expecting to be mind blown, but it was just like any other good pizza in New York. I think the main appeal is the wall full of photos of celebrities who have visited this pizzeria. I think you feel more love for this place once you spot photos of your favorite celebrities. I certainly smiled when I saw some of my favorites.Definitely worth trying at least once just for the experience.

Retroactive to February 2018:I came in with high expectations. Someone I trust a great deal touts Keens as the best steakhouse in NYC. Jury's still out on that for me, but it was definitely very good.Porterhouse for 2: seems like the only logical option for two carnivores. Cooked perfectly to medium rare. Could have been seasoned a tad more.Side dishes were forgettable; I literally do not remember which we got. Caesar salad app was excellent however.Love the way the bill is dropped off in a "Bad News" envelope. A fun(?) way to settle up at the end of the night.

Title: A Slice Above in an Unexpected Place

As someone who's always on the lookout for a praiseworthy pie, my recent dining experience at Marta managed to impress, despite the steep prices. Tucked away in an almost desolate block, it's a beacon for those craving quality in an area overshadowed by Koreatown. Be forewarned that the restaurant inconspicuously shares its entrance with a hotel, but once inside, you're in for a culinary treat.

Marta's takes on pizza diverge from the Neapolitan style I hold dear, such as that from Motorino. Opting for an ultra-thin, cracker-like crust, their Roman-style pizzas offer a lighter, if not airier, bite. True, my preference leans towards a more substantial chew, similar to a classic New York slice or the offerings at Rubirosa. However, I must acknowledge the appeal Marta's version may hold for aficionados of crispier crusts.

Our table indulged in four varieties, with the Margherita standing tall as the undisputed favorite, closely tailed by the savory clam and hearty fungi options. Complementing the pizzas was a surprisingly standout house salad, which, despite its simplicity and eyebrow-raising $18 tag, justified every penny with its fresh greens and perfect pairing with the mains.

While appetizers might take a backseat for those prioritizing pizza indulgence, they're a commendable addition for larger groups. The ricotta with grilled bread was notably generous and well-balanced – a pet peeve of mine resolved, as they didn't skimp on the bread needed to savor every last dollop of ricotta.

Admittedly, we didn't venture into dessert territory, having fully surrendered to the preceding courses. The service was affable, with our waitress adding a touch of humor about the quirky charm of crabapples playfully dropping from an overhead plant.

The only shortfall came from the cocktail menu. My usual penchant for sweet and fizzy concoctions found no ally here – a rarity for me but a hiccup in an otherwise delightful dining ordeal.

In essence, Marta serves up an experience worthy of its price tag for those who appreciate its distinct take on pizza and who prefer quality over quantity. Next time you find yourself near Koreatown, let your appetite guide you to this unexpected gem.

Title: A Slice of Heaven at Sofia's Pizza Shop

If you find yourself in the city with a pizza craving, Sofia's is the place to go. Their New York-style pizza is a must-try, boasting a perfect thin crust that I personally prefer. Though, for those who enjoy a bit more chew, the thicker crust options are definitely worth sampling.

My introduction to Sofia's was nothing short of an adventure – a mad dash through the city streets, culminating in a victorious, last-minute arrival. Their staff's generosity, gifting my friend and I a free slice each upon closing, made for an unforgettable first visit.

Nowadays, living just two blocks away, Sofia's has become my weekend staple. The service remains consistently fast and welcoming, while the pizzas continue to impress with robust flavors and an ideally crispy-chewy crust balance. Despite a price that's a bit above average, the quality and experience consistently prove its value.

Drop in and savor your pie fresh out of the oven – Sofia's is a neighborhood gem that shouldn't be overlooked.

My partner and I chose this restaurant for our date night and were thoroughly impressed. The ambiance exuded a warm charm that set the stage for an unforgettable evening. To our delight, live music played gently in the background, adding an exquisite touch to the experience. The cuisine was nothing short of incredible, making every bite a celebration of flavor. This establishment has quickly become a treasured local favorite and a hidden gem for any meal. We're already looking forward to our next visit.

Beautiful restaurant inside of Grand Central. We noted that it was our anniversary when we made the reservation on their website, and they gave us a cute little note that said "happy anniversary" and complimentary champagne. The place has a tasting menu with six courses, but it cost $165 per person, and that was just out of our price range, so we ended up getting one appetizer and one entrée per person. I wasn't a fan of the sunchoke salad, but the beef tartare, Atlantic cod, and wagyu beef were amazing. My only complaint (which is expected from this kind of restaurant, I guess) is that the portions were extremely small for the price that they charged. We left the restaurant still hungry and ended up going across the street to get Chinese food... lol. Also... still not really sure what  Scandinavian food is.

This shop has huge pizza slices with decadent toppings, but still has the feel of a family run pie shop. It is definitely pricey but you won't be disappointed with the slices. Try splitting one of the samplers with a buddy so you can taste a few of their specialty pies. Of course the artichoke basil variety is incredible, but don't sleep on the crab pizza. Pro tip: take leftovers home and reheat the crab pizza for brunch. They are also open late night.

This place was PACKED. As in, line all the way out in a snake assembly line kinda packed too.Well. We ordered the carne asada and nopal tacos, and the pollo asado and adobada tostadas. Pros: Very authentic flavor! We especially loved the adobada - the marinated pork was seasoned wonderfully. Carne asada was pretty good too. The tortillas by themselves overall was just eh. Nothing much to shout about. Probably the least favorite meat of all was the pollo, but it still tasted pretty good. Also another pro - their selection of sauces. Insane. If you know how to season your tacos well with the salsas and sauces they have, it'll be a pretty fantastic ride for you. Cons - the nopal. We were kinda sad about this one! Heard rave reviews and we've had nopal elsewhere but this one was just had some texture we couldn't finish. It was just a little bit too slimy for us. So. Was it worth the queue? Sorta. I think flavor wise they were authentic, but I don't think I'd come back because it just gets way too packed, and while the tacos were great - they weren't 45 minutes in-the-cold great. But still - worth a try.

Really cute place with a neighborhood feel. The drinks were tasty. We ordered the steak tartare and spinach and artichoke dip. The ambiance was very cozy and the service was good. I would recommend this place. I heard the happy hour is great and that they have late night happy hour as well on some days.

Pretty good lamb over rice and it's only $5 including a soda or water! The cart is located by Hunter College and they were very friendly. They have three types of sauces, white, hot, and green. I'm not sure what is in the green sauce since it doesn't taste much different from the white sauce, but it has a bright artificial green color to it. They also have three types of rice, white, spicy (I think that's what he said), and vegetable rice. You can opt to choose one or mix it up. I recommend the vegetable rice. It's almost like fried rice with pieces of vegetables in it and unique to this cart!

Title: Mixed Feelings During Restaurant Week

My recent visit to [Restaurant Name] during Restaurant Week was a rollercoaster of experiences. While the restaurant was a newcomer to the event, the service was mediocre. A ten-minute wait for water after being seated set a lukewarm tone for the evening.

Additionally, a reservation mishap left a bitter taste. Although I confirmed my reservation via email, upon arrival, the staff could not locate it. Fortunately, the empty dining room meant seating was not an issue. To my dismay, post-meal, I discovered an unwarranted cancellation email sent that very morning.

On a positive note, the chilled corn soup was the star of the night—delicious and refreshing. The crispy skin salmon, despite its perfect tenderness, had an unfortunate fishy taste. The roasted chicken fared better, moist and flavorful, though its accompanying side was overly salty.

Priced at $31 for two courses without the expectation of tipping, Restaurant Week at [Restaurant Name] was indeed a bargain. However, considering the overall experience, I am hesitant to return at full price.

My friend and I have been wanting to try this place for quite a while because of the hype around their burger. We finally made our way to get their famous Emmy burger as well as Arenstein pizza. The burger was juicy and the patty was deliciously cooked. It was flavorful but also very greasy. The pizza was good, but not as much as the burger. It was a bit too salty for my taste. While I recommend getting the burger if you ever visit the restaurant, I don't think it's worth the wait or the price. $26 for a burger is very pricey especially when there wasn't anything super special about it.

Title: A Delightful Discovery Away from Chinatown

I recently had the pleasure of stumbling upon a delightful spot that exceeded my expectations for a culinary adventure. Initially curious about the difference between pot stickers and soup dumplings, a recommendation led me to this bustling haven that's a stone's throw from Chinatown.

Despite it being a busy Saturday night, the wait was minimal, and the atmosphere was vibrant with a hip decor – an added perk was our table's view of the dim sum making process, which was fascinating to watch.

To start, I indulged in a Moulin Rouge cocktail that hit all the right notes, while my friend opted for the Adorable Woman. The server expertly guided us on how much to order. Thanks to a Yelp check-in, we sipped on a complimentary glass of surprisingly good wine.

Our appetizer choices, which included the crab soup dumplings, pan-fried pork buns, and a scallion pancake, were all exceptionally delicious. For mains, the Black pepper beef with macadamia was succulent, and the Typhoon Shelter garlic shrimp was flavorful, although we would have preferred it shelled for easier enjoyment.

This place has firmly established itself as a must-visit whenever I'm in the area. And I've made it clear to my friend, should she dine here without me, I'd be green with envy! A gem indeed, this restaurant is worthy of all the praise.

The spicy coco soup gets 5 stars! I ordered that and enjoyed it right away while sitting by the window for all to see on the most frigid day. It was awesome. The shrimp in the soup were perfectly cooked and the broth was delicious. I ordered the shrimp pad Thai to go and that was ordinary and a bit dry. I would make a trip to Washington Heights for that soup though for sure!

Came here on a Thursday night with my sister. The atmosphere is great and I love the decor inside, the food & service- not so much. To start, we told our waitress about how our table was shaky and uneven and she said she had something to put underneath one of the legs for us... that never happened. We even asked a second time, nothing. Our drinks were okay, nothing to write home about. The food was (unsurprisingly) lack luster. I've eaten at another Smith location before and had the same reaction but I decided to give it another go. The hot potato chips with the blue cheese was actually the best, but very heavy. We ate about a quarter of the bowl so I'd say if there's only two of you- make sure you're hungry - or skip it. The fried green tomatoes were okay but also very heavy. The tagliatelle was good but later on both my sister and I had horrible stomach pains. Throughout the night I felt sick and we spent a good $45 each. Waste of money, won't be trying another Smith restaurant.

Sofia's doesn't disappoint when it comes to delivering a variety of tasty pizza slices in the neighborhood. The service is commendably fast, ensuring you're not waiting long for your meal. On my visit, the seating area was largely taken up by a group, but the attentive staff quickly accommodated me with an extra stool. A big thank you to the team at Sofia's for going the extra mile!

I ordered the Cacio e Pepe because I've been dying to try pasta tossed in cheese...and because I just love cheese. The dish came topped with prosciutto which was a good protein to complement the dish, however the dish was cheesy without enough flavor. But, I did ask the waiter for some chili peppers and it definitely helped add some kick!

We came here with out receipts in hand from Maharlika, in order to redeem our free cocktails. The waitress tried to make it difficult for us to use these vouchers, trying to say that we had to order a side to use them and that only a few options were available to choose from when neither of these were stated on the receipt. The drinks were good and mine actually tasted like ube but also had a nice alcoholic kick to it. I would have ordered more, but they were also quite pricey.

Title: Numero 28 - Mediocre at Best

I have tried Numero 28 on several occasions through Seamless, enticed by the seemingly attractive 30% discount. Despite this, I'm convinced the menu is marked up to compensate. They offer an extensive array of creative pizzas, such as the Giulietta topped with pumpkin, pecorino, and pancetta for $19. However, their "artisan" pies are disappointingly small given the price, especially when compared to competitors like Roberta's or Marta.

Priced similarly, pasta dishes like the farfalle al salmone also underwhelm in both portion and taste, raising doubts about the pasta being homemade – a suspicion that adds to the sting of the price tag. On a positive note, the quality of the ingredients is high, and the sauce on the pizzas is commendable. I'd lean towards the red pies over the white for a better experience.

They are reliable for on-time delivery, but overall, while the food is decent, you're likely to find better value and satisfaction elsewhere.

Title: A Tasty First at Artichoke's Pizza

As a New Yorker who had never sampled Artichoke's pizza, the ribbing from my boyfriend finally got us through the door for a late lunch. We settled in at 3:30pm, adhering to the 3 slice table minimum, and opted for their artichoke, margherita, and meatball slices.

Three slices hit the spot for our modest appetites. The margherita was a standout—light, flavorful, and topped with delightfully crunchy basil. Artichoke's titular pizza lived up to its fame with its creamy, indulgent richness, but be warned—it's a heavy hitter. Thanks to the generous sizing, one slice is plenty filling.

In brief, Artichoke's offers up quality pizza that demands a detour for any enthusiast. Just one slice might just be your meal for the day.

My boyfriend and I opted for a delightful twist on our latest visit to Luke's Lobster—we took our shrimp rolls and potato chips to go. While their famed lobster rolls are indeed mouthwatering, I personally have a soft spot for their shrimp variation. Savory and satisfying, these rolls hit the spot. We enjoyed our meal under the open skies of Governor's Island, and it was, without a doubt, the best decision we could have made. A simple yet perfect dining experience.

Restaurant Review: EDH - A Hidden Gem for Dumpling Devotees

Do not be fooled by its unassuming appearance; EDH proves that a simple setting can deliver mouthwatering results. This no-frills eatery serves up a storm with its speedy and neat service. The stars of the menu are undoubtedly the Xiao Long Bao, priced at $8.25, each pork-filled morsel is a juicy delight. The Shumai, a bargain at $7.50, arrives in generous portions that are guaranteed to satisfy, served piping hot. For a perfect side, the Scallion Pancakes at $3.90 make for a crispy, flavorful companion to the dumplings. EDH is your quintessential dumpling dive where the prices are as appealing as the food. I left with the intention to return, next time with an appetite for their Mapo Tofu. If you're seeking delicious food without the frills, EDH is your spot.

Title: A Flavorful Addition to St. Marks: Dry Hot Pot Heaven

Recently, a new culinary gem from Flushing has nestled itself into the bustling St. Marks area, adjacent to NYU – a strategic spot for students with a penchant for customizable dry hot pot. This chain restaurant sports a fresh, clean interior and boasts an attentive staff ready to guide your culinary adventure.

Patrons can select their preferred meats by the pound and veggies by the basket, with an ample variety to satisfy diverse tastes, though the selection is slightly narrower compared to its Flushing counterpart. The spice levels cater to all, ranging from the spice-averse to the thrill-seeking chili aficionados, with a "small" kick that satisfies my moderate spice tolerance.

One should note that rice comes at an additional cost, and prices overall are a touch higher than what one might expect in Flushing – possibly a premium for the convenience of its new locale. The flavors are intensely spicy and numbing, mirroring the Flushing experience, yet I found the dishes to lack the perfect punch of salt, necessitating a quick fix at home to reach that savory sweet spot.

While it might not fully transport you to the food courts of Flushing, this new spot is a welcome addition for NYU students and anyone in St. Marks looking to indulge in the joy of dry hot pot, with a personalized touch.

Title: Budget-Friendly Delight with Comforting Flavors

My recent visit to this spot was an absolute treat for the budget-conscious foodie. With an October special offering buy one get one free ramen, plus a free scoop of gelato for checking in on Yelp, I enjoyed a hearty lunch and dessert for a mere $8.

I opted for the Spicy Miso ramen, which delivered on flavor without overwhelming spice, perfect for those who prefer a milder kick. The portion was generous with plenty of noodles, a perfectly gooey marinated egg, and two succulent slices of tender, well-seasoned pork. I would happily return for another bowl.

My dining partner chose the Ma Yu Ramen but found the broth a tad on the salty side. Despite this, the ramen experience was largely positive.

The rose lychee gelato was the crown jewel of the meal—creamy, smooth, with the delicate balance of rose and lychee to cleanse the palate beautifully after the savory ramen.

The atmosphere of the restaurant is casual with a self-service vibe, complemented by complimentary hot and cold tea. Customer service was attentive and added to the overall pleasant dining experience. Highly recommend for a fulfilling meal that won't break the bank.

Stumbled upon Chicken Curry House on Seamless, and it didn't disappoint. Though meat entrees were a tad pricy for their size – hovering around the $20 mark – the overall experience was delightful.

The Lamb Biryani ($23.99) hit the perfect note of spiciness for thrill-seeking palates without overwhelming them. On the other hand, the Chicken Karahi ($17.99) promised more heat but delivered less kick, though its rich blend of spices, tangy tomato, and ginger won over my roommates and me, securing its spot as our favorite dish.

For a milder, yet equally enjoyable option, the Tarka Dal ($13.99) offered a tasty vegetarian alternative. As for sides, the Garlic Naan ($5.99) is non-negotiable — an ideal complement to every dish. And the Veggie Samosas ($6.99) were a revelation when combined with Raita, green chutney, and a dab of tamarind sauce — an appetizer that didn't last long enough to see the next day.

I recently dined at this local Thai spot and found it to be fairly average. The pad thai was somewhat disappointing, with a scant helping of bean sprouts and egg, and only a few pieces of meat. Unfortunately, the noodles themselves lacked flavor. On a brighter note, the Thai angel wings were a highlight — large, crispy, and quite flavorful even without the accompanying sauce. The prices are reasonable, making this restaurant an acceptable choice for those seeking decent quality Thai fare without the expectation of culinary fireworks.
Bustling NYC eatery, super cool to unexpectedly get 'caught' on one of the evenings for 5 year anniversary, you can always 'catch' deliciously, simply seared seafood hereOrig Post 9/13/16#dodrinkdine

After weeks of buzz, I decided to visit the much-acclaimed new bar in town and it certainly lived up to the hype. The place is a revelation with its ingenious concept of self-service on tap. Boasting an impressive array of 40 taps at the entry, pricing is reasonable, with most offerings between $0.60 to $0.80 per ounce, except for the premium Truly original flavor at $1.10 an ounce.

The setup is intuitive: pick a glass - with chilled ones available for a superior experience - tap your card at your chosen beer, pour within the generous 10-second window, and the display informs you of the cost and remaining card balance. With glass cleaners at the ready, sampling various beers is a breeze.

For non-beer enthusiasts, a full-service bar beckons with the same spirit of variety, including the Truly original flavor on tap and the attractive Truly buckets deal.

I dropped by on a serene Wednesday evening and enjoyed the calm ambiance. However, I've noted the weekend crowds, suggesting this spot is a hit at peak times.

The bar exudes a futuristic vibe, signaling a thrilling direction for the nightlife scene. I'm eagerly looking forward to my next visit!

Title: A Gem for Chinese Comfort Food in the Upper East Side

I've been a regular at this charming spot since my partner's move to the Upper East Side, drawn in by the comforting Chinese cuisine that's both affordable and accommodating to a range of dietary needs (yes, that's inclusive!). This place has become my go-to, even outshining many of New York's ramen joints—and believe me, I've sampled my fair share.

On a particularly blustery Thursday evening, I found warmth not just in the ambience but also in the service—prompt, endearing, and attentive without being intrusive. Despite knowing the menu by heart, I enjoy the ritual of perusal before settling on my customary tan tan men ramen, tweaked with extra kale due to my soybean allergy.

The pork dumplings here are a must-try, easily on par with the best I've savored in Flushing. They're a steal, succulent, and have me secretly hoping they'll be sold in bulk one day. My friend, who was fashionably late, opted for the tonkatsu and wasn't disappointed. My ramen came as a soul-soothing bowl, with a broth perfectly balanced in salinity, fatty pork melting in my mouth, and kale surprisingly uplifting the dish. The only slight drawback was the oiliness from the pork, which can induce a twinge of guilt.

Homemade noodles, irresistibly chewy and generously portioned, make carb-lovers like myself swoon. To close, a refreshing fruit plate cleansed our palates, allowing us to lounge comfortably without the nudge to vacate.

Even a minor mishap with a water spill was handled graciously—with a complimentary vanilla mocha dessert as a delicious apology.

In sum, this restaurant serves delightful, sometimes guilt-free, indulgence with a personal touch, making it a stand-out in the neighborhood for those seeking great food, friendly service, and a cozy dining experience.

Title: Wings That Soar Above the Rest

I recently discovered a wing haven in the city that truly impressed me after a minor hiccup on my first visit. Initially opting for boneless chicken with a dry rub, which turned out excessively dry for my taste, I decided to give it another go. My second attempt was a soaring success – the Mexi and Thai wings / drumsticks were nothing short of scrumptious. The size of the wings is monumental; my boyfriend and I couldn't conquer an 18-piece in one go.

One thing that stood out was the balance of the sauce – abundant yet not overpowering in saltiness or sweetness. As a side note, the fries deserve a shout-out. They're remarkable for delivery food, arriving crispy and flavorful.

During these trying times, I'm thrilled that this establishment offers takeout and delivery. I'm committed to supporting them now and look forward to patronizing them long after the pandemic has passed.

My only problem with this place is that it was a little too warm for my liking. I came with my friend about two weeks ago, and I was still sweating upon entering. I think the air conditioning works here, but it's not too strong. This might be a restaurant to visit on a day that isn't too hot, because you might need it when eating hot food. Make sure to ask them for the ice water. The lunch deal is the way to go here. There are a lot of great looking items on the dinner menu, but it's not as good of a deal as the lunch, which is only like $10.95-11.95, and gives you a ton of food. I ordered the chicken lunch set, and got the degh murgh (my friend got the kolhapuri), and I tried some of his- both were very good.The lunch set (known as thalis) are served with rice, bread, lentils (dal), saag, and some other vegetables of the way. The stuff all tastes excellent, and though the saag tastes a little funny/strong, it pairs excellently with the naan. You also get a small rice pudding. It's honestly a lot of food, so you get a good bang for your buck. Sure, you can actually visit AYCE buffets here in curry hill for just 1 dollar more, but the quality here is pretty high. Totally would come back. The only thing I would recommend to these guys is to fix the air con.

My partner and I recently dined at a unique midtown eatery with an outpost in Osaka, a fun teaser for our upcoming trip to Japan. The experience is an engaging novelty: dining in private booths, communicating with servers via a hidden screen that only lifts when you submit your order or finish your meal. 

Opting for the Recommended set at $24 may seem steep for ramen, but it's the ambiance that adds to the bill. Unlike the standard tonkotsu ramen, this set includes a soft-boiled egg, seaweed, and mushrooms. 

I customized my bowl with medium heat, dashi, and richness, selecting firm noodles, and took advantage of a coupon for a complimentary extra serving of even firmer noodles—a choice I'll repeat.

Though my ramen tended a bit towards the salty side, it's not uncommon for ramen dishes. Next time, I'll scale back the dashi. Overall, it's an entertaining spot for a taste of Japan and a novel dining setup.

The restaurant can be a little bit pricey for what you get. The best value probably is the $30 lunch meal set but it's too much food, but the other options are around $20 and felt like too little food. I had the tea soba and it was just okay, not particularly that different from what I could make from boiling a package at home.

Title: A Bustling Big Apple Debut for a Chicago Favorite

Upon securing a coveted Sunday night reservation at NYC's latest Chicago import via Resy, my anticipation was as high as the crowd levels I encountered. The venue, surprisingly dim and clamorous, challenged my senses before the main event—the famous Single Cheeseburger.

Celebrating a birthday? The restaurant offers a sparkling touch of sparklers atop your burger, delivered with a smile by the affable staff. My partner and I couldn't resist adding an extra egg and bacon to our burger order.

The burger itself, priced at $26, was a decent affair—tasty but overpowered by salt. The bacon paired with the double patty was, for my taste, an overindulgence of meat, though the unconventional addition of a runny egg was a welcome twist. In essence, a good burger, but not exceptional.

While the atmosphere might thrill some, the cacophony made conversation nearly impossible. Despite this, the Windy City's culinary offering is something to experience at least once, even if the space doesn't quite encourage lingering.

Title: A Hidden Gem for Sunday Dim Sum

If you're craving dim sum without the typical weekend wait, this cozy spot is a delightful find. Notably famous for their charming and tasty carrot buns, the restaurant offers a range of dim sum delights that are sure to please. The shumai and shrimp dumplings stood out, bursting with flavor in every bite. Although the chicken feet were passable, they were overshadowed by the delectably prepared ribs and the star attraction – the carrot cake buns. These buns steal the show with their playful appearance and perfectly balanced sweetness.

For anyone looking to escape the long lines of Chinatown, this small establishment is a recommendable alternative. Bear in mind, they incorporate a 15 percent service charge into the final bill, so there's no need to worry about tipping. All things considered, it’s a great pick for a relaxed and satisfying Sunday lunch.

Was going for brunch at Flex Mussels, but they were closed so we decided to try out Sotto 13. They have a 'weekend social brunch', which is basically family style. You get to choose 1 pizza, 2 brunch entrees, 1 side, and 1 drink - which comes in a carafe or bottle depending on your party size. Food portion is determined by the party size, so there should be enough to eat for everyone. Priced at $37 pp, it's a pretty good deal. You can also order a la carte if preferred. Sat in the bar area which started out quiet and we were able to sit right away, but it did quickly fill up. Looks like the kind of place you will have to either go early for or make a reservation. A little mixed on the food. The mushroom pizza was very good and had a lot of flavor. The tuscan eggs were fairly bland - the chickpea had no flavor. Sounded like it would be great, but it just didn't meet expectations at all. The focaccia french toast was ok - average, the creme fraiche it came with was good and made the dish. Ordered the bellini but barely drank it. It was more peach than bubbles. Next time I would just get bubbles with no mixer, if anything.Overall not my favorite spot for brunch, although we did like the pizza and would consider coming back for that. I was a little underwhelmed overall. Service and atmosphere were good, I just wasn't in love with the food. I may give dinner a shot to see if that's any better. Tips: Mushroom pizza

Taboga is such a nice little spot... the bar area has a nice set up... the big screen, the seatings and the pool tables are placed in a way that make the space look bigger than it is!!!However, they have to work on their team. The waitress had no idea what she was doing or how the business works; everytime my coworkers or I asked a question, she would tell us to give that she was going to find out... the girl did not even know what color sangria they had! She did not know at what time happy hour ended, what items (drinks/food) were included, what beers they had... like come on-- that should be like WAITRESS 101.The food was delicious! I got the chimi combo, which came with fries. The fries were to die for!!!! I would actually go back and order fries alone, HAHAHAHAHA; I sound so fat! The beers were nice and cold and the RED sangria was good too!This spot is basically whatever you make it... go with some friends and have a good time. My friends and I went after work, and it was nice!!!! This was the final spot we hit, after two others, and this is the one I liked the most.

Title: A Cozy Gem in the Big Apple

I stumbled upon an absolute treasure of a diner in the heart of New York City. Craving a caffeine fix and a quick bite, this little place was a beacon at 9pm, welcoming us with immediate seating and prompt drink service. The coffee was exceptional – a perfect pick-me-up.

What really sets this diner apart is its sensational deal: for under $18, you're treated to a choice of a main course from a selection of five or six options, an appetizer, and a slice of pie to top it off. Each dish tasted homemade and burst with flavor, a true testament to the care put into their food.

I wholeheartedly recommend this spot for anyone looking to escape the city's frenetic pace and indulge in some comforting, delicious fare. Apologies for the lack of photos – our phones were left to charge back at the hotel. But trust me, the memory of that meal doesn't need visual aids to be unforgettable.

La Contenta truly deserves its five-star rating, and I'm here to tell you why. This gem may be small, but its popularity is well-founded. From the moment I walked in, the festive vibe and pitch-perfect music complemented by the friendly staff made for an excellent start. Surprisingly, they seated me immediately, despite arriving before my friend—an exceptional touch.

The service was swift, as I was quickly greeted with fresh chips and salsa. Their drinks menu shines, with skilled bartenders crafting each beverage to perfection—we sampled four different ones, and each was remarkable.

Dinner was no different. I indulged in a shrimp enchilada with red sauce and grilled brussels sprouts, a meal so satisfying I couldn't finish it. La Contenta is one of those places you don't want to just walk by and admire—you need to experience it. Treat yourself today; it's an absolute culinary delight.

Found this place on yelp (obviously) and came for a weekday lunch. It has a modern feel to it and a bunch of tables running length wise through the restaurant.  Not sure if there is an upstairs as well. The restaurant was pretty empty when we came at noon on a weekday but then it fills up. It has a bar that runs the length of the restaurant and a few people were sitting there as well enjoying a cocktail. We say at one of the tables and although they are small tables they do the job. We started with the buffalo wings. These were standard a wing appetizer as you can get. Decent flavor thought they could use some more heat. For my main meal I had the BH salad which was a spinach salad with chickpeas and a few other vegetables. You have the option to add a protein or avocado. I added avocado for an extra $3. It was pretty good nothing groundbreaking. The salad did the job. The one thing I noticed is the prices here are seemed on the higher side for a typical nyc lunch in a restaurant like that. $20 for a burger seems steep even for nyc standards.  My coworker ordered the oriental salad with shrimp and wasnt blown away by it but it was decent. The shrimp was a $10 upcharge. That is insane. Bh kitchen is nice but not that nice. Overall, we had a good time here and enjoyed our lunch. The price could have been lower and the food a little better but it is what it is. I would come back but I am not dying to.

Tucked away in the bustling Chelsea Market, this gem of a taco spot is worth the inevitable wait. The queue might seem daunting, but the staff operates with impressive efficiency, ensuring a swift and organized experience. Payment is conveniently handled on one side, with receipt in hand, you seamlessly transition to pick-up where your order is prepared before your eyes with lightning speed.

I indulged in the carne asada taco, which I must say, ranks amongst the finest I've tasted. Its savory flavors and perfectly cooked meat made for a memorable meal. My sister's choice of the pollo taco didn't hit the same high notes, turning out rather dry. Nevertheless, this should not dissuade the poultry enthusiasts.

Don't miss the opportunity to give this place a try when you're in the Chelsea Market, especially if a taco craving strikes. Their carne asada taco alone is a compelling reason to stop by.

Lacey was our server and she was a delight there were three adults and one child and two of us ordered the unlimited mimosas for $18 which is definitely a steel if you're not driving. She was very on top of making sure our drinks stayed full, and I was very pleased with the service that we received! Thanks Lacey hope to see you soon

If you're on the hunt for a taco joint that truly walks the walk, look no further than the bustling hotspot known as "Taco the Talk." Don't expect to be taking a stroll after indulging here, though; you might find yourself needing a siesta instead! Their tacos are nothing short of 'money,' and the constant crowd is a testament to their greatness.

My go-to order? A classic taco paired with their 'especial'—a sinfully delicious fried quesadilla. It's greasy, it's indulgent, and it's the kind of treat you justify as a once-in-a-while necessity.

Here's the game plan: order up, pay, then take your receipt to the topping station. Customize your feast with toppings and salsas to your heart's content, then scout out a seat away from the envious gaze of those still queuing. Dive in, and prepare for an experience so good you'll be planning your next visit before you even leave. Just remember: get your receipt, dress your dish, and enjoy the bliss. Thank me later.

My friend and I came to Mint Masala around 2:30pm on a Saturday.  We came across it walking down Macdougal looking for someplace to eat without a crazy line.  The shop is more of a take-out spot but there is seating for about 4-5 small parties.  My friend ordered the vegetarian lunch special ($9.95) and I got the poultry lunch special ($10.95).  We also added naan to the lunch special for $1.50.  The lunch special comes with a curry of the day, veggie side of the day, and rice.  It's a pretty good deal!  I believe my friend's curry was the palak paneer and mine was chicken tikka masala.  The side was a chickpea curry that was delicious!  I wish I just had the side as my full lunch!  I'm normally a big fan of the spinach curries, but my friend's tasted like baby food.  I wish it was more textured, less watery, and had stronger flavors.  The sauce of the chicken tikka masala was so off-putting to me.  It tasted more like tomato sauce and did not blend well at all with the chicken and rice.  I wish they had used the chickpea sauce for the chicken.  With the exception of a few charred end pieces, the naan was a generous portion and tasted good.The workers here are friendly and welcoming.  Service is what you would expect for more of a take-out place.  Overall, I think the lunch specials here are a fantastic deal but I would need to come back to find entrees that taste better.

Got the margherita slice for $3.25 and I would say it was a decent slice. It was super thin crusted and felt a little dry on the sauce side. It was worth it for a try because I was in the area, but it's not my favorite NYC slice.

They hype is real AF yo. After seeing a few of my IG foodie friends post some stuff, I found myself thinking, "Maybe i should give this spot a go." So, on a work trip to NYC, I decided to give it a go. Also, the location is right around the corner from our hotel.Only one thing that is on the menu. So Tonkotsu Ramen it is. Then you decide on what other things you want in it. I went with the works plus some extra. This is bowl of ramen is definitely one of the best ramen I have ever had. The noodles are nice and al dente. Broth was so wonderful, its like a slice of heaven. The egg was perfect too, runny yolk is always something close to my heart. I literally can't think of anything to ding this bowl of soup. I would totally recommend it to anyone who is trying to find the perfect bowl of ramen.I adore everything that they're doing here. They even have a box kit if you want to bring that good stuff at home. This spot will definitely be in my rinse and repeat collection. Thank you so much for reading my review. I hope this helps with you decision making experience. Enjoy your awesome yelptastic day!

Title: Mixed Feelings at The Capital Grille - Wall Street
