My boyfriend and I decided to give The Capital Grille on Wall Street a try during Restaurant Week. The place boasts an impressive wine cellar vault dining room which certainly sets a unique atmosphere. To kick off our lunch, we both opted for the creamy Clam Chowder, which did not disappoint with its generous helping of clams.

For mains, the Grille's Signature Cheeseburger was a hit, cooked to a perfect medium rare, but the true star was the Truffle Fries - absolutely to die for! However, my Tenderloin Salad fell short, looking rather lonely on its large plate. An attempt to elevate it with filet mignon was thwarted by the restaurant's policy – a disappointing surcharge rather than a simple swap putting me off.

I took a chance on their beef offering but found the dry-aged steak on my salad lacking the juiciness I craved. It was more reminiscent of beef stew than a premium steakhouse experience. Additionally, while the arugula salad had cherry tomatoes, it could have used a boost of flavor.

In sum, despite some highlights, the meal was not the standout I had hoped for, especially considering the steep prices. For those seeking the best steak in the city, there may be other venues in NYC that offer a better combination of taste, value, and service.

I visited Jack's Wife Freda for brunch on a bustling Saturday alongside three friends. Predictably, we encountered a lengthy queue—a testament to the spot's weekend allure. The staff graciously suggested we explore the vicinity during our one-hour wait, which was a pleasant alternative to standing idle.

The culinary highlight was the Green Shakshuka, priced at $12, delivering just the right touch of heat without overpowering the palate—one of the finest renditions I've savored. The Black Berry Caipirinha complemented the meal nicely. While the portions could be considered modest, especially the Green Shakshuka, they are in line with standard NYC pricing.

For those with heartier appetites, I recommend an appetizer to share or keeping an eye out for a budget-friendly eatery post-brunch. All in all, Jack's Wife Freda offers a charming brunch experience in the city worthy of a try.

Title: Lunch with a Side of Indifference

If you're looking for a satisfactory lunch spot in NYC without breaking the bank, this place across from my office is a decent option. Hitting the scene on a bustling Tuesday, we were greeted with a nice lunch menu featuring around ten choices at the sweet price point of $10 - a rarity in the city.

I went for the classic cheeseburger with fries, which was quite tasty, while my colleague opted for the Coffee Rub Burger, which he reported was just okay. The service, however, left something to be desired. Stationed downstairs near the bar, our server seemed disinterested to the point of walking away mid-order - a clear sign of her lackluster engagement.

In the end, while the food holds up, the service does not. It's a solid three-star experience; the eats satisfy, but the service might just leave a bitter taste.

I recently visited the world-renowned Lombardi's, and let me tell you, it was AMAZING. The pizza transported me back to my childhood in the Upper Peninsula of Michigan, specifically the slices from Congress Pizza. The sauce at Lombardi's struck the perfect balance—smooth with a hint of sweetness, embodying what I believe should be the gold standard for all pizzas.

I also ventured to try an Italian Raspberry soda, which was pleasant but slightly overpowered by the cream. While the food was nearly flawless, the service experience didn't quite match up; the waitstaff seemed to be in too much of a hurry. This small hiccup is the only thing holding me back from awarding Lombardi's a full five stars.

As a newcomer to Malaysian cuisine, my visit to this restaurant was an absolute delight. The extensive menu, complete with illustrative photos, made decision-making a breeze. Opting for beef chow fun, seaweed seafood soup with an egg, and fried buns with condensed milk, my friend and I were thoroughly impressed. Each dish was a burst of flavor, served in generous portions with prices that won't break the bank - expect to pay between $12 and $15 for mains, and $5 to $7 for starters or desserts. The value for money here is remarkable, and I'm already planning my next visit when I'm in Chinatown. One thing to remember: it's a cash-only establishment, so come prepared.

I recently paid a visit to a local eatery well-known for its dumplings, and I found myself particularly impressed by their fried pork dumplings. Each bite was a burst of flavor, truly standing out. The steamed pork dumplings also held their own, although I would recommend a dash of chili oil for an extra kick. As for the beef brisket hand-pulled noodles, they were fine, but not remarkable; if you're after truly exceptional noodle soup, Lan Zhou Noodles in the New World Mall remains my top pick.

Title: A Broadway Gem Serving Up Soulful Delights

My recent lunch at this Broadway-themed restaurant was a revelation - a serene spot steeped in theatrical history. The convenience of online reservations set the tone for a surprisingly quiet midday meal; it felt like we had discovered a secret hideaway amid the bustle of New York City.

The ambiance is a tribute to Broadway's legacy, with an enchanting slideshow of star-studded visitors and storied events adorning the walls. The promise of live piano performances and singing during evening service left me yearning to return for dinner.

The southern soul food was exceptional, particularly the shrimp and grits – a dish that truly showcased its high-quality ingredients. Rich, creamy grits paired with perfectly cooked shrimp demonstrated their culinary prowess.

Service was attentive and personal, with the delightful surprise of the chef not only seeking feedback but serenading us with impromptu Broadway tunes. This personal touch cemented our experience as memorable.

I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant and eagerly anticipate my next visit to indulge in its food and atmosphere once more.

I recently stumbled upon a delightful gem in the Upper East Side – a cozy eatery perfect for small gatherings of up to four. Their pork ramen, a star on the menu, offers a generous portion that guarantees value for your buck. The noodles met my expectations for doneness, while the savory broth, albeit a bit thick for my taste, promises comfort, particularly on chilly New York nights. Each bowl comes with a hearty helping of meat, ensuring a satisfying meal. Even when the place seems packed, the efficient service suggests you won't be left waiting long, except perhaps during peak weekend hours. This spot is undoubtedly a great discovery in the UES, and it's on my list for a return visit.

Title: A Flavorful Feast for the Bold

From the moment we arrived, the buzz around this culinary hotspot was palpable, a testament to the delectable delights awaiting inside. Our party of five, sans reservation, beat the odds and snagged a table immediately upon opening—a rare feat given the notorious lines.

Our adventurous palates took us through an array of small plates. The Hoi Tak, a green curry snail dish, was an unexpected marvel—one that could easily convert a skeptic. The Chicken & Banana Blossom Salad, while notably delicious, brought the heat to a near-unbearable level for those less inclined toward the spicy side of life. Grilled Baby Octopus and Fried Conch Balls rounded out the starters, the former hitting all the right notes, the latter being a somewhat forgettable offering.

The large plates provided a symphony of flavors. The Khao Soi Kai's rich curry cradled tender chicken and egg noodles, each bowl scraped clean in testament to its allure. The Crab Fried Rice shone as the meal's milder choice without compromising taste. A classic Rotisserie Half Chicken was well-executed—juicy, if not overly remarkable. The pièce de résistance, however, was the Whole Dorade, exuding freshness despite an odd-tasting stuffing which was promptly sidelined in favor of the fish's natural savor.

A simple but satisfying side of garlic stir-fried pea shoots provided a necessary verdant balance to our feast. Our collective verdict hailed the meal as an outstanding dining adventure, although those with a preference for less seasoning found some dishes over-salted. But for the flavor-seekers among us, this place was a treasure trove.

In conclusion, if bold and full-bodied fare is your calling, this restaurant is a must-visit. For the more timorous taste buds, consider this your cautionary tale. And if possible, beat the crowd with a reservation, or join the early birds in line—you won't regret it.

Dinner with a friend here after an event...nice quaint little place in the East Village for southern comfort food. No wait time at all for a table given it was a bit late. Not a big menu but enough choices to make some quick decisions since we were hungry.We share fried chicken (dark meat eaters) and market vegetables. Service was good and food came out quick. Will have to come back again to try some other items from the menu.

Title: A Flavorful First Foray into Tapas at Boqueria

My maiden voyage into the realm of Spanish tapas took place at Boqueria during happy hour, a time bustling with eager diners and an atmosphere ripe for sampling. The evening was a tapestry of hits and misses.

On the hit list, their albondigas made an impression. The lamb meatballs were initially a bit tough, but improved to tender perfection in later servings. The sheep's milk cheese was sublime – a creamy delight that melded seamlessly with the robust tomato sauce and the unexpected yet refreshing crunch of cucumber. Another star was the fritura mixta; the fried squid paired with a slightly spicy marinara and tangy peppers was a satisfying crunch-fest.

Less impressive were the bacon-wrapped dates. They promised a dance of almond and blue cheese inside, but unfortunately, the bacon hijacked the show with its overcooked crispness, and the anticipated layering of flavors fell flat. The grilled octopus, served whole and cooked to perfection, was accompanied by potatoes and an unremarkable garlic aioli that resembled plain mayo more than the pungent spread I had hoped for. It was pleasant but not particularly memorable.

Word to the wise for happy hour enthusiasts: seating is a competitive sport here. Keep a hawk's eye on the bar and cocktail tables, and when an opportunity presents itself, swoop in swiftly to claim your spot.

Overall, Boqueria provided an enjoyable introduction to tapas despite its culinary rollercoaster. Certain dishes I would eagerly revisit, while others I'd pass in favor of exploring more of the menu.

Despite this review being somewhat overdue, I couldn't pass up the chance to share my experience at Ichiran Ramen during my New York visit. Admittedly, I'm not the biggest ramen enthusiast, but the buzz around the place was too loud to ignore. My friends and I braved the prime dinner rush, a time when hunger levels were at their peak, and decided for the unique experience of sitting separately in individual spaces. The setup was intriguing, offering a novel dining encounter.

While the taste was undoubtedly good, what stood out more for me was the experience itself rather than the food. Price-wise, it veered toward the expensive side, with a bowl of ramen and an added egg setting me back roughly $20. Yet, it's fair to note that the portions were generous. Overall, if you're seeking both a culinary and singular experience, Ichiran Ramen is worth the visit, especially if you're a ramen aficionado.

Title: A Hit or Miss Steakhouse Experience With a Classic Twist

I've dined at this steakhouse multiple times with varying experiences. The food generally impresses, especially the steak, meriting a solid 4 out of 5. Just recently, the sirloin I ordered on a rainy day hit all the right notes – it was succulent, perfectly seasoned, and cooked to a tantalizing medium rare. Despite my petite frame, I devoured it with gusto, barely pausing between bites. Accompanying sides were a mixed bag; the mac and cheese was decent but unremarkable at 2.5 out of 5, though the creamed spinach stood out with a 4 out of 5, albeit still second to my preferred Wollensky's version.

One minor disappointment was the lack of space for dessert – missing out on their coconut cake was a regrettable end to an otherwise indulgent meal.

Service was impeccable – the staff earned a well-deserved 5 out of 5 for their attentive, respectful, and professional manner.

As for ambiance, it's a traditional 3 out of 5 from me. The steakhouse exudes an old-school charm with its wood decor and a clientele that often includes business associates, though it doesn't break the mold of your typical historic steakhouse.

In essence, while consistency may waver, the highs are worth noting, and with such attentive service, it's a venue I'll likely return to, potentially giving the porterhouse a try next time.

Title: A Peruvian Delight at Chirp

If you find yourself yearning for a mouthwatering twist on chicken, look no further than Chirp. Situated conveniently on the way to Penn Station, this gem caught my attention thanks to the buzz from my coworkers and the tantalizing long lines that speak volumes of its popularity.

I decided to dive into the Chirp Salad, a steal at $10. This dish is an orchestra of flavors, featuring tender shredded Peruvian chicken atop a bed of crisp mixed greens and lettuce, paired with juicy grapes, hearty potato, the crunch of candied walnuts, and a zingy jalapeño aioli, all harmoniously brought together by a robust red pepper dressing. The blend of the sweet elements with the savory chicken creates a flavor profile that is both nuanced and satisfying.

For those seeking a meal that hits all the right notes with a balance of sweet and savory, the Chirp Salad comes highly recommended. It's clear that Chirp has mastered the art of the perfect chicken salad. Don't miss out on this Peruvian delight!

During my lunch break, I dined at Basso56, an Italian gem that truly satisfied my cravings. Although the menu is a tad on the expensive side, you're investing in both top-notch quality and delectable flavors. The servings were generous, yet curiously, I found myself hungry again a few hours later. Despite that minor point, Basso56 still earns my hearty recommendation for anyone seeking an authentic Italian experience.

Heading out to catch a Broadway show and in need of a pre-theater dining spot? Look no further than Dos Caminos. With a reservation made just a day in advance, my party of three snagged a spot amidst the Friday evening bustle and were promptly seated in a cozy downstairs setting. 

Here's a quick rundown of our sumptuous spread:

- Spiced Calabaza + Bacon Guacamole ($18): An absolute standout. The guacamole boasted the perfect blend of seasoning and a delightful hint of sweetness.

- Baja Surf & Turf Tacos ($23): A trio of tacos that hit all the right notes – tender steak and flawlessly cooked shrimp.

- Sizzling Fajitas: Chicken and Steak Combo ($30): A heavenly mix that just melted away with each bite.

- Short Rib Tinga Chile Relleno ($22): A delectable surprise that paired rich, savory braised short ribs with a harmonious assortment of flavors.

Yes, the prices reflect its prime Times Square location, but the culinary experience was entirely justifiable. Coupled with excellent service that never made us feel hurried, Dos Caminos proved its worth. I'm already planning my next visit. Highly recommend!

I recently dined at Uskudar and enjoyed the quality of the food and the attentive service. The red lentil soup, accompanied by warm toasted bread, was a satisfying start, and the shrimp shish kebab I ordered was cooked to perfection. However, I was disappointed by the lack of variety in their vegan options, as they were heavily reliant on eggplant, which I avoid due to dietary restrictions. While I could opt for a cold meze platter, I chose to eat pescatarian for the night. Despite the enjoyable meal, the limited vegan choices for someone with my dietary needs mean I am unlikely to return.

Stepping into L Room Cafe is like entering a page of a fairy tale, where the charm is not just in the taste but also in the presentation. I surrendered to the allure of their peach lavender-ade, a visual poem in a glass. This mocktail, served with artistically frozen pansies inside spherical ice cubes, caught not only my eyes but also my palate with its delicate balance of sparkling water and the gentle nudge of sweetness from the lavender syrup, served separately for a personalized touch of flair.

At $12 a pop, it's a luxury for the eyes as much as for the taste buds, a price that might give one pause. However, for those who appreciate the aesthetics of their dining experience as much as the flavors, L Room delivers an enchanting escapade. It's a reminder that beauty has its price, but for an occasional treat, it's a whimsical little cafe that's sure to leave a lasting impression.

Came by for dinner the other night and it was a tasty albeit efficient experience. The wait for the table was minimal despite what appeared to be a line to the door. Most importantly, this restaurant is cash only.Started off with the roti and it was delicious. Super light and fluffy with a curry sauce that had a nice kick to it.The hainan chicken 1/4 was excellent. Served chilled, the chicken was very juicy and slippery. The soy sauce on top was excellent as was the sweet chili sauce.The beef chow fun with runny scrambled eggs was also decent. The rice noodles were very fresh and well wok-fried. The beef was a touch tough, although still edible.The spinach with preserved beancurd was delicious too.Service was extremely efficient.~$22/head after tax and gratuity for dinner, with leftovers. Cash only!

Title: A Mixed Experience at 886

Rating: ★★★☆☆

As a Taiwanese native, my quest for authentic Taiwanese cuisine led me to 886, but the journey there was met with both anticipation and trepidation. My friend and I braved a bustling Saturday night crowd, encountering a 40-minute wait, which was somewhat mitigated by the convenience of a phone notification when our table was ready.

The vibe of 886 was quintessentially St Marks—dark, noisy, and with a gritty charm within its narrow confines. Among our beverage selections, the Apple Sidra was nostalgically satisfying, a true reminder of home; however, our sake experience fell flat due to a disappointingly diluted flavor.

Our culinary adventure commenced with the Oyster Pancake, which regrettably didn't live up to my cherished snack standards. The pancake itself was bland, overshadowed by a robust egg flavor and an ill-fitting abundance of bean sprouts that bore an overpowering vinegar note. The excessive fried onions and scallions could not salvage the dish.

The Haka Stir Fry flirted with the right balance but succumbed to over-salinity and a conspicuous absence of the customary squid. It did, however, pair nicely with plain white rice.

The Beef Noodle Soup was the highlight where the broth and noodles danced harmoniously, punctuated by tender beef and fresh Bok Choy. Yet, the absence of the usual pickled vegetables and the unavailability of white vinegar, an essential accompaniment for me, stripped away a layer of authenticity I yearned for.

In reflection, 886 presented a meal that oscillated between hits and misses. It was an earnest attempt to capture the essence of Taiwanese cuisine, but ultimately, some intangible quality I sought remained elusive.

I recently ordered from a restaurant that seems to be a hit online, boasting an impressive 3,000 reviews on Seamless, which dwarfs the modest 18 found on other review platforms. Opting for their lunch specials on a Sunday, I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of their offerings. The salmon fried rice was particularly delectable, and the maki 3-roll special didn't disappoint. 

In the lineup of rolls - the salmon, spicy tuna, and mango shrimp - the spicy tuna roll emerged as the standout favorite. Each roll came with a choice of miso soup or salad, a nice touch to complete the meal. I also sampled the Manhattan roll; while it was somewhat unremarkable in taste, it was well-made. 

Service-wise, the delivery was prompt and everything in my order was correct, which definitely adds to the positive experience. While one dish didn't thrill me, the overall meal was satisfying. This is a spot I'd revisit, especially for those standout dishes.

Small hole in the wall place that has your budget in mind. We went out of our way to try their cost friendly dumplings and there's not much to say. Pork filling was tasty and hot. The dumping skin was not crispy (likely fried hours ago) and skin was dry at times. We ended up getting extra dumplings since they stuck together so that was a nice bonus. I do NOT recommend the scallion pancake. Just stick to the dumplings. Some places to sit, people eat pretty quickly.

Title: A Surefire Hit for Out-of-Towners at Balthazar

If you're looking to impress visitors with New York's vibrant dining scene, Balthazar should be at the top of your list. From the moment you're seated and the freshly baked bread hits the table, resisting the urge to indulge is a feat. Their baked goods never disappoint, with the croissants being a personal highlight on previous visits.

Although eyebrows were raised when I ordered the beef stroganoff, my confidence in Balthazar's culinary consistency was rewarded. The dish was delicious, with beef so tender it practically melted in my mouth, paralleling the exquisite texture of the mussels we also enjoyed.

Securing a table for Sunday brunch requires foresight—a month in advance, in my case—but the wait is a small price for a memorable meal that's sure to please any guest. Balthazar remains a steadfast favorite for a reason.

Great location, spacious, friendly staff, subpar food and drinks...what you would expect from a chain. While the Irish Whiskey cocktail with Bailey's and whiskey with drip coffee was unmemorable, I didn't mind paying to sit down and not have to rub elbows with my neighbors like most restaurants and bars in Manhattan. Personal space mattered more to me than quality of the drinks and the gregarious bartenders made the experience worth it.

Perfect 4 star lunch. Get here early. I dined nearly alone today at 11:30 but I know this place gets mobbed during rush. For a Friday during Lent, went with the first pita on the menu: Kruveet: roasted cauliflower, eggplant, squash, arugula herbed salad, hummus and tahini. Yum. Not sure why it wasn't mixed up more. If getting the pita, eat fast or sit next to a napkin dispenser.

Service was nice here.Fritto Misto - definitely not the best, they use a lot of small pieces of seafood and just lots of breading. Also doesn't taste like fresh seafood.Panzerotti di funghi - mixed mushrooms, chestnuts, mascarpone. Love this dish, all my liking ingredients together.Bigoli cacio e pepe - pecorino romano, black pepper. Love the thick pasta used but wish was cooked slightly longer, the pasta was almost too raw for me.

First off, the pictures don't do this place justice!Highly recommend for a group dinner, especially if you're planning to go out after in LES / East Village. As opposed to other frequented options where the service is chaotic and you can barely hear your friends, this place is lower key, with a quieter ambiance to actually facilitate good conversations. My friends and I came here and each picked two tapas for the group to share. Favorites included the Arroz (Saffron Fried Rice, Shrimp, Bacon, Peas, Pea Leaves, Egg, Aioli) and Setas (mushrooms). The Spanish wine coolers were surprisingly good - the Rosita (add tequila) was like a much better, less sweet version of a margarita. We may or may not have gone through two pitchers of it...As a plus, all prices are gratuity-included!

Everyone talks about New York pizza.  This place is by far the best pizza I had in new York.  The pizza is so light,and huge slices.  The line was long when I got in it but they move fast.  When I come back I will definitely visit this or one of there other locations.  I recommend this place to anyone who likes or wants to try NY pizza

Title: A Noodle Lover's Delight at [Restaurant Name]

I stumbled upon [Restaurant Name] through a Yelp event and have been hooked on their noodles ever since. Their spinach noodles are a standout, especially when twirled with pesto sauce and topped with chicken, broccoli, and tomatoes – a combination that sings with freshness and flavor.

The drink options are far from ordinary. I took a chance on the Blueberry soda and it was a revelation, offering a perfect burst of refreshment.

On my second visit, I again opted for the spinach noodles, this time adding a variety of veggies. The simplicity of broccoli, corn, carrots, and tomatoes created a dish that was both wholesome and satisfying.

The space is cozy with enough seating and I've never encountered a wait, with service being notably quick. The pricing is fair, making for an affordable and healthy dining experience.

[Restaurant Name] has quickly become a favorite of mine and I eagerly anticipate my next visit for those irresistible noodles.

Title: A Ramen Haven for Heat Seekers and Kindness Lovers

If you're yearning for a mouthwatering and hearty bowl of ramen that offers fantastic value, this spot is a must-visit! My experience was nothing short of delightful, with lightning-fast service and a staff exuding unwavering kindness.

I ventured into the spicy culinary world with their chili chicken ramen—it's a bold choice tailored for true heat aficionados. The fiery flavors were more than I bargained for, but spice lovers will revel in its intensity. On the flip side, the spicy miso ramen, brimming with savory shredded pork, was an absolute triumph. The pork was luscious and plentiful, melding with impeccable al dente noodles and a soul-soothing broth that warmed me to the core.

A special nod to our server, who exemplified customer service perfection. Upon noticing my struggle with the heat, she promptly offered a replacement dish with no additional cost and no questions asked—a gesture of goodwill that's hard to come by in NYC.

In summary, visit this gem for an exceptional ramen experience coupled with extraordinary service. Thank you to the kind waitress who made our dining experience memorable!

I've been to Her Name is Han three times now, and it's been fantastic every time! The interior is warm, cozy, and stylish -- light wood panels, little nooks, exposed lightbulbs. I've heard the wait can get really long, but I've had a reservation each time I've been, and would highly recommend it. As others have mentioned, their standout dish is the rice cakes, coated in a sweet spicy sauce, chewy on the inside and just crisped on the outside. Their kimchi pancake is delicious (albeit a little overpriced for what it is, I think), and their shared pots are perfect for small groups on a cold day. Most recently, I ordered the noodle soup with clam, which is individually portioned but sizable and delicious. Perfectly chewy noodles, delicious broth. I also started with the sowuju (soju aged for 100 days!), which I enjoyed, and finished the meal with the Ginger Caramel, which features a beautiful sauce that you drizzle over vanilla ice cream (topped with candied ginger) and a glazed plantain, served hot. Yum. Definitely one of my go-tos (and conveniently close to Penn Station, since I'm always coming up from DC). Would recommend!

On a recent trip to NYC, I visited Jack's Wife Freda for the first time with a friend. Although it was a first-time visit, it might just be my new favorite breakfast spot in NYC. The space is cozy, quaint, and has a old-euro feel to it, partially due to the decor. The service is great, and the food came quickly. I ordered the Mediterranean breakfast which came with 2 eggs any style, chopped salad, labne, avocado and pita bread ($14). It was absolutely delicious and something I will definitely make at home as well. My friend ordered the Green Shakshuka which came with 2 baked eggs in a green tomatillo shakshuka and served with challah toast ($13). She loved her meal as well! Definitely check this spot out if you are ever looking for a breakfast spot in New York.

I visited this restaurant for a post-work happy hour with my colleagues and left quite satisfied. The value was notable, with an offering of two tacos and a side for a little over $10. Among the taco options, the vegan chorizo was passable, but the chicken taco impressed me with its flavors. As for the side, the Mexican street corn was a tasty choice, though served cold—a preparation some may find unconventional but still delightful. The experience as a whole was pleasant, and I'm inclined to return.

Title: A Flavor Fiesta with Room for More

If you're on the hunt for a nouveau Mexican culinary experience, look no further. The service is as commendable as the diverse range of dishes that I've had the pleasure of tasting – I've nearly eaten my way through the entire menu and haven't met a dish I didn't savor. The portion sizes are the only hiccup in the adventure; a tad more generous serving would save me from leaving with a lingering appetite, despite indulging in numerous plates.

Meat typically dominates my plate, but the vegetarian options here, particularly the mushroom tacos, are a revelation; they're simply irresistible. For the spice enthusiasts among us, the homemade hot sauce adds a vibrant yet harmonious heat that accentuates rather than overwhelms the food's natural flavors.

Weekends bring a brunch menu that's well worth exploring. While the dishes might leave you craving just a bit more, the overall quality ensures you'll return for another taste.

Title: A Delightful Discovery of Vegan Korean Ramen

As a first-timer to Korean cuisine, I was pleasantly surprised by the exceptional vegan ramen at this gem of a restaurant. Finding vegetarian options in Korean dishes is a challenge, but this eatery hits the mark with its vegan offerings. The ramen arrived in a generous portion, easily shared between two, and boasted a rich tapestry of flavors that did not rely on an overabundance of tofu.

The shiitake mushrooms were a standout, seasoned to salty perfection. While I personally could pass on the seaweed garnish, it didn't detract from the overall enjoyment. A word to the wise: elevate the experience with a touch of their hot sauce for an added kick that complements the dish's depth. This restaurant is a must-visit for anyone craving vegan-friendly Korean eats.

Hidden within the vibrant streets of NYC lies a gem that epitomizes the city's spirit in every bite and sight—let's talk about a perennial favorite among the locals that masterfully marries the old and the new. This place is an embodiment of timeless elegance, yet it never ceases to surprise with its ever-changing ambiance that is so quintessentially New York.

From the moment you step in, the trained and pleasant staff make you feel right at home within the dynamic setting. For any food lover, this spot is an absolute must. Here, comfort meets innovation on a plate, offering a dining experience that delights and surprises in equal measure. Truly, a culinary highlight not to be missed in the Big Apple. Visited on 9/12/16, the memory of the meal lingers, beckoning a return visit. #dodrinkdine

Title: Fresh Seafood Delight at Seamores

Seamores is a seafood aficionado's paradise, boasting an impressive array of dishes that cater to every palate, from the delectable tuna poke to classic fish & chips and sumptuous lobster rolls. The quality of the seafood is top-notch, ensuring every bite is a burst of freshness. 

The ambiance adds to the dining experience with its vibrant vibe and bustling bar scene, complemented by a selection of good drinks to toast the occasion. While the service is commendable, be mindful of peak hours when the staff may be stretched thin. Nonetheless, the overall experience at Seamores is gratifying and well worth a visit for seafood lovers.

(This was originally posted on Indian King Biryani House cart...moved it here to its rightful spot, oops!) ---Came here today on 11/27/2019 with a coworker around 1130. Said the line gets insane. This is located in a group of halal carts, but off by itself. Some interesting Indian options here, but I just got the basic Hyderabad chicken for  $6. The seasoning was done well. They have this good green hot sauce that you can ask for. Not the hottest but good. I'd say the only issue I could find that they're a little slow compared to other carts but just get there early.I'll be back to try some other neat dishes.Oh and they take card thankfully.

Title: A Cozy, Luxurious Dining Experience Worth Every Penny

Last evening at this fine establishment left a lasting impression with a culinary experience that tickles the taste buds and warms the heart — a testament to its 4/5 food rating. While my companion orchestrated our orders, the table was adorned with a variety of wagyu cuts, perfectly paired with sides of rice, noodles, and vegetables. Each morsel was succulent, though be warned, the tantalizing aroma of barbecue will become your temporary perfume.

For a duo, our indulgence came with a price tag of around $300, which felt justified for the quality and quantity received. Despite my memory lapse on our exact orders, the accompanying photos serve as a visual feast and guide for future patrons.

Service was impeccable, a full score without hesitation. The waitress, Pauline, displayed exceptional attentiveness, gracing our table with expertly cooked dishes and ensuring we wanted for nothing throughout our visit.

As for the ambiance, it's imbued with a romantic charm – dimly lit to set a mood that's both luxurious and cozy, earning another well-deserved 5/5. Whether it's a special date or a night out to splurge, this restaurant has crafted an experience that's as memorable as it is delicious.

My latest dining experience at this local seafood spot during happy hour was quite delightful. The allure of their happy hour advertising had me eager to dive into their menu, and it did not disappoint. The $1 oysters were a steal and absolutely fantastic, rivaling the value and taste of the $1 cherrystones also available. I indulged in fried lobster ravioli and mussels for appetizers, both of which were delectable and set a high bar for the meal. While the paella was just decent and didn't stand out, the fish and chips truly shone, with a perfectly golden and deliciously crispy coating. Whether it's the power of marketing or the actual quality of the food, this restaurant's happy hour is a hit.

Title: Decent Thai Fare for Spur-of-the-Moment Dining

My dinner at this Thai spot was a pleasant surprise for a last-minute Friday night meal. Service was commendably quick, an advantage for anyone with late-night cravings. The Thai iced tea was a highlight – a perfect balance of sweet and creamy. Unfortunately, the food, while generally good, didn't quite hit the mark. The Drunken Noodles, in particular, were a letdown; the spice distribution seemed like an afterthought rather than being well-incorporated. If you're in search of a reliable Thai dinner in a pinch, this place will do, but don't expect culinary fireworks.

Not a fan of this place. A friend and I came to this place after walking past it a few weeks ago. We came for a weekend brunch. I ordered the eggs florentine. When I got my food, the english muffin was soggy, the eggs were rubbery and the potatoes tasted like bacon grease, even though I told my server that I'm a vegetarian (although my server wasn't the one who cooked the food). Perhaps this was because the place was busy. Nonetheless, I wish the food was made with the same attention to quality as other restaurants, especially given the prices they charge for it. I will say that the service here was pretty good. My server was pleasant and attentive. She did her best given how crowded it was, and I never felt like I had to wait too long to get her attention. I also liked the decor. It had the feeling of a hip but cozy pub, and it would have otherwise been an ideal date spot. That said, I wish the food here was as good as the service and decor.

Went here for dinner before a concert at Terminal 5 and would definitely go back. Their service was very fast and the food was great. I got the Kimchi Fried Rice and would highly recommend. We made a reservation ahead of time and I'm glad we did - although it was pretty empty when we got there, it filled up fast and we would have had to wait for a table if we got there 15 minutes later.

Rubirosa was one of the first Italian restaurants I visited when I first moved to NYC 8 years ago. I haven't been back in so long (diet and all) that we decided to drive for pick up during the quarantine. We picked up two pastas (carbonara and cacio e pepe) and a large tie dye pizza. The pastas were both great tasting. But the obvious star was the pizza. The pesto and vodka combo is impossible to surpass. Thin and delicious crust. It's one of my favorite special pizzas by far. Rubirosa still makes my top 10 pizza list.

Same menu as the one in flushing. Almost same taste but smaller portion and much longer waiting time (space is tiny inside). Only because it's in Manhattan - if not because of the convenience I would still go to the flushing one. 很喜欢一开始送的泡菜。酸汤肥牛不错的。石锅青椒鱼味道差不多一样（不咋辣）。炝白菜很失望，全是老白菜梆子炒得也非常生都嚼不怎么动。麻婆豆腐正常。最后送的红豆水挺好的。

Chapati House delivers a unique twist to the fast-casual dining scene, steering clear of the bland predictability found at many "Chipotle of..." establishments. Their rice bowl generously offers a choice of two entrees, surpassing the usual one. On my visit, I savored the rich and creamy chicken tikka masala alongside a robust lamb bhuna, both impeccably complemented by a zesty spicy relish and a tangy tamarind sauce. Additional flavor enhancements are conveniently stationed at the tables with tamarind and a fiery green sauce, ready to please those in search of an extra kick. Chapati House is a standout choice for anyone craving the depth and variety of authentic Indian flavors served up quickly and without fuss.

Title: Hit-or-Miss Shanghainese Fare

I've dined at this establishment multiple times, more out of necessity than desire, as it's a frequent pick for group events. Unfortunately, the experience consistently falls flat. Service is lackluster, and gaining the attention of the staff feels like a sport in itself—ironically, except when they're prematurely presenting the bill.

As for the cuisine, it largely underwhelms. The soup dumplings, a staple for Shanghainese palates, fail to impress with their thick, doughy skins and unremarkable broth. While the scallion pancakes have a delightful flavor, their portion size doesn't quite justify the cost.

With main courses, your satisfaction may vary; they're as unpredictable as a game of roulette. Given the wealth of options in Chinatown for this cuisine, I'm hard-pressed to recommend this spot when others shine more brightly in both service and culinary delight.

Came in tonight for restaurant week and it was really good!  The ambiance is pretty although very dark.  The service was good.  For our meals we started with the ricotta crostini and the arancini.  Both were delicious.  For my main meal I had the chicken Milanese.  It was a good version but not great.  The chicken could have been salted or seasoned.  I didn't really care for the choice of the wild arugula on top either.  It had a lot of stems.  My friends both had the cacio de Pepe and I tried it and it was really delicious.  For desert we all had gelatos we had vanilla pistachio and hazelnut.  The pistachio was my favorite.  I would definitely return

Title: A Customizable Delight for Afternoon Tea Lovers

My afternoon tea experience at this venue was nothing short of excellent. With an extensive selection of high-quality teas, there's a flavor to satisfy every palate. The flexibility in customizing sandwiches to accommodate dislikes is a notable perk – a relief for a cucumber-averse diner like myself.

The scones, delightfully buttery, were a joy despite my personal aversion to the raisins embedded within. A pleasant surprise came in the form of complimentary popovers with a sweet strawberry jam, alongside a hearty and remarkable chicken broth served on the house.

Service was superb, striking the perfect balance between attentiveness and discretion. Both hot and cold water were replenished swiftly, ensuring our constant comfort.

While the ambience presented a classier atmosphere with stunning views from window tables, it lacked the cozy intimacy found in some other tea spots. Nevertheless, this wasn't a drawback but rather a different charm.

I am already looking forward to my next visit; this establishment has firmly secured its spot in my rotation of preferred afternoon tea havens.

After having a not so good experience here, I came here again and this time was a lot better.As soon as my friend and I walked in, we were greeted with smiles and were taken to our table. I was surprised that there was no wait time on a Sunday afternoon... then I realized, duh... they do not have a wait; it is Sunday and nearly every spot around here does brunch (with unlimited drinks), so why would people come to Guadalupe where they have no brunch? ... I can tell you why... the delicious food!The chips and sauce was AMAZING... that sauce was definitely rich in flavor. I should have asked for a bottle of it to take home- hahaha!My friend got the sizzling chicken fajita plate-- huge portions! She literally had enough food for two. I got the steak tacos... with the rice and beans. The steak was perfectly cooked. Those were probably the BEST steak tacos I have ever had! The frozen mango margarita was nice; I was asked if I wanted salt on the rim, and even though I said yes, it did not bring any... the margarita could have looked more presentable. ** We had to ask for water; it appeared that they had no plans in bringing us water... and when they did, my friend's glass had someone's lip mark on the rim. Please clean these glasses correctly!Would I return? Probably!

Just ordered delivery last night as I have been craving this all week. I was falling asleep early one night and I do not know how I ended up on Yelp and looking at their menu and their yelp photos. I was craving for the kimchi fried rice since in LA we have a lot of Korean BBQ spots and I had a lot of Korean friends in HS that brought kimchi fried rice for lunch so it has always been my favorite. I ordered for delivery and it came fast and the serving was a lot. It is a bit pricey but it is fair for the quality and the amount of food I got. I ordered the kimchi fried rice, the wings (half and half of the sauce) and the spicy hot ramen soup and they were all wonderful! I ate like there was no tomorrow and I am so happy I was able to try this place as when I first passed by I have been meaning to try it but have forgotten about it. Whatever spirit woke me up that one night from falling asleep early and guided me to their menu on yelp, is a guardian angel. Such a great place to check out in the UWS. For my followers: Panties dropped status aka 5 stars your calvin kleins will drop with just the first bite of their chicken wings.

I recently visited this gem of a restaurant with friends and was pleasantly surprised by the delectable menu. We dived into a variety of dishes that included lightly fried chicken karage, flaky branzino, tuna rib, and an assortment of sushi and sashimi.

The branzino was particularly enjoyable, with a subtle blend of flavors that hinted at lemon and soy sauce, creating a taste that was both unique and delicious. However, the true highlight of our meal was the tuna rib. This dish offered a fun and interactive DIY sushi experience, allowing us to carve out the succulent meat and roll our own sushi with provided seaweed, chopped scallions, and a side of rice.

The whole meal was an adventure for our taste buds and left us thoroughly content and stuffed. I highly recommend this restaurant for anyone looking for a unique dining experience with flavors that will leave you craving for more.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this gem of a restaurant and I must say, the experience was nothing short of exceptional. The presentation of the dishes, as evidenced by the photos I took, was truly magnificent. The staff's politeness and professionalism stood out, enhancing the already comfortable and civilized ambiance of the establishment.

A rarity in upscale dining, there was a genuine sense of respect and excellent treatment towards customers by the staff. But the highlight of the evening was undoubtedly the food. The meat was exceptional—cooked to perfection and bursting with flavor. The sides did not disappoint either; they were absolutely delightful and complemented the meal perfectly.

I am eager to return, especially to try the much talked-about "Pastrami Steak." My next visit can't come soon enough. It was a memorable evening, deserving of an A+ rating. Thank you for such a splendid dining experience.

came a little after 6 on a weekday and was quickly seated to the bar. You can get a free drink if you write them a Google review! Once I placed my order, you are able to watch them put your order together and serve it right away - which I absolutely loved. Because the kitchen is in front of the bar table, the food is served very quickly. Ordered pork buns and miso soup, both highly recommend! *please note this is cash only!

Title: Quick Bite at a Convenient Pizza Spot

During a tight schedule on our city tour, we found a pizza place close to our hotel that catered perfectly to our time constraints. They offered a fantastic deal of two cheese slices and a 20oz drink for about $6-7, which suited our group of five excellently.

Taking advice from previous visitors, we asked for our pizza to be reheated. This little touch made our slices taste fresher. Although compact, the restaurant had a spacious dining area at the back, which was a nice contrast to the cramped front space with just two tables.

The staff were courteous and welcoming, adding to the positive experience. We did notice a few imperfections, like slightly burnt garlic knots and bits of what seemed like ash in the pizza crust, likely from the oven. However, these did not detract significantly from the enjoyment of our meal, as the overall taste, especially the unique texture of the crust, was pleasing.

For anyone in need of a quick meal without sacrificing taste, this pizza joint is worth stopping by.

This place has a very nice, roomy, airy, and bright interior, and it's nice to sit inside and have brunch. I got the blueberry acai bowl, which tasted great, had the perfect consistency, and had yummy toppings, but the bowl was SO shallow and there was so little food. I spent about $16 in total after tax and tip, which is really expensive for an acai bowl, but I wasn't full at all. I could've eaten two of them.

I recently visited Gotham Pizza for a lunchtime meal and was met with an uncomfortably hot interior, lacking proper ventilation. The ordering process was straightforward, selecting from pre-made options at the counter. Unfortunately, cleanliness was neglected, with dirty tables and chairs.

I tried a slice of pepperoni, which was excessively greasy to the point of the thin crust becoming soggy. The buffalo chicken slice offered a more favorable flavor, but it suffered the same fate with its thin, soggy crust. Overall, Gotham Pizza might satisfy a quick pizza craving but expect a less-than-pleasant dine-in experience and be prepared for a heavy dose of oil with your meal.

Came here with high hopes, but maybe I just hyped it up too much in my head.  Wanted to try this place that's direct from Kagoshima.  Got there and it was this sort of weird setup where they serve bento boxes during the day and then add on the availability of ramen in the evening.Went for the sakurajima ramen, which is their spicy pork and chicken broth ramen.  What came out looked really impressive, but somehow it just wasn't doing it for me.  The broth didn't seem very thick or rich and the flavor was very one-note.  I was surprised because the reviews seemed to all say the broth here was wonderful.  I feel like I might have just had it on an off day.  In any case, the noodles were cooked quite firm, which I like.  I added on the ajitama and the egg was nicely seasoned, but a bit overcooked.  I like the extra flavor that fried garlic provided it.  The pork was another part of the bowl I wasn't thrilled with.  The pork was tough and very lean, with minimal flavor.  What surprised me was how much bean sprouts were given with the meal.  They're raw, so the flavor the bean sprouts is quite pronounced.  I don't know if it was all the raw bean sprouts or just the broth being a bit lacking, but I found myself just not enjoying the bowl much.  Maybe it's just this style of ramen that doesn't appeal to me?I came here on a week day between 5pm and 7pm, so I qualified for their "happy set", which is like happy hour.  A bowl of ramen is only $10.  And they have combos where you get ramen, a side, and rice for less than the usual cost of the ramen itself.  And you still get a full size portion of the ramen.  A great deal!Menya Jiro must be good since they have so many great reviews and multiple locations in Manhattan.  It just didn't do it for me today.

Oh boy oh boy!!! Just when you think you have all of your NYC hot-spots bookmarked on Yelp, a coworker throws a curveball at you telling you that Joe's Pizza is LEO DICAPRIO'S fave place in all of NYC. I couldn't pass this up; I HAD to get here!As you may see from my Yelp profile, Leo is my favorite actor, so of course as soon as a coworker told me that, I googled it and it was totally legit! The articles I found pretty much said he's here at Joe's (this particular location) any time he's in NYC. Wow! Move over Lombardi's---you just got replaced with Joe's on the bookmark list!I was in NYC for Marathon weekend and wanted to eat super healthy before the race, so Fri-Sun I wasn't able to pig out like I normally do on vacations. But luckily my cousins agreed to come here with me on Monday for lunch! I'm very grateful they went with me because there was a Joe's closer to our hotel in Times Square but I was not going to just any Joe's...it had to be LEO'S Joe's! We got here around 11a on a Monday. It wasn't super packed like I've seen in other pics, but there really wasn't any seating. I'd say there are probably 10 spots total in this joint. Any more than that would feel super cramped.There are sooo many pics of celebrities enjoying Joe's on the walls. I counted at least 4 of Leo which I of course loved. He is for sure a regular here! My cousins and I each ordered a slice of fresh mozz and a slice of regular cheese. I couldn't wait to try this New York Slice! We took them across the street to the park and after snapping some pics for Yelp, I dug in! The fresh mozz was THE BOMB! SOOOO good! Delicious, tangy marinara sauce, creamy mozzarella. You can't go wrong what that slice! I devoured it and enjoyed every delectable bite! I ate the cheese next and it wasn't quite as good. However, we left the pizza box open and all three of us agreed that our second slices were cold. Whoops. If I ever go back, I would get a whole pie of the fresh mozz. It's that good! (I'd share of course!).All in all, I can't imagine there being a better New York slice than Joe's! I have wanted to try Lombardi's for awhile, but this is a classic NYC experience that everyone should try! I will be sure to be back (and will hopefully spot Leo next time!)

Tucked away among a sea of Thai options on 9th Avenue, my friend and I were drawn into this gem by the enticing menu displayed outside. The experience kicked off authentically with metal cups reminiscent of Thai street food vendors, instantly setting the tone for the meal.

I indulged in the Dam Noen Noodle dish, pairing egg noodles with exceptionally tasty meatballs, delightfully avoiding the overly sweet broth trap many Thai eateries fall into. The condiments tray was an adventure in customization, offering everything from dried chili flakes to Thai-style pickled chilis for a personalized kick.

On my suggestion, my companion savored the Yen Ta Fo Noodle, a childhood staple of mine. With flat rice noodles soaking in a pink sauce, this dish struck the perfect balance of sweet, tangy, and spicy, enhanced by a generous helping of crunchy Chinese watercress.

Overall, this spot boasts authenticity, balanced flavors, and notable service. It's a Thai noodle haven that has earned a swift return visit. Highly recommended for a taste of Thailand right in the heart of the city.

Pizza time! If you want flavorful pizza come to this place. It's Michelin recommended and famous for their fried pizza. We ordered Montenara truffle and pizza pianeta. Our favorite (for most flavor) was the truffle one! Wow! We would get it again and again. As for Pianeta, we would have to pass. It was soggy on the inside and lacked flavor once you tried the truffle one. The place is nice with accommodating staff and good service. No outside seating that we saw. Earning a solid 4.5* thanks to truffle pizza.

Title: A Gem of Authentic Flavors and Charming Vibes

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this great little spot, and it honestly charmed me from the get-go. The decor exudes a welcoming atmosphere, perfectly setting the stage for an authentic culinary experience.

The Penang char kway teow on the menu did not disappoint. Each bite was a testament to genuine flavors, transporting me to the streets of Penang. Accompanying the dish, I had a roti whose specific name escapes me, but the taste lingers — it was delectable.

Adding to the experience were the super nice and helpful servers, making my visit all the more delightful. This place easily earns my recommendation, and I'm eagerly looking forward to my next visit.

Charlie Bird did not disappoint whatsoever!!  We started out sharing some small plates, then we each ordered an appetizer and an entree..  I got the little gems salad with a buttermilk dressing..   simple, yummy, and tasty!!  For an entree I moved to the ribeye off the bone..   only complaint:  the serving size was more for 2 people, I couldn't finish the dish.  Lol. Not really a complaint.  I liked the vibe of the restaurant, the crowd was interesting.   Service was spot on, not rushed and not slow..  the wine we had was great too.

Title: Dim Sum Delights Overshadow Dinner Experience at Local Favorite

My go-to spot for exquisite dim sum decided to test its dinner waters, and I tagged along for the ride. The quiet of a Monday evening was a stark contrast to their bustling weekend mornings. True, the menu felt limited, especially when pitted against the extensive offerings at other Chinese eateries. To my surprise, they pitch dim sum in the PM too, albeit at a premium.

Diving into the main affair, the Pineapple Shrimp was a scene-stealer, but only if savored warm - its mayo dressing loses charm as it cools. The showstopper? The braised arerib with its velvety texture swimming in a sauce that hugged each rib like a long-lost friend. The Garlic Chicken, on the other hand, was just passing through - satisfactory but forgettable. Accompaniments like vegetables and noodles played their roles without much fanfare.

While the dinner didn't rise to the occasion with an average of $37 denting the wallet per patron, I'm still pledged to their dim sum mornings. The evening's foray was a single act play that won't be seeing an encore from me.

Great meal! Started with the Pisco Sour cocktail which had a nice bright flavor thanks to the yuzu and shisoWe ordered the duck nigiri (our favorite) , tuna ceviche (tasty but similar flavor profile from others I've had)Everyone raves about the seafood fried rice... the seafood chunks were huge and it was good but my least favorite of all the dishes The wagyu on the other hand was amazing. You won't be disappointed We ended with the miso sesame banana dessert which we loved

I recently enjoyed a delightful brunch experience at a local gem I discovered through Eatery. Despite initial skepticism due to mixed online reviews about wait times and food quality, I was pleasantly surprised.

Securing a reservation for Saturday brunch was a breeze, and I highly recommend this due to the restaurant's cozy size. Upon arrival, we were seated promptly at the charming outdoor patio, which was comfortably heated and adorned with pretty string lights.

The service was swift, starting with complimentary bread served with olive oil. The highlight of our meal was the prosciutto eggs benedict and the duck bacon benedict from the daily special. Although the prosciutto variant won our favor, the duck bacon was a close contender, and I’m curious to try the lobster benedict on my next visit. Additionally, the homemade Berkshire pork sausage was a standout.

While the brunch itself was fantastic, the only downside was the single bathroom facility, which became a bottleneck. The clean and spacious bathroom would benefit from a companion to better accommodate the guests.

Overall, this restaurant proved to be a culinary delight, and I'm already looking forward to my next brunch outing here.

Love this place for a cheap warm meal under $10. I got the thick hand pulled noodles with roasted duck on top. The soup was flavorful and perfect for a cold day. This location, in my opinion is also better than the one in chinatown because it feels less cramped and cleaner.

The Spanish Diner was the only eatery that was open at 10am on a Monday.My entree, the Arros a la Cubana - Two Fried Eggs, Three Pork Sausages, over Rice w/Tomato Sauce was slightly disappointing.  The eggs had wrinkly edges which were stringy as if they had been sitting for a while waiting to be served.  The yolk was soft but a bit cool over the rice.  The rice was very flavorful but was a tad bit too al dente.  Finally the sausages were good and a little salty, garlicky and lean.The Zumo Verde, a Spinach, Apple, Grape and Lime drink, was not sweet which I'm not sure is by design.  Speaking to the server, this was the sweetest fruity drink but it wasn't at all.  It certainly could have been more refreshing if chilled more.The service was friendly and efficient.

What a hidden gem I found. I was craving greek food and this place was on my bookmark for a long time, so I decided to dine in with my friend. I feel like this place is more classier than Souvlaki GR and any other greek restaurants I have been to in NYC.we ordered;1. roasted beets filled with feta mousse for appetizer - 5/5 (I do not like beets or feta cheese.. but highly recommend this dish)2. baby lamb chops - 4/5 meat was perfectly cooked, but it was a bit bland3. shrimp and sea scallops in tomato sauce - 4/5. I wish the pasta was long. it was only 2-3inches long. idk why..? but the favor was amazing.They also serve warm pita and their version of a hummus to start. It was really delicious and I wanted to take them home lol. service was attentive, price is affordable. I will definitely come back when I crave greek food.

Title: A Gluten-Free Revelation in NYC

My inaugural trip to the Big Apple came with hefty culinary expectations, and this restaurant didn't just meet them—it soared beyond. The menu brimmed with a tantalizing selection that took us on a delectable journey from appetizers to entrées. But the pièce de résistance was the gluten-free layered dessert, RAKE—a discovery that delighted our gluten-sensitive palates. This airy, flavorful confection was the culinary highlight of our New York City adventure.

Hats off to the pastry chef and the owner for their generosity in sharing the recipe, enabling us to bring a slice of New York excellence to Texas. A word of advice: arrive early; this popular spot fills quickly, yet diners are never rushed. A resounding FIVE STARS for an exceptional dining experience!

Came here on a Monday night with a friend at 7:30pm. The place was half empty which I thought was surprising. Service was impeccable and the food was delicious. We ordered the baba appetizer which was better than I expected since I'm not a fan of babaganoush. This felt denser and more eggplant-y which I liked. For entrees we ordered the lamb shank and the Caspian platter. I deducted a star for the lamb since it was a bit fatty and had some tendons but honestly that's probably just me being nit picky. Overall would highly recommend this place! Definitely get the rice with sour cherries. I'd come back just for that honestly.

I recently celebrated a friend's birthday at this restaurant with a party of ten, and we had a delightful experience. Despite a busy Saturday night, our table was ready shortly after our 8 pm reservation, and the staff impressively managed the transition.

The service throughout the evening was commendable; from the moment we sat down with pitchers of water already on the table to consistent refills, the wait staff was attentive and friendly, standing out from many other dining experiences.

While the price of soju was a tad steep at $16 a bottle, the spicier-than-usual kimchi and appetizing radish set a promising start. My order of large Korean wings and marinated short rib (LA Galbi) with corn cheese did not disappoint—both were flavorful and satisfying, perfectly complemented by rice.

The menu had a fun "have fun with" section ideal for sharing, which contributed to the cozy vibe of the evening. A highlight was the thoughtful touch of complimentary birthday dumplings with candles, making the celebration even more special.

The restaurant also offers a happy hour from Monday to Friday until 8 pm, which I'm eager to try. A lovely place for a group dining experience that combines great food with thoughtful service.

Title: A Culinary Gem at Top Thai Vintage

If you're familiar with Top Thai Greenwich, imagine that with the volume turned up in space and taste. Top Thai Vintage has room to spare – a blessing for big parties and popular dining times. 

My dining experience kicked off with a delightful lychee lemonade, but don't stop there; their drink list is a treasure trove for both mocktail and cocktail lovers. We feasted on crispy calamari, which was the epitome of crunch and flavor, easily a strong start to any meal. 

The star, however, was the grilled skirt steak in 5 spice sauce. It's a dish I urge everyone to try, cooked to a perfect medium rare with sublime dipping sauces on the side. Sharing the spotlight was the seafood tom yum noodle soup, reminiscent of Thailand's street food glory and bursting with fresh seafood - a new go-to for me.

Despite being pleasantly full, we couldn't pass on the coconut pudding. It's a must-have finale – though limited in quantity, it's huge in satisfaction. Ending our meal on this sweet note, I'm already looking forward to my next visit. Top Thai Vintage isn't just a meal; it's a journey through Thailand's flavors.

Title: A Culinary Triumph in Chelsea Market!

If I could offer one piece of advice for your visit to this Chelsea Market marvel, it would be to ORDER THE MUSSELS. As a weekly mussel connoisseur, I can confidently proclaim these the finest I've ever indulged in. Picture a generous serving of tender, perfectly cooked mussels accompanied by crusty bread ideal for sopping up the most exquisite, silky herbaceous broth imaginable.

Onward to the beet carpaccio, a symphony of flavors so masterfully composed, it’s like a sonnet on a plate. The toasted hazelnuts add a delightful crunch that dances well with the dill and other herbs.

Don't overlook the market salad, graced with a light and smooth lemon vinaigrette that brings just the right amount of zest, completed with the crunchy, buttery tones of sunflower seeds. Each dish had us, a typically discerning family, scraping our plates clean.

I left bewildered by the absence of a Michelin Star because, folks, this establishment is a hidden gem radiating amidst the plethora of Chelsea Market eateries. Bravo to the culinary team - you have my utmost cheers and a resounding woot woot! Keep dazzling the palates of New Yorkers and beyond!

Came here on a whim cos we couldn't get a table at our favorite restaurant, but definitely enjoyed the experience. Food is amazing, service is quick for bottomless mimosas and bellinis. Kinda like the cute little tables nestled into a nook with book shelves right above them. Overall I'd come back for the lovely service, great ambience and the food really, it's so good!! Suffice to say this is a great addition the wonderful collection on brunch places in this busy part of NYC.

Came here for my friend's birthday. Pretty cool date spot but pretty expensive. Logistical things: Pretty small place - maybe seats around 30 - 40 people. They do not take reservations and won't seat you unless your whole party is there so make sure you arrive in a timely fashion. When we got there at 6:15PM on Wednesday, we didn't have to wait for our table for 3 people. The space is awesome and the acoustics are great so that you can talk to each other and actually hear each other. Onto the appetizers. We had some jeju chicken wings, which extremely small and only come with 5. I feel like they were a little soggy, and also the meat was not that juicy. The flavor was interesting - definitely a Korean spice, but I couldn't place my finger on it. It wasn't something that blew my socks off, especially not at $14 for those small wings. We also had the Toro Ssam Bap which was fatty tuna, rice, eggs and we opted for the uni. They bring out some nori seaweed so that you can make your own little tacos / hand rolls. This was amazing and definitely the star of the night. Quite delicious and we asked for some additional seaweed that was well deserved. For actual ramen, I got the So Ramyun. I have mixed review for this. The beef itself was extremely tender and the fried garlic was quite a delicious touch. That being said, the broth felt a little "dirty" in that my teeth felt like they were grimy afterwards. Additionally, there were zero vegetables to break up the richness of the noodles. Although that being said, I think that the pot of noodles looked small, but it was actually very filling. Could be due to the richness of the broth. Overall, a pretty nice date spot. I probably wouldn't come again, but wouldn't warn people against this place. Definitely try the Toro Ssam Bap and other than that would just go with whatever ramen you think is best.

Came for Restaurant Week 2019. I ordered the Charred Octopus and the Organic Scottish Salmon. The Octopus was excellent. The portion was large. The skin was crisp. The meat was tender. There was ample fat remaining on the tentacle.The Scottish Salmon was pretty good. The skin was dense and crispy. The salmon was relatively juicy, though I prefer farmed salmon for it's added fat and flavor.Overall this was a very good restaurant week meal.

I had the best lobster roll I've ever had here!! Unlike most lobster rolls, the lobster roll I got here was filled with lots of tender lobster meat. The price of the lobster roll is worth it here! (Other lobster rolls I've had were more expensive with less lobster meat). The roll itself was buttered and crispy and not soggy at all. I ordered the winter special lobster Mac and cheese as well and was not disappointed at all. The flavor of the Mac and cheese was great and had a lot of lobster meat as well. I highly recommend Luke's Lobster to seafood lovers!

Title: A Dependable Delight: Lunch Tasting Menu Review

I recently indulged in the lunch tasting menu at a local gem, pleasantly priced at $89, gratuity pleasantly included. The experience comprised five well-executed courses, a refreshing palate cleanser, and an appetizing bread starter, making for a satisfying midday gourmet journey.

The menu kicked off with a fluffy, crisp-edged whole wheat bun, lightly salted to pique the taste buds. A fluke starter with apples and kohlrabi followed, showcasing meaty fish chunks in a well-balanced acidic dressing. Although the subsequent seafood course escapes my memory, its similarity to scallops and its delicious sauce left a positive impression.

A standout was the squid ink pasta with a rich, umami lobster sauce that truly delighted my palate. The duck course that followed was expertly cooked but left me briefly concerned about portion sizes—concerns that were quelled with the arrival of dessert.

The palate cleanser, an adult twist on applesauce with its apple sorbet and vanilla oil, prepared us for the finale—a vanilla yogurt mousse with pomegranate sauce. This light, fruit-based dessert ended the meal on a high note, leaving me satisfied without the post-meal slump.

However, the duration of the meal—a full two hours—felt unnecessarily prolonged. Additionally, the menu differed slightly from the one advertised online, a minor detail worth noting.

In summary, while the tasting menu may not ascend to the dizzying heights of its more expensive counterparts, it delivers consistent quality and taste at a value that is hard to beat.

I was Excited to try this Latin Caribbean Spot!I walked in (with NO Welcome, Hi, Hola, or Good Afternoon) and ordered Chivo Guisado aka Goat Stew. (Flavorful yet Thickly Sauced) The Beans stew needed more Flavor. There is no Restroom for Customers but they have Hand Sanitizer if needed... (I asked for a Wet Paper towel instead) The food was good but I was tired & wanted to finish it at home. I asked for a bag to go & Extra Napkins. The guy said to his female colleagues in Spanish that this guy is coming here for all the papers, I already gave him 1 sheet of Wet Paper Towel. I responded politely that my hands were Dirty, I just came from Work, & I was just Eating. His Eyes Opened Wider & he responded with an "Oh Shit". I continued on speaking in Spanish saying that I came here to Stuff myself & now I'm heading home. He gave me the Napkins & I said thank you.Pros1. Rice is well done.2. Chivo Guisado is flavorful and tender. Cons1. Better customer service (Everyone should feel Welcomed when entering the place)2. At 3:30pm the food should not look Unappetizing. Stir the Food, Add some Water, lmake it Presentable! 3. If it's Quiet then Change the Garbage! Why the Garbage is Full to the top??4. No Restroom.

I ditto all the comparisons to Eataly - this feels like a Spanish version! I ordered the patatas bravas, jamon and cheese bocata, and an order of churros with chocolate. The food was absolutely delicious. I'd recommend getting the patatas bravas with the aioli. The churros with chocolate are a great treat but also very sweet.While the food is delicious, it's also incredibly expensive. A small soda is $4, so I'd save this place for a special occasion.

Food was okay. Went on a wednesday night at 7pm for a professionals meetup there. We had a 12 top booked so we were immediately seated. Disclaimer: I think my experiences weren't the best here (compared to other Elite reviews here) since we ordered a whole bunch of dishes to share, and I didn't get the chance to sample everything on the table. I guess that happens when you go to these big networking events!Of the dishes that I did try, I tried a little bit of the beef noodle soup and the Zhajiangmian. The beef noodle soup was a little bland to my liking, and it felt the broth wasn't developed long enough to have all the flavors that you commonly associate with a normal bowl of beef noodle soup. Zhajiangmian was also a little salty for my taste, but the sauce was definitely only point as it packed quite a umami taste to it. Managed to try bits and pieces of the stir fry chicken. Chicken reminded me of the Sanbei Chicken you get in Taiwan! I love the use of Shaoxing wine in terms of bringing the freshness and umami of the chicken flavors, and there were lots of other vegetables in the dish which I like. We also got fried breadsticks for the night which were surprisingly good! Tasted like a vegan version of popcorn chicken (for all my Chinese food fanatics here!). Oh btw, check in here on Yelp to redeem for a free cucumber salad! Salad was a little too pungent and acidic for my taste, and one person from our table thought the red peppers added too much heat to the dish. We also got the fried chicken skewers, but unfortunately I didn't get to try any of that. Overall - I think its because I went with a large group where one person ordered for everyone made the meal a little chaotic and could have affected the quality of food that we had tonight. I think I would give it a second try though sometime in the future with a smaller crowd or with just one friend if I'm nearby Dunhuang.

Walking into this establishment was a breath of fresh air – the ambiance was electric, and the beats dropping in the background were absolutely spot-on, infusing an undeniable energy that was truly invigorating. The trendiness of the atmosphere did not go unnoticed and added to the overall experience, making it a fabulous spot to unwind and soak in the vibes.

Unfortunately, the food did not quite live up to the hype. The Mimosas served lacked the punch I was hoping for, skimping a bit too much on the bubbly. More disappointingly, the $26 price tag on the fried chicken and waffles felt steep, as the dish fell short of the culinary delight one might expect for such a premium.

Despite the culinary missteps, the sheer vibrancy of the setting provided a great time overall. My take – this place has the potential for a full five-star experience but for now, it's a solid three stars from me.

Title: Hip Vibes and Fusion Flavors at NYC Eatery

My recent visit to my sister’s favorite NYC restaurant was a tale of highs and lows. While not utterly blown away, I did enjoy aspects of the dining experience. The early evening arrival strategy paid off, allowing us to skip the notoriously long queues and revel in our foresight as the line swelled behind us.

The ambiance was decidedly youthful, with servers exuding an effortless cool that set an upbeat tone for the evening. We embarked on a culinary exploration, sampling a broad selection of dishes. The Angry Sweet Potato, though unremarkable, was satisfactory with its spicy kick. However, the Lucky Noodle shone with its succulent noodles and a savory sauce that left me craving more of the modest portion.

The visual appeal of the Tuna Tataki was matched by its taste, but it was the Edamame Dumplings that stole the show, despite the server’s honest revelation that truffle oil substituted for the real deal. The pork offered a pleasant sweet and spicy balance, while the Kimchi Paella was a close runner-up, even though it lacked the characteristic crispy base I'd hoped for.

Not all was perfect; the Popcorn Chicken fell flat, echoing the ubiquitous General Tso's from any standard Chinese takeaway. On a high note, the Eel Tacos delivered with delectable one-bite wonders, perfectly complemented by a generous dollop of guacamole.

In summary, while the restaurant had its hits and misses, the standout dishes suggest it's worth a try for those in search of a trendy dining scene with some delightful fusion twists.

I was pleasantly surprised to find no wait for a table on a Tuesday evening. Opted for the recommended combo at $24.90, which is on the pricier side compared to the typical $15-$20 ramen bowls around the city. The experience is novel – you order via a paper slip from a private stall equipped with a service window. Stalls can be opened up for dining companions, ensuring you're not entirely secluded.

My visit coincided with a free noodle refill promo, but the generous portion meant I didn't need the extra. The ramen itself was tasty and struck a good balance in richness. Notably, the noodles are thinner than at other spots. While I would love to return, it would be more appealing if the price were slightly lower. Also, they don’t encourage tipping, which is a plus for budget-conscious diners.
Had a nice grilled cheese and tomato soup along with an earl grey tea.  It was good but overpriced for what it was.

Best Tarte Tatin in NYC?  Rotisserie Georgette... any questions?Ok, the poultry dishes are great... If you don't want to cook for Thanksgiving, this is the place to be...Rotisserie Georgette is always a wonderful choice!See you there... I will be the guy eating their best 3-course meal:Appetizer - Tarte TatinMain Course - Tarte TatinDessert - Tarte TatinAny questions?

Came here on a Saturday night for dinner with the girls : We ordered a few things to share 1. oysters : I would skip these , this was the only thing I didn't like 2. Sliders : delicious and perfect sizing 3. Lobster Mac and cheese : small portion, could use more cheese but still was good 4. Shrimp tempura roll : amazing 5. Wagyu and lobster roll ; probably my favorite item there ! Nothing like I've ever had before !! Drinks were good, service was very good , our waitress Jovanna was amazing . The vibe was great , beautiful inside ! The crowd was lovely and the whole feel of the place was very adult and sexy , I really liked it

Round seating around the sushi bar for seating and it was a pleasant experience here. It is a little more expensive from Kazunori and this is a tipping establishment unlike kazunori. They offer hand rolls, omakase, and temaki rolls. I did the hand rolls and my favorite was the yelllowtail hand roll. I also got the green tea creme brûlée and it was pretty good but very small. And yes I made reservations!

Mercer Kitchen is such a chic restaurant and food is always good. I come here every once in a while and am never bored with this place! My meals are always enjoyable here! I had the warm madeleines today they were so awesome!!!!

Title: High Hopes Dashed at Local Eatery

After eagerly anticipating a meal at a spot I’d often admired from afar, my experience unfortunately did not live up to the tantalizing photos I’d seen on Yelp. The shrimp quesadilla, while enveloped in a delightful corn tortilla, suffered from an ill-conceived mix of queso fresco, lettuce, and pico de gallo that clashed rather than complemented, leading me to discard everything but the shrimp. The regular nachos fell victim to overbaking, resulting in a mostly inedible mass fused to the container, despite promising ingredients. My sweet note, a flan, was disappointingly watery and lacked the creamy richness one anticipates from this dessert staple—it might, however, be a hit for the lactose intolerant. My beverage, a pineapple Jarrito, was the only item that met expectations. At the end of my meal, I found myself $26 lighter with little satisfaction. On the bright side, the service was amiable and the cleanliness was commendable, but unfortunately, these aspects could not rescue the overall dining experience.

Title: Authentic Vietnamese Haven in Chinatown

If you find yourself craving Pho or other Vietnamese delicacies, I'd highly recommend this gem in Chinatown. The restaurant's ambiance is familiar and comforting, much like its counterparts, fostering an authentic dining experience.

The menu is impressively varied, catering to diverse tastes with dishes ranging from savory pork chops to classic spring rolls – perfect for sharing. As for the Pho, each steaming bowl is a personalized invitation to culinary bliss.
