Service efficiency is commendable, with food arriving promptly after ordering. Prices are on par with the neighborhood standard, providing good value for your money. A notable mention is the availability of brown rice for a healthier option, albeit for a small additional cost.

For those on the go, takeout service is readily available. And while the restrooms are reserved for patrons, the convenience of both cash and credit card acceptance for payment rounds off the welcoming experience.
Fu Zhou style cheap eats! We ordered a noodle and a soup for $5! What a great deal! The soup came with many small wontons and the peanut sauce with noodles was good.

Title: Sophisticated Sushi Soiree

My dining experience at this establishment, away from the exclusive omakase counter, was nothing short of delightful. The ambiance is notably elegant, setting a perfect stage for either a romantic date night or a celebration of a special event. The service mirrored the environment, with our waitress exuding an air of professionalism that enhanced our evening.

We opted for the tableside omakase, a decision I'd make again in a heartbeat. The sushi arrived in sets of five, clearly paced to allow for savoring each bite. A particular highlight was the tuna selection, served in a tantalizing crescendo from least to most fatty, each piece melting in the mouth more decadently than the last.

Accompanying these oceanic gems were the rich, perfectly executed uni and a miso cod that will be etched in my flavor memories for some time. To wash down these delights, we indulged in a few choices from their impressive sake collection, a perfect match for the exquisite sashimi and sushi.

In sum, you can expect to pay up for the quality and atmosphere at this venue, but for sushi aficionados and those with a penchant for finery, it is unquestionably worth the splurge.

I came here to try something new and a place I had heard about when I was at Barrier Brewing out on Long Island.  They make the really good Uncle Boons brew chile-style beer.In any case, we were able to get to Uncle Boons at night without a reservation and got VERY lucky that a bar table opened up right as we came downstairs and we grabbed the table as those are first come, first served.  Otherwise the place was packed.We had pretty good service overall.  The water was refilled often.I ended up getting a Chang slushy, which was interesting as they put the bottle in another cup with salt water to make the inside slushy and super cold.  Chang is your basic export lager, but it was an interesting way they served this. I still highly suggest the uncle boons brew though.The server suggested two small plates and a large plate for two people.  We ended up with one small plate and one large plate and that was plenty IMHO.  For the small plate, we got the the  Yum Kai Hua Pli (roasted chicken and banana blossom salad) and for the large plate, the Massman Neuh (Beef Ribs with Massaman Curry). We also got a side of roti, which was one piece of flatbread.Both were supposedly spicy dishes. I'd say the Hua Pli was spicier.  Both were very good and overall, was filling with the roti and the drinks.The ambiance was nice, tho being by the door, the cold air as people came in was refreshing to me, but could be cold to others.  The lighting was on the darker side, so my food photos did not come out well.I'd definitely come back or try the sister location.

I came here with a party of 3 for dinner around 6pm on a Saturday. Place was around half full and so we were seated right away. The interior is very nicely decorated and it's very spacious so you don't feel cramped. We got the classic beef pho with classic broth, spicy beef pho, and shaking beef with rice. The flavor of everything was very good! The portions of the pho were good with lots of meat in both. Only reason I docked a star was for both pho dishes, the noodles had clumped together and needed some prying apart, kind of like they'd been sitting there for a bit in the bowl before the broth had been added. For the beef slices also, they were all sort of stuck together. I would definitely come here again for some more pho!

Title: A Mixed Bag at No-Frills Dim Sum Spot

On a bustling Saturday morning, a group of us ventured into what appeared to be a local, off-the-beaten-path establishment for dim sum—unmarked by the footsteps of tourists. This no-frills spot offered a classic menu at appealingly low prices, but ironically, it was the lackluster execution that cost them their charm. The fare, which included shrimp dumplings, tofu skin rolls, shrimp rice crepe, spare ribs, chicken feet, and shu mai, arrived overcooked, causing the dumplings to stick together—a disappointing kitchen misstep.

Absent were the bustling carts typical of traditional dim sum restaurants; instead, we placed our orders with a waiter, though service lagged uncharacteristically for such an eatery. Despite this, the baked pork bun shone as a beacon of popularity among patrons—an item I've noted to return for, bypassing the dim sum offerings next time around.

Service: Great! I do have to say that the service was phenomenal! Our server was so nice and let my group take their time looking over the menu. I can't stress how nice the service was. The location has TVs around the whole seating area and they allow people to change the channels to their liking!Food:Sean's Kitchen Sink (Wings, Mozzarella Sticks, Chicken Tenders, Waffle Fries, Onion Rings) - FRIED FOOD GALORE! All the items were placed in a small kitchen sink for people to enjoy out of. It was whimsical and fun to have at the table. I do have to say that it was all waffle fries and onion rings; there were only a count of 4 of the other items. The menu suggests that this should be ordered among three people but I would suggest to get this for a group of 5 or more and order extra sides of protein.On to my next food adventure...

I visited this charming spot for Sunday brunch and the experience was delightful. Although the outdoor area tempted with its cuteness, the heat nudged us indoors for comfort. My boyfriend and I shared a diversity of dishes: the yogurt and granola bowl was outstanding, the artfully presented melon bowl impressed, the avocado bacon egg sandwich hit all the right savory notes, and the toast adorned with honey and ham rounded out our meal with a sweet and salty touch. Each dish was a testament to the kitchen's prowess. Highly recommend for a great brunch experience.

Title: A Cozy Anniversary Lunch to Remember at [Restaurant Name]

My fiancé and I chose [Restaurant Name] to celebrate our anniversary on a Sunday, anticipating a crowd. Even with a reservation secured through Yelp, we were pleasantly surprised to be seated immediately at 1 pm, amidst an abundance of available seating.

The restaurant's design smartly places tables at the back, shielding diners from cold winter drafts—a thoughtful touch. Our meal commenced with delectable crispy spring rolls, a quartet of perfectly fried delights blended with pork, shrimp, mushroom, and taro—a unique and, in my opinion, superior take on the traditional pork version. Paired with crisp lettuce, shredded carrots, and fish sauce, it was a faultless appetizer for two.

For the main course, the Pad See Iew, with its New Zealand grass-fed beef, was a standout, earning the 'best ever' accolade from both my fiancé and myself. My Pad Thai, customized with chicken instead of shrimp, was pleasing albeit outshone by the Pad See Iew. A distinctive touch was the poached egg topping, a novel complement that I couldn't resist.

While the portions were slightly smaller compared to other local establishments, they remained generous—testament to their quality over quantity ethos, as I was unable to finish mine.

In summary, [Restaurant Name] not only met but exceeded our expectations, making our anniversary lunch an event to remember.

Title: Hidden Gem for Lunch Specials

I recently stumbled upon a fantastic lunch spot I'd often passed by without a second glance. Lured in by an attractive lunch special sign, I decided to give it a try, and I was pleasantly surprised by what I found. The moment I entered, the tantalizing aroma of Kasian spices and fresh seafood was overwhelmingly inviting.

Priced at a mere $10.99, their lunch specials are an absolute steal. The service was top-notch; both waitresses and waiters greeted us with friendly smiles and took our orders without delay. Since the restaurant wasn't crowded, our meals arrived promptly.

I indulged in a shrimp Po' boy that was generously packed with perfectly cooked shrimp, complemented by a delightful wasabi aioli. My coworker enjoyed a tasty shrimp wrap, and both of our dishes came with a fresh side salad.

For anyone looking for a delicious and affordable seafood lunch, this place is a must-try. Count me in as a new regular!

Title: A Delightful Culinary Experience at Miznon

My visit to Miznon last Saturday at lunchtime confirmed the buzz around this bustling eatery. Despite the crowd, we managed to nab a table for four at the front—luck was on our side.

We started off with the baby cauliflower, a deceptively simple dish that was bursting with flavor. For my main course, I opted for the roasted chicken, succulent and perfectly seasoned. My companions indulged in the folded burger, an oozing cheese sensation, the rib eye steak, and the ratatouille, each dish earning high praise. The freshness of the meats and the harmony of sauces and pickles with each bite created a rich tapestry of textures and flavors.

Miznon lived up to its reputation—every dish a testament to their culinary expertise. The experience was nothing short of awesome, proving that sometimes, the most crowded places are indeed worth the wait.

Title: Authentic Thai Flavors in a Cozy Setting

I recently dined at this charming Thai spot on a Friday afternoon, perfectly timing my visit before the evening crowd. This restaurant is a haven for those seeking traditional Thai country cuisine in a relaxed ambiance. The staff's warmth and attentiveness only enhanced the experience. 

A unique touch was being invited to view the day's offerings simmering in pots at the back, which felt like a hospitable peek into a family kitchen. Sitting down to a complimentary jar of house-made pickles was a delightful start.

The menu caters well to diverse diets with vegan and vegetarian options. I opted for a combination of stewed market vegetables and a lush green vegetable curry over organic red rice. Each dish was a testament to the authentic Thai flavors.

We also indulged in a Thai omelette, a refreshing greens basket, and the highlight - a heavenly dessert of kombucha squash and taro in a sweet coconut sauce. It's a must-try and a perfect round-off to a sumptuous meal.

I'm already looking forward to my next visit to this gem of a restaurant for another taste of their exceptional food and hospitality.

We ventured out for a taste of Latin cuisine and sampled an array of dishes including Queso Frito con Maduros, Alcapurria, and Pastelillo de Queso. Each dish was quite flavorful, though they did err on the side of being overly oily.

I had been craving Ethiopian food, and Benyam did not disappoint. For a group of six, we split a meat sample (for 2) and a veg sampler (also for 2), which seemed to be the perfect amount of food. The platters came with a variety of sides, all of which were tasty. I think my favorites were the Doro Wat that came with the meat sampler and a beet side that came with the veg sample. Service was also friendly.

Solely because my co workers enjoyed their food did I give it 4 stars. I was teetering on 3 because I had the lunch special personal pizza and salad and was not at all impressed. It was a house salad and I said hey I'll just trust them with whatever dressing they thought complimented it. Salad was meehhhh and the dressing a strong no. One of my co workers had a pizza that had shrimp on it. The other had a chicken parm sandwich and the other a salad which they all said was good. I had an Arnold Palmer which tasted like sour mix - my co worker who also ordered that agreed.I am a new Yorker through and through and pizza is very important to me. From the crust to the sauce and the cheese. It all matters. This was sub par unfortunately for me. There was little to no sauce . The texture was like cheese on thin cardboard. I really hate when I don't have a great food experience so I want to go back to maybe try a sandwich and hopefully my taste buds will have a better experience. However, I'm not rushing to do so.

Simply delicious pizza. Definitely worth the wait. While the line is long it moves pretty quickly. The Sicilian with pepperoni was the only thing I tried because that's what all the hype is about. It definitely lives up to the hype. Sauce has a sweet little tang and the pepperoni was perfection while the crust was light and airy and perfectly well done and crispy. Prince street pizza has just become a top 10 in nyc to me

I visited this bustling spot for a Friday lunch and was promptly seated despite the crowd. A complimentary lychee soju, courtesy of a Yelp check-in, was a delightful start, albeit on the smaller side. The crunchy tofu appetizer was a standout—potentially the star of the menu. My main course featured a mix-up where I received truffle fries with my omurice instead of the ordered salad, which they later rectified, allowing me to enjoy both. The truffle fries were a revelation, boasting a robust truffle essence paired exquisitely with a tangy orange sauce. In comparison, the salad was underwhelming and didn't offer the same value. I'd recommend opting for the fries alongside the omurice. The Chicken Katsu's crispiness impressed, though it would benefit from a generous drizzle of curry rather than a modest side serving. Overall, a satisfying experience with just a couple of tweaks needed for perfection.

Title: A Hotpot Hustle Worth the Wait

Last Saturday at 7 PM, my party of six hit up this spot for an all-you-can-eat hotpot experience. Despite a lengthy wait of an hour, the anticipation was part of the charm. A slight hiccup in seating meant we had to cozy up around single pots rather than the communal one we expected, but teamwork made it work for a shared feast.

Our waitress was on the ball, promptly taking our orders while the kitchen churned out dishes with impressive speed. A soup base too fiery for our tastes was swapped out with a smile, showcasing their accommodating service. As the evening bustle peaked, subsequent orders lagged a tad, with the occasional forgotten item requiring a nudge. But let's talk about the food: simply delicious, served in an environment that radiated cleanliness.

A previous visit to their Brooklyn joint during a weekday lunch hinted at their potential for perfection - a benchmark for what their service can be when not swamped. In the end, the pros decidedly outweigh the cons. If you're a hotpot enthusiast, this place is a solid bet.

ehh this is more of a 3.5 star review actually. I do feel a little harsh to give it 3 stars, but I was just not too impressed with the meal. They have a great lunch set deal at $21 where they give you a lot of mini portioned servings of a variety of dishes along with your main course - soba noodles. I made the mistake of ordering hot soba instead of cold. For some reason, I thought the hot soba would be on a dry platter like the cold one, but just warmer, but mine was in soup. It was good, but nothing too special. I was very disappointed at the mini chirashi rice, because I thought there would be at least some sashimi slices on top but nope there was only egg and some salmon roe. The salad was refreshing and so was the pumpkin on the side. The broiled salmon is okay - I'm not a big fan of it. My boyfriend got the mini lunch set which I think personally is a better deal because he got to pick a rice bowl dish and get to have soba/udon on the side. That's what I would do next time, because they seem to have a lot of interesting rice bowl dishes there. He got the one with eel on top and it tasted great! I'm usually not a big fan of eel rice bowls, but I really liked this one. Overall, this is a great place for its value but I'd try something different from them next time.

Atoboy offers a delightfully fun dining experience with its chic and contemporary atmosphere. The concept of shareable dishes adds a convivial touch reminiscent of Spanish tapas, fostering a sense of community at the table. The thoughtfully crafted aesthetics of the cuisine are striking, with every dish boasting vivid colors and flavors that excite the palate. Standouts include the Uni dish, which is simply sublime, and the octopus dish, a close contender that tantalizes with its taste and presentation. Atoboy is a must-visit for those seeking a modern and memorable culinary adventure.

I thought the chicken was excellent. I purchased the ranch one. I like the cone idea so you don't need a fork but I did not enjoy the cone as much as the chicken. My friend purchased the maple one and the syrup was a bit messy. I don't prefer maple anything so I did not like that one. If you like those kinds of flavors, I'm sure you will enjoy it.

Title: Decent KBBQ Experience with a Steep Price Tag

I recently dined at a Korean BBQ joint that boasted a spacious interior and an interesting twist to the typical grilling experience. Instead of the usual table grills, this restaurant featured grills on rolling platforms, with servers handling the cooking. This innovation was rather convenient, eliminating the usual smoke and odors associated with grilling at the table.

As for the food, the flavors were generally satisfying but not exceptional. The beef platter, along with some side dishes, came with a hefty price tag of $80 per person, which felt quite steep for the quality provided. A major letdown was the scallion in the seafood pancake; it was distractingly oversized and lacked the careful preparation I'd have appreciated.

However, it wasn't all underwhelming. The marinated beef short ribs were a standout, delivering a succulent and tender taste that was a cut above the rest. While the overall experience was decent, I had hoped for a more refined meal to justify the cost.

I finally got to visit my namesake today! I've heard all the raves about the famous Emily burger and that's why my friends and I braved the Sunday MTA hell and got to the restaurant just as they opened. The restaurant itself is a bit on the small side so I can imagine that it fills up fast as the day goes on. There were 5 other people waiting outside with me when I got there. We sat down in the corner and were almost immediately acknowledged by a waiter to take our orders. Three of us got the Double Stack burger, two got pizzas and the chicken sandwich. We got the Dear Friend cocktail and the Barrier Imposter Pilsner to drink. Both were delicious! Our food came out about 15-20 minutes later. The burger was smaller than I expected it to be but I hoped that it made up in flavor. I took a bite, and all the flavors of the pretzel bun, cheese, special Emmy sauce (spicy soy and mayo) and patties blended together amazingly. It was definitely worth the trip out to the city on a Sunday morning. My only bone to pick with my experience is that they definitely went heavy on the toppings. All of the flavors were overtaking the meat. I honestly couldn't even taste it, which is sad because it's the best part of a burger. I think next time they should put a small spoon of Emmy Sauce and put the rest on the side. I would say it was worth more like $20. Overall I would give my experience a 4.5. Great service, pretty good food.

Title: Sauce - A Genuine Slice of NYC

Sauce is one of those unassuming NYC pizza sanctuaries that manages to stand out in a city saturated with formidable pie contenders. With two sister locations in Rivington and the Lower East Side, Sauce has firmly planted its roots in the New York pizza landscape.

I recall trying their plain slice, which has been highly praised by the likes of El Presidente, and I must concur that it does the acclaim justice. Is it a perfect 9.1? Perhaps not until a second tasting, but it certainly towers well above the fold.

Their variety isn't limited to the classics; square slices like the El Pastor are worth a mention, artistically topped with a vibrant mix of tomato and pineapple sauce, stretchy mozzarella, sharp pecorino, tender roasted pork, tangy pickled red onion, fiery jalapeño, and a sprinkle of cilantro. As a self-proclaimed pineapple-on-pizza skeptic, I was surprised that the fruit didn't overpower, but rather complemented the other bold flavors.

With their active social media presence and frequent promotions, Sauce makes it easy to choose them over countless others for your pizza fix. Whether you're a traditionalist or an adventurous eater, Sauce delivers a pie that's hard to forget.

Title: My Weekly Lunch Indulgence

I frequent this spot for its reliably good lunch, typically opting for the large bowl accompanied by six free toppings. Despite the price being a tad steep for my daily lunch budget, it's a worthwhile splurge given its nutritious offerings compared to other lunchtime options.

The standout is their unique black garlic aioli—a rarity that I can't resist. It's an absolute must-try, enhancing the already fresh and flavorful fish, with the salmon being a personal highlight.

My bowl is a delightful mix of textures and tastes, thanks to my chosen toppings: sweet and crunchy onions, salty masago, tender edamame, earthy hijiki, and a kick from crushed red pepper flakes. I go half-and-half with white and brown rice and split my protein between ahi tuna and salmon for the perfect balance.

A small gripe: the poke bowl does lean towards the expensive side, and they could be more generous with the nori when included as a topping. However, these are minor compared to the overall satisfying experience.

I recently visited this halal cart, and it was a delightful experience. The food is not only delicious but also quite affordable, making it stand out as one of the city's top carts. Despite dropping by late at night, my friends and I were served promptly, and the taste of the food was incredible. I'm looking forward to coming back. Highly recommended!

Title: A Satisfying Buffet with Standout Goat and Okra

I recently enjoyed a lunch buffet that I must say, is an incredible deal for anyone looking for variety and value. The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the goat dish, which was rich in flavor and cooked to perfection, and it paired wonderfully with the freshly baked naan. The okra also deserves special mention for its perfectly crispy texture and seasoning.

While most of the offerings were the usual fare and decent in quality, I found the condiments to be a bit of a letdown. The green sauce and the orange-red colored onions, which are usually a burst of fresh flavors, had a slightly fermented taste that didn't quite hit the mark for me.

Despite that, the overall experience was a positive one, thanks to the standout dishes. The goat and the okra alone are worth a return visit.

I visited China Blue with a group and had a great experience. We shared:+ Red cooked pork w taro+ Pan fried pork buns+ Crispy eel+ Soup dumplings+ Rice cake with duck egg+ Bok choy+ Sausage riceThe red cooked pork, crispy eel, soup dumplings and bok choy were my favorites. Service was great and the space is large and nicely decorated. While the food is different, I did like China Blue more than Cafe China. Definitely recommended!

Koku Ramen, 2w 32nd St - NYCHappy Hour:  Mon-Thurs 3p-6p & 10p-closing, Fri 3p-6pComing into this next eat, I had high hopes for this little find. I attended the happy hour time slot and found a few nice selections on there menu, reasonably priced. We were seated pretty quick and service for the most part was good, with lots of room for improvement.I started off with the Chashu Bun, 2 pc ($5).  A soft white milk bread bun, with pickled cucumbers, red cabbage, pineapple hosin sauce, and a spicy Sambal mayo dipping sauce. First bite was grand, the flavors of the cucumbers, cabbage and pineapple hosin , made my mouth jump for joy. Next came the Chicken Karaage, ($6),  But I will tell you about this at the end.... So onto the Main..  Koku Ramen ($14 D) ($9.99 L). A Tonkotsu based ramen broth, with Chashu, Kikarage, black garlic oil, baby bok choy, mung bean sprouts, scallions, nori, and a Soft boiled egg. I ordered it Medium spicy, and here is where it all came crashing down. On first taste, the broth was good and spicy, and I thought Wow, Medium spicy was Spicy !  and Spicy it was, as I later found out they gave me Hot Spicy.  Luckily, I was able to taste what medium spicy was supposed to taste like, but by then, I thing my taste buds were done for the day. The egg was overdone, more firm than soft, as a tonkotsu egg should be. and the charsui was not tender as needed but there was 2 hardy pieces.  So Back to the Chicken Karaage. This made me happy, Crispy savory bites of Chicken topped with scallions, and accompanied with a Shiracha mayo.  Yes these were good.... So, a rating of 3 stars from me, as the simplest things and attention to detail would have rated them higher. Hope the next time will be better.Follow me on Twitter, Facebook, Youtube, Insta and Yelp, as I travel the world in search of the perfect bowl of noodle soup. @noodlesoupreview #noodlesoupr
Yes the Crunchy French Toast is delicious and the service is excellent, but this place is EXTREMELY overpriced. Mimosas were also good but, again, can find better for cheaper in the city.

On a side street removed from the melee of Mykonos during Pride Week or Times Square any day of the week, you'll find Loi Estiatorio, the passion project of Chef/Owner Maria Loi. The room is quiet and lit low. (There is a line between "romantic" and can't see what's moving on my plate). Loi is romantic. The Decor is Spartan. Stark white with a few monochromatic enlarged photos of Greece. (Greece on the walls is much better than grease on the meatballs). Booths line the long narrow dining room just past the half moon bar. The seats might have been cannibalized from an old school bus, so you'll need a pillow for support or to reach your Tzatziki, but settle in, kick back, Chef Loi will be by shortly to chat and guide you on the Hellenic journey you've come for.You'll be so relaxed by now you'll hardly realize the music loop has played Never On A Sunday for the 5th time. The Staff: The family of the family owned place. They are polite and thoughtful, and no, it is civilized here, so don't expect a hail of cheap dinner plates hitting the floor to the delight of Ouzo soaked Greek truck drivers yelling "yasou" at you.   The Vibe: Who goes there? Date night for anyone of Greek ancestry, and tourists who just loved their Seabourn Cruise that docked in Athens for 3 hours. The Bar: Four signature cocktails. Skip them all and have a classic. My Xios Spritz with Aperol, Ya Mastiha (resin from the Mastic Tree) and Blink (Gin) was a cold pink drink that had notes of Red Hots and Lavoris. The customized Amaro with Lemon and Ginger Syrup needs to be on the menu, not just because it was something I asked the bar tender to create it but because it was really delicious. The Food: Have the seafood recommended by Chef Loi. Pay attention to only her suggestions. Fish is flown in daily for her from Greece to order. So, that's what's to order here, and those are orders. A welcome warm bowl of house made Pita arrived with two little nuggets of pillowy biscuit dough balls on top. All to be dipped in the house made yogurt, Feta, and Dill Sauce. The Pita strips were hot and crisped at the edges which means you can eat them and still gesticulate wildly while talking like any good Greek. The Octopus was tender as a baby's butt and piled on a puree of cooked Fava Beans with grated Onion, Bell Pepper bits, and a few Capers. While not stellar, this dish was as described on the menu and a good start for starters. The Spanokopita, on the other hand, was stellar. Two Garbage Burrito sized hand pies, generously stuffed with fresh Spinach and Feta, Dill and Mint all encased in shattering crisp warm Phyllo. Push it through the dollop of whipped Feta and you've eaten something for the Gods.  At Chef Loi's urging I ordered the Fish en Papiotte, (Parchment Paper) which was the daily special. It was Bacalao (Cod) and special it was. The Cod was absolutely perfect and impressively presented in the opened paper boat in which it was expertly baked. The large Cod filet shared space with pureed Potato, Spinach, Thyme all lubricated with cold pressed Olive Oil made in the homeland for the restaurant and a splash of Lemon. The fish was moist, flaky, meaty and all the things a dead Cod is supposed to be. Praise Cod. Helen of Troy launched 1,000 ships and so could Chef Loi's fish.                                    The Lamb Shank with grated Tomatoes, Onion, Lamb Jus and Orzo was touted by the server. "Oh, it is great. It sits in a braise for a long time". Yes, it seats in the braise until it is cooked to death and desert dry. The large Lamb chunk rested on a mound of over cooked Orzo. A healthy sprinkle of aged Myzithra salvaged this, if barely, as this salty cheese grated on Alpo at a party would disappear off the Buffet Table in a hurry. Sadly the Lamb was a Greek tragedy.  Finally, the Ekmek Kadaifi (sounds like a Dr Suess character) for dessert was a custard on Kadaifi (shredded Phyllo) with Yogurt, Honey and Walnuts on the side.The creamy square was dusted with Cinnamon, but the nest of Kadaifi was mushy instead of crunchy as it had been nesting and resting since the afternoon prep. Maybe there's a nice Chocolate something waiting for you on your pillow at the Hotel. Have that. If you're gonna do it Greek style, overall, this place will make you happy.

I recently visited this local gem for brunch and was pleasantly surprised by their unique brunch pizza topped with avocado. Initially underwhelming in appearance, the dish was delightfully flavorful and satisfying. The ambiance was perfect for a relaxed catch-up with friends, due in part to the uncrowded setting. With a tempting array of other brunch options on the menu, I'm already looking forward to my next visit. Highly recommend for a cozy and tasty brunch experience!

Spot is one of my favorite dessert spots in the city. When you come they have their standard 6 choice signature desserts and they have 3 seasonal desserts. I chose to get a signature dessert that was a cookie/brownie based with pretzels and scoop of condensed milk ice cream. The dessert was served fresh and warm in a hot skillet. Very sweet just like I love it.

Title: A Flavorful Adventure at Poke Green – FiDi's Latest Delight

Poke Green has carved its niche in the Financial District, offering yet another vibrant lunch option amidst the bustling scene. The establishment is a sanctuary for poke lovers, catering to both those who crave the ease of a pre-set bowl and those who yearn for culinary exploration with the "Poke Your Way" option. 

I dove into the latter during my visit, reveling in the robust list of customizations. The process is surprisingly straightforward: pick a base, select proteins (with eight ocean-fresh choices), mix in your favorites, flavor it with sauce, load up on toppings (hint: approach the Wasabi with caution), and add some crunch to finish. It's akin to the familiar assembly lines of Chipotle or Subway, and despite an initial illusion of modesty, the bowl was hearty and satisfying.

Quality is a high point here, with the Ahi Tuna and Salmon shining amidst a sea of fresh ingredients. The poke bowl was delicious, aligned with expectations, though not transcending past poke experiences. A small word of advice — opt for a bowl over a burrito until the staff perfects their rolling technique.

While the prices edge on the premium side (around $12-$14), Poke Green stands as a worthy indulgence for those looking to splurge on flavor and freshness.

An oldie and a newbie in a way, but even better than before with a brand new menu to boot.Fresh from a new renovation and seemingly under some new management, Chenny's Kitchen (formerly Chen's Buffet Bar and Oriental Express way back in the day), just opened up on Cedar Street and it looks better than ever.I recently took a lunch trip to what was one of my favorite local, reasonably priced eats, Chen's Buffet Bar, only to see that everything had been revamped. What?????? But nothing to fear though because they had just re-branded and renovated. Although the layout was the same, everything else was brand spankin' new. Revamped as in new floors, walls, buffet, tables and seats and, best of all, a new menu! When I walked in, the fresh smell of Chinese fast food permeated through the air and I was genuinely excited to see what they were now serving since I last visited the old restaurant.First, I walked around and took a look at the buffet bar, where the food was looking very fresh and going at a crazy low price of $7.99/lb from 11am-1:45pm and the shocking deal of $4.99/lb from 1:45-3:00pm! I could see the steam rising out of the trays on the sides of the walls and everything looked very clean and neat. To be honest, that's a shocker nowadays when it comes to buffet bars, so I was glad to see it was well maintained here. However, I was really feeling for something from the kitchen, so decided to save the buffet bar for my next trip.The kitchen specials (platters, noodle soups, fried rice and appetizers/dim sum) were all clearly displayed over the cashier on 3 LCDs. The noodle soups were all $9-$10, which was quite fair for the FiDi, and featured Chinatown favorites like roast pork, roast duck, beef stew, seafood, wonton to name a few. On the middle screen were Chenny's Platters, which were basically entrees served with white/brown/pork fried rice/lo mein and $8 or $9 each. Entrees included chicken/vegetable or pork/beef/shrimp/seafood items, such as everyday favorites like sesame chicken, chicken w/ string beans, curry chicken, roast pork, salt pepper pork chop, etc. I could go on and on as they were 20+ items on it. Finally, on the right screen, there were fried rices and noodles, and for a first in the FiDi, dim sum dishes! Yes, dim sum has made its way to the FiDi finally ... and at Chinatown prices to boot.For my lunch, I ended up ordering a Singapore Chow Mai Fun from the kitchen. It was on par with what I expected the flavors of a good Singapore Chow Mai Fun to be. What I really loved though was the portioning. The amount of noodle in the bowl easily could have fed a cow! OK, maybe it would need a bit more something to supplement its meal, but you get my point. In addition, the Mai Fun was a bit moist, which was nice to see, considering many restaurants make it just too dang dry these days.Overall, there aren't many Chinese restaurant options in the FiDi, so it was definitely nice to see Chenny's back up and running after their renovation. With the new digs, fresh and clean interior and new menu, I'll be back to check off that list of things to try because there were plenty of things I wanted, but there just isn't enough space in my stomach for it. In this age of rising prices in 2020, especially in the FiDi, Chenny's is one of those spots that you don't have to worry about breaking the bank just to buy lunch ... and you'll enjoy the actual flavor of the food too while saving a few bucks!

My boyfriend and I visited this restaurant for a late breakfast and we had a mixed experience. The service could have been warmer; the staff's lack of friendliness, absent smiles, and minimal interaction left a bit to be desired. However, they seated us promptly and took our order without delay.

On to the food - it was the highlight of our visit. I ordered the Nutella s'mores waffle paired with eggs and ham. While the waffle was slightly on the dry side, it was still flavorful and generously sized. My boyfriend's choice, the banana chocolate chip pancakes accompanied by eggs and sausage, hit the mark for him.

In conclusion, despite the service not being particularly welcoming, the quality of the meal compensated for it. We were satisfied and would consider returning for the food.

Title: Pleasant Surprise at Riverside Grill

My colleagues and I visited Riverside Grill for a holiday team lunch, having reserved a table for nine at 12:30. On arrival, the place was noticeably quiet, setting a relaxed tone for our meal.

We kicked things off with calamari and burrata appetizers, both of which were delightful without any shortcomings. I opted for the Mixed Grill Kebab as my main course – an ample platter featuring chicken, beef, and kofta skewers alongside mushrooms, peppers, onions, and a generous helping of rice. Contrary to its appearance, the chicken was succulent, while the beef met my medium-rare preference. The kofta, slightly underdone, was a minor hiccup, yet it didn't detract from the overall experience or my well-being.

Although the dish didn't include a side salad as advertised, the portion was satisfying without it. The meal left me curious to explore more of the menu. With its proximity to the water, I look forward to returning in the warmer months to take advantage of the outdoor seating. Overall, Riverside Grill is worth another visit for anyone in the mood for a hearty meal with a view.

Title: A Delightful Indian Buffet Experience at a New Local Spot

I recently had the pleasure of dining at the new Indian restaurant that I had been eagerly monitoring. Their advertised all-you-can-eat lunch buffet for $17.95, available daily from 11:30 am to 3:30 pm, drew me in for a midday meal.

The space is a large square area that's been thoughtfully decorated, creating a pleasant ambiance. As I took my seat among the few other diners, I was promptly asked if I'd be partaking in the buffet. With a filled water glass in hand, I eagerly approached the spread.

The buffet offered an impressive array of dishes, including fragrant Basmati rice, hearty daal (black lentils), indulgent kadi pakada, creamy saag paneer, rich chicken tikka masala, a savory lamb and peas curry, and a selection of tandoori chicken. Though the naan wasn't part of the buffet lineup, it was served fresh to my table—a slight wait, but worth it.

While the tandoori chicken was a tad on the dry side, the rest of the food was quite delectable. The staff were both helpful and accommodating throughout my visit.

Although one might consider the price a bit steep, it felt suitable for the area, and the quality of the food justified the cost. My experience was overall quite positive, and I would not only recommend this place but also look forward to returning soon.

Title: A Solid Vietnamese Staple in Chinatown

Tucked away in the bustling streets of NYC's Chinatown, this Vietnamese restaurant might seem like your typical neighborhood haunt. It mirrors the menus, décor, and service of its local counterparts and yet, draws a crowd during peak hours with its budget-friendly, hearty offerings.

On my last visit, a plate of spring rolls surpassed expectations. Unlike many places where the heat has long dissipated before arriving at your table, these rolls were served piping hot and exceptionally crispy - a delightful deviation from the norm.

The star of the meal, however, was the 16a - Hu Tieu My Tho. A first for me, the dish's rich and flavorful broth was brimming with a harmonious mix of shrimp, pork, and quaint quail eggs, despite a tad too much sodium. This bowl stood out as a testament to the restaurant's ability to deliver well-executed traditional dishes.

Service was efficiently brisk, aligning with expectations for such an establishment. While it may not be a culinary revelation, the surprising quality of the spring rolls and the Hu Tieu My Tho noodle bowl certainly left an impression, elevating this spot above the common fray.

**Spice Symphony: A Haven for Indian-Chinese Cravings**

If Indian-style Chinese cuisine is what you're after, Spice Symphony is the spot to beat. I headed there recently to satisfy my urge for Chicken Manchurian—pro-tip: it's not listed, but you can order it anyway. It was my inaugural visit to this location, as I usually frequent the Murray Hill establishment.

Choosing an off-peak Saturday time paid off, as the place was nearly empty, perfect for dining with a baby. The ambiance was pleasant, with a large, spacious, and well-lit interior. However, the experience was slightly marred by the overly attentive manager (or owner), whose constant chit-chat and jokes felt a bit intrusive, perhaps a distraction from the somewhat delayed service.

Despite the wait, they graciously applied a 20% off coupon at checkout, which softened the blow. As expected, the food maintained its high standards—particularly the Gobi appetizer, which was a hit.

In summary, Spice Symphony continues to deliver on flavor but could benefit from a less imposing approach to customer interaction.

I don't mean to imply the place is average-- the pizza is pretty decent, service is quick enough, and yes, if you love a grandma slice, you'll probably enjoy this one.But we all know the pizza scene here is more than just competitive. It's tough as hell. Village Square Pizza holds its own as a neighborhood joint, but it's not yet at the level to compete with the best.

Salty salad- Salty bread -(There was 8 of us at the table) I felt like I was eating food dipped in the ocean. The others at the table agreed and even asked to replace the bread dish with new unsalted rolls. The lunches came out in a sloppy manner. The food (pre-cut RAW hanger Steak) was not placed in the fan like decoration for all the plates. There was nothing else on the plate, just meat. Fries came on the side. I had to get my steak cooked again.  I do like my meat rare-- but in this case, it was so raw, I couldn't chew it. Later I had tea which was nice and came with real tea leaves. However, I was given a desert and a fruit dish that didn't look very nice. Again, not prepared nicely just dropped on the plate. We thought this was for the table -- but later found out it was some else"s fruit platter. Hey, they put it in front of us.

Title: A Hearty Aussie Fare at Ruby's

I stumbled upon Ruby's charm at a Soho pop-up, enticed by their well-received catering service. Driven by curiosity and an impressive first taste, my family and I ventured to their restaurant for a more extensive experience.

Ruby's menu, purportedly Aussie-influenced, is an adventure in itself. While I can't vouch for its authenticity, the delectable flavors speak volumes. We kicked off our culinary journey with the Green Pesto Rice, which, despite its freshness, fell short of expectations next to the other savory stars of the evening.

The Spicy Italian Sausage with rigatoni took our palates to a delightful high until the Shrimp Pasta came along. The latter, customized to accommodate my vegetarian mother, was a sensational hit – the shrimp (served on the side) brimming with juiciness and zest.

The highlight for me was the Bronte burger, a well-crafted stack that provided the necessary warmth and satiation. Complementing it were the sides – sumptuous sweet potato fries and the addictive signature fries with Ruby's famed truffle aioli, a unanimous favorite that kept us reaching for more.

Ruby's offers a tantalizing glimpse into Aussie cuisine, and with each dish outperforming the last, I am already planning my next visit, eager to dive into their breakfast offerings.

If you're planning a night out on the town, consider starting or wrapping up your festivities at this vibrant spot that greets you with bouncers at the door, hinting at its popularity. As you step inside, you'll be charmed by the whimsical decor, featuring cute lights and colorful bottle caps adorning the ceiling. The layout with large round tables fosters a communal and social vibe, making it an ideal choice for groups of 3-4 people.

One of the highlights here is the watermelon soju, a refreshing concoction that's gained somewhat of a cult following; you'll notice it's the drink of choice on almost every table. As for the menu, it's an adventure for your taste buds, with every dish bursting with flavor. A notable surprise is their unique take on fries, served with tomatoes, adding a fresh twist to a classic snack.

Be prepared for a lively atmosphere, as the place tends to get quite loud, a testament to its constant crowd. One thing to note before you plan your visit: the restaurant operates on a cash, American Express, or Mastercard basis, so leave your Visa cards at home.

Really liked the food here. Would definitely come back. The front of the restaurant is filled with smaller booths and group seating is in the back. Clean and modern decor.  The lamb chops were super tender and basically fell off the bone. The sauces (green cilantro and green spicy) added a nice zest. My only complaint is the vermicelli in the rice. The knafeh was a little different from what I've had before and could have been more toasted but was still good. Probably would skip it next time though. Come here for the entrees tho! Very tasty and filling

A bustling vegetarian kosher asian eatery right in the heart of chinatown. Enough seating available for  larger parties as well. I was with a friend catching up, we were seated right away. They bring a hot pot of tea to the table to sip on throughout your meal and while sorting through the lengthy menu options. All "meats" on the menu are made from soy or wheat protein, that includes chicken, duck and everything else in between. We started with the pan friend dumplings which where veggie and pretty solid but not spectacular. Next we had the general tso vegetarian chicken and the triple mushroom pan fried noodles. The general tso was good, the soy protein was tender enough to get the chicken like texture but there was a lot of breading! I guess you need that in supplement of the meat? My favorite was the pan fried noodles! I would come back just for that with some hot tea. The noodles are crispy yet soften from the sauce of the hot mushrooms which sit on top. True to the name there are three different kinds of mushrooms sautéed in a brown gravy. Service here is very good! They are super attentive and quick. We barley waited at all for the food. My friend who is a relaxed vegan loved it! Great place for those trying to meet somewhere in between.

Title: Delightful Second Visit Reveals True Gems

I'm thrilled to report that my second visit to this charming dessert spot solidified its spot on my go-to list. The first time around, the long queue deterred me from trying the gelato as I was pressed for time before a show. Opting for one of their pastries instead, I enjoyed a delightful teaser to what this place could offer. Today, with a much shorter line, I delved into their gelato and it was a revelation – creamy, rich, and utterly satisfying. But the real star of the show was their raspberry macaroon; it burst with such an unexpected intensity of flavor, it took me by sweet surprise. Given its proximity to Broadway, this eatery is not only a treat for the taste buds but also a convenient indulgence for theatre-goers. Count on seeing me back here soon!

Title: A Gem for Rice Noodle Lovers

If you're hunting for the smoothest rice noodles, your search might just end at this unassuming hole-in-the-wall spot I stumbled upon on my daily commute. Though its exterior is easy to miss, the queue inside hints at the culinary delights that await.

Specializing in rice noodles, this place serves up a variety of them, alongside delectable curry fish balls and a comforting cup of soy milk. I've sampled my fair share of noodle spots across Chinatown and Brooklyn, and this establishment easily ranks among the best.

One caveat: the prices here are steeper compared to other local options, including carts, bakeries, and restaurants, and the portions could be more generous. Hence, I've docked one star from a perfect score.

Despite this, the noodle quality is worth the extra bucks and time. For a dollar, you can also grab a small cup of their fairly good soy milk - a perfect complement to your meal. A spot I'd recommend, especially if you're not in a rush and your budget can stretch a bit further for quality.

I was hungry and cold, could not find any place opened past 2am. Luckily Veselka was open and I decided to order beef stroganoff from this place. I am glad I made that decision! The only Ukrainian food I know/love is stroganoff and this place is good at making it! The creamy texture and tenderness of meat was just perfect. The coleslaw they provide as a side is delicious and I could tell it was home made! I will def pay a visit to place when I have chance to visit the area again in the future!

After a previous visit that left me less than satisfied, I feel compelled to update my review to 5 stars. The incident regarding an unsatisfactory steak experience lingered on my mind, urging me to return to the restaurant right when it opened at 5pm. Upon my return, I had the pleasure of speaking with the manager, Jeffery Horn, who turned the situation around and truly saved the day with his outstanding service. His intervention reminded me of the exceptional qualities of this establishment: the service is attentive, the decor is inviting, and the food, when issues are resolved, is top-notch. My advice to fellow diners is to be proactive—pack your own essentials or double-check your takeout orders before leaving. With that said, the overall dining experience here is truly remarkable.

I'm absolutely thrilled to share my experience with the ginger beef bone broth I had on a brisk 48-degree day. The warmth and depth of flavor completely bowled me over—pure, sumptuous bliss in a bowl. The broth itself was velvety smooth, and the ginger left a delightful zingy aftertaste that elevated the entire experience. It's the finesse in the details, like that ginger zing, that truly sets a Brodo broth apart. Highly recommend!

I order the same salad from this place and I love it! It's the kale salad and I add chicken or grilled shrimp. The salad is huge and very filling could probably be two meals for some people. I've also ordered a side of plantains before decent. The only thing that turns me off about this spot is the hostess. She isn't the friendliest, she isn't rude but there is just something about her that makes me feel uncomfortable each time I pick up my food.

Title: A Pleasant Surprise Despite the Price Tag

Entering the restaurant with a mix of caution and curiosity, I found myself pleasantly surprised by the end of my dining experience. Admittedly, the restaurant walks a fine line with its Americanized twist on dishes, which can be off-putting for purists, but in this instance, it added to the charm.

Starting with the appetizers, the dry rub chicken wings were the highlight of the evening. The balance of sweet, spicy, and sour notes in the seasoning was intriguing and worked surprisingly well, tied together by a delightful accompanying sauce. An accidental order of saucy chicken wings, given complimentary, leaned into spicier territory, but lacked the unique appeal of the dry rub.

The Graffiti sliders, featuring pork belly, had potential but were undermined by meat that was tougher than desired. As for the Xiao Long Bao, they were a flavorful accomplishment, although the broken skins upon arrival were a letdown.

Moving on to the mains, the Wok lobster pasta, requested al dente, hit the mark with its cream sauce. Yet, the stinginess of the lobster serving felt disproportionate to its $34 price point. The beef flank steak, paired with beautifully cooked cauliflower, was tender though slightly overdone for our preference.

While I thoroughly enjoyed the flavors encountered at this restaurant, I cannot ignore the price-to-portion disparity. It is worth noting that the Seated cashback made the dining experience more palatable. Without it, I might be more hesitant to return. Overall, the food is certainly good, but the value for money is something to consider before visiting.

Decided to give this place a shot, I been seeing it around Instagram. I must say the food was truly spectacular. We had a reservation set for 7pm, and it seemed busy from the outside , but they had our table reserved. We did the Mazze Trio which includes and 3 Appetizers or small bites you would say . Went with Hummus , Babaganoush and Falafel. Only thing I found a bit strange was that it only came with a single pita. Two out the 3 appetizers were like dips and a split pita didn't cut it . But they brought another one right away when I asked for it. We got a bit full from it and decided to order just a single entree as it seems like a huge portion . The Chicken Shawarma was delicious and good size portion. Ended out meal with a chocolate mouse cake and coconut dessert . Overall I truly recommended this spot !! Ambiance- 10/10Service - 10/10Reservation- Yes Happy Hour - Yes Parking - Good Luck WiFi - Not Sure

You can never get enough of Xian Famous Foods! Decided to stop by here before seeing a movie. I ordered the lamb dumplings and my friend ordered the spicy cumin noodles with lamb. We decided to get mild because the spicy would have been too much. Delicious!

Nestled in the Lower East Side, this vibrant Filipino restaurant is an absolute brunch gem. The Pineapple Tocino Liempo, Bangsilog, and Beef Tapsilog were divine, each dish accompanied by a beautifully cooked egg complementing the well-seasoned, delectable meats. Do not miss out on the Pinsit Frito and Silvanas for a true taste of Filipino indulgence. Their cocktail list and selection of teas are worth exploring too. The whimsically nostalgic soundtrack adds a touch of humor to the already delightful atmosphere. Highly recommended for an impeccable brunch experience!

Absolutely ADORE this place.The food is always on point and the people are always efficient and friendly. I love that they have self service screens that's super intuitive and easy to use. The line can look long but moves super fast. You can't go wrong with any of the items on the menu. Be sure to get the spicy green sauce! It's like Cuban/Peruvian green sauce but a little bit creamier. With the bowls you have the option to get white rice, brown rice, or shredded cabbage or a MIX (game changer I tell you). And don't miss out on the fries. Be warned, the portion is HUGE. Be sure to try the Vietnamese coffee! It is slightly pricy at $4.95 but worth every penny. (Especially when you compare it to Blue Stone Lane or Gregory's right next door). Get more condensed milk if you like it sweeter! You also have the option to adjust the ice level :)

Title: Quick Bites at Kazunori: A Handroll Haven with a Side of Haste

Upon my recent visit to Kazunori, the bustling popularity of this joint was unmistakable. No reservations, just a queue that's a testament to its acclaim—but fret not, it's a swift wait. Be aware, the Kazunori handroll departs from your traditional maki with a few twists.

The rice takes the limelight, flawlessly warm and seasoned to impress. It juxtaposes the seaweed—a crisp at first bite that demands immediate consumption lest you wish to wrestle with chewiness. A word of caution: dialogue lovers may find the 'eat-at-once' ethos limiting for leisurely chat.

Simplicity rules the seafood—think pasty textures for toro, yellowtail, and salmon, all savory, yet shadowed by the dominating chill that contrasts with the rice's comforting warmth. The mayo-laden scallops, crab, and lobster, although palatable, tend to lose their identity in a saucy sea.

In summation, Kazunori is your go-to for a speedy, tasty foray into unconventional handrolls. For an optimal experience, I'd suggest bypassing the mayo-mingled options in favor of the straightforward fish selections.

I recently dined at a local Mexican eatery where the Adobada taco was an absolute standout and an essential try for any visitor. Curiosity led us to try the Nopal taco, and while eating cactus was a novel experience, it was merely passable in taste. Be warned, both tacos presented a bit of a challenge to eat tidily, so come prepared for a hands-on meal.

The drink selection was diverse and enjoyable, though my aunt didn't share the same enthusiasm. One of the perks of our visit was the short waiting time coupled with the entertaining view of the chefs artfully preparing our dishes. A vibrant spot for those looking to explore traditional flavors with a front-row seat to the culinary action!

Upon visiting this hidden gem, one immediately realizes that Turkish cuisine is a culinary art mastered at this establishment. Nestled in the bustling city of New York, it stands out as a paragon of Turkish gastronomy, serving an exquisite selection of dishes that tantalize the taste buds with their exceptional flavors and preparation.

The ambiance of the restaurant is as delightful as its menu, offering a friendly, serene, and unexpectedly refined dining experience. Each bite brings a sense of joy and satisfaction, a testament to the culinary prowess on display. Truly, this is a Turkish delight not to be missed by connoisseurs and casual diners alike.

Title: Cozy Vibes and Delightful Bites at Local Gem

Last Friday, my party of four was swiftly seated upon our late reservation at this charming, casual establishment. The vibe was immediately welcoming, with a devoted atmosphere that set the stage for a wonderful dining experience.

Our culinary journey commenced with veal and pork meatballs, which were a resounding success. They arrived bathed in a savory sauce, perfect for dipping the accompanying bread slices. The meatballs themselves were moist and packed with flavor—definitely a crowd-pleaser.

I indulged in a tricolor salad from the specials, a refreshing dish with a satisfying crunch and an added touch of indulgence in the form of a toasty parmesan crisp. Another member of our group customized a farro salad with grilled chicken, and it too garnered high praise for taste and freshness.

We also shared two pizzas—the signature burrata pizza and a cherry tomato variant. Each was delectable in its own right, the burrata pizza earning its accolades with every bite. Not to be overshadowed were the garlic knot chicken parm sliders, which were the epitome of moist and flavorful in a perfectly portioned package.

From beginning to end, our dinner was nothing short of thoroughly enjoyable. This casual spot has won us over, and we're already planning our next visit. Highly recommend for anyone seeking great food in a relaxed setting.

This was such an amazing surprise to be able to come here at around 5:45 and not have to wait to sit. It is a small restaurant but there are many seats/tables close to each other .  We sat at the bar which is always fun since you get to see all the excitement. Now into the food! All was so amazing. We decided to do the $55 tasting menu (in the picture attached). Everything had so much flavor and was so delicious but I think my favorite was the (Toro Ssam Nap) it is a Tuna dish which is bursting with flavor . The So Ramyun was also so amazing. I have never had noodles  and broth this full of flavor. I was caught off guard when I first tasted it but loved it after the first bite. I highly recommend the tasting menu because you get all the amazing dishes  - all of which I would get again. The only part I could do without was the dessert. This is not saying it wasn't good, its just hard to have anything after the delicious Ramyum.  The choices were lemon sorbet which was very sweet and tart or chocolate ice cream which was so creamy. The service was so great. They constantly kept our water glasses filled and also put a caraf of water on our table incase they weren't around to fill it up. They also kept clearing our space and cleaning it between each part of the meal. To top it all off, the bathroom smelled nice and was very clean!

I'm awarding this establishment a full 5 stars, primarily thanks to their exceptional BEC sandwich. Service efficiency is noteworthy; with real-time wait updates available on Yelp, we were seated immediately. The kitchen maintained promptness in delivering our orders. Admittedly, the ricotta scrabble and truffle hash browns left me indifferent. However, the tequila-based drink was notably potent and enjoyable for those who appreciate a strong cocktail. The undeniable highlight was the BEC sandwich – an absolute delight that had me savoring every last crumb. Though I opted for a bacon-free version, I can only imagine the additional flavor the bacon would contribute for those who prefer their sandwiches with meat.

I eagerly reserved a table at Chef Lee's new spot as soon as it opened on November 25, 2019, having missed the chance to experience his earlier pop-up. My group and I sampled a variety of dishes, starting with the Honey Butter Tater Tots which were elevated by an unexpected but delightful blend of labneh and seaweed seasoning.

The Shin Ramyun Chicken Wings had a subtle noodle-inspired twist I didn't quite catch, but nonetheless were irresistibly crispy with a harmonious mix of gochujang glaze and buttermilk. Diving into the Wok Fried Jjajang Clams was like a nostalgic trip through my Chinese American childhood, with its cozy black bean sauce and succulently cooked clams.

Despite initially missing out on the Dry Aged Double Cheeseburger due to its limited serving time (5-7pm), Chef Lee personally ensured we got a taste, and it did not disappoint with its rich flavors and impeccable sauce. The 53rd and 6th Beef Rib Ssam was delightfully tender, though I could have done without the shiso and felt the portion size didn't quite justify the price.

Chef Lee's table visits made the experience feel personal and authentic, and even without a liquor license, the cuisine was top-notch. Once they pair these offerings with some fine spirits, it's sure to be an unbeatable combination.

Last evening, my partner and I decided to indulge our carnivorous cravings at American Cut Steakhouse, conveniently located just across the street from my evening class. Capitalizing on a double bonus points offer, I effortlessly secured a 6:30 reservation through the Open Table app.

Upon arrival, we were promptly seated, joining the lively energy emulated by a group of happy hour enthusiasts. The ambiance struck a perfect balance between dimly lit sophistication and a vibrant social scene.

Our server was exceptionally attentive, providing expert drink recommendations that perfectly complemented our meal choices. I opted for the NY Strip steak accompanied by bacon-roasted Brussels sprouts—a dish so mouth-wateringly exquisite that it left me playfully envious of my oblivious neighbor for not having sung its praises sooner. My companion savored a perfectly prepared filet mignon with a side of creamy mashed potatoes, a combination that left her both satiated and pleasantly tipsy.

All in all, our visit to American Cut Steakhouse was a resounding success. The food, atmosphere, and service left us thoroughly impressed and eager to return.

Title: A Big Apple Win for Au Cheval

As a dedicated fan of Au Cheval's legendary burgers from their West Loop location in Chicago, I was ecstatic to find they've graced New York with their presence. No more grueling three-hour waits for me; Au Cheval New York's larger space and the ability to snag a reservation through Resy is a game-changer.

The New York outpost captures the essence of the original, delivering the same mouthwatering burger bliss I remember. Don't be fooled by the ‘single’ cheeseburger; it's a hearty double-stack that demands your attention. To do it justice, top it with a perfectly cooked egg and their signature thick-cut, smoky-sweet bacon - this combo elevates the burger to a culinary masterpiece.

While the allure of the full menu might tempt you, I'd steer clear from the more forgettable dishes like the yellowfin tuna salad. Instead, go all in on the fries to complement your burger feast. Trust me, for a taste of burger nirvana, Au Cheval is the pilgrimage every New Yorker—and visitor—should make.

Title: A Fiery Experience at Fort Washington Public House

After a morning at Columbia University Medical Center, I ventured across the street to the Fort Washington Public House, lured in by promising Yelp reviews and the temptation of a lobster roll. The interior greeted me with the charm of an old-school Irish pub, replete with inviting wood paneling.

To my disappointment, the lobster roll was absent from the menu, perhaps a seasonal lapse. Nonetheless, our server Joanna's guidance led us to the Fiery Burger and French Dip. The burger was a revelation, perfectly cooked with a balance of spices that left an unforgettable impression. It alone warranted a five-star rating.

On the opposite end of the spectrum sat the French Dip, a lackluster dish that suffered from dryness and a baffling absence of flavor. It was an unanticipated letdown in an otherwise pleasing meal.

In summary, Fort Washington Public House serves up a dichotomy of dishes. While the ambience fits the quintessential Manhattan Irish pub mold, the Fiery Burger stands out as a must-try. Steer clear of the French Dip, though, and your palate will thank you.

Recommended: Fiery Burger. Avoid: French Dip. A mixed bag, but the burger is not to be missed.

Having been a patron since its days as Avenida, I can vouch for the consistently great food served at the now-rechristened East Point. It remains a beloved neighborhood gem. My only gripe? The music volume has seen a notable uptick post-rebrand, which can overpower conversation at times. Nonetheless, it continues to be a favorite spot of mine.

I cana understand why some people think Korean Fried Chicken is expensive, or too spicy (if you get the spicy version), but it's actually amazing.This is the fried chicken place - Korean style - which I first discovered when I was in Queens, and first ate at. I like it although it has nothing on my favorite one which is in Houston called Lim's, which is now called Ramen Okidoki but still serves Lim's. Lim's, the same brand from Korea, which is arguably the one that invented it all.Nevertheless Pelicana is a really good option if you want some Korean Fried Chicken in Manhattan. The employees are nicer than the ones in Queens.

Popped in here while in the area. We tried the grandma slice, bianco, margarita and sophia loren. Grandma slice was my favorite. We got the pizza to go and ate it more than half hour after purchasing so it wasnt as hot and fresh. The slices still were very tasty and filling. The triangle slices are huge! Also try the garlic knots!!

Title: A Gem Worth the Buzz

I recently dined at a highly recommended spot and was delighted by the experience. From the moment we entered, the warmth of the owner was palpable, though his unique name escaped me. Service was exceptional thanks to Winny, our server, who expertly guided us through the menu.

We began with appetizers - the wonton soup and fried wontons were enjoyable, but the standout was my friend's seafood Tom Yum soup, teeming with fresh seafood and robust in flavor; a choice I envied.

For the main course, Winny's recommendation was spot on. I indulged in a dish referred to simply as '#1 flat noodle' - its portion generous enough to be a main entree. The noodles were perfectly complemented by fresh scallions, bean sprouts, and a savory brown sauce with just the right level of heat.

This bustling establishment is one I wish we had back in North Miami. With its attentive service and remarkable flavors, it's clear why this place is so popular. Unquestionably, a dining experience that cannot be missed.

Tucked away in the bustling heart of Midtown, this trendy spot proved its popularity with a packed house on a Tuesday night. By 9 pm, the bar was brimming with patrons, yet the welcoming hostess accommodated us with a table in the lively back room, bustling with diners.

Opting for seasonal sips, I indulged in the Fabled Leaves cocktail, a delightful blend with a hint of pumpkin purée and cinnamon - a perfect fall concoction, albeit potent for lightweights. My companion's Bird Cage was equally a hit. Service was top-notch, with not a moment of thirsty neglect, as our water glasses remained perpetually full.

The ambiance was comfortably casual with an energetic buzz, and although the noise levels were on the higher side, conversation was still manageable. Clean, single-use bathrooms offered a classic touch.

Overall, this place left a memorable impression. Whether it's for a round of expertly crafted drinks at the Blushing Bar or to explore their culinary offerings, a return visit is definitely in the cards.

Anytime anyone asks me to take them to REAL NY PIZZA, I bring them here. Pizza is always fresh and I'll miss the hell out of this place when I leave nyc. Thank you for being consistent, delicious, and classic!

Rolled into town at a later hour and needed a filling snack before bed. Lions & Tigers & Squares is open until 4 am. Score!Walked on over and found this tiny pizza counter (they have 4 high tops to stand at if you want to eat there).Detroit Style Pizza? This was a new one for me. Reminds me of a combo of a pan & Deep dish pizza. Rectangular, with a very thick crust and very crispy on bottom. They had a variety of flavors, but we went with basic pepperoni. Its pre-made, but they warm it up in the oven. The pizza was hot, very greasy, but they DO NOT skimp on the pepperoni.  The secret to me is a good quality mozzarella, quality pepperoni and a good sauce. This hit all 3 marks. Plus, they put extra sauce on top.So glad I got to try this; a first for me.

Located where cutting board use to be located. Read there was a soft opening and it's basically hot pot style soup noodles so had to come and try it out.Generally the dishes are $9.99 for soup base with noodles and meat. For a little extra, more meat can be added (which I definitely recommend). There were some appetizers available during the soft opening as well.We started out with salt and pepper chicken as the appetizer. It was $6.45 (definitely more costly than other places), I got the herbal soup base with lamb meat and extra lamb ($2.99). My partner got the spicy soup with lamb and extra lamb. The chicken came out first, it's essentially popcorn chicken with a small plate of sauce. The redeeming factor was that the chicken was both incredibly juicy and meaty. They're unlike other places where there's so much better that you're eating more skin than meat. These chicken were definitely meaty, and made me feel better about the price.The noodles came out next. They present your sides/meat/noodles first on a plate. You'd think it's a great deal at $9.99 but bare in mind there's about 2-4 slices of whatever meat you're ordering, making the extra meat essential to get a hearty meal and pushing the actual price of it to $14 or so. Noodles came out in a mini cauldron with our soup base and extra meat. You then proceed to pour all (or as much as you want) of the sides in. My soup was the herbal soup, which is a bit bland: I expected it to taste like hot pot soup, but I added some soy sauce and there's some flavor. They give you plenty of noodles and for $1 extra, you can have unlimited noodles.Noodles were chewy and the lamb was decent. Id definitely like to try other options they have once it opens but for now this place is more gimmicky than good food.For now, I'd say you should just give the extra $10And go to a ayce hot pot and get noodles there

Title: A Brunch Delight Despite Reservation Snafu

I visited this gem a few months back for brunch, and though there was initially a hiccup with our reservation, the accommodating setup at the bar meant all four of us could still enjoy a face-to-face meal. The service was noteworthy; the wait staff was amiable and proficient at keeping our glasses brimful with bottomless mimosas.

As for the food, it was nothing short of delightful. The Chili Cheese Toast offered a zesty kick to start the day, while the Wild Mushroom & Truffle Khichdi was a luxurious dance of flavors that I highly recommend. Quality fare coupled with reasonable prices and the perk of unlimited mimosas left us all thoroughly gratified. Definitely, a brunch spot worth revisiting!

Title: A Disappointing Lunch Experience

My recent lunch outing left much to be desired both in service and culinary satisfaction. Upon arrival on a sweltering summer day, clutching a beverage for hydration, I was met with a curt and unwelcoming admonition from an unfriendly waitress about bringing an outside drink. An easy opportunity for a polite reminder was instead a regrettable first impression.

The restaurant was scarcely populated, yet the service did not benefit from the light attendance. A male waiter mirrored the cold demeanor of his colleague, handling his duties with visible reluctance and an air of impatience that only served to amplify our discomfort.

Our meal commenced with five-spice tofu, which, while aesthetically pleasing, was underwhelming in flavor. The tofu's freshness could not compensate for the uninspiring presentation. The seafood pancakes, regrettably, fared worse—an oily disappointment scant with low-quality imitation seafood.

The solitary redeeming feature was the meatball soup, boasting a flavorful base and satisfactory texture to the noodles, though it fell short of memorable or recommendable.

On a side note, the restroom facilities were commendably clean, and the restaurant's interior did present a visually appealing ambiance. Nonetheless, the lackluster service paired with predominantly mediocre dishes means that I am unlikely to return or suggest this establishment to others.

I've been to a handful of AYCE restaurants, but never have I been to one that was both All-you-can-eat and All-you-can-drink. The food was all quite good and it was quite fun to order through the iPad. As it got later into the night, the atmosphere changed and got even more fun as the lights dimmed and the music got louder.  The staff brought out glowsticks and other light-up accessories and it began to feel like a small rave. At one point, half the restaurant was doing sake bombs together. Definitely great vibes. The only small complaint I would have is that we were very rushed to leave, even before we got to our 2 hour limit.

Yum yum yum! It was my first time trying to place. I went after work with a friend. We had a 20 minute wait and was able to grab a drink at the bar while we waited. The bartender was super super sweet and greeted us with a great smile :) We were then called to be seated. We sat and ordered our food. We were soo hungry. The food came out in a nice pace. It was perfect. As we left I say around 7:30 it was super crowded in the front. So I would say try to get there by 7 to not have a long wait or overcrowded while you wait.

What a great find. I was in the mood for pork and something cheap when I found this little gem. It's a bit in the middle of nowhere, but also is a place easy to pass through when walking from east NY to west NY.The shop itself is definitely a grab and go, very casual. The service was great, I had a lovely conversation with the person behind the counter.Ok- the good part, food! I got the scallion pancake, the vegan dumplings and the pulled pork bao.Let me put it this way, BAO= WOW! The pork is so tender and flavorful and is a bit different than other pork bao's I've experienced. It truly stood out to me. (I believe it was $5)The vegan dumplings were unique, but I love that they offer a vegan option for those specific diners. It had a lot going on for me but I would still eat it again. If you are a meat eater though, probably stick to the original dumpling. The scallion pancake was also different then what I'm use to, it was thicker but so good and flavorful. You know what it reminded me of? A potato pancake. It was absolutely delicious.But of course the very best part of everything was their house made hot chili oil!  I think I'll take the trip over here literally just to have some more of their hot oil. My meal totaled at $13.00- I thought it was a great deal and I left happy and full. 4.7/5

Title: A Delightful Lunch Experience Near Lincoln Center

My dining companion and I stopped in for lunch before catching a show at Lincoln Center and we were pleasantly surprised by the culinary experience. We both indulged in the Salmon main course which was nothing short of perfection—moist on the inside, with a superbly crispy skin. The dish was artfully arranged with a delectable sauce and a fresh salad to accompany it.

We couldn't resist ending our meal with the chocolate mousse for dessert. The sweet and rich flavors were expertly balanced with a hint of salt and lemon olive oil, creating a memorable finish to our meal.

The experience was undoubtedly good, and despite the slightly steep prices, the quality justifies the cost. Those with a hearty appetite might find the portions modest, but it was perfectly satisfying for a moderate hunger. I would readily return for another meal.

Title: A Flavorful Surprise Near Rockefeller Center

I had the pleasure of trying a new cuisine on the recommendation of a local and was pleasantly surprised. Despite not being a pork aficionado, I decided to indulge in the pork loin lunch, and it did not disappoint. The meat was tender, encased in a perfectly fried batter, and the combination of sesame seeds and sauce created an intriguing and delightful taste profile—not too spicy, just wonderfully pleasant.

The miso soup served alongside was comforting, and the cabbage salad, accentuated by the tableside dressing, was a fresh complement to the meal. Despite the bustling Wednesday afternoon crowd, we snagged a table for four and enjoyed prompt service without feeling rushed, even as the lunchtime rush wound down.

Situated within walking distance from the bustling Rockefeller Center, this restaurant is a cozy haven ideal for a satisfying lunch on a cold, snowy day. If you're in midtown and craving some pork loin or just an overall enjoyable lunch, this spot is definitely worth a visit.

I've visited Num Pang on several occasions and have generally found it to be a satisfactory option for those in search of a healthier take on Asian cuisine, with a Cambodian twist that recalls Vietnamese flavors. On my latest visit, I decided to try the coconut shrimp, which unfortunately fell short of expectations. The dish comprised only four shrimp that were disappointingly reminiscent of something easily whipped up at home, lacking any special touch.

However, not all was lost, as the jasmine rice continues to be a highlight, delivering both fluffiness and taste. A sample of the lemongrass short rib from my mom's plate showed promise; it was quite decent, though a more pronounced lemongrass flavor would have been appreciated.

Num Pang offers a range of options beyond rice bowls, including salads and their can't-miss sandwiches. While there was a miss this time with the shrimp, the experience suggests that some dishes do stand out more than others.

Title: A Hidden Lunchtime Gem

I recently visited this dining spot for an early business meeting and was immediately struck by the spaciousness of both its dining and bar areas. With its Italian Mediterranean aesthetic and a cafeteria-style layout, the place exuded a comfortable yet sophisticated ambience.
