Opting for a seat by the window, we enjoyed watching passersby, lending a delightful backdrop to our sensitive discussions. Though my experience with the menu was limited to just a small bite accompanied by coffee, what I tasted piqued my curiosity for more.

Remarkably, within half an hour, the previously empty restaurant transformed into a bustling hub of activity, with every table occupied by eager lunch-goers. This rapid shift speaks volumes about the restaurant's popularity among locals.

While my visit was brief, the combination of the pleasant atmosphere and the promise of good food has me looking forward to my next lunch here, where I plan to fully dive into their culinary offerings.

My daughter who's 16 choose this restaurant after seeing pics in Pinterest. I'm so glad she did! The food was outstanding! And the restaurant was so cozy and the service was warm, efficient and professional. She got the truffled ricotta ravioli and I got the octopus. Since it was late and I try to watch my carb intake I thought this was the best choice. I couldn't believe all the yummy ingredients in my octopus and how well they went together. I'm very picky about my octo but this one is by far, the best I've ever had!

Title: A Xiao Long Bao Gem in NYC

I've discovered a culinary treasure in NYC that stands out for its exceptional xiao long bao (XLB). Many establishments in the city offer decent XLB, but they often fall short with overly thick skins and an odd texture. However, this place sets the standard for how it's done - the dumplings here have delicately thin skins and a texture that's simply perfect.

Let's not overlook the beef noodle soup, which deserves high praise. It's a bowl of warmth and heartiness that manages to taste incredibly clean and comforting. In a city overflowing with dining options, making a decision to return to the same place says a lot. I would eagerly come back to this spot. It's rare to make such a commitment in NYC, but this restaurant has undoubtedly secured its place at the top of my list.

Title: A Mixed Bag at Brunch – Stellar Service Overshadowed by Management Missteps

Rating: ⭐⭐⭐

I recently visited a local brunch spot hoping for a quick and delightful dining experience, but what I encountered was a tale of two stories. While the service and food deserved applause, the management's handling of wait times soured the beginning of our meal.

Upon arrival, having been quoted a mere 10-15 minute wait over the phone, my party and I were met with a daunting line that stretched out the door. We were seated after an hour's wait - a stark contrast to our expectations set by the management. Another group echoed our frustration, having been given the same misleading timeframe as us.

Once seated, the service did a commendable job at turning our frowns upside down. Our server was exceptionally attentive and efficient, ensuring our drinks, appetizers, and main courses were served with admirable speed. We kicked off with the avocado tartare, which set a promising tone for the meal. My green juice and egg white scramble were satisfactory, but, while good, didn't dazzle my palate enough to be memorable.

In conclusion, though the staff's commendable service deserves recognition, the initial management misstep paired with unremarkable food means I'm unlikely to return. There's potential here, but accuracy in wait times and food that truly impresses are necessary to complete the experience.

Ordered a Bench Girl. To be fair, beautifully composed sandwich at first sight (as in the kind of sandwich that looks so good you're excited to dive in). Thankfully, my gut told me to look inside before doing so.I found that the Alheira was completely raw (as my pic shows).Called City Sandwich (during their business hours) four times to inform of the issue, trusting they'd make it right one way or another. Called a total of four times before giving up. Three of those times the phone rang (ten rings every time) with no answer, ending with a fax tone. One time someone did pick up, but the second I heard another phone ring they hung up while I was speaking.So the only practical exposure I have to CS is raw food (which could easily have made me ill) being served, and non-responsive if even available phone customer service. No thanks.

Venturing into Little Spain provides a delightful taste of market-style dining, with its array of specialty food shops offering a variety of flavors. My recent visit entailed a brief 10-minute wait to enter on a bustling Saturday afternoon, just 30 minutes post-opening at 3pm.

I was eager to savor a quick snack and soak in the locale's vibrant atmosphere. Although I secured my modest nibble, it came with a substantial price tag. While the experience was enjoyable, the splurge seems more suited for a one-time tourist indulgence rather than a regular haunt.

Danji is a hole in the wall in Hells Kitchen, where you would never expect a Korean restaurant. The place is primarily made of communal high tops where the menu is hidden in the drawer. I enjoy the concept. Let's talk food. Don't expect Korean BBQ here, it's mostly bibimbap. This place reminds me of Her Name Is Han. It's the same type of simplicity done right. The food is good and so is the service. My only compliant is that the price point is a bit high for the amount of food that you receive. Overall I'll probably be back but not if I was starving that day. It's bougie Korean but in a good way. Note: I came here for lunch only.

Title: A Flavorful Fiesta at a Mexican Gem

Last Thursday evening, my group of eight was promptly seated at a bustling Mexican restaurant, which struck us immediately with its impressive array of over 20 margarita and mojito flavors. The freshly made guacamole, spiced to our liking right at our table, was a delightful start to our meal.

Not only was the service friendly, but also impressively efficient. As we dined, a trio of musicians added to the vibrant atmosphere, serenading diners with traditional melodies, though we skipped the dancing floor for a more relaxed experience.

The menu's variety did not disappoint, with my choice of pecan-crusted salmon standing out as an unexpectedly perfect fusion of flavors. We ended our feast with a shared kahlua chocolate mousse topped with fresh fruit that left us wishing for more room to savor every spoonful.

Highly recommend for an authentic taste and experience that tantalizes the senses. This place is a must-visit!

It's difficult to find a restaurant that serves delicious food quickly and at a reasonable price around Grand Central, but this place manages to do all that! I actually stumbled upon this restaurant by accident while looking for another restaurant  I was seated immediately and given the menu and cup of water seconds later. A minute after I placed my order (Thai iced tea with milk and mo shio ramen), my drink came. 5 minutes after, my ramen came. I have never experienced such fast service before! It smelt absolutely delicious. There were a lot of flavors happening in the ramen, but they all worked well with each other. There was the broth, the pork slices, the butter, the corn, the sesame oil/seeds...everything was spot on. Nothing overwhelmed the others! And the Thai iced tea was perfectly balanced too! Usually it's either mostly tea or overly sweet, but this one had a good amount of tea and sweetness to it.If you're in the neighborhood, definitely stop by! You will not be disappointed

I had been wanting to come to 4 Charles Prime Rib for awhile, seeing as it was extremely difficult to get a reservation, and based on its superb Yelp rating, I came here thinking I was in for the best meat of my life. In my experience, 4 Charles Prime Rib has been the hardest restaurant to get reservations at. I stayed up until midnight, not once, but twice to get a dinner reservation here. It books out within minutes. I was glad to get a reservation even at 5pm 30 days out. We came here on a Tuesday evening. I came in first and was seated immediately- even at 5pm, there was already a seated table about to order. The host was very attentive and took care of all my needs. The people working here have high attention to detail, and are very knowledgeable and welcoming. My husband came in shortly after, and we ordered promptly after that. The table next to us (4 young men), highly recommended that we get the French dip sandwich (a menu special), so we settled on that, and the English cut. Our host settled that we'd get the French dip sandwich first, and the English cut and sides afterwards. The sandwich was served quickly after ordering. It consisted of a hero roll, with beef shavings and Swiss cheese, along with something resembling cole slaw, horseradish cream, and au jus. The beef shavings are made from the prior day's leftover prime rib. The beef was fatty and rich, complemented by the au jus, while the sharp tang of the horseradish cream contrasted with the richness of the beef and cheese. The bread was fresh and soft. Overall, it was quite good, but also reminded me of a dressed up Philly cheese steak. The prime rib was a bit of a disappointment. I have had prime rib previously and was a fan. Perhaps my expectations were too high, but the English cut fell sadly short. The cut is mostly rare, and is a thinner cut. Ours got cold quickly, and gave me the sensation of eating a chunk of cold, raw meat, hearkening back to paleolithic times. My husband did not like it at all. The creamed spinach also contained melted cheese, and was one of the heavier renditions of this dish that I've had before. The fries were good, but this is not something you can really go wrong with. During our dinner that evening, we looked around to take note of the other clientele; funnily enough, I was one of five women in the restaurant at that time, I suppose due to the meat heavy nature of the menu. The burger looked delicious when we were there, but as they recently opened Au Cheval, I can't justify staying up until midnight to come back for the burger.

These Thai peeps obviously want us to try their chicken because the word "Gai" means chicken. They're located at the new Essex Market food hall serving Thai street food.From their small menu, we ordered their regular Hainanese Chicken. It came with seasoned rice, cucumber garnish, a hot soup, and three dipping sauces. The hainanese chicken was tender, savory, and cooked just right and served alongside a portion of chicken gizzards (or innards) which my partner wanted no part of. She left all the gizzards for me and/or the trash. The seasoned rice was very tasty with umami flavor and the hot soup was a nice complementary item to the chicken and rice. All of this together with their three delicious dipping sauces. Yum! And for just $8.95.We didn't try the fried chicken this time and I'm having regrets on passing up on the $5 fresh coconut, but I shall return.

Title: Hustle, Flavor, and a Fork-Free Feast at Chick'n Cone

My impromptu visit to Chick'n Cone in the bustling Turnstyle Underground Market near Columbus Circle was a pleasantly unexpected adventure fueled by a free chicken sample's siren call. The guy with the golden hustle at the counter knew exactly how to reel in a passerby like myself – with a friendly demeanor and an in-depth explanation of their mouth-watering menu.

Opting for the chick'n cone and fries meal, including a drink at a reasonable $12, my taste buds were treated to a unique culinary twist: succulent pieces of chicken doused in my choice of Yella BBQ or Kick'n Ranch sauce, all snugly nestled in a not-too-sweet waffle cone. The concept was novel and the execution, flawless; the chicken was authentic in flavor and generously filled the cone to brim.

Although the Cajun-seasoned fries erred on the side of overly salty for my liking, they were still enjoyable. Pairing those with a canned drink, I navigated my meal with a toothpick initially, but soon enough, I was diving in face-first to fully indulge in the experience.

Seating was a non-issue, with common shared tables set up right outside the counter, allowing for a casual and relaxed dining atmosphere. Despite its slightly hidden location, Chick'n Cone is a gem worth seeking out – for its salesmanship, flavorful offerings, and a fun, fork-free foray into fast food.

My brother claims this is the best Dominican spot in Washington Heights. I'll have to say, it did not disappoint. The restaurant is known for their steaks and oxtail soup. Combine it with rice, plantains and beans and your taste buds are in heaven. I highly recommend this place if your nearby. The prices are extremely reasonable as well. $40 for the steak, rice, plantains, beans, oxtail soup, and bread.

Came here with some cousins before a show. We were in a bit of a hurry but the wait staff accommodated us accordingly (even though we didn't have a reservation). The service was great! We ordered the Cacio e Pepe, Chicken Parm, Spaghetti and Meatballs, and Gnocchi. Will definitely be eating here again when I am back in the UWS.

This place rocks!! I'm actually shocked at how good this place is. As a self proclaimed ramen connoisseur, this is one of the best soups you'll have anywhere. Phenomenal mixture of flavors, never crazy crowded (yet), and a great menu. One of the best places I've been to in a while.

Title: Quick Service, Tasty Dumplings Despite the Lunch Rush

I stopped by this bustling eatery during my lunch break, slightly anxious about the crowd and the ticking clock. To my surprise, I was seated immediately, which was the first of many pleasant experiences here. The restaurant was teeming with patrons, yet the service remained impressively swift.

The highlight of my meal was, without a doubt, the pork soup dumplings alongside the shrimp dumplings. While the soup dumplings were on the smaller side, they did not disappoint in flavor. Both varieties were served quickly and were a delightful midday treat.

One caveat for potential diners: there's a $20 minimum for credit card payments, and they only accept Visa or MasterCard. Despite this, the rapid service and delicious offerings more than made up for the minor inconvenience. I'll definitely be back for more!

If you're on the hunt for a delightful bakery that's both unassuming and wallet-friendly, look no further than this Chinatown gem. The fresh churn fun here is a must-try, and it's a steal compared to the overpriced options at Joe's over at Canal St. Market.

We've popped into this bake shop numerous times, always leaving with an armful of their tasty baos and refreshing lai-cha. The hot food section, conveniently situated on the left, is equally impressive. The ham & egg bao is a kid-approved favorite, boasting fluffy eggs and a slice of ham wrapped in a perfectly baked bao.

Next door, indulge in the pre-cooked, then freshly fried "gaow-ji" – savory dumplings packed with pork and vegetables. Don't miss the steamed pearl chicken, a delightful package of glutinous rice and minced pork that always pleases the little ones.

An assortment of treats, including two fried dumplings, two fresh shrimp churn fun, and three Jun Ji Cai, sets me back just about $13. With its cozy atmosphere and grab-and-go convenience, this spot offers a few stools for solo diners craving a quiet moment. It's a commendable and budget-friendly alternative to the city's pricier dim sum offerings. #happyfeasting

Joe's Pizza epitomizes the quintessential New York pizzeria. Simple yet satisfying, this no-frills joint serves up classic slices like pepperoni and white pizza that hit the spot whether you're winding down after a night out or just craving an honest-to-goodness slice. The hype, bolstered by celebrity patrons and even nods from Spider-man, might inflate expectations, but the truth remains: Joe's Pizza delivers on quality. At $4 a slice, some may question its value, but for a taste of authentic NYC pizza, it's certainly worth considering for both locals and visitors alike.

I went here for late lunch  at 2:30 pm on Wednesday. One of my favorite restaurant " Bocherie" has this cozy French bistro as their 3rd Location. They are  located  on  Christpher street, and Most of audience seemed French chic neighbor and stylish people,   feels really Bistoro in Paris atmosphere.My friend order Steak frites and I order Burger.And  I just had  Bocherie burger however I ordered Truffle Kobe Beef Burger.But Bocherie Burger. was not bad. thick juicy beef ( see my picture) and rich cheese,  such a great value! I recommend here  as Ideal Cozy, neighborhood French bistro ! , hidden lunch - drinking spot for escape noise Manhattan.Wanna try Truffle Kobe beef burger next time!!!

Title: Satisfying Cravings with Room for Improvement at K-Town

My dining experience at this K-town locale was satisfactory but not without its pitfalls, reflecting a mixed 3.5-star rating. The prevalent grumble about the pricing seemed on par with other Korean food spots in the area, so no major shocks there, though the debate on value for money lingers on.

We ordered the kimchi chicken twice, opting for the medium spice level which, disappointingly, lacked the fiery kick I hoped for. Next time, I'm inclined to turn up the heat. The ramen, which scored a 7/10, fell short as it was delivered overcooked — a misstep in an otherwise eager service, as it was prepped in the kitchen rather than at our table. 

The fried rice shone brightly in the meal, worthy of a 9/10. Its preparation at the table was a delightful touch, enhancing the dining experience and adding to the dish's fresh, savory notes. Despite some letdowns, this spot remains on my radar for those days when the craving for Korean fare strikes.

I think this is one of the better Pizza places for typically NYC pizza.  The building looks nothing special and then you wonder why there is a line.  Once you try the pizza you realize why there was a line.  The sauce is just right not too sweet and somehow they manage to make the crust so it crunches but is not brittle.  This is near Penn Station which makes it easy for a quick bite on the way to Boston or DC.

Title: A Xiaolongbao Delight with Room for Improvement

I recently visited this spot with friends, eagerly anticipating their famed xiaolongbao (XLB). The pork and seafood soup dumplings lived up to our expectations – they were simply amazing. We also tried the shrimp fried rice, bok choy, beef chow fun, and a chicken dish. The bok choy stood out, perfectly seasoned and full of flavor. The other dishes, while served fresh and hot, were somewhat underwhelming; they lacked the robust flavors we craved and could benefit from a pinch more salt.

The clientele was diverse, which spoke to the restaurant's broad appeal. Nestled in an ideal location, the prices were a tad high for Chinese fare, but for those XLB, I'd argue they're justified. If you're here for the soup dumplings, you're in for a treat. For the rest of the menu, you might want to explore other places.

Title: A Mixed Experience at a Charming Eatery

I recently visited a restaurant that charmed me with its tasteful atmosphere, boasting tables of deep cherry wood and cozy booth seating against a backdrop of cream-colored and blue flower print walls. In a moment of indecision between the seitan piccata and the Blossom burger, the waiter recommended the popular seitan piccata. Unfortunately, the dish, with its pan-seared seitan cutlets in white wine-lemon-caper sauce, truffle mashed potatoes, and sautéed kale, was a letdown – the sauce was too salty and overshadowed the delicate truffle flavor, while the seitan's rubbery texture was off-putting. The staff, however, was accommodating, allowing me to switch to the Blossom burger, which was a relief to the palate. This Beyond patty creation – complemented with caramelized onions, tapioca cheddar, soy bacon, sautéed mushrooms, crisp lettuce, tomato, chipotle aioli, and a side of seasoned fries – was a savory delight, delivering a medley of flavors and textures that were spot-on. The service throughout was attentive and kind, although the culinary miss with the piccata gives me pause on whether I'd revisit. Overall, I left satisfied with the burger and service but uncertain about a return.

Title: Pig & Khao - Hits and Misses

I had high hopes for Pig & Khao given its stellar reputation, but I came away feeling underwhelmed. My dining experience was a mixed bag, with some dishes like the coconut rice and pork belly adobo standing out with flying colors, while others were forgettable.

The much-anticipated fried chicken fell short, lacking the robust seasoning I craved, even when paired with chutney and sambal. Similarly, the sisig and mushroom salad failed to leave a lasting impression, echoing a sentiment of 'meh' throughout the meal.

In its favor, Pig & Khao offers commendable service, which did add a positive touch to the evening. While I believe every restaurant has room to wow, Pig & Khao has yet to find its consistent stride across the menu.

Solid food for the price. I've always loved hand rolls and came here due to many recommendations from friends. Although I didn't have to wait in line, a bit after I arrived the line started to get very long. I got the six roll combo which I feel like a pretty good deal to feel comfortably full after. I didn't think I would, but was surprised. The six roll combo includes toro, salmon, yellowtail, scallops, crab, and lobster. The rice is warm and well seasoned. The nori is nice and crispy. The fish melt in your mouth. One thing though that did confuse me is how the chefs remember who has gotten what when there is one or two chefs serving twenty something people. I ended up getting a repeat, and no lobster on my last trip which I guess doesn't really matter that much. But some people may get finicky about it. It would be helpful for them to let us know when they give us the last one, because often times if you go with friends you lose track of what is happening around you and how much you have eaten. It may not be hard to count up to six but when you're not paying attention it can be pretty easy to lose track. Anyway, I would definitely come back if the line isn't too long. The hand rolls are worth it.

During my recent visit to a local eatery, I discovered a gem in their veggie burger. Remarkably, it harbors a taste reminiscent of actual meat, an impressive feat for a plant-based option. The freshness and flavor profile of the food here stand out, with the egg scramble deserving a special mention. The chefs scramble eggs with a finesse that transforms a simple dish into a delightful experience. If your journey leads you to this restaurant, the veggie burger is a must-try.

Title: A Rooftop Delight with Stellar Service

I recently dined at this charming restaurant and was thoroughly impressed, prompting me to recommend it to all. The ambiance strikes the perfect balance between upscale intimacy on the lower level and a vibrant energy on the rooftop. Opting for the rooftop at an early hour secured us a prime seat, although the space filled up quickly as the evening progressed.

The service was exceptional from the moment we were greeted. Our server, Enver, was outstanding and ensured our experience was memorable—an accolade I've noticed he rightly earns often.

The culinary journey began with the crispy rice with salmon, which was enjoyable despite the salmon needing a hint of salt. The fire dragon roll turned up the heat but was a hit for those who appreciate a spicy kick.

For our main courses, the pan-seared salmon and marrow crusted filet, both requested well done, did not disappoint. The dishes were fresh and flavorful, with the Pinot Grigio pairing beautifully with the salmon. A minor hiccup with dessert availability turned into a delightful surprise as the citrus olive oil cake outshone the originally intended white wine poached pear, leaving an unforgettable taste that lingers.

In summary, my visit was marked by great food, superb service, and a wonderful atmosphere. This restaurant has certainly earned my intent to return.

After an art-filled morning at the Met, hunger led me just a couple of blocks away to a charming cafe reminiscent of a Viennese retreat. Despite the lunchtime rush, I ventured to the downstairs area where the same enticing menu was available. The offerings, while on the pricey side – with desserts like cake at $10.50 and a hearty schnitzel demanding around $30 – provide a selection broad enough to satisfy any craving, from drinks and desserts to full meals.

Deciding to go vegetarian, I opted for a delightful spaetzle, brimming with carrots, peas, and mushrooms. It struck a perfect balance, mimicking the comfort of pot pie innards, yet light enough to avoid the dreaded post-lunch lethargy, thanks to the expertly cooked, non-gummy spaetzle.

The ambiance was as authentic as the food, with German conversations mingling with the clinks of coffee cups, creating an atmosphere that almost transported me to the streets of Vienna. For those in search of a genuine Viennese cafe experience without crossing the Atlantic, this cafe is a slice of Austria tucked away just a stone's throw from the museum's grandeur.

My husband and I are fans of Dim Sum especially for Chang Fen (Rice Roll). We can't wait to try Yin Ji, which is one of the hot topics among friends and family. We came in on a Friday night at about 6:30pm and the wait was about 30+ minutes. Be mindful that Yin Ji, same as other restaurant in Chinatown, is cash only.  We had C5 Lai Wan Style Assorted Congee with extra egg and pork liver, R1 Marinated Beef & Shrimp with chives and R13 Marinated Chicken sliced with chives. The Cantonese congee was authentic that you barely see rice in it and full of fresh ingredients. The pork liver  was tender, juicy and well cooked. Their Chang Fan (Rice Roll) was thin, soft and tasty. We highly recommend to order with extra egg, the mixture of rice roll and egg layer was amazing.

Being a fellow dumpling lover, this place does not disappoint. You can see the dumplings being pan-fried right in front of the restaurant. It's a small intimate place, good for small parties. The staff was attentive and friendly and I really enjoyed my meal.     I got the fried tofu as an appetizer and I was really happy with my choice. The tofu was cooked perfectly, the skin was egg based and the inside was fluffy. The sauce on top tied it all together. The fried dumplings were seared just right and the stuffing was delicious. My favorite was the kimchi dumplings. The first bite was full of flavor and it had a kick of spice I immensely appreciated. I am definitely coming back to try the rest of the dumplings on the menu.

This place has liked my Instagram posts for the past few months so it's been on my list to visit this place.  So it was National Margarita Day yesterday and I saw that this place was selling $8 margaritas the whole evening.  When I saw the place, it turns out that they are open at 6pm because they transition from the morning and afternoon place called "Hole in the Wall" which serves really awesome Nutella Mocha.  Anyways, the staff is really accommodating and knowledgeable.  The place has very cool cozy low key vibe.  The margarita variety were awesome and my server recommended the pomegranate margarita, which was refreshing and tasty.  My friend got the spicy margarita and he liked it.  We also ordered food so our server recommended the avocado and tofu guacamole $9 which was worth every cent because of the portion size and the flavors were incredible.  The sticky pork belly ($14) and side of rice ($3) entree was perfect for two people.  The pork belly was perfectly crispy on the outside and very tender on the inside.  I left the place very satisfied and I definitely want to come back especially when I am craving the guacamole.

Title: Stellar Service at Late Hours

My boyfriend and I popped into the restaurant at 10 pm for drinks and were greeted with an exceptional bar experience, thanks to our bartender Shayna. It was clear the place had her juggling multiple roles, yet she managed to deliver the best customer service I've witnessed in a long time. Patient and attentive despite the apparent workload, Shayna turned our visit into a memorable outing. I highly recommend asking for her by name when you visit — you're in for a treat. Can't wait to return!

I had no idea the old mew mew ramen was replaced with a new place! While the inside set up is exactly the same as the old ramen restaurant, the menu is very different. The prices are definitely a little more than I would expect...but it's the west village. Despite the $18 price tag, I would definitely come back to order the Tan Tan Men again - the miso + right amount of spiciness + sesame paste made this bowl of ramen truly unique. The sesame paste in particular added a distinct nutty flavor that is so uncommon in most ramen. And the kaedama (extra noodles) was only $3, which was perfect for the making this amazing broth last longer!

I love coming here for a drink before going out to celebrate anything. If you haven't been here yet you must make the trip. Just be aware that they don't open until 5 pm and if you come after 8:30, there is an $8 cover fee per person. I came here with my family before going to dinner near Rockefeller Center, mainly because of the ambiance here. One side of the restaurant rotates so that you can circulate around the city. Each time you look out the window, you have a different view outside. It's spectacular. The service was a bit slow this time. We ordered one round of drinks, and after checking in on Yelp I had a $5 off coupon on the second round of drinks for every person. However, it didn't specify that it would only apply for other Yelp users (and I'm the only Yelp user in my family). But then again, this wasn't the restaurant's fault. My mom asked for a second glass of wine and the waitress forgot about it twice. However, she did bring it quickly and gave us a hefty second round of chips for our small plate (the Mediterranean plate, which I would highly recommend). Other than that, the drinks were great and the waitress was very friendly and apologetic. I'll also add that they only have a few waiting staff to serve tons of people, so perhaps that is where the issue stems from. Either way, definitely stop by here if you ever have the chance!

I left equal parts impressed with the space, service and eats. Five stars all around!The interior is absolutely gorgeous with so much attention to every detail. Stunning artwork and mirrors all over the walls, pink velvet chairs, white marble countertops... even the gold forks were downright glamorous. I also loved the open kitchen concept.Service was speedy and our food came out no more than ten minutes after we ordered. Every lunch special comes with a soup, salad and spring rolls and our server was nice enough to bring the same out for those at the table who did not order the special. It did take a while for the bill to come out, but that was the only snafu.The menu is large -- there is an entire page dedicated to lunch specials and then a full menu with a ton of other options. We mainly stuck to the lunch special section which featured a variety of noodle, rice and stir fry dishes. Specials are around 15 dollars and come with a soup, salad and spring rolls. Given the area and quality it's definitely a solid deal. My ginger chicken was coated in a sweet soy sauce, mixed with lots of fresh veggies and served with a heaping mound of rice. The Thai iced tea was easily some of the best that I've had. I look forward to returning and trying out more of the menu!

I recently visited a new dipping ramen spot and the anticipation was high. Despite a reasonable 20-minute wait at 8 PM on a Thursday, the no-reservation policy meant we were quickly seated at the bar. The staff was prompt and helpful with the menu.

We started with the karage, which was a delight - perfectly light batter and succulent on the inside. As for the main event, the tonkotsu tsukemen, it was a mixed bag. The thicker noodles were a delectable twist, but the dish was marred by the egg not being soft-boiled as I had hoped, turning out quite firm instead. The major letdown, however, was the broth's overwhelming saltiness. It overpowered my palate, leaving me chugging water, and the taste lingered longer than desired.

While the experience fell short due to the saline assault, I'm willing to give the restaurant another try, perhaps with their traditional ramen next time, hoping for a more balanced flavor profile.

So I've been here twice now. Each time I enjoy my food but there's always little things that happen that put a damper on my experience.The first time I came, I asked for the Mac and cheese instead of fries. They forgot about the Mac and cheese and by the time I actually got it, everyone else in my party already finished eating. However, the Mac and cheese was so yummy! My main meal was the turkey burger which I found bland. The second time, everyone in my party received their meal, and then mine didn't show up for five minutes after everyone else's. But again, the chicken sandwich I had (pictured) was so good, I would totally order it again... and again. The bacon jam was delightful. They don't take reservations and will only seat you if your party is there fully. So take that into consideration. They also have a pretty prime location in Times Square close to multiple theaters, so it's a nice option for a pre show dinner.The bathroom situation is strange. The restaurant is connected to a hotel and you have to use the hotel lobby bathrooms. The bathrooms are always crowded and messy (they are also super small).Overall, it's a nice meal in a nice touristy area.

Title: A Delightful Quick Dinner Spot

I recently had the pleasure of dining at the new branch of a restaurant that I was quite excited about. Visiting on a Tuesday evening, my friend and I were greeted by an almost empty establishment, allowing for a pick of seats. Orders are taken at the front; a simple procedure where you're handed a number for table service.

The ambience was inviting, characterized by its open, spacious layout. I decided on the classic pepper beef rice, a choice that didn't disappoint my wallet or appetite at roughly $13. The food was served promptly, in portions generous enough to leave one satisfied.

One of the highlights was the interactive element of finalizing the cooking at the table, enhancing the experience with tantalizing aromas and freshness. The robust flavors of the dish were further amplified by adding some of the recommended sauces.

In summary, this restaurant offers a great option for a quick, tasty, and affordable dinner, especially given its location. I would definitely suggest giving it a try for those looking for a satisfying meal in a casual setting.

Fantastic burgers in the heart of times square! Came here on a Sunday night at around ~630pm. Restaurant was half full so we were immediately seated. I got the bacon bbq burger in medium rare, and a side of regular fries which you can get for free with any purchase of a burger if you check in on Yelp! Burger was $16, tax and tip not included. Burger was very juicy! The patty was delicious. The bacon on top and the fried onions added a nice crunchy texture to the patty. Patty seasoned very well. The fries were really crispy and airy. Definitely portion wise its good for a meal! Would come back again whenever I'm around the area!

I recently visited a restaurant that's elevating the fast food game with a fresh, whole food approach, and I must say, it's a game-changer. Their customizable menu options allow you to pick and choose to your taste while still keeping things healthy and nourishing. After work, I swung by for a quick pick-up and ordered shrimp, couscous, and sweet potatoes. Each item was superb, with flavors that made for an enjoyable ride home. This spot is ideal for anyone seeking a quick yet wholesome meal on the go.

Title: A Hidden Gem in West Harlem – Exceptional Thai Cuisine on a Budget

During a stroll through West Harlem in search of a quick lunch option, I stumbled upon an unassuming Thai restaurant that truly caught me by surprise. Contrary to my initial skepticism, what I found inside was, without exaggeration, some of the best Thai food available in NYC.

The Pad Thai, served in a generous portion, arrived perfectly hot, expertly seasoned, and teeming with succulent shrimp – a testament to its authenticity. Equally impressive was the Pad See Ew, packed with a hearty serving of chicken and delightfully savory noodles. Both dishes were fresh and left my taste buds thoroughly satisfied.

What elevated the experience, however, was the lunch special. Alongside your entrée, you have the choice of an appetizer—either a salad or soup—completing your meal for an astonishingly reasonable $7 to $10. It's a filling, flavorful deal that seems almost too good to be true.

In conclusion, this restaurant is a must-visit for anyone seeking an authentic Thai meal without breaking the bank. It's a culinary treasure that proves the best experiences can often come from the most unexpected places.

Cuba Restaurant and Run Bar is definitely a place to drop in on the next time you want to have brunch. Cuba Restaurant and Run Bar is a short walk from the West 4th station. It's not a large place but big enough to enjoy a great meal with a few friends. Also, I will say that It was clear from the moment I walked in that each worker takes great pride in all they do. I love going into resturants and everyone is smiling not only at me but at each other in a welcome to our house, were glad your here kind of way. To that point, the staff was absolutely lovely and our waiter was both knowledgeable and quick. So for our meal and drinks, I enjoyed several caipirinha that were both delicious and potent. For my brunch meal, I had the seasoned pork with rice. I enjoyed the meal but unfortunately the pork was a bit dry. Like I said, it was seasoned well but just a bit dry for my taste. My friend had a different dish off the menu and enjoyed it as well. I will definitely be back because the ambiance is awesome, the drinks were amazing, food was authentic and I love being in a restaurant were you truly feel at home.

Absolutely delighted with my recent visit to this gem of a restaurant, particularly during their fantastic happy hour. Not only does each drink come with a complimentary skewer, making it an incredible value, but the flavors are out of this world. Both cumin and lemongrass skewers, available in chicken or pork, are packed with taste and cooked to perfect tenderness. I also ventured to try the frog legs accompanied by the house sauce, and while labeled mild, the spice level had quite the kick. The frog legs themselves were succulent, even more so than chicken, adding a unique twist to the meal. This experience has me eager to return and sample more from their tempting menu.

My husband and I frequently return to this gem for its vibrant ambiance, and our latest visit did not disappoint. Although we typically come for drinks, this time we ventured into their food menu, starting with the Quesadilla de Pollo. The marinated grilled chicken, smothered in chipotle BBQ sauce and accompanied by a rich medley of Mexican cheeses, was an absolute delight. The guacamole and crema drizzle added an extra layer of flavor that had us savoring every bite.

Venturing further, we tried the Skirt Steak Asada. The marinated-grilled steak was cooked to perfection, and the tomato chipotle salsita, paired with borracho beans and queso, provided a robust and satisfying combination. The chile toreados and cilantro chimichurri were flavorful accents that tied the dish together beautifully.

Our meal was made even more enjoyable with the pairing of some truly excellent margaritas, which complemented the flavors of our dishes perfectly. Overall, our experience was a delightful culinary journey. This restaurant continues to impress us with its lively atmosphere and delicious offerings.

My friend and I decided to try this place for dinner yesterday. Place wasn't super crowded. There were seats at the high table but we denied that. So we had to wait about 15mins for a table for 2.The menu has some decent options but my friend and I were disappointed there wasn't any soondubu on the menu. But at least there was Tang since my friend wanted soup.My friend ordered the seolleong tang and I decided to get the seafood dolsot bibimbap. We also shared the crispy mandu appetizer. The mandu was average, tasted ok but I've tasted better elsewhere. The bibimbap wasn't bad. Just less seafood to rice ratio in my opinion.

Title: A Late-Night Haven with a Touch of Authenticity

I stumbled into this tucked-away gem late one night around 2 AM, in search of a quick meal. Descending into the quaint underground setting, I immediately felt a wave of cozy, welcoming vibes. The service was commendable; a very nice young lady greeted me promptly and ensured I had a pleasant experience.

I ordered the Ramen, which arrived speedily - a plus for any late-night hunger pangs. However, my palate wasn't entirely satisfied; the broth lacked the depth I crave in a good Ramen, and the noodles were a tad too al dente for my liking. Nonetheless, the ingredients nestled within my bowl were truly "oishii" - echoing the little Japanese I've picked up, meaning "good taste."

This spot has potential, especially for those late-night food adventurers. Give them a try and don't hesitate to share your thoughts with them - feedback is the broth of improvement, after all!

Great service, cool ambiance and excellent food. My friend and I shared:+ Strip house roasted bacon - by far the best thing we ate, definitely don't miss this+ Filet mignon - great + Caesar salad - only thing that was meh, would skip best time + Sautéed wild mushrooms - amazing+ Haricot verts - decent+ Patatas bravas - decent Next time, I'd try the lobster bisque and the crab cake. 4.5 stars.

Title: A Delightful Homestyle Eastern European Brunch

I recently enjoyed an amazing brunch at a local spot that serves up homestyle Eastern European fare, perfectly timed before joining the Pride celebrations. The menu was satisfyingly traditional with a splendid twist. My order of French toast and bacon was excellently prepared, but the shared table items truly stole the show.

We indulged in potato pancakes, blintze, and an innovative take on pierogis—fried and breaded, an unexpectedly delicious departure from the norm. As someone with Polish roots, this was a delightful surprise that connected me to my heritage in a new way. Those potato pancakes were particularly memorable, "out of this world," and make a strong case for a return visit.

This 24-hour gem combines the charm of a diner with the soul of Eastern Europe, making it a rare and wonderful find. It's heartwarming to see traditional cuisine like that of my family's being served with such authenticity. For anyone craving Eastern European comfort food, especially those delightful potato pancakes, I can't recommend this place enough.

So glad my friend told me about this place. After Googling it found that this place has excellent unique foods.When making reservations online the full amount of the meal needs to be paid. Tipping isn't allowed.13 course meal with locally sourced ingredients that were all beautifully prepared. Reminded me of Forage in Utah that closed down. Oddly the Chef/Owner Flynn McGarry that was talking about the foods knew about Forage as well.The food portions were just right and spaced out in a comfortable manner. Not a single thing came out that I didn't enjoy. Took my palate for a rollercoaster ride as I had to ask what flavors/ingredients were used. They gave the menu at the end so my curiosity was satisfied.For sure will be back, and with a larger group. It didn't break the bank for the quality of the dishes.

Title: Pleasant Visit with Minor Hiccups

I swung by this eatery for a late lunch on Easter Sunday and was greeted by a warm and alert staff. The menu boasted a wide array of options. I chose to start with the Tom Yum soup, which to my surprise was more of a light broth than the coconut-rich Thai version I had anticipated. The edamame, while standard, was satisfactory. The highlight of my meal was the green curry with squid; it was flavorful, but I found myself wishing for a more generous helping of vegetables. The presentation in a deep bowl gave it an unexpected soup-like feel, differing from my usual experience of curry served in a shallower dish.

My companion opted for a lychee margarita, which unfortunately came with an entire lime blended in, making the texture less than pleasing for her taste. Despite these small letdowns, the overall experience was positive. While I wouldn’t go out of my way to return, it was a good stop for a holiday meal.

Came here for the New York Times Travel Show unofficial afterparty. The vibe was awesome upon entry! The ambiance in the various bars of the 18th floor was really mellow and gave off a tropical tone. The bartenders were speedy and made a mean margarita! I'd love to be back in the summertime!

I came here for a weekend brunch. This place had really great service and a great ambiance! I ordered the pepper chicken, banana leaf chicken, goat curry, and aloo tikki. The chicken dishes were not bad but not memorable. The goat curry and the aloo tikki appetizer were so good! A great spice level too.

Visited for the brunch special and it was fantastic! The atmosphere was wonderfully relaxing, enhanced by some delightful live music. Service was top-notch, and every bite was a joy. Highly recommend!

Title: Quick, Tasty Tacos in the Heart of Times Square: Los Tacos No. 1

If your belly is rumbling for a quick bite in the bustling area of Times Square, Los Tacos No. 1 is your go-to taco haven. Perfect for those moments when you're saving room for dinner but need something to tide you over, this spot offers the convenience of dollar-slice pizza joints, but with the zest and flavor of authentic Mexican tacos.

The storefront, conveniently located across from the Harry Potter Broadway theater, boasts enough space to accommodate the constant crowd it draws. The menu, plastered on the wall, is impossible to overlook and features staple items like tacos, quesadillas, and an array of drinks and sides. Ordering is a breeze, even when you're specifying your taco toppings, or as they say, "con todo" (with everything).

Prices are fair, with the option to pay cash for smaller purchases or credit card for anything above $5. Efficiency is key here; the cashiers work at lightning speed and you'll have your food ticket ready in a flash. Watch as the cooks assemble your meal with deft hands, then feel free to fine-tune your tacos with a side selection of salsa and sauces.

I sampled the carne asada, which was succulently juicy, and the adobada, which wasn't my favorite but still satisfying. Los Tacos No. 1 delivers a no-fuss, delectably messy, and swift taco experience that's worth every bite.

Great place for getting drinks with your coworkers or friends. They're all bench like seatings.  I got my schofferhofer beer and ate one of the pretzels. The pretzels are pretty big so I shared that and then the chicken schnitzel was okay. The food is meh there so just go there for the drinks and hanging out.

I came here on a weekday evening and overall, had a pleasant time.The menu is very thorough and extensive with several pages and pictures of the most popular items. We started with the scallion pancakes ($5.95) which were  delectable-- crispy, oozing fresh from the oven, and with an oily coating. I think they were some of the best I've ever tried and I liked how it was a low price point rather than having a very large portion size and a huge pancake the size of a pizza or something (which is how it is at other restaurants I believe). I think the sauce that accompanied the pancake could have been more flavorful. Next, we had the pork dumplings in chili ($7.95). Again, these were just right- the chili oil was plentiful and extremely spicy. (I also used it to coat the pancakes). The price point is pretty good for these.We tried the bok choy with mushrooms ($15.95), which seemed a bit bland compared to the other dishes and I don't particularly recommend it. However, if you're not as into spicy dishes, perhaps you would like it.For entrees, we had the chef's special (mixed seafood- squid, shrimp, and scallops), which was $25. It was made fried and crispy/crunchy while also being very spicy (made with green and red chilis) so it was very flavorful still. It almost reminded me of Szechuan popcorn chicken in terms of the texture and cooking style. I found it to be very unique for scallops to be fried as it was my first time eating them that way... and I really enjoyed it actually. I think it was a definite highlight of the meal because it was so nuanced. We also tried the beef with cabbage and chili ($19.95). It was a huge portion size, spicy but not in an overpowering way, and it pairs well with white rice, which is ordered separately. One disappointing aspect was that we actually ordered the pork with cabbage and chili but were given beef... we didn't want to waste it as it was a big and generous portion of beef, but I actually came for the pork so would come back to try it.For a drink, we had the Thai iced tea... it was $4.95 and it was diluted, watered down, or just didn't taste right somehow (no condensed milk and the tea flavor didn't come through) and I don't recommend it. It also didn't come with boba so I felt $4.95 was expensive for it. Each person is given a complimentary dessert which was white fungus or snow fungus soup. I really liked it because of the texture of the fungus and the authenticity of the dish. I thought the "soup" base tasted like agave syrup, which I loved as someone with a sweet tooth. Overall, I would say the flavor of the Szechuan spices, variety in terms do the menu options, large portion sizes, and fair price points led me to a 5 star rating. I will say though that the service and ambiance were more of a 3.5.

My boyfriend and I came here many times during our first New York trip, since it's very close to Times Square on 8th St. We love the beautiful presentation of the rose-shaped gelatos. When I came to New York alone, I decided to swing by here once during my last couple of days in New York for old time's sake, even though I wasn't supposed to eat sweets. Thank goodness for the nutrition facts sheet that they have up on the wall!I indulged in a small gelato arranged into a rose on a cone, topped with a macaron right around when they were closing shop at midnight. I enjoyed every bite.

The grandma pizza here is my favorite in the city! I always get delivery from here when I'm craving pizza and have friends over. It is a hit every time. I usually get a regular pie, but opted for buffalo chicken the last time I ordered from here. Wasn't the best buffalo chicken pizza I ever had, so I would just stick to regular or normal toppings like pepperoni. There regular pies are great too, the crust is some of the best in the city. They have breadcrumbs baked into the pizza crust that gives it that extra something. Delivery is always on time.

Maybe it was over hyped to me so that my 3 visits were decent, but let downs. I just don't get the hype. It was okay. I've tried their prawn, the avocado sandwich, koji-cured salami, and the steak and potatoes. It was all okay, but small portions. I'm a grazer so I'm not into huge portions, but these were even too small for my liking. My friend always gets the ricotta dumplings which again are okay. Maybe it's just me, I'm just underwhelmed.

I recently visited this local spot for their $9 lunch special and it did not disappoint. I opted for the fried dumplings and chicken pad thai - both dishes exceeded my expectations. The pad thai was generous in portion, perfectly saucy, and packed with tender chicken. The fried dumplings were a hit too, especially when drizzled with duck sauce. Service was impressively quick and attentive. Based on this experience, I am already planning my next visit. Highly recommended for a satisfying and affordable lunch!

Visited on a bustling Saturday morning and, as expected, faced a bit of a wait – the Yelp wait-list feature was convenient but didn't quite hit the mark on timing accuracy. That minor inconvenience aside, the Nova Benny was a revelation – absolutely delicious, confirming the good impression from my initial visit at Friedman's. Opted for takeout this time and it didn’t disappoint. Service was commendable, with our waiter being attentive and efficient. The lively atmosphere, complete with a full house and the pleasant buzz of conversation, added to the overall enjoyable experience. Would recommend for a tasty brunch, but maybe plan for a little extra waiting time.

I recently dined at this gem of a restaurant and left utterly impressed. From the moment we stepped in, the ambiance enveloped us in a welcoming warmth that only amplified the experience. The food was nothing short of amazing; the Eggs Benedict, in particular, was a delectable delight, perfectly prepared and a testament to the culinary prowess on display. Service matched the high quality of the food; our waiter was attentive and personable, noticing and removing an untouched side of grits from our bill, a thoughtful gesture that didn't go unnoticed.

Advice to future patrons: reservations are a must, especially to avoid lengthy waits, as my initial drop-in resulted in a 45-minute to an hour long wait. But with a reservation, even on a bustling Sunday morning, we were seated promptly.

In conclusion, this establishment isn't just a restaurant; it's an experience, one that stands out in the bustling NYC culinary scene. It's an absolute must-visit.

This is a Michelin Star rated Japanese Yakitori restaurant (which means grilled chicken).We were a large group and had a private dining space at the loft level.Service:  excellent service from the staff and getting a group of 15 served in 90 mins for a tasting menu.Food:  we did the 10 skewer tasting menu, which included several meat and veggie skewers.  The flavors are right on point and grilled to perfection.  But the main focus is chicken, so you get grills of different chicken parts, including heart and liver.  We enjoyed our meal a lot and service was impeccable but I just don't love chicken, so not sure I would do a repeat for the price of the meal.  Definitely worth experiencing once.

Solid choice for breakfast in midtown Manhattan. My sister, my cousin and I found ourselves in midtown on Sunday morning with a few errands to run. Before jumping into our tasks we wanted to have breakfast. We opted for Skylight Diner because it was the first option we saw. We were seated on entry and quickly placed our order for drinks as we scanned the menu. The restaurant was fairly busy at mid-morning. The space is inviting, well lighted, and seemingly clean. The staff was professional and efficient. We ordered standard breakfast fare: Sis had a fried egg sandwich on wheat, Cuz had a spinach and avocado omelet, and I had a hash and cheese omelet. The food arrived in relatively short order and was well-prepared, the home fries were particularly tasty. I had a quibble with my omelet as there was not a lot of hash in it, and it was dry--not sure there was a lot of cheese in it, either. My cousin's omelet looked fantastic, and she acknowledged as much. Overall, Skylight Diner is a decent bet for a quick meal in midtown.

I had an afternoon meeting at New York Presbyterian and had a few minutes to kill before the meeting.  I was a little hungry and looking for something better than Mickey D but faster than Patsy's ... Sophie's Cuban Cuisine hits that sweet spot ... the food is already cooked and ready to serve ... cafeteria style!  Looking over the options, I was torn between the Ropa Vieja and the Breaded Chicken.  Ultimately, my love of fried chicken won out.  I ordered:Breaded ChickenYellow RiceSweet PlantainsAvocadoThe chicken was delicious (come to think of it, most fried foods are delicious).  It was seasoned and moist with a crunchy batter.  Adding the "green sauce" kicked it up a notch.  What do they put in that sauce???  I practically drowned the chicken in green sauce.  The yellow rice and plantains were standard fare.Ambience/Decor:  If you have been to a food court at a mall, you'll get the idea:  The food is cooked and placed behind a glass counter where you order and they assemble a plate.  You then proceed to find a table and eat.Service:  Just like a food court, it is strictly self serve.TLDR:  Food was FAST and GOOD.  Sophie makes a great Breaded Chicken with green sauce.  I would definitely go back again for lunch.

Found them on yelp. Went there for a double date. When we arrived we got seated pretty quickly then it started getting busy. I read that their pastas were all handmade there. For appetizers we got the burrata, truffle fries, and calamari. For entree we got chicken parm, squid ink pasta with shrimp and lobster sauce, mushroom purse pasta, and garlic oil pasta with broccoli rabe. My squid ink was very good! The porcini purse pasta was good but not my favorite. The calamari was good, not oily and light. The truffle fries were soft not crunchy at all. It was actually kind of soggy. I would skip that next time. My friend got the side pasta of garlic oil and parm. They said it was very good. So next time I go I think I would try either the chicken parm or Marsala. I also read that they can BYOB with no cork fee. I don't drink but for you guys that don't guess it a good sign lol. Dessert they said they have canoli, tiramisu, and something else but I only caught those two. My friend also got a shot of expresso at the end. Worth a try if you are around the area!

Getting reservations here is pretty difficult unless you book way far in advance. The first thing I noticed here was the vibe / decor really transports you back into another era. Fairly intimate restaurant with limited seating and excellent service. Came with a group of 4 and was able to share all the dishes. 4 charles cut - largest cut. Thickest prime rib ever! absolutely delicious with the horseradish sauce. This is an absolute must! 24 oz with bone in. chicago cut - medium cut. thick-cut bacon - soft and savory. sweeter than expected. great for sharing, honestly was perfectly happy with 1/4 of a piece. buttery mashed potatoes - this was delicious. can never go wrong with butter and mashed potatoes but they didn't over do it with the butter and the mashed potatoes had a smooth consistency. gem salad with crab cake - surprisingly refreshing and the crab cake was a delight. Can actually taste the crab in it and it was still moist! fries - gotta get this if you get the cheeseburger. aioli is a must.american cheeseburger - this was a surprisingly tasty burger that we split. pretty buttery tasty and overwhelmingly flavorful. I was satisfied with eating only 1/3 of it.

Title: A Tasty Yet Pricey Dining Experience

Upon entering the establishment, expect to encounter a setting that leans towards the pricier side, with a menu that may initially cause a bit of sticker shock due to its three-dollar-sign price point. The service, however, starts on a high note with a complimentary basket of fresh bread, of which the standout is a delectably warm biscuit that should not be missed.

The main courses of salmon and chicken pot pie were generous in portion and quite satisfying in flavor. The salmon, with its crisply seared skin and appetizing sauce, was delightful, though it did verge on being overly oily by the last few bites. Meanwhile, the chicken pot pie was substantial and enjoyable, though it lacked a certain je ne sais quoi to elevate it to culinary greatness.

While the food was commendable, the value for money was less convincing. The restaurant's ambiance, characterized by its clean and simple interior, didn't quite match the premium pricing, leading to a rating that falls just short of stellar.

In summary, this place dishes out good meals that are slightly marred by a cost that doesn't quite align with the overall dining experience.

Title: A Slice Above the Rest in NYC

In the great pizza debate of New York City, this spot may just take the crown. Controversial it may be, but their artichoke pizza is a game-changer - a colossal slice so satisfying it's a meal in and of its own. Ideal for the ravenous, no matter the size of your hunger (or how sober you are). Despite its popularity, don't let the lines deter you; they move with impressive speed. From sober snacking to satiating the late-night munchies, this place is a must-visit for any pizza aficionado.

I recently visited a local pizzeria where the flavor experience was akin to diving into a bowl of clam chowder – rich, indulgent, and utterly delicious. Sharing two slices with a friend was the perfect choice, as finishing both on my own might have been a challenge given the generous portion and hearty taste. This is certainly some of the best pizza I've had, and I'm already planning my return trip. Next time, I'll remember that a little goes a long way with these decadent slices.

Saw all the reviews and was so excited to have Uncle Gussy's for lunch. I ordered the Chicken Breast Platter which comes with rice, chicken and salad for $9 (oh my word! It was a ton of food) which was awesome for being in New York City and expecting to spend a lot . Two people can eat comfortably from one platter. I will say however that next time I'll opt for the Chicken Thigh Platter as the chicken breast was a little on the dry side but it was well flavored and tasty. Ps. Plan ahead before you get super hungry, the line was a little lengthy but moved speedily.

Visiting NYC we wanted to get the classic Italian dinner experience.  Heard about a lot of "hole in the wall" places, but chose a more famous place at Patsy's.  Great choice in a very NYC traditional venue.  Wife had an off the menu Lasagna with huge pieces of sausage within multiple layers of pasta.  I went with a traditional Spaghetti and veal meatballs.  Wines were all priced at $13 a glass which allowed for easy pickings.  Dessert tray was rolled over but we were just too full from dinner.  We'll be back on our next visit

Title: Mixed Feelings at a Beloved Vegan Spot

I've frequented the original Chinatown location and had high expectations for my latest visit. After a slightly confusing start without a hostess stand, I was seated quickly thanks to Yelp's waitlist feature. As usual, I ordered my favorites: irresistible nachos with guacamole, a vibrant chorizo burrito, and a fresh dinosaur kale salad. The mangolada and pomegranate cocktail accompanied the meal perfectly.

The nachos were, as always, a highlight. Even my non-vegan friends agree they're exceptional, surpassing traditional dairy cheese varieties. However, our dining experience was marred by the overzealous service. The server's repeated interruptions asking if we were finished, despite our barely touched plates, were incredibly frustrating. Instead of being allowed to savor our meal and possibly order another round of drinks or indulge in dessert, we felt rushed and unwelcomed – a stark contrast to the relaxed atmosphere I've enjoyed previously.

Despite the pushy service, the food remains excellent, and my love for the restaurant's concept stands. However, this visit was a letdown, and I'm hesitant to grant more than 2 stars. Here’s to hoping this was a one-off and not a new trend. I recommend a refresher in hospitality for the staff; in the meantime, I’ll stick to the Chinatown location where the experience consistently matches the quality of the food.

Title: Mixed Feelings on Mixed Orders

I recently opted for delivery from a local restaurant, enticed by the promises of their flavorful salmon rose salad and mushroom vareniki. The delivery experience itself was commendable – prompt arrival, hot dishes, and meticulous packaging, complete with utensils and napkins. The sour cream provided with the vareniki was a highlight, so fresh that I found myself longing for more than the small container supplied. The salmon rose salad's dressing did not disappoint either, with a generous portion that married well with the excellent, perfectly cooked salmon that was both flavorsome and juicy. The romaine lettuce, though not the mixed greens advertised, was fresh.

However, the evening's offerings fell short with the mushroom vareniki. To my dismay, what I received were potato-filled pierogies rather than the mushroom ones ordered. Not only was this an unpleasant surprise given my aversion to potatoes, but also a significant oversight when considering the $15 spent. Moreover, the salmon salad, while fresh, was missing the promised red caviar topping – a letdown that didn't justify its $18 price tag.

While the freshness and flavors were there, the inaccuracies in the order were too disappointing to overlook. Unfortunately, due to these mistakes, I will not be reordering. My experience serves as a cautionary tale for those expecting precise fulfillment of their orders.

We dined with Terrence Brennan of Picholine fame at the helm of the stoves at Chef's Club.  Picholine was one of the finest restaurants in the United States, and Chef Brennan can cook his butt off.  It was depressing when Picholine closed.  Trips to the city weren't the same.When I saw that Chef Brennan was at the Chef's Club for a short engagement, I jumped at getting a reservation.  The nine course dinner was just amazing, creative, delicious, and often mind blowing.  I travel the world for good food, and this tasting was very special.  A knowledgeable sommelier helped with our wine choices and service by Steven was professional, but so much fun.  He charmed all of us, and the four hour meal flew by quick.y.  The only caveat was the final bill.  We split checks and the total for two of us came to $468.00.  That's a lot of money anywhere.  Was it worth that expenditure of cash?  Only your financial planner knows for sure. Mine had a heart attack and added a year to our retirement date.

Ordered from here via Postmates because I saw their famous pasta on NYC Date Night's Instagram Story, and she deemed this her go-to for ordering in Gramercy. I got the Radiatori in Cartoccio and was so excited to try it. The dish has all my favorite things: radiatori, mushrooms, tomatoes, and a cream-based sauce. When it finally arrived (an hour late- thank you, Postmates) it was cold. Even arriving in the tin foil, it was cold. That wasn't the restaurant's fault though. After heating it up and taking my first bite, it was completely flavorless. Now, I've had many a pasta in my life, and I've never had one as flavorless as this. Also, the radiatori was soft and not al dente as pasta should be. It was so mushy.I wanted to like this so badly. It was just immensely disappointing with every bite. The only reason I am not giving this 2 stars is that I have yet to go to the actual restaurant, and I'm basing this review off of the one pasta dish. But after that, and with all the Italian restaurant options in the city, I won't be ordering again.

We came here after watching  Hamilton for late night snack. We ran into a problem of not having any CASH since they were cash only. But the ATM was right on the street next door. They seemed to be specialized in their chasu pork. Pork bun ordered as an appetizer was so tasty. I ordered chasu pork ramen and it was very greasy and porky. I loved it! My sister didn't care too much about fatty ramen though. I liked it overall. It is tight, small and busy inside. Expect a long wait. Don't dress too nicely. The inside feels like one of those tiny corner restaurant in Japan. Overall, not bad but I've had better ramen before.

What an amazing new gem! Pretty spacious yet very intimate considering there's only 16 seats at the counter. I had a wonderful experience at Kissaki with Chef John. Everything was perfect and super fresh! My omakase consisted of 1. Bonito Miso with a prawn head (not pictured)2. Bonito 2 ways - tataki & smoked with a lightly torched skipjack underneath.. absolutely delicious  3. Madai (Japanese red snapper)4. Shima Aji (striped jack fish)5. Sawara (Japanese-Spanish mackerel)6. Mackerel Namero (tartare)7. Saba (Japanese mackerel)8. Akami (lean part of the Spanish bluefin tuna)9. Teka Tamaki (Tuna handroll not pictured)10. Smoked in-house Uni which is by the way, UNREAL  one of the best I've had in a while 11. Botan Ebi (Newfound Canada shrimp also not pictured)12. Kinmedai (Japenese goldenized snapper)13. Toro (jaw section of Spanish bluefin tuna)14. Mango ice cream with Japanese black beans (not pictured)Will be coming back!

On a quiet Wednesday evening visit at 6 PM, I discovered a gem of a restaurant that, while not initially packed, filled up within 30 minutes – clearly a popular spot. The watermelon salad, which we started with, was a vibrant and refreshing choice, embodying freshness with each bite. The star of the meal had to be the Parma mussels; succulent and plentiful, I found myself savoring each one and nearly finished the generous portion single-handedly. Joined by oysters crowned with a tantalizingly melted cheese, the flavors were memorable and stood out as a highlight of the dining experience.

The service matched the food in quality, attentive without being intrusive. The only slight downside was the poor cell phone reception within the restaurant, but it was a minor hiccup in an otherwise delightful visit. With its delicious offerings and convivial atmosphere, this restaurant definitely has me planning my next visit.

Solid brunch spot. Overall, the savory dishes are better than the sweet ones.I've come here twice-- I've tried the salmon toast, sicilian baked eggs, pancakes, and french toast. The sicilian baked eggs were amazing with a little kick of spice, (also came with burrata!!) and it is now one of my favorite brunch dishes. The rest are also good, but the sweet dishes (the pancakes and french toast) were a bit too sweet for my taste so I could only eat a few bites. Service is always great, and I love how spacious it is inside.

Title: Unforgettable Ramen Experience Deserving the Wait

I finally had the chance to dine at a no-reservations ramen spot that has been on my radar after several attempts. The key? Arriving early. A previous two-hour wait dissuaded me, but this time, my strategy to show up at 5 PM paid off with a mere 39-minute wait for our party of six. We kicked off with Shishito peppers – tasty but pack a punch – and the must-try pork and chicken buns, which lived up to their hype.

The star of the evening was the Akamaru Shinaji ramen. It was a masterpiece, setting a new standard for ramen with its rich, extraordinary broth. Customizing with an added egg and corn only enhanced the experience. My verdict: this place justifies the buzz, and I’m already planning my next visit.

Title: Delicious Food, Disappointing Service

Review:

My recent visit to this restaurant left me with mixed feelings, which now makes sense of the low ratings it has received. On a positive note, the food was impeccable; the Mysore Masala onion dosa hit the spot and truly satisfied my cravings. The mango lassi was average, nothing remarkable but decent enough.

Unfortunately, the service was where the experience fell short. There was confusion regarding the opening times, with Yelp stating 11 am and Google 12 pm. When I arrived at the earlier time, I was told to return later. Upon my return at noon, the establishment was still unprepared, and an employee ungraciously informed me that the kitchen wasn't ready, asking me to wait an additional 10-15 minutes. I was directed, rather dismissively, to sit at an outdoor table in chilly 60-degree weather.

Additionally, the lack of toilet paper in the restroom highlighted a negligence for customer comfort and basic amenities. While the food may be a draw, the service leaves a lot to be desired.

Title: A Romantic Gem for Date Night

My partner and I chose this enchanting restaurant for our Valentine's evening, and it did not disappoint. The view offered a breathtaking backdrop that elevated our night from simply special to spectacular. An ambiance that struck the perfect balance between spaciousness and intimacy made our dinner feel exclusive and cozy. The staff, both friendly and knowledgeable, guided us through the menu with ease, ensuring our entree and wine selections perfectly complemented one another. In summary, it was a delightful experience that left us both thoroughly impressed. Highly recommended for a romantic outing.

Came here for my friend birthday on Tuesday night. The place was pretty much empty. We ordered fish curry, lamb curry, garlic naan, rosemary naan, lollipop chicken, biryani chicken rice and samosas. Naan bread was garlicky and hot, lamb curry was nice but the fish curry was very spicy as the biryani chicken rice. The lollipop chicken were the best but they were a bit greasy. Service was good and the give 10% off with yelp check in.

Title: A Serendipitous Find for Adventurous Foodies

I stumbled upon a hidden gem while wandering in search of a bite-sized yet satisfying meal. To my delight, I discovered a spot where freshness and flavor take center stage. Their pork buns are a game-changer - even for someone who's typically not a fan. With a hint of sweet teriyaki or BBQ, these stuffed delights are absolutely amazing.

I couldn't resist trying the 8-piece classic potstickers, and they did not disappoint. Served with a tantalizing sauce, they were the epitome of deliciousness. Surprisingly filling, they were more than enough for two.

The only downside? No restroom facilities. But don't let that stop you - this place is a must-visit. Trust me, your taste buds will thank you! Highly recommended for a quick, flavorsome meal during your travels.

Better than expected!We've been here for HH and it was really good but didn't think that brunch would be that good. Happy for that!Sunday brunch around 2pm, not pack at all but busy and super kids/baby friendly.We were accomodated in no time woth a soace for the stroller (baby was sleeping)We noticed that there was a big group of parents with babies and all they accomodated them as well (with several high chairs and space for 3 strollers!). So really recommending it for a boozy brunch with friends!We has a breads basket as appetizer, a bruger, benedicts and brooklyn blackout cake. A bloodymary for each of us.YUM!!!Bread basket/pastries basket was ok, bit pricey maybe. Cornbread and croissant were spectacular but the other two muffins meh.Burger came medium rare as ordered, super juicy with a side of fries and real onion rings yummy.Benedict was ordered with salmon and it was really good too.Cake was good too, came with a vanilla ice creamW come back!

Came here on a Thursday night with a a party of 9 around 7:30pm. It was pretty empty when we arrived but filled up by 8-9pm. Since it was such a large party, I got to try about ten different dishes including fried rice, soup dumplings, walnut shrimp, twice cooked pork, lamb with cumin, Chinese broccoli, Dan Dan noodles, Kung Pao chicken, and Szechuan spicy dumplings. The fried rice and soup dumplings are exactly the taste and quality you can expect at any Chinese restaurant. It's nothing special in particular but you can know exactly what to expect if that's what you're looking for. I would say out of all the dishes I tried that night, the best were the twice cooked pork and the Szechuan spicy dumplings. It took me by surprise by how flavorful these dishes were and they definitely stood out from all the other dishes. I would highly recommend. A close second would be the walnut shrimp. The shrimp was super crispy and the sauce they put on top was very creamy and sweet. It was just a little expensive for the amount of shrimp on the plate.

I thoroughly enjoyed the shrimp roll at this establishment. The shrimp were abundant, the bread toasted to perfection, and the seasoning was spot on. However, the portion size left me wanting more. To feel satiated for lunch, you might need to order multiple rolls. This is the only reason I'm holding back on a full 5-star rating. If the roll was larger, it would've been a perfect meal.

I absolutely adore this local gem, where the Latin flavors truly shine through in their diverse rice offerings – they're authentic and exceptionally tasty. The variety of dishes keeps me coming back, but the oxtails, available Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays, are my absolute favorite. Highly recommend for a genuine taste experience!

Right in the Grand Central terminal we found this wonderful pizza place which of course had New York style pizza. It was the best we've ever had! I got the slice of chicken which was so generous and my husband got the special Prova slice. Delicious, authentic and highly recommend

I had veggie eggs Benedict and was so happy with my choice. I am a HUGE brunch fan and have very specific taste and order for my brunch. Being very picky and never ordering eggs Benedict says a lot when one decides to have it and very much like it. Every ingredient complimented each other in that dish. The cafe itself is nothing special and the decor is basic, but food is really good. Yes to brunches in Motel Morris

Title: Cozy Spot for a Working Breakfast with a Chill

I recently visited this restaurant for a weekday breakfast and appreciated the ample seating, which allowed me to find a quiet spot in the back for some work. The ambiance, though, comes with a caveat; the elegant full-length windows, ideal for summer breezes, brought a noticeable chill to my winter dining experience. It's something to keep in mind if you're planning to sit near them.

On the culinary side, I opted for a healthier start with their granola, yogurt, and fruit combo. While tasty, it reinforced the age-old diner's dilemma - the simplicity of the dish hardly seemed to justify the price, despite the convenience.

A redeeming feature was the reliable wifi, which supported an efficient and productive morning. So, if you're looking to combine work with a bite to eat, this spot ticks the boxes, just remember to dress warmly if you're visiting in the cooler months.

Small place and a bit loud. There were three of us with a reservation and they sat us at a corner table that sat two on one side and one to the right.  Awkward to have a conversation. That aside, the waiter was friendly and always checked how we were doing. We ordered a really nice bottle of Malbec. For starters we had the GRILLED BUCHERON CHEESE and two orders of the GRILLED NUESKE'S BACON.  This bacon dish is incredibly good!  For the main course two of us had the Prime Rib and one had the Filet. Each was cooked perfectly. What really made the steak was their house steak sauce.  Excellent!  We also shared the cream spinach hush puppies.  For dessert we had the chocolate cake. Very pricy so not a weekly spot but worth the trip to treat yourself.

Now that I'm in the neighborhood, I frequently see the lines at this place. I wanted to finally see what the hype is about. We came for an early Friday dinner and decided to just order all snacks.The duck fat fries were good but a bit overpowered by the truffle. The grilled cheese sandwich was simple but perfect. The deviled brussel sprouts were also very simple but enjoyable. My favorite was definitely the scotch eggs with grainy mustard. The brioche went surprisingly well with the rillette.
