Overall a very enjoyable meal. I would come back again.

Despite previous unfavorable critiques, I decided to dine at this establishment, a decision I now regret. I ordered a burger and my husband opted for the steak salad. At $28, the steak salad was lacking in substance — more meat was expected for the price. My burger experience was equally disappointing, offering nothing to write home about. Ironically, the ketchup emerged as the meal's standout, a testament to our underwhelming dining experience.

Tucked away in the heart of the city is a delightful spot ideal for noodle and salad aficionados. On my recent visit, I indulged in their Thai Basil noodles, a harmonious blend of chow mein-style noodles bursting with the unmistakable zest of Pad Thai. They were so flavorsome on their own that the additional soy sauce I playfully drizzled was merely a nod to my penchant for extra condiments – a testament to the dish's standalone appeal.

The restaurant also offers complimentary still and sparkling water, a refreshing touch to the dining experience. I paired my meal with a crisp Sapporo beer, which proved to be a perfect complement. The portions are generous, ensuring good value for your money.

My only suggestion for improvement would be to introduce a customizable spice level, perhaps on a scale of 1 to 5, as is customary in many Thai and noodle joints. This would allow patrons to tailor the heat to their liking and enhance the already enjoyable dining experience.

What a hidden gem. I came for the six course omakase meal (prepared and served by Chef Yoshiko), and I was highly impressed with every dish. Each course was delicate and refined, yet also had bold and innovative flavors. My two favorite dishes were the edamame tofu with uni, shiso, ponzu jelly, and balsamic reduction and the truffle-miso duck confit with GF gnocci and dandelion greens. These dishes have flavor combinations that you don't see often (for example, the creative edamame tofu creation!), and as the courses continued on, I found myself getting more excited for the next dish. It was a fantastic meal from start to finish.Although it was a quiet night for Wednesday dinner and we only saw two other customers, I actually liked that we had a more private and intimate experience. I'm hoping more customers discover this spot though, since this restaurant is a true gem. I'm already looking forward to returning for Rabbit House's next seasonal menu, which should be released in April for Spring.

I've been to Lombardi's twice and and both times left disappointed. Second time around we got the white pizza and it was very dry. Service was terrible also. Waiter forgot our drinks and we asked for it twice and never received it. I guess we're done with Lombardi's.

This place is efficient. In and out. Wait wasn't that long on a Sunday night. Ramen is made right in front of you. It is a very small place but it didn't bother me much. The extra spicy miso,  wasn't spicy at all, probably 1/5 spice level for me. The broth is very rich and delicious.

Quick, affordable and good. I ordered the Fish and Shrimp taco. Nice that you can order drinks there too. They have sangria and beers. I recommend both tacos but if I had to choose one, I'd choose the Shrimp. Went back to the counter and ordered another shrimp tacos. Didn't feel overly stuffed. The perfect amount of food. Small place but still able to find a place to sit by the window. They were packed with people but the food didn't take long to come out. You order at the register. Nice spot to grab a quick bite to eat with a friend or alone.

Title: A Disappointing Experience at the Center Station

I recently visited the Center Station restaurant, conveniently located just beneath my office, twice with the hope of finding a new go-to spot for quick meals. Unfortunately, both of my visits left me severely disappointed.

My first visit was for a small snack, and I ordered fries, expecting this simple staple to be a safe bet. To my dismay, the fries managed to be both soggy and burnt simultaneously – a perplexing and unappetizing combination.

Encouraged by my boyfriend, I decided to give the restaurant another chance, especially due to its proximity to my workplace. I tried an assortment of items from the weight-based food station. Sadly, the experience went from bad to worse. The pasta had a peculiar sour taste, and the other items – including panko tofu, sesame noodles, broccoli, and salads – lacked freshness and were notably flavorless. I found the meal so unpalatable that I left it unfinished.

Considering the price, I expected much more, especially when there are better options like Duke Eatery or Dig Inn nearby that offer superior meals for the same cost. I am disheartened to report that I won't be returning to Center Station.

We were satisfied with our dining experience at Amy Ruth's. The waiters served quickly so the wait wasn't bad even there were always lines. Chicken and waffle is definitely a must try . Their chicken was really juicy with crispy fried layers and the texture of waffle wasn't dry at all. My favorite was their complimentary corn bread which was really soft with great corn-smell.

I had recently traveled to Spain and was really missing Spanish food, so I picked Txikito to have dinner with some friends. I had the Casco Viejo cocktail (strong!) and we all shared a pitcher of white sangria that was really good (sweet, but not too sweet). The complimentary cod was amazing and might have been my favorite part of the meal. It was simple, but so delicious. Could have eaten it all day. We ordered a bunch of items off the menu and shared everything, including cod croquettes, foie micuit (foie gras terrine), patatas mentaiko (fries with spicy cod roe mayo), arraultza (chorizo, quail egg on top), octopus, squid ribbons, txarripatak (beef tripe, chickpeas, beef tendon, pig ear), and a rice special of the day. All of the dishes were great, but notable items were the foie gras terrine (so tasty and creamy), octopus (super fresh), and the fries (crispy, great mayo, and also because I just love fries).We enjoyed everything and my Spanish food craving was definitely satisfied! Of course, this made me miss Spain even more, but at least I know I can always come back to Txikito for amazing Spanish food.Taste | 4.5Atmosphere | 4Presentation | 4Service | 4OVERALL | 4.5

I recently tried a $13 "chipotle style" bibimbap that was generously portioned but fell short on warmth and freshness. The sheer amount of rice made the dish overwhelmingly filling, though it could conveniently serve as two meals. I chose bulgogi as my protein, adding a standard four toppings, with the option for more at an additional cost.

The serving temperature was disappointingly room temperature, which detracted from the experience one would expect from a traditional bibimbap. Also, the dish seemed to have an excessive amount of water content.

As for carbohydrates, they offer a selection including Korean fried rice, white rice, purple rice, japchae, and an extra-cost kimchi fried rice. I opted for the purple rice, which lacked the expected vibrancy and flavor.

In conclusion, while you get your money's worth in quantity, the experience is compromised by the lack of heat and freshness, leaving it less satisfying than a proper stone pot bibimbap from a Korean restaurant.

Our waiter was great! It's dark upstairs.Crispy shrimp was really good and I don't even like shrimp!Mahi mahi wonton tacos were only meh. Mostly guac.Scallop gnocchi - the gnocchi was good! Soft a little fall apart, good texture. Flavor was good as well.Waygu gyoza was really good! I wasn't expecting it, but might have been my favorite. Brussels sprouts - kinda weird. One of my friends said they tasted dank. Def a strange flavor in there.Mac and cheese - don't bother. Not good. I took one bite and didn't want any more. Truffle sashimi - I had had this before and it was good! Both times.

Part of the Gallery 32 food court. Food is run-of-the-mill, nothing special.  They offer a verity of bunsik-type food like kimchi fried rice and bibibob. Service is fast and very friendly but you can find better in K-town.

Title: A Taste of Taiwan in the Heart of Manhattan

Manhattan has been long overdue for a place that celebrates Taiwanese culinary delights, and this new establishment is a breath of fresh air for aficionados of the island's delectable dishes. The restaurant has carved out a space for itself with a menu that distinguishes Taiwanese fare from the broader spectrum of Chinese cuisine.

On a gloomy Saturday morning this January, the restaurant offered a quiet respite with my friend and I walking in at 11 am to a mostly empty locale. By the time lunch hour neared, however, the space began to fill - a testament to the growing interest in their offerings.

The savory soy milk I ordered was a revelation, rich and comforting, while my friend's corn and cheese danbing was a delightful spin on the traditional egg-stuffed crepe. The showstopper, however, was the 'sausage party' - a playful ensemble of Taiwanese-style pork sausage encased in a sticky rice sausage, all paired with a zesty sauce that brought the dish together.

The flavors were authentic, the dishes well-executed, and the experience left us eager to return for more - with items like loba beng, the iconic oyster omelet, and the hearty beef noodle soup high on our list for the next visit. This spot is a must-visit for anyone wanting to explore the rich tapestry of Taiwanese cuisine right in the heart of the city.

From the onset, STK delivers an electrifying atmosphere that persists throughout the dining experience. My visit on a bustling Friday night, amidst Restaurant Week, was one for the books. Despite a hiccup with seating due to their full-party policy—costing us an hour's wait—the staff's generous gesture of a complimentary bottle of champagne smoothed things over.

The pre-fixe menu was a culinary journey, starting with a fresh tuna tartare, moving onto a perfectly adequate salmon and potatoes, and culminating in a standout dessert of vanilla ice cream with a chocolate chip cookie—a sweet finale that stole the show.

What truly sets STK apart is the infectious energy. A hip DJ kept us grooving in our seats with the latest hits until the host amped things up, weaving through the crowds with champagne shots and fostering a party atmosphere that spilled into the walkways.

While the food may not have been the highlight, the overall vibe and the beautiful crowd made for a memorable night. I'd definitely return to STK, although next time I'll grab a bite beforehand to focus fully on the vibrant scene.

I try to mark every 100th Yelp review of mine with someplace special or interesting, so I'm pleased to write about JeJu Noodle Bar for my 5100th review. Note that my experience came several months ago before our coronavirus apocalypse shut things down (hopefully temporarily).For a restaurant with a Michelin star, JeJu is surprisingly accessible and casual. I was able to stroll in first thing on a recent weekend morning without a reservation for brunch, when they offer both an a la carte menu as well as a prix fixe menu from which you can order individual items a la carte. The toro ssam bap, for example, was more expensive than my "main" dish, but, boy, was it worth it. A delightful, surprisingly complementary melange of fatty tuna, scrambled egg, tobiko rice, and toasted seaweed that packed soooo much umami to it. Despite its compact size and despite the fact that I didn't want it to end, it packed so much flavor to it that it was a very satisfying dish.JeJu specializes in ramyun and related dishes that are similar to, say, Japanese ramen for the uninitiated but are nevertheless 100% Korean takes. The JeJu bibimmyun with JeJu ragu, black bean, cucumber, lettuce, and poached egg came without broth, but, due to all these savory ingredients, formed a coherent, slurpable whole once mixed together. Enough to be filling on its own. Together with the toro ssam bap and a house beer, it was a most indulgent brunch. For dessert, a serving of three oishi strawberries on ice for $9 seemed a bit extravagant in terms of price, but apparently these are rare, specially sourced berries that JeJu gets at prices that are competitive with what us mere mortals can achieve on our own. Service is at once casual and approachable as well as refined and detail-oriented. Perhaps the best surprise about this venue, however, is the venue itself. The fact that there's a tongue-in-cheek adaptation of Edward Hopper's "Nighthawks" in a corner - but with JeJu personalities sprinkled about in a far more convivial atmosphere - awakened me to the fact that this triangular space looks awfully like that in the original painting. See for yourself here (facebook.com/jejunoodleb…) and here, for the previous tenant at this space (nypost.com/2014/11/07/is…).

I actually think this place is a couple of bucks more expensive than usual Viet places. It deserves a $$ mark. Nonetheless, this has been my go to places for banh mi when I was little. I noticed they have  avocado smoothies on their menu now which is pretty interesting. I've heard about avocado smoothies from my vegan friends but I didn't expect to find it in a Viet place. I got #47 spring roll with vermicelli. Number 48 has spring roll AND grilled pork. I'm a bigger fan of grilled chicken so I asked if I could change it and they said no so I opted for #47. It looked like a lot of vermicelli but I think there was a lot more lettuce, lemongrass, etc... at the bottom. Don't get me wrong, this place is still authentic as heck. I just think that the prices are a bit inflated because the rent here is not the cheapest. I would come here if I was craving Viet food and I was in this area. But I wouldn't eat here on a daily since there are definitely cheaper eats in this area. P.S. the avocado smoothie was surprisingly good. It irked me in how I KNEW there'd be avocado in there but the taste was good. It tastes very light, creamy, and kind of like those steamed egg desserts except with a healthy aftertaste for about $5.50! I'm not sure if I would get it again though. When I think of smoothies, I think of something fruity or leafy. It was too sweet for me towards the end so I didn't finish it.

Healthy fast casual that knows how to keep it simple. I like it! They stay open pretty late, 9 PM I think, so I was able to come here after class at 8:30 and get a good, protein-heavy meal with plenty of vegetables. Half riceberry,half cabbage, with a side of vinegar slaw and cucumbers. Went with the chicken and massaman curry.

Title: Charming Brunch Haven Near Chinatown

Tucked away in the bustling intersection between Chinatown and Soho lies a quaint brunch gem that's definitely worth the wait—and yes, there's typically a bit of a wait. Its cozy interior is as adorable as it is compact, accommodating a handful of tables that fill up quickly during peak brunch hours. But fear not, I found myself seated within a mere 10 minutes during the rush.

Our table opted for the El Camino and Hey Chix. The El Camino, seemingly a deconstructed breakfast bowl, surprised me with its hearty bean base and a whirlwind of flavors. The pork stood out, succulent and seasoned, alongside an impeccably cooked egg. If I'd change one thing, it would be to plead for more potatoes, yet the pickled onions were a stroke of brilliance, cutting through with just enough acidity.

The Hey Chix is a must-try for fried chicken aficionados. Encased in brioche, each bite was a symphony of juicy, crispy, and spicy notes. Despite the potential for a messy affair, I found myself diving in for more, without that all-too-familiar post-meal heaviness.

This charming spot is a winner for a delightful brunch that leaves your taste buds tingling and your belly contentedly full.

I came here and solo'd it for lunch after trying out a new church one Sunday.  Thankfully, church ends early and so it wasn't too crowded.  I am not the biggest connoisseur of mediterranean food, but I knew I couldn't go wrong with a lamb pita and definitely cannot turn down fresh hummus.  Lamb pita with side of fresh hummusPROS:- super soft lamb: if you don't like gamey meat, I'd opt for something else or a different kind of protein (or falafel).  This was super tender, well seasoned, and just got a great amount of that meaty fat that soaks real well into the pita- pita was warm and soft, not super hard, didn't dry out either- hummus was fresh, went well with the lamb as it came out nice and cold- comes with a nice side of sweet potato chips (upon request)- not too much dressing on top of the lamb and veggies, feels very healthy even with a significantly greasy and fatty meat.CONS:- none

Title: A Delightful Dining Experience During Restaurant Week

My recent visit to this gem during restaurant week was nothing short of delightful. Despite the usual weekday bustle, the ambiance remained comfortably casual, setting the stage for a memorable meal.

The cocktail offerings are a thrill, with the Hemingway Spritz standing out as a particular highlight — a must-try for any patron.

The starter, a crisp wedge salad adorned with bacon, was a refreshing prelude to the main course. The bavette cut steak, a hearty alternative to my preferred filet, didn't disappoint, especially paired with the whimsical curl of accompanying fries.

But the real star was the chocolate pie for dessert. Rich and indulgent, it came perfectly paired with whipped cream and a hint of peanut butter, rounding off the meal spectacularly.

I'm already looking forward to my next visit to relive the comfort and culinary pleasure this place effortlessly serves up.

Title: A Slice of Italy Tucked Away in the City

From the moment I stepped into this charming establishment, I was transported to what felt like the heart of Italy. It's the most authentic Italian restaurant I've had the pleasure of dining in for a long time. The no-reservation policy means it's wise to aim for an early dinner to secure a spot, as the place is quite cozy. And if you do visit, don't miss the bathroom – the wallpaper is a conversation starter (see my photos for a sneak peek).

Our family outing was made even more special by the delectable dishes we shared. For starters, the baked little neck clams were a hit, and my pasta e fagioli took me on a nostalgic trip back to my Nonni's kitchen, thanks to its authenticity. My wife savored the fresh flavors of her caprese salad, followed by a spicy delight, the Shrimp fra Diavolo. My choice, the linguine with white clam sauce, was flawlessly executed, while the kids enjoyed a classic pasta pomodoro.

The service was nothing short of exceptional – present when needed but far from overbearing, with a continuous supply of water for the table. And let's not forget the bread. Its perfectly hard crust and soft inside were the epitome of true Italian baking.

Yes, it's a tad pricey, but honestly, it's worth every penny for an experience such as this. Treat yourself to this culinary gem when you're looking to enjoy the best authentic Italian food.
Good bar for Midtown. Reasonably priced drinks. Around the corner from NY Hilton so if you're there for a conference it's a good a choice. Slider are a good option for late night meel.

Came back for a dinner visit. I was little sad the Pumpkin Seafood soup base was not on the menu anymore. We went for the Sweet & Sour Tomato soup base and Mushroom soup base. The Tomato one was rich with single tomato flavor, we enjoyed more; Mushroom soup base was very light and plain, quite disappointed on this one... Hot Pot igredients in general were very fresh, we mainly went with beef, seafood, and vegetables. - Miyazaki Kobe Ribeye: $65 for 7 slices, perfect marbling and melt in your mouth. - Beef Tongue: very good- Beef Ball with Soup Filling: generous amount and enjoy the runny soup inside! Seafood were lit sorta our highlight of the meal as all were very fresh. - Sea Bass and Scallop: were delicious just need to be careful not overcooked. - Tiger Prawn: not really tiger prawn given the size in my opinion, more like regular shrimp but 8 big regular shrimps were delicious. - Shrimp Paste: very flavorful also a much order. - Vegetables were expected. - Fried Dough Stick - the only ingredient we didn't like tonight, it was not fresh quite stale. Service was definately more attentive during dinner service.

Returned for lunch yesterday since I had another $5 credit from Allset. I remembered how great the Chicken Rice Bowl was, but wasn't exactly in the mood for it... so I decided to make my own bowl again. I gave the Sesame Peanut Noodles another shot as well as the yuzu brussels sprouts - generally 2 of my favorite foods lol. As for protein/main, I had a little trouble choosing but eventually went with the lemongrass chicken breast with Thai basil pesto.The chicken was a little too dry for my liking - basically what you would expect from chicken breast. I wonder if I would've liked the chipotle braised chicken (the chicken from the chicken rice bowl) with this combo instead... I thought the flavor of the sesame peanut noodles was actually on point this time, I'd just prefer egg noodles instead of the thin rice noodles/vermicelli. So not my favorite here, but the flavor is def there! And brussels are always solid. All ingredients were fresh, and again a good filling lunch option around work. Clearly it's the free credits I get from the food apps that keep me coming back lol.

Tucked away in the bustling heart of Koreatown, this gem of a spot strikes the perfect balance between ambiance and affordability. The vast selection of liquors and beers is nothing short of impressive, catering to every imaginable preference at prices that don't break the bank. What's more, their unique bottle service allows you to purchase a bottle, and if unfinished, they'll store it for your next visit with a personalized note marking your name and date — a thoughtful touch that ensures I'll be a regular here. A definite must-visit; I'm already planning my return.

Title: Tasty Cuisine with a Side of Patience Required

If you're seeking culinary delight and willing to overlook a few inconveniences, this might be the place for you. The deliciousness of the dishes certainly lives up to the hype, making each bite a flavorful adventure. However, be prepared to pay a premium for the experience, as the prices lean towards the higher end.

Service can be leisurely, so it's best to come without a tight schedule. One quirky aspect of this establishment is the separation of the bar and restaurant areas, requiring patrons to settle their bar tab before transitioning to the dining experience. While slightly irksome, the exceptional food could be worth the extra steps for food enthusiasts with time to spare.

I recently dropped by "Empanada's All Day," a delightful Dominican gem nestled in the heart of the bustling Essex Street Market. The spot is a haven for empanada enthusiasts, offering an array of fried empanadas perfect for when you need a satisfying munch on the go. With an enticing lineup including chimi, shrimp, cheeseburger, and mozzarella, there's a flavor to cater to every palate.

The best part? These little pockets of joy are a steal at just $2.50 a pop, making it a wallet-friendly indulgence. The shop itself contributes to the market's vibrant atmosphere, making it a must-visit destination for both locals and tourists alike.

If you find yourself with an empanada craving, "Empanada's All Day!" should be at the top of your list. It's a straightforward choice for a quick, tasty, and affordable bite.

Title: A Gastronomic Surprise at a Georgian Gem

My foray into Georgian cuisine at this hidden gem left me pleasantly surprised and eager to return. The highlight, without a doubt, is the Adjaruli — a delectable, freshly baked bread bowl filled with melted cheese, butter, and a perfectly runny egg. This dish alone defies the traditional warning against filling up on bread; it's absolutely worth indulging in.

The Georgian wine selection intrigued my palate, especially the robust red that I had chosen. It would have perfectly complemented the Chakapuli, a succulent braised lamb in a tangy white wine sauce, had I not eagerly finished it beforehand. The combination of the tender lamb, enriched with herbs and the acidity of the white wine sauce, was a revelation.

Dessert did not disappoint, with the napoleoni standing out as a flaky, creamy wonder. Despite its size, it was a delightful finish for two to share.

Intrigued by the array of appetizing dishes on neighboring tables, I am already planning my next visit to explore more of the menu. This restaurant is a must-try for anyone looking to dive into the flavors of Georgia.

My husband booked this because it was nostalgic for many many trips with grandparents etc. It was mentioned in a book I'm reading so I was excited. Maybe too high of expectations or unaware there would be STUFF hanging everywhere overhead - like a collector's garage. The food was good - nothing new, just tasted good.  I got the Caesar salad and the chicken hash. Old school. Trip down memory lane, accomplished. Would I come back? Maybe if we were around for more than a week and could make sure we hit other spots too.

Eataly who??? Just kidding, sort of.I love Spanish foods and I definitely love this place! Everything looked and smell delicious--it was hard to decide what to eat. I visited early on a Sunday night and it was super poppin' because: it has been open for less than a month, it's a Sunday and it's been hyped up. I'm just glad it lives up to the hype. There is something for everyone here. If you want to sit and enjoy a meal, there's Mar or Lena (with a tilde over the n) but if you just feel like a little something to tide you over, there are plenty of options....you can get churros, papas bravas (spicy fried potatoes), ham and cheese plates, and of course paella! I didn't eat the paella but it was definitely tempting. Prices are on the high side (duh). It's a fancy food hall in a brand new touristy attraction so that's just expected.

When I first came to Bubby's it was about 10yrs ago and I had just moved to NYC and the prices were completely throwing me off. It seemed so expensive for what you would get. But now, I'm extremely used to paying between $100-$200 for a quality meal in NYC. Bubby's is not that expensive in comparison, but of course we went for brunch.   I ordered the chicken & pancakes and OMG, it was the biggest portion of chicken I'd ever seen! It could have fed 3 people on just my one dish. My husband ordered eggs and bacon with cheese grits. His was a pretty normal size.   Our seating was tight, as expected in a popular NYC restaurant. But if you're not used to that, remember, things are different in NY. I was even thrown off a bit by it this time because the people on either side of us were having such loud conversations that I could hear everything they were talking about.   One of my favorite things about TriBeCa is the fun celeb sightings you can catch. On this occasion we got a little glimpse of Donald Glover (Childish Gambino), having brunch with his family.

Let me just say.. I was in NYC for less than 48 hours and ate here TWICE. Of course, I had done some research prior to arriving in NYC and Prince Street rose to the top of my list. This is a little family owned pizza place right in the middle of prince street. Inside you will find hundreds of photos of famous people who have eaten there as a testament. There are standing tables and no chairs so you are able to enjoy your slice like a real New Yorker. We ate their famous pepperoni slice. Their 'roni cups are unlike any other.. salty pepperoni with crispy edges and a slight kick of spice! The dough is thick, perfectly cooked with a golden brown crust. I ate this pizza so fast that there was sauce all over my face and running down my hand. Guys, please EAT HERE. Also, expect a line :)

Title: Cozy Spot with a Slight Ordering Mix-Up

I recently visited a snug little eatery with limited seating, just 5 or 6 barstools lining the front window, suggesting that takeout might be the best option for this locale. The ordering process was a bit unusual; customers need to refer to menu numbers rather than dish names at the counter, which took a moment to navigate.

Unfortunately, there was a hiccup with my order - I received a savory egg noodle and chicken dish instead of the rice noodle pho I intended to try. Despite the mix-up, the dish I got was unexpectedly tasty. However, the prices here are on the upper end, with noodle dishes ranging from $13-$15, a bit steep compared to other city offerings.

On a sweet note, the Thai Iced Tea, though priced at a premium $4.50, was a delightful treat and came highly recommended. Overall, an enjoyable experience, albeit with a couple of wrinkles worth ironing out.

Title: A Lively Spot with Quirky Drinks and Casual Bites

My recent visit to this vibrant hangout spot solidified its status as a fun and trendy destination. Despite it being packed on one occasion due to an engagement party, the atmosphere remained inviting with space still available at the bar. The establishment boasts a whimsical selection of drinks that perfectly complement its eclectic decor, not to mention the charming signature Lost Lady cup that adds a unique touch to the experience.

While the snack-friendly menu is a thoughtful addition, particularly for those who enjoy nibbling while sipping on their beverages, the tacos could benefit from a flavor boost and sturdier tortillas to prevent sogginess. That said, these are minor quibbles in an otherwise delightful setting.

Although it's not the most conveniently located in relation to subway access, the charm and ambiance of the place make up for the extra travel effort. It's a locale I'll happily frequent for its convivial vibe and enjoyable light fare.

The atmosphere is light, fun and musical. The waitstaff takes turns singing to the dinning guests, while food is being served. Like any diner, it's your typical diner food and there's nothing spectacular or outstanding about the food.On top of that, it was my first time here and the service was awful. I came in for breakfast and it took 25 minutes for bacon and scrambled eggs to come out and 30 minutes for avocado toast to come out. Seriously, is it that challenging to get these two dishes together? That was a very low point in my experience here.The waiter who waited on us deducted the avocado toast from my tab because he knew it was taking an absurd amount of time for it to even come out. I won't be going back to this diner.

Looking for fast food but Japanese style then this is the place. There's multiple locations in mid/upper Manhattan but each location isn't very big so getting it to-go is your best bet if you don't have the leisure to wait. Good thing I nabbed a seat at this branch despite arriving near the end of the lunch rush hour. I ordered a spicy tuna burger for myself while my friend ordered the Kobeyaki burger. We shared a order of sweet potato fries which was $4 for a small McDonald size fries but packed quite fully. I was hesitant to get it cause of the price but there was a lot of good reviews so we gave it a shot. The sweet potato fries was truly the highlight of the meal. If you like salty-sweet then this is perfect. It was nicely fried and crunchy with a saltier outside but still has the softish sweetness of the sweet potato in the inside. I definitely would recommend to order this if you were to get something from here.The burger - cute packaging with the soup dumpling style wrapping but the taste was mediocre compared to presentation. I should have known better since WASABI was listed in the ingredients but boy, every bite of the spicy tuna burger was a kick of wasabi to my nose. It wasn't very spicy otherwise and the actual tuna patty was just eh. For people who want more veggies in their burgers, this is it. 50% veggie 50% patty My friend thought the kobeyaki burger was just ok too. The burgers aren't something I would get again.

Tucked away in the bustling cityscape of New York, the burger joint I visited lived up to its pop culture fame, as touted in "How I Met Your Mother". The bistro burger, a no-fuss classic cheeseburger adorned with savory bacon, delivered a comforting throwback to simpler, yet perfected tastes. Accompanying the burger, the crispy fries offered a delightful crunch that harmonized with the succulence of the main dish. This spot earns an honorable mention on any food tour in the city. For those swinging by, the bistro burger is a must-try, and don't you dare skip out on the fries!

A cute cafe serving elevated brunch food. I'm surprised the cafe has been around for 21 years and how did I just dined here, I don't know. To start, I love the decor of the place, from the subway tiled floor to the cozy table tops. The staff were great and attentive. They are strict about all the parties being present to be able to sit down, which is understandable since the cafe is tiny. My suggestion is to dine as they open for brunch, or to the end of brunch time because outside of those times, you will have to wait.The Bloody Mary menu for brunch was impressive with so many choices. My sister ordered the Danish Bloody Mary, garnished with anchovies and onion. It came with a chaser, which I thought was a bit odd, but when you sip the bloody and topped it off with the chaser, the Bloody was next level. Another plus was the Bloody was not salty. I ordered the fried oyster omelette and shared an order of potatoes rosti. The oysters were fried and breaded, mixed with the remoulade sauce and wrapped by a bright yellow omelette. A unique take of a brunch staple with a twist. I enjoyed each bite immensely and cleared my plate. The table shared the Dutch styled pancake, which I was expecting a more traditional iteration, unlike what was served, which was similar to a regular fluffy American pancake. A traditional dutch pancake has a crepe like texture, thin in nature and takes in the syrup. The Prune version has a hard exterior texture, fluffy inside and the syrup doesn't absorbed in the pancake. As an American pancake, it was unique since the toppings were pears, but nothing spectacular and 2 pieces of ham, can do without. I would dine here again because other dishes caught my eye.

Yum - Melt Shop has some great "fast" food! The service here is great for takeout - the employees are extremely nice and the order was ready within 5 minutes. The food was hot, fresh and of course, delicious. We tried the Burger Melt, Shop Tots, Buffalo Tenders, Chicken Bacon Ranch and the Oreo Milkshake. They also threw in a side of Melt Sauce and Ranch for free! Everything was amazing but my favorite was the Burger Melt with the Melt Sauce.Overall I would definitely recommend Melt shop for a delicious, quick comfort meal. And I highly recommend getting the Burger Melt with a side of Melt Sauce for extra dipping.

Title: A Solid Middle-Tier Sushi Experience

If you're caught between the poles of high-end omakase and budget sushi joints, this spot will suit your palate without draining your wallet. Opting for their "Box of Dreams," I found the fish quality commendable – it's the kind of sushi that nods to your taste buds with an "ah yes, quality" without making a scene about it.

One gripe, however, is that all pieces arrive simultaneously, which might irk those who prefer their sushi served piece by piece to maintain peak freshness. Their 10 piece deluxe allows for personal selection, but expect some repetition in your choices.

While it lacks the intimacy of pricier omakase establishments, the price point of roughly $50 per person makes it approachable. This is a recommendable venue for sushi novices or those seeking a laid-back dining experience with reliably good sushi.

I am beyond thrilled to share my experience at this hidden gem of a dim sum haven! Breakfast turned into a feast for the senses this morning with offerings that were nothing short of stellar. I'm already planning my next weekend indulgence here.

This restaurant is a pleasant surprise, combining an elegant and pristine ambiance with the kind of budget-friendly pricing that defies its upscale atmosphere. It stands in contrast to the bustling, less-refined spots in Chinatown, delivering exceptional quality without the premium cost.

Each dish we savored deserved a standing ovation, but here are the all-stars that you simply must try:

- Snow Mountain BBQ Pork Buns: Crispy, sweet, and delightfully fluffy – they achieved the epitome of perfection.
- Creamy Egg Yolk Buns: An unexpected twist with a coconut essence that made them an irresistible creamy dessert.
- Shrimp Dumplings: These squid ink marvels were the juiciest and most exquisite I've ever encountered.
- Crab Meat Scallion Noodle: The noodles were braided art, fresh and balanced with a harmonious blend of salt, scallion, and succulent crab.
- Jasmine Tea: Far from an afterthought, this tea was exceptionally flavorful and aromatic, a true standout.
- Soup Dumplings: The definition of comfort in a bite, as soupy and divine as one could wish for.

I cannot recommend this place enough – a resounding 5 stars!

I recently visited a local ramen spot while grappling with a serious ramen craving. An unusual menu offering caught my eye – ramen topped with a unique whip cream made from potatoes. Unfortunately, while this novelty was intriguing, the ramen itself was unremarkable and didn't quite justify the steep price. Additionally, the scant serving of pork left me feeling unsatisfied. Although I'm glad I tried it, the overall experience was underwhelming, and I'm not compelled to return.

Title: A Step Down from Memories at Noodle Nirvana

I recently revisited the once bustling Noodle Nirvana, only to find it oddly desolate on a Thursday night - a stark contrast to my memory of long waits and vibrant crowds. The menu still offers a versatile selection with a choice of cold and hot soba/udon, appetizers, and rice bowls, allowing for portion control with small, regular, and large dish sizes.

In pursuit of satisfaction, I opted for their chirashi cold soba, while my partner tried the uni cold soba. Both dishes deviated from the traditional dipping style, instead served in a bowl with a side of cold broth intended to be poured over the noodles. Yet, neither of us found our meals particularly remarkable, especially considering the steep price for what was offered. My partner noted that the uni soba lacked the flavors we'd enjoyed at a competitor, Soba Totto. Additionally, the soba's texture didn't meet my expectations, coming across as too thin and lacking the desired chewiness.

Service faltered slightly when our waitress made presumptions about our familiarity with the dining process, notably neglecting to guide us through the ritual of enriching our cold broth with the additional hot broth she provided post-noodles. An explanation should be standard practice, ensuring all guests can fully appreciate the culinary experience. It's an intimate detail easily overlooked but essential for those looking to savor every aspect of their meal.

Title: A Memorable Birthday Dinner at a Quaint Gem

Review:

Celebrating my birthday at this charming restaurant was an experience to remember, marking my 1000th review with a delightful bang! Despite being short-staffed that evening, the impeccable service made it seem as though they were fully staffed, handling the bustling environment with ease. 

The interior decor immediately sets a warm ambiance, while a fascinating tidbit about the establishment caught my attention – they staunchly accept only cash and American Express. This quirky policy, in homage to American Express aiding the owner's credit history, has been a steadfast rule since their opening in 2007.

Now, onto the crux of any restaurant review – the food. The Tartelette de Chèvre was my highlight; even as someone who isn't a goat cheese aficionado, I found the blend of flavors and perfect tart execution utterly irresistible. The Pâté de Campagne Maison, though, didn't hit the mark for me. It leaned too heavily towards a sausage texture and was overwhelmed by a pungent mustard flavor.

The Tournedos Rossini, lavished with Foie Gras and a rich truffle sauce, was luxuriously indulgent if a touch too rich and salty. Equally rich but pleasingly creamy was the Gnocchi Parisian au Gratin, akin to soft, flavorful pillows bathed in a Mornay sauce.

The Carré d'Agneau au Jus de Truffes showcased perfectly cooked lamb, although the accompanying sauce tipped the scales towards a higher salt level than I prefer.

To cap off the meal, the Big Profiteroles with bittersweet dark chocolate was a decadent shared treat that left a sweet final impression.

This restaurant, with its heartfelt origins and commitment to service and quality, made my birthday dinner one to recall fondly. P.S. Make sure to bring cash or your Amex card!

Title: A Slice of France Right Here at Home

Review:

Whether you're fluent in French or just craving an authentic French culinary experience, this restaurant is a must-visit. It's an established gem in the neighborhood, renowned for its exceptional fare. My meal - comprised of French Onion soup and a Caesar salad - was reminiscent of dishes I've savored in Paris. The details matter here; even the croutons were elevated, baked in-house and perfectly seasoned. It's a place where every bite is a delight. I'm already looking forward to my next visit, with steak tartare in my sights. Bon appétit, indeed!

Title: Disappointing BBQ Experience Near the Hospital

My sister and I stopped at Dallas BBQ for a quick lunch while we were by the hospital, but if you're seeking authentic Texas-style BBQ, you may want to keep looking. I made the mistake of going for the beef ribs, which were unfortunately tough and slathered in what tasted like bargain-bin BBQ sauce. The fries didn't fare much better, being bland and forgettable. I didn't even venture to try the cornbread.

On a positive note, the service was commendable with attentive waitstaff. Looking back, opting for something more straightforward like a burger or the chicken and waffles, which seemed popular among other patrons, might have been wiser. Alas, for me, or any true BBQ aficionado, Dallas BBQ might just not hit the mark.

Title: A Bittersweet Experience at KF Kitchen

My search for the perfect bao led me to KF Kitchen, lured in by the promise of eye-catching rainbow dumplings featured on Yelp. Upon arrival, the restaurant was quiet, but it quickly filled to capacity by 12:30 PM, a testament to its popularity.

However, my excitement turned to confusion when I learned that the advertised rainbow dumplings did not exist. It was a disappointing case of mistaken expectations, akin to the display photos at other eateries that merely illustrate menu offerings without actually being available.

Shifting focus from the letdown, we ordered other dishes. My mother enjoyed her beef hand-shaped noodle soup, while I indulged in an assortment of bao and dumplings. The pork dumplings were unremarkable, and the dumpling soup failed to impress. The saving grace was the steamed pork juicy buns (XLB), which were scrumptious with delightfully thicker skins that held together well.

The billing process introduced additional confusion with a mandatory service charge labeled as such, and an ambiguous tip section on the bill, prompting a need for clarification.

Lastly, the 'Check-in Offer' for a 10% discount at KF Kitchen was misleading, as it apparently required a written review rather than just a check-in, adding to the mixed feelings about the restaurant.

In summary, KF Kitchen delivered a mixed bag of culinary hits and misses, marred by some misleading advertising and perplexing billing practices.

Finally took part in Restaurant Week with a fantastic weeknight dinner at Smith & Wollensky!Truly the greatest steak experience of my life and although there have been few, it likely will not be bested any time soon. But let's start at the beginning: our appetizers were fried calamari and Caesar salad. Suitable, good appetizers to accompany the nice bread basket. We had the rosé and a red off the Restaurant Week menu (which, by the way, are not included in the price!). Our entrees were a bit slow coming after the apps, but worth the wait! I had filet mignon (medium well) and my friend had sirloin. Our waiter convinced us to get a side of whipped potatoes, which were heavenly. And the STEAK. Just melted in your mouth and was so juicy! I'm going to dream about it forever. By the dessert course, we barely had any more room in our stomachs but we toughed it out for the cheesecake (rich and SUBLIME) and coconut layer cake (not as good as I hoped, sadly). All around a great experience and well worth the (Restaurant Week) price tag.

We were greeted and seated pretty quickly (I had a reservation. The food was good; ordered the mushroom bun (a little too acidic for my tastes), the special spicy sausage and Korean rice cake (I could only eat the pieces of cake without sausage...and they were super crispy, I liked it but there was too much sauce for my mom to enjoy it), and the shellfish and sambal (flavors were solid and not overpowering, the oyster was yummy but there were only 2, mussels were fine probably 4 in the bowl, best part was the grilled prawns, amazing). I am giving 3 stars because when we were ordering, I had my menu open for my mom (she had her own) but I was talking to her about something and the server just picked up my menu put it back in front of me, took my moms and then opened it in front of her....we knew there were two menus. I just felt like that was a little awkward? I don't know. Everything else was fine.

Precious gem with a wonderful vibe and super friendly owners. We visited on December 26 for their happy hour and before our dinner reservation at a nearby favorite of mine. They were not too busy, surprisingly, so the owners did not mind us peppering them with questions. They have an interesting story.Delighted to learn about their grand selection of California wines and their technological opener that enables them to serve any wine by the glass. So pleased to see Tillman and Truchard wines as options for HH. Beautiful lighting structure being built from main ceiling.Place is charming. Though small, it is light and bright and open. I could see doing a fun casual party event here for some nice occasion.We tried their meat and cheese board with olives and more. Very nicely presented with a nice amount of charcuterie.Need to get a nice dose of California wine country in Brooklyn. Go here and taste some great vino. Cheers.

Lovely casual space, very friendly ajumma, better than decent fried chicken, the kim chi pancake actually has large chunks of kim chi in it . Will definitely be back if Korean craving hits and I'm too lazy to make my way all the way to ktown.

Decent Italian restaurant in area but I expect t there are many others that are as good or better too. The handmade mushroom and truffle oil pasta was the hit of the visit along with all 3 really food cocktails and drinks we had which were on happy hour. Bread was decent too and they provided butter and oil and vinegar to dip in which nice too. Mussels in garlic were good but waiter failed to bring a small fork for it or bowl to place shells in which was a service gap.Fettuccine Alfredo was a nice portion but lacked flavor unfortunately otherwise I'd given a higher. star but honestly would rate 3 1/2 stars if it were an option.

Solid place for pho / standard Viet food. Nothing too special, but will satisfy your cravings. Pretty damn similar to the few other Viet places nearby. Typically would rate this a 3 or 3.5 (if I could) but giving it a whole 4 stars because we wanted to try something new this weekend and our nice waitress was super accommodating and understanding!Now if you're Vietnamese (or even just from Toronto, which my boyfriend is) you might be familiar with the DIY-style platters that you can wrap up in rice paper after dipping them in hot water. Think: Vietnamese summer rolls, but DIY. Or, DIY lettuce wraps but with an additional layer of rice paper.As a Chinese-American who grew up in NYC, I had no idea this was a thing, even though I had thought I was well-acquainted with the Viet culture (#noob). My boyfriend, a Chinese-Canadian however, had insisted numerous times that this is a staple dish when his family gets Viet food in Toronto... I didn't rly believe him until this weekend when he finally showed me up and specifically asked for a side of rice paper + a bowl of hot water (off menu!), to accompany an order of the grilled pork bánh hoi (angel hair noodle). This order (ON menu) is a platter of bite-sized pieces of grilled pork that sits on a bed of angel hair noodles, and comes with cucumbers, lettuce, pickled carrots/daikon, basil leaves and fish sauce.At first our waitress was a little confused about this request, but eventually had an aha moment and said "summer roll skin!" - totally understanding what we wanted and told us it'd be an additional $2. She brought over a plate of the raw, hard skin (probably exactly what they use to make summer rolls) and a large bowl of hot water. What you do is soak the individual rice paper for a minute or less until it softens, and build the wrap on your plate with each ingredient from the platter. Delicious and fun authentic experience!! Secret's out, my fellow New Yorkers, it's not that this doesn't exist in the city -- it's usually just a secret menu item at your local Viet spot. #staywoke

The atmosphere bumps it up to 4 star.  I loved the decor especially the dragon!  I had the pad prik king and it was very tasty.  I especially liked the string beans and red/green peppers...lots of crunchy flavor.  The spice was normal for me with this dish...which means spicier than most menu items.  For the app, I had the chicken and shrimp dumplings...they were enormous.  It was very good, lots of meat.  BTW, I went to a show afterwards and the theater was very close.I'd definitely go back and try one of the curries.Check it out!

Writing an updated review for brunch because I've been converted into a fan.The last time I was here, I had a mediocre dinner experience. However, brunch has changed my perspective on Root & Bone, and the food blew me away. I ordered the Fried Chicken Biscuits which are no joke. Imagine a chicken cutlet topped with crunchy chips and sandwiched between two dense, soft biscuits. Now multiply that by two, and you have the dish I ate yesterday. Absolutely fantastic - the chicken was crispy and the chips added a nice crunch. My friend got the Waffle Benedict which she seemed to enjoy, although the portions did seem a bit small for that one. We also split the macaroni and cheese, which was okay but not worth the $9 price tag. If you're looking for somewhere to grab brunch, I would definitely recommend stopping at Root & Bone. Brunch has 100% restored my faith in this restaurant.

Great spot for after work happy hour, spacious, open air, friendly staffs.Pretty good selection of food and drinks.HH fries and shrimps were alright, regular menu looked interesting, would love to come back to try!
